northern_bald_ibis: A colony of northern bald ibis roosts and forages together across badlands and mountain slopes, feeding mainly on insects. Adults weigh about 1.3 kilograms, and the species is still alive today. Its range once stretched from the North African coast through Arabia, Iran, Anatolia, the Alps, and the Sahel, and the birds still migrate between these regions.
reeves_pheasant: Reeves's pheasant lives in the lowlands of China, where it moves between forest and mountain terrain. Adults weigh about 1.4 kg, and the males carry a tail that can stretch to roughly 2 m. Its diet includes both plant and animal food, and it remains a living species that people have hunted.
victoria_crowned_pigeon: The Victoria crowned pigeon lives in the jungles of Wallacea and New Guinea, where it spends most of its time on the forest floor. It is a ground feeder that eats fruit, and adults weigh about 2.4 kilograms. Its lacy crest and blue-gray plumage make it a prized target for hunters, and the species is still alive today.
house_centipede: The house centipede is a long-legged arthropod found across the Mediterranean and throughout Europe. It moves quickly and hunts mostly at night, preying on other small animals. An adult weighs only about half a gram, and it can be found in caves and forests where it is still thriving today.
owl_butterfly: Found across Central America, southern Mexico, and the Amazon basin, the owl butterfly lives in jungle habitats. Adults weigh about 0.003 kg and feed on fruit. They are active at dusk, and the large eyespots on their wings help deter predators. This species is still living and is not extinct.
yellowtail_amberjack: Found across warm seas, from the Caribbean and the North Atlantic to the Mediterranean, the Indian Ocean, and the southern Pacific, the greater amberjack patrols reefs and open warm water. This meat-eating fish can grow to about 60 kilograms as an adult, and it is still common today. Anglers hunt it for sport, and its flesh is prized as food.
black_mamo: The black mamo was a small honeyeater that lived in the forests of Hawaii, where its range spanned roughly 21.05 to 21.2 degrees north and 156.7 to 157.3 degrees west. It fed mainly on nectar and weighed about 0.03 kilograms as an adult. The species was declared extinct in 1907, and its feathers and flight were noted features of the bird.
american_white_pelican: The American white pelican breeds across the Great Plains and the Canadian Shield, then spends the colder months in Mexico and along the Florida and Gulf coasts. It favors lakes and coastal waters, where it feeds mainly on fish. Adults weigh about 7 kg, and the species nests in large colonies and travels long distances each year.
black_crappie: Black crappie are freshwater fish found across eastern North America and the Great Plains. They live in both lakes and rivers, where they feed on other animals. Adults typically reach about 1 kilogram, and they are still widespread and common. Anglers and cooks value them as a good eating fish.
red_grouper: Along the reefs of Florida, the Gulf, and the Caribbean Sea, the red grouper (Epinephelus morio) makes its home. This meat-eating fish can grow to about 23 kilograms as an adult, and it remains common in the wild. People also value it as a food fish.
australian_box_jelly: The Australian box jellyfish, Chironex fleckeri, lives along coasts and reefs across the Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle, Australia, and Wallacea and New Guinea. It is a carnivore that swims through these waters and reaches an adult mass of about 2 kg. Among the world's jellyfish, it is considered the most venomous, and its stings can be deadly to people.
totoaba: The totoaba is a large croaker that lives along the coasts of Mexico in the western part of North America. Adults can reach about 100 kg, and this carnivore hunts in coastal waters. Its swim bladder has long been traded illegally, which has led to strong legal protection for the species, though it still survives today.
convict_cichlid: The convict cichlid makes its home in Central America, where it lives in both lakes and rivers. It is an omnivore, so it eats a mix of plant and animal food. A full-grown adult weighs about 0.05 kg, and this species is still alive in the wild today. It is known for its swimming.
crown_of_thorns: The crown-of-thorns starfish is found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It lives on reefs, where adults can reach about 3 kilograms. Covered in venomous spines, this carnivorous starfish feeds on coral, and it is still living today.
great_tinamou: The great tinamou is a ground-dwelling bird found in Central America and the Amazon basin. It lives in jungle and forest habitats and eats both plants and animals. Adults weigh about 1.0 kg, and the species is still alive, though it is hunted and its eggs are gathered.
nile_perch: Found across the Nile valley, the Sahel, and the Congo basin in Africa, the Nile perch lives in both rivers and lakes. It is a carnivore that hunts other fish, and adults can reach about 200 kg. Still living in the wild, this giant swimmer is hunted by people and its flesh is eaten.
spanish_mackerel_narrow: The narrow-barred Spanish mackerel lives in warm coastal waters across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and the Red Sea. It is a carnivore that swims in open water near shore, and adults can reach about 70 kg. It is still common, it can be hunted by anglers, and its flesh is eaten by people.
aepyornis_hildebrandti: Hildebrandt's elephant bird once roamed the forests and mountain slopes of Madagascar, feeding on plants and herbs. Adults weighed around 230 kg, making it a heavy, flightless bird covered in feathers. It was hunted by people before it vanished around the year 1000 AD.
tiger_prawn: The giant tiger prawn lives along coasts from the Indian Ocean through the Coral Triangle, Sundaland, Indochina, and Australia. Adults can reach about 0.3 kg, and the species eats both plants and animals. It is still widespread, and its shell is edible and it can be raised in farms.
short_toed_eagle: The short-toed snake eagle is a diurnal bird of prey that still thrives today. It weighs about 1.9 kilograms as an adult and hunts mainly snakes, which it catches while soaring over forest and plains. Its range spans the Mediterranean, Iran and Anatolia, the Indian subcontinent, and the Sahel, and many of these birds travel between those regions each year.
great_bustard: Among the heaviest flying birds in the world, this species reaches an adult mass of about 13 kg. It lives across Europe and the eastern steppes, including the Mongolian steppe, where it favors open plains and grassland. Its diet is omnivorous, and males gather at display grounds called leks to attract mates.
new_zealand_grayling: The New Zealand grayling lived in the rivers of New Zealand, where it fed on insects and grew to an adult mass of about 0.2 kg. It swam through these waters until habitat loss and introduced trout drove it toward extinction, which was recorded in 1930 AD.
satin_bowerbird: The satin bowerbird is a bird of the eastern forests of Australia, where it spends its time among the trees. Adults weigh about 0.23 kg, and they feed mainly on fruit. Males build a bower, a structure they decorate with feathers, and they are still very much alive today.
carolina_wolf: The Carolina wolf spider roams the eastern and southern United States, moving through forests and open grassland alike. It hunts other small creatures, and a grown adult weighs about 0.01 kilograms. Females dig burrows where they can retreat, and they carry their young on their backs after the eggs hatch.
giant_oarfish: The giant oarfish lives in deep ocean waters across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, along with tropical seas and the Mediterranean. It is the longest bony fish known, and adults can reach about 270 kilograms. Its rarity and long, snake-like body helped inspire sea serpent legends.
whip_scorpion: Active at night, the giant vinegaroon digs burrows in desert and forest ground across the southern United States, Mexico, and the Florida and Gulf coast. It hunts other creatures for food. When threatened, it sprays a sharp acid that gives it the name vinegaroon. Adults weigh about 0.02 kg, and the species is still living today.
mozambique_tilapia: The Mozambique tilapia calls the rivers, lakes, and coastal waters of southern Africa home. It eats both plants and animals, and a fully grown adult typically weighs about 1.5 kilograms. This fish is still thriving in the wild, and people have long valued it as a food source and as a species that can be kept in captivity.
tautog: The tautog, known scientifically as Tautoga onitis, makes its home along the eastern coast of North America. It favors reefs and rocky shores, where it feeds on other animals. Adults can reach a mass of about 10 kilograms, and the species is still thriving today. People also consider it good to eat.
leaf_insect: Dwelling in the jungles of Sundaland and Indochina, the giant leaf insect is a herbivore that feeds on plants. An adult weighs about 0.01 kilograms, and its body is shaped and colored so closely like a leaf that it can blend into foliage. The species is still alive and widespread in the wild.
mourning_dove: Found across North America, Mexico, and Central America, the mourning dove makes its home on open plains and in deserts. It feeds mainly on seeds and other plant material, and an adult weighs about 0.12 kg. Though still common and widespread today, this bird is hunted in many areas and often gathers in flocks.
northern_snakehead: The northern snakehead lives in the lowlands of China, the Siberian taiga, and parts of Japan and Korea, where it hunts in lakes, wetlands, and rivers. It is a carnivore that can reach about 8 kilograms as an adult. This species is still living in the wild, and it can breathe air as well as use gills, while its flesh is considered good to eat.
rifleman: The rifleman, known to science as Acanthisitta chloris, lives in the forests of New Zealand and feeds mainly on insects. Adults weigh only about 0.007 kg, which makes this bird the smallest native songbird of its country. Though tiny, it is still alive and continues to flit through the woodland canopy.
lionfish: The red lionfish, known scientifically as Pterois volitans, lives on reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Polynesia. It is a carnivore that hunts by ambush, waiting for small prey to drift close before striking. Adults can reach about 1 kilogram, and their venomous spines serve as a defense against predators.
white_backed_vulture: The white-backed vulture lives across Africa south of the Sahara and throughout the Sahel. It favors open savanna, where it feeds mainly on carrion. Adults weigh about 5.5 kilograms. It is active during the day and soars on the wind as it searches for its next meal.
catla: The catla is a large freshwater fish found across the Indian subcontinent, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It feeds mainly on filamentous algae and can grow to an adult mass of about 25 kg. Catla is still widespread, is a strong swimmer, is valued as food, and can be raised in captivity.
muscovy_duck: Muscovy ducks are found from Mexico through Central America, across the Amazon basin, and into the Pampas and Gran Chaco. They favor swamps, rivers, and forest edges, and they often roost in trees. Their diet is omnivorous, and an adult weighs about 2.5 kg. Muscovy ducks can be domesticated, and they are still hunted for food and their feathers.
eurasian_scops_owl: The Eurasian scops owl is a small nocturnal bird that roams the Mediterranean, Europe, and Africa south of the Sahara. It favors forested areas, where it hunts flying insects. An adult weighs about 0.08 kg, and this migratory species is still thriving across its range.
torrent_duck: Torrent ducks make their home on fast, rocky rivers high in the Andes. They feed mainly on insects and are at home in the swift water, where they swim and dive among the currents. An adult typically weighs about 0.4 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
head_louse: Human lice are tiny wingless insects that cling to human hair and clothing, and they are found across the world. Their listed habitat is forest, and an adult weighs only about one microgram. Though small, this parasite remains very much alive today, feeding on the blood of its host.
sailfish_atlantic: Found across warm ocean waters from the northern and southern Atlantic to the Caribbean, the Gulf of Mexico, and the western African coast, this predator reaches around 60 kilograms as an adult. It hunts smaller fish and is prized by anglers for its speed and its large dorsal sail. Its flesh is edible, and it remains abundant in the wild.
cuban_gar: The Cuban gar, Atractosteus tristoechus, still swims through the swamps and rivers of the Caribbean. It is a meat eater that can reach about 50 kilograms as an adult. Its body is covered in tough, armour-like scales, and the species is legally protected.
fiddler_crab: The males of this small crab carry one oversized claw, which they wave in courtship displays along muddy coasts. Adults weigh about 0.01 kg, and they are still common today. You can find them across the eastern part of North America, around Florida and the Gulf, in both swamps and coastal marshes. They feed mainly on plants.
greenland_halibut: The Greenland halibut lives in cold, deep ocean waters across the Arctic and northern Atlantic, around Iceland and Greenland, and in the northern Pacific. It is a meat eater that swims through these chilly depths. Adults can reach about 45 kg, and the species is still thriving and prized as a food fish.
nukupuu: The Nukupuu was a small honeycreeper that lived in the forests of Hawaii, where it fed on insects. An adult weighed about 16 grams, roughly the mass of a few coins. This bird was last recorded in 1996, and it is now extinct.
albacore: Albacore tuna roam the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans as well as the Mediterranean Sea, moving between warm and cold waters. Adults can reach about 40 kilograms, and they feed on other fish and marine creatures. Their long migrations and firm, mild flesh make them an important food fish that remains abundant today.
hooded_grebe: The Titicaca flightless grebe lives on Lake Titicaca in the Andes, where it hunts fish in cold mountain waters. Adults weigh about 0.6 kilograms. Though it cannot fly, this bird remains alive today, and its dense feathers help keep it warm in the lake.
rohu: The rohu is a freshwater fish that lives in rivers and lakes across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina. Adults can reach a mass of about 15 kilograms, and they feed mainly on plants. People eat this species widely, and it can also be raised under human care. It remains alive in the wild today.
smalltooth_sawfish: The smalltooth sawfish is a ray with a long, flattened snout lined with toothed edges that it sweeps through the water to stun and catch its prey. Adults can reach about 350 kilograms, and they live along coasts in Florida, the Gulf, the Caribbean, the western coast of Africa, and the Mediterranean. Though still alive, this species is protected because its numbers have declined.
white_tailed_tropicbird: The white-tailed tropicbird lives over tropical seas, including the Caribbean, and nests on islands. It feeds mainly on fish, which it catches by plunging into the water from the air. Adults weigh about 0.4 kg, and this species is still alive and widespread in its range.
pacific_oyster: The Pacific oyster is found along coastlines in Japan, Korea, and the lowlands of China. It spends its adult life fixed in place, filtering food from the water as it feeds. A grown individual weighs about 0.25 kg, and its shell is both protective and edible. This species is still living today.
dinornis_robustus: The South Island giant moa once roamed the forests, grasslands, and mountains of New Zealand, where it grazed on herbs. Standing among the tallest birds ever to live, this flightless bird weighed about 240 kg, and its feathers and eggs were valued by people. Hunted by the Maori and preyed upon by Haast's eagle, it vanished around 1450 AD.
marbled_murrelet: The marbled murrelet is a small seabird of the North Pacific, found along the coasts from the Pacific Northwest up through Alaska and into the Yukon. It feeds mainly on fish, which it catches by diving and swimming underwater. Unusually for a seabird, it nests inland in old-growth trees, where it lays a single egg on a mossy branch.
orangetip: The orange tip is a small butterfly found across Europe and northern Asia, where it lives in both grassland and woodland. Adults feed on nectar and weigh only about 0.0002 kg. This species is still common and continues to take to the air across its range.
band_tailed_pigeon: The band-tailed pigeon is found across western North America, Mexico, and the Andes. It lives in forests and mountain country, feeding mainly on fruit. Adults weigh about 0.35 kg, and the species is still widespread today, though it is hunted in some areas.
blenny_redlip: Small and quick, the redlip blenny is a fish that moves through reef waters across the Caribbean and the western tropical Atlantic. It makes its home among the rocks and coral of shallow reefs, where it grazes on plant matter. An adult weighs only about 0.01 kilograms, and the species is still alive and widespread today.
california_condor: The California condor is a large scavenger that lives across western North America and into Mexico, where it soars over mountains and coastlines. Adults weigh about 9 kilograms, and they feed on carrion during daylight hours. By 1987 the species had come close to extinction, and it is now protected, though it survives today.
porcupine_ray: The porcupine ray is a still-living species found along coasts of the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, and the Great Barrier Reef. It feeds on meat and can grow to an adult mass of around 40 kg. Its body is covered in spines, and it swims through its coastal waters with ease.
slender_billed_curlew: The slender-billed curlew once travelled between Siberian taiga, the Mediterranean, and the regions of Iran and Anatolia. It favoured wetlands, where it fed on insects, and it weighed about 0.3 kg as an adult. Its feathers and migratory habits are noted in its record, and it was declared extinct in 2000 AD.
camel_spider: The Egyptian giant solpugid, Galeodes arabs, roams the deserts of the Sahara, Arabia, and the Nile valley. Despite its common name of camel spider, it is not a true spider. This fast, nocturnal hunter eats other animals and weighs about 0.03 kg as an adult. It is still living today.
yellow_eyed_penguin: The yellow-eyed penguin, also called hoiho, lives in New Zealand and the subantarctic islands. It nests in coastal forest and feeds mainly on fish. Adults weigh about 5.5 kg, and this rare bird is still alive today, swimming along the coast in search of its meals.
red_headed_woodpecker: Found across eastern North America and the Great Plains, this woodpecker moves between forest and open plains country. It eats a mix of foods and weighs about 0.07 kg as an adult. Its feathers are striking, it flies with a strong flapping style, and it stores food in hidden spots for later.
stonefish: Lurking on reefs and rocky coasts across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia, this fish blends almost perfectly into its surroundings. It feeds on other animals and can reach about 2 kilograms as an adult. Its venom is considered the most potent of any fish, so divers are advised to step carefully and keep clear of it.
honeypot_ant: Some desert colonies keep living storage ants called repletes, whose swollen abdomens hold sweet nectar for the rest of the nest. This species lives in the southern United States, Mexico, and Australia, where it feeds on nectar and remains alive today. Adults weigh about 0.0002 kg, and the stored honey is edible.
great_argus: The great argus roams the jungles of Sundaland and Indochina, where it forages for seeds, fruit, insects, and small animals on the forest floor. Adults weigh about 2 kilograms. Males are known for their enormous wing feathers, which carry striking eyespot patterns used in courtship displays.
peruvian_pelican: Along the coasts of Peru and Chile, the Peruvian pelican lives where cold ocean currents bring fish close to shore. Adults weigh about 6 kilograms and feed mainly on fish. These birds nest in large colonies, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
heath_hen: Once common across the grasslands and scrub forests of eastern North America, this bird fed mostly on plants and weighed about a kilogram as an adult. Hunting pressure made the heath hen a game target, and the last known individuals survived on Martha's Vineyard until the species disappeared in 1932.
japanese_spider_crab: Living in the deep waters around Japan and Korea, this crab is the largest arthropod known for its leg span. Adults can reach about 19 kilograms, and they feed as scavengers on whatever food settles to the seafloor. Their hard shell protects them, and they are also prized as a food, while their long lifespan keeps them a steady presence in those seas.
water_strider: The common pond skater is a slender insect that lives across Europe and North America. It makes its home on lakes and rivers, where it glides over the water's surface. As a carnivore, it feeds on small creatures it catches on or near the water. An adult weighs only about 0.00002 kilograms, and it is still widespread today.
fiordland_penguin: The Fiordland penguin is a species found in New Zealand, where it lives along both forested land and the rocky coast. It feeds mainly on fish and can swim well through the cold waters around its home. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms, and the species is still alive today.
little_skate: The little skate lives along the eastern coast of North America and in the northern Atlantic, where it spends its time near the shore. It feeds on other animals and typically grows to about 1 kilogram as an adult. This species is still alive and swims through coastal waters, and its flesh is edible.
southern_rock_lobster: Found along the reefs of Australia, Tasmania, and New Zealand, the southern rock lobster is an omnivore that can grow to about 8 kilograms as an adult. Its hard shell makes it a sturdy resident of rocky reef habitats. People hunt it for food, and it remains widespread today with no extinction concerns.
titicaca_orestias_pupfish: This small fish lives in the Andes, where it inhabits both the lake and the surrounding mountain waters. It feeds on insects and grows to about 0.1 kg as an adult. It swims freely, is found nowhere else in the world, and is still alive today, and people also eat it.
kori_bustard: The Kori bustard is a still-living bird of the East African and Southern African savanna, where it roams open grassland. Adults weigh about 14 kilograms, making it one of the heaviest birds that can still fly. It eats a varied, omnivorous diet, and its large body and heavy wings make it a notable flier, though it is also a huntable species.
tigerfish: The Goliath tigerfish lives in the rivers of the Congo basin, where it swims through the current in search of meat. Adults can reach a mass of about 50 kilograms, and they are known for their razor-sharp teeth. Though still common and very much alive, the species is hunted by people, and it often moves through the water in packs.
oscar: The oscar is a freshwater fish from the Amazon basin, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It feeds on other animals and can grow to about 1.5 kilograms as an adult. Oscars are still widespread in the wild, and people also eat them.
mascarene_grey_parakeet: The Mascarene grey parakeet once lived in the forests of islands in the Mascarene group, a stretch of ocean between -20.5 and -20.2 degrees latitude and 57.3 to 57.8 degrees longitude. Its diet was mostly fruit, and an adult weighed about 0.15 kilograms. Known for its feathers and flight, this small bird was last recorded in 1730 AD and is now extinct.
common_bream: The common bream lives across Europe, including the British Isles and the Black and Caspian seas. It is found in lakes and rivers, where it feeds on both plants and small animals. Adults can reach a mass of about 4 kg, and the species forms schools as it swims. It remains widespread today and is edible.
common_guitarfish: The common guitarfish is a ray with a flattened, guitar-shaped body that lives along coastal waters. It can be found in the Mediterranean Sea, the Atlantic coast of Europe, and the coast of West Africa. Adults weigh around 10 kilograms, and it feeds on other creatures of the seabed. It is still alive in the wild and is also eaten by people.
butterflyfish_raccoon: Colourful and quick, the raccoon butterflyfish is found on reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, Polynesia, and Hawaii. This omnivore typically weighs about 0.2 kg as an adult. It remains widespread and is still living today.
bumblebee_buff: Found across Europe, the British Isles, and the Mediterranean, the buff-tailed bumblebee makes its home in grassland. Adults weigh about 0.0006 kg and feed mainly on nectar. This furry flier is a busy pollinator and remains widespread today.
european_perch: The European perch is still living and can be found across Europe, northern Asia, and the British Isles. It makes its home in lakes and rivers, where it hunts smaller fish and other prey. Adults can reach about 1.5 kg, and the species is valued as both a catch for anglers and a fish for the table.
silk_moth: The wild ancestor of the domestic silk moth lives in the lowlands of China, Japan, and Korea, where it roams forest edges and woodland. Adults are small, weighing about a gram, and they feed on nectar while flying through the night. Although they remain wild and free, this species can be domesticated, and it is the parent stock from which silk-producing moths were bred.
grey_heron: Wading through shallow water on long legs, the grey heron hunts fish in wetlands, rivers, and lakes. It ranges across the Palearctic, Africa, and the Indian subcontinent, and it is still widespread today. An adult typically weighs about 1.8 kilograms.
european_pilchard: Schools of this small fish move through the coastal and warmer ocean waters of Atlantic Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas. It feeds by filtering, and an adult weighs about 0.1 kg. Still widespread today, it is valued as an edible species and is known for swimming in tight, coordinated schools.
asian_redtail: The giant gourami is a large freshwater fish found across Sundaland and Indochina, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It eats both plants and animals, and adults can reach about 20 kg. Still living in the wild, this species is valued as food and can be domesticated.
rusty_patched_bumblebee: The rusty patched bumblebee lives across eastern North America, where it favors open grasslands. Adults weigh roughly 0.0004 kg and feed on nectar as they move from flower to flower. Although it still survives, this bumblebee is protected because its numbers have fallen sharply.
madagascar_fish_eagle: The Madagascar fish eagle lives only on the island of Madagascar, where it hunts along coasts and around lakes. Adults weigh about 3 kg, and their diet is made up of fish. These birds are active during the day, and they fly over the water to search for prey. The species is still alive and is legally protected.
signal_crayfish: Native to the northwestern part of North America, the signal crayfish makes its home in rivers and lakes. It eats almost anything it can find, from plants to small animals, and a fully grown adult weighs about 0.1 kg. People can eat it, and its hard shell is one of its notable features. The species is still alive and widespread.
martial_eagle: The martial eagle, known to science as Polemaetus bellicosus, ranges across Africa south of the Sahara. It favors open savanna and plains, where it hunts during daylight. Adults weigh about 5 kg, making it one of the largest eagles in the world, and it remains widespread today.
south_american_lungfish: The South American lungfish inhabits swamps and wetlands across the Amazon basin and the Pampas and Gran Chaco regions. Adults can reach about 10 kilograms, and they feed on other animals. This species breathes air using lungs, and during dry spells it can aestivate, sheltering in mud until the water returns.
northern_pike: Found across Europe, northern North America, and northern Asia, the northern pike haunts lakes, rivers, and marshy wetlands. This meat-eating fish can reach about 10 kilograms as an adult and still thrives today. It lies in wait among weeds and ambushes its prey, and anglers and cooks both prize it as a catch worth taking home.
paper_nautilus: The greater argonaut lives in tropical and temperate seas across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, as well as the Mediterranean. It is a carnivore that swims through open warm waters. Adults weigh about 0.3 kg, and the females build a thin, papery egg case that serves as a shell.
bigfin_reef_squid: The bigfin reef squid lives in shallow waters across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It favors reefs and coastal zones, where it hunts meat-based prey. Adults can reach about 2 kg, and the species is still thriving. It swims with agility and changes its colours to send signals to others.
dodo: The dodo was a flightless bird that once lived in the forests of Mauritius, an island in the Indian Ocean. Adults weighed about 12 kilograms, and they fed on fruit. Because they showed little fear of people, they were easy to hunt, and the species was gone by 1681.
rock_dove: Rock doves are found along Mediterranean, European, and African coasts, as well as in Iran, Anatolia, and across the Indian subcontinent. They favor both seaside cliffs and mountain terrain, and they feed on plant matter. An adult weighs about 0.35 kg, and the species remains widespread today. It can be domesticated, it is hunted in some areas, and it is known for its strong homing ability.
common_kingfisher: Along slow rivers and quiet lakes across the Palearctic, Indomalaya, and Wallacea and New Guinea, this small bird hunts fish by diving from a perch. Adults weigh only about 0.04 kg, yet they fly fast and low over the water. Each pair excavates a burrow in a riverbank to raise its young.
splendid_fairywren: The splendid fairywren lives across Australia, where it moves through desert and badlands country. Its diet is made up of insects, and an adult weighs only about 0.009 kg. This small bird is still alive and is known for its feathers and quick flight.
cory_shearwater: Cory's shearwater is a seabird that breeds on islands and ranges across the North Atlantic, the Mediterranean Sea, and the South Atlantic. It feeds mainly on fish and spends most of its life over warm ocean waters. Adults weigh about 0.8 kilograms, and the species is migratory, flying long distances between its breeding and wintering grounds. It is still living today.
bigeye_thresher: The bigeye thresher shark lives in warm tropical seas and deeper ocean waters across the Indian, Atlantic, and Pacific oceans, including the Coral Triangle and the Caribbean. It is a carnivore, and adults can reach about 360 kilograms. Its long upper tail is used to slap at prey, and it is still living today.
red_footed_booby: The red-footed booby is a seabird of tropical oceans, found in the Galapagos and Hawaii as well as other warm seas. It hunts fish over open water and returns to islands to rest and breed. Adults weigh about 1 kg, and this species nests in trees, perching high above the ground where few predators reach it.
freshwater_pearl_mussel: Anchored in clean, flowing rivers, this filter feeder draws in water and strains out tiny food particles. Adults can weigh around 0.15 kilograms, and the species is known for living a very long time. Its shell sometimes produces pearls, and because populations have declined, it is now a protected animal across parts of Europe, Scandinavia, the British Isles, and eastern North America.
newtons_parakeet: Once found across the forests of Réunion, a small island in the Indian Ocean, this parakeet fed on fruit and weighed about 0.12 kg as an adult. Its feathers and its flight are the details recorded about it. The species was declared extinct in 1875.
earwig_common: The common earwig is a tiny insect found across Europe and northern Asia, where it lives in forests. It weighs only about 0.0001 kilograms as an adult and feeds on both plant and animal matter. Females are known for caring for their young, and the species remains widespread today, with the pincers at the rear of its body easy to recognize.
chambered_nautilus: The chambered nautilus lives in reef and deep ocean waters across the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Indian Ocean, and Sundaland. It is a scavenger, and an adult typically weighs about 0.8 kg. Often called a living fossil, it still survives today and is protected.
european_flounder: Along European coasts, the flounder ranges from the Baltic and North Sea to the Atlantic, the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas. It lives in coastal waters and also ventures up rivers. A carnivore, it can reach about 2 kg as an adult, and it remains common today. People also eat it.
rainbow_stag: The rainbow stag beetle is still found today, living in jungle across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea. Adults weigh about 6 grams and feed on fruit, a diet that suits their forest home. Their shells shimmer with iridescent colors, and they are capable fliers.
garibaldi: The Garibaldi is a bright orange damselfish found along the western coast of North America and in Mexico, where it lives among reefs. It eats both plants and small animals, and an adult typically weighs about 0.4 kg. Known for its territorial nature, this fish is protected and remains common in its range today.
electric_catfish: The electric catfish makes its home in rivers across Africa, including the Nile valley and the Congo basin. It hunts other animals and can grow to about 20 kg. This species is still alive and can deliver an electric shock, and it is also eaten by people.
mascarene_parrot: The Mascarene parrot once lived in forests on the islands of the Mascarene group, a small cluster of islands in the Indian Ocean. It fed mainly on fruit and weighed about 0.3 kg as an adult. Its feathers and talent for mimicry made it a favorite of collectors, and it was kept in menageries before it vanished entirely in 1834.
tufted_duck: Dives beneath the surface are a regular part of life for this diving duck, which forages on lakes across the Palearctic, Africa, and the Indian subcontinent. Adults weigh about 0.7 kg, and the species eats both plant and animal food. It is a migratory bird that remains widespread today and is also hunted in some areas.
weka: The weka is a flightless bird native to New Zealand, where it lives in both forest and coastal areas. It eats a wide range of foods and weighs about 0.9 kg as an adult. Known for its bold habit of stealing from campers, this species remains alive today and can be hunted in some places.
mute_swan: Mute swans live across Europe, the eastern steppe, the Mediterranean, and the Kazakh steppe, where they favor lakes, rivers, and coastal waters. They feed mainly on plants and can weigh about 11 kg as adults. Their feathers have long been valued, and in some places the species has been hunted, while the birds are also known for being aggressive when defending their territory.
lears_macaw: Lear's macaw is a large, mostly blue parrot that still survives in the wild. It makes its home in the badlands, where it nests in cliffs and feeds on frugivorous fare such as palm nuts. An adult weighs about 0.95 kilograms.
white_marlin: The white marlin roams warm open waters across the North and South Atlantic, the Caribbean, the Gulf of Mexico near Florida, and the Mediterranean Sea. It feeds on other fish and grows to roughly 80 kilograms as an adult. Its long, spear-shaped bill sets it apart, and it is still common enough to be hunted and eaten.
red_breasted_merganser: The red-breasted merganser breeds across Arctic, Palearctic, and Nearctic regions, and it is found along coasts and on lakes. Its diet consists mainly of fish, which it catches by diving beneath the water. Adults weigh about 1.1 kilograms, and the species is migratory and still widespread today.
japanese_quail: The Japanese quail is a small game bird found across Japan, Korea, the Siberian taiga, and the lowlands of China. It favors grassland habitats and eats both plant matter and small animals. An adult weighs about 0.1 kg. It is still widespread, and people have long valued it for its feathers and eggs, as well as for its ability to be domesticated and hunted.
eastern_bluebird: The Eastern bluebird lives across eastern North America and into Mexico, where it makes its home in forests and open plains. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.03 kg as an adult. This songbird is still common across its range, and its feathers help it take to the air in flight.
indian_peafowl: The Indian peafowl makes its home across the Indian subcontinent, where it roams both forests and open plains. Adults weigh about 4.5 kg, and they eat a mix of plant and animal foods. Its long, eye-patterned feathers are prized, the bird can be hunted or kept in captivity, and it gathers in herds and holds a sacred place in local traditions.
dragonfish_black: Drifting through the dark depths of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, the black dragonfish hunts smaller prey as a carnivore. An adult weighs about 0.05 kilograms, roughly the mass of a small apple. It swims through the deep ocean and produces its own light through bioluminescence.
upside_down_catfish: Native to the Congo basin, this small catfish makes its home in rivers, where it feeds on a mix of plant and animal matter. A fully grown adult weighs only about 0.05 kilograms. Unlike many species, it is not endangered and remains alive today, and it is known for swimming upside down.
grass_carp: Native to the lowlands of China, the grass carp also lives in the taiga of Siberia and in Japan and Korea. It inhabits rivers and lakes, feeding on plants, and adults can reach about 25 kg. Still widespread today, this fish is edible and has been domesticated.
robber_crab_tropical: The blue land crab lives in burrows dug along coasts and swamps, where it returns to moisture after feeding. Its diet is mostly plant matter, and adults can reach about half a kilogram. It ranges across the Caribbean Sea as well as Florida and the Gulf coast, and it remains widespread today. People in parts of its range harvest it as a food source.
royal_penguin: The royal penguin is a seabird that lives on islands, feeding mainly on fish. Adults weigh about 5.5 kg, and the species is still alive today. Its feathers help it swim well, and it gathers in large groups, with Macquarie among the places where it can be found.
horned_lark: The horned lark ranges across the Nearctic, the Palearctic, and Mexico, where it makes its home on open plains and tundra. Adults weigh about 0.04 kg, and this species is still widespread and alive today. Its diet is omnivorous, and it is known for its feathers and its flight.
sand_dollar: The Pacific sand dollar lives along the western coast of North America, especially in the Pacific Northwest, where it makes its home on the shore. It feeds by filtering food particles from the water, and an adult weighs only about 0.03 kilograms. Its flat, disk-shaped skeleton is one of its most recognizable features, and the species remains widespread today.
peacock_bass: Peacock bass are found across the Amazon and Orinoco basins, where they live in rivers and lakes. These carnivores can reach about 6 kg as adults, and they are still common in the wild. People hunt them for sport and for food, since their flesh is good to eat.
clown_triggerfish: The clown triggerfish is a colourful reef dweller found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Polynesia. It is a carnivore that can reach an adult mass of about 9 kg. It remains alive today and is known for its bright markings and steady swimming among the reef.
spectacled_cormorant: The spectacled cormorant lived along coasts and islands in a range spanning roughly 54.5 to 55.5 degrees north and 165 to 167.5 degrees east, around the Commander Islands. It fed mainly on fish and grew to an adult mass of about 6 kg. Though it could not fly, it was hunted heavily by sailors, and it disappeared entirely by 1852.
giant_guitarfish: The giant guitarfish roams coastal waters of the Indian Ocean and the Red Sea, where it feeds on meat-based prey. Adults can reach about 227 kilograms. Its flattened, shark-and-ray hybrid body makes it an unusual swimmer, and its flesh is considered edible.
long_tailed_tit: Found across Europe and the wider Palearctic, the long-tailed tit lives in woodland where it forages for insects. An adult weighs only about 8 grams, making it a very small bird. These sociable birds move through the trees in flocks, and they are still common and widespread today.
giant_pacific_octopus: The largest octopus in the world, the giant Pacific octopus can reach about 30 kilograms as an adult. It lives in cold coastal waters across the North Pacific, from Japan and Korea up through Alaska and the Yukon and down the western coast of North America. This carnivore hunts prey along the seafloor, and it defends itself by releasing ink. Known for its intelligence, it remains alive today and is hunted and eaten by people in parts of its range.
discus: The discus, Symphysodon aequifasciatus, lives in the Amazon basin, where it moves through both rivers and lakes. It eats a mixed diet of plant and animal matter. Adults reach about 0.3 kg, and this brightly coloured fish remains common in the wild.
dalmatian_pelican: The Dalmatian pelican ranges across Europe, the eastern steppe, Iran and Anatolia, the Mongolian steppe, and the Indian subcontinent. It favors lakes and coasts, where it hunts fish. Among pelicans it is the largest species, with adults weighing about 11.5 kg, and it nests in colonies.
kangaroo_island_emu: The Kangaroo Island emu once roamed the island and nearby forest of South Australia, where it fed on a varied diet of plants and small animals. Adults weighed around 25 kilograms, and this dwarf island form was a smaller relative of the mainland emu. Its feathers and its ease of being hunted contributed to its disappearance, and the last one is recorded to have died in 1827.
red_sea_urchin: Red sea urchins make their home along the rocky coasts of western North America, from the Pacific Northwest up through Alaska and the Yukon. They graze mainly on plants and can grow to about 0.8 kg as adults. Their long spines guard the body, and their roe is prized as edible uni. These urchins are known for living a long time.
barn_owl: Found across much of the world, the barn owl makes its home in plains, grasslands, and forests. This nocturnal bird is a skilled rodent hunter that flies silently over open ground, and adults typically weigh about 0.45 kg. It is a carnivore and remains very much alive today.
atlantic_herring: Atlantic herring roam the cold coastal waters of the North Atlantic, the Baltic and North Sea, around Iceland and Greenland, and along the eastern shores of North America. These schooling fish filter plankton from the water and typically weigh about half a kilogram as adults. They migrate over long distances and are hunted and eaten by people, and they remain abundant today.
cownose_ray: Gliding through coastal waters, the cownose ray roams from eastern North America down through Florida, the Gulf, and the Caribbean Sea. Adults typically weigh about 20 kilograms. These animals feed on meat and move in schools as they migrate, and the species is still thriving today.
common_stingray: The common stingray lives along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the Mediterranean Sea, and the Black and Caspian seas. It is a carnivore that favors shallow coastal waters, where it swims over the seabed. Adults can reach a mass of about 15 kg, and this species is still alive today. Its tail carries a venomous spine that it uses for defense.
atlantic_football_fish: The Atlantic football fish lives in the deep ocean across the North Atlantic, near Iceland and Greenland, and also in the South Atlantic. Adults can reach about 60 kilograms. It hunts other creatures, using a glowing lure to attract prey in the dark water of the deep sea.
yangtze_paddlefish: The Yangtze paddlefish was a giant river fish of the China lowlands, where adults could reach about 300 kg. It fed on other animals and swept through its river home, using a long flat rostrum shaped like a paddle. Dams and overfishing drove the species to extinction, which was recorded in 2005 AD despite legal protection.
murray_cod: Murray cod are freshwater fish found in the rivers of Australia, where they make their homes in slow and deep waters. As carnivores, they lie in wait and ambush their prey before striking, and adults can reach a weight of around 40 kilograms. Although they are still alive in the wild, they are protected, and their flesh is considered good to eat.
european_plaice_goby: The rock goby lives along rocky coasts in Atlantic Europe and the Mediterranean Sea. It is a small fish, with adults weighing only about 0.02 kg, and it moves through the water with a steady swimming motion. Its diet consists of insects, and it remains common today.
andean_flamingo: The Andean flamingo makes its home on high mountain lakes in the Andes, where it lives in colonies. It filters food from the water, and adults weigh about 3 kilograms. This species is still alive, and its feathers and high-altitude way of life set it apart from many other flamingos.
turkey_vulture: Turkey vultures range across the Nearctic, Mexico, Central America, and much of South America, living over plains, forests, and deserts. Adults weigh about 2 kilograms, and they feed on carrion. Unlike many scavengers, they track their meals partly by smell, and they fly during daylight. Populations in the north migrate.
bald_eagle: Found across the Nearctic, the bald eagle makes its home along coasts, lakes, rivers, and forests. Its diet centers on fish, and adults weigh around 4.5 kilograms. Active during the day, this species is protected, and it remains very much alive today.
luna_moth: Drifting through the forests of eastern North America, the luna moth is a pale green insect that flies only at night. Its long, trailing tails give it a graceful silhouette, and the adult weighs about 3 grams. Still widespread today, it sips nectar as an adult.
emeus_crassus: The eastern moa was a flightless bird native to New Zealand, where it roamed both forest and grassland. It was an herbivore, and adults weighed about 75 kg. Hunted by people, it had disappeared by around 1450 AD.
northern_cassowary: The northern cassowary is a large flightless bird found in Wallacea and New Guinea, where it moves through jungle and swamp. Adults can reach about 45 kg, and the species is still alive today. Its diet consists mainly of fruit, and it lives in lowland areas, where it is known to be dangerous to people who approach too closely.
goonch: The goonch lives in rivers across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, where it still survives in the wild. Adults can reach about 70 kilograms, and this carnivorous catfish is known for its strong swimming. Local tales describe it as a man-eater, and it is also eaten by people in the region.
giant_australian_cuttlefish: The giant Australian cuttlefish is the largest cuttlefish known, and adults can reach about 12 kg. It lives in coastal waters and reefs across a broad stretch of southern Australia, and it feeds on other animals. Its skin can change color and pattern to blend into its surroundings, and it gathers in large numbers to spawn.
alaska_pollock: The Alaska pollock is a cold-water fish of the North Pacific, found in waters near Japan, Korea, Alaska, and the Yukon. Adults typically reach about 2 kilograms. It is a meat-eating species that swims in schools, and it remains widespread today. People harvest it as a food fish.
broadnose_sevengill: Seven pairs of gill slits set this shark apart from most others, which typically have five. Living in coastal waters across the Atlantic, Pacific, Indian Ocean, Mediterranean, and off Australia, it is a meat eater that can reach about 107 kilograms as an adult. It remains widespread and is not extinct.
tasmanian_giant_freshwater_lobster: The Tasmanian giant freshwater lobster is a river dweller found only in Tasmania. Adults can reach about 4 kilograms, making it the largest freshwater invertebrate in the world. It feeds on both plant and animal matter, and its hard shell is protected by law.
turbot: Turbot are flatfish that live on the seabed along coasts. They are found across Atlantic Europe, the Baltic and North Sea, the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas. Adults can reach about 25 kg, and they are a prized, edible fish that remains very much alive today.
song_thrush: The song thrush is a songbird found across Europe, Iran, Anatolia, and the Mediterranean region. It lives in forests and plains and eats a mix of foods. Adults weigh about 0.08 kg, and the northern populations migrate, while the species remains common and alive today.
french_angelfish: The French angelfish is a colourful fish that glides over reefs in the tropical waters of the Caribbean Sea and the western Atlantic. It eats both plants and animals, and a full-grown adult weighs about 1 kilogram. This species is still thriving in the wild and can be found swimming among the coral.
lesser_flamingo: The lesser flamingo lives across East and Southern Africa, the Indian subcontinent, and the Sahel. It favors lakes, especially soda lakes, where it gathers in large colonial herds. Adults weigh about 2 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
hawaiian_rail: The moho, also called the Hawaii rail, lived on islands in the Hawaiian chain between roughly latitude 19 to 20 north and longitude 155 to 156 west. Each adult weighed only about 0.07 kilograms, and it fed on insects it found on the ground. Its feathers and its inability to fly made it a distinctive bird, and it was declared extinct in 1893.
wahoo: The wahoo is a still-thriving fish that roams warm tropical seas, including the Indian Ocean, the northern and southern Pacific, and the Caribbean. It is a meat eater that hunts other fish, and adults can reach about 83 kilograms. Known for its speed, it is a prized catch for anglers and its flesh is considered good to eat.
superb_lyrebird: The superb lyrebird lives on the ground in forests of mainland Australia and Tasmania, where it searches the leaf litter for insects. An adult weighs about 1 kilogram. Males are known for fanning their long tail feathers over their heads during displays, and they are skilled mimics of other birds and sounds.
hooded_vulture: Across sub-Saharan Africa and the Sahel, the hooded vulture moves through open savanna in search of carrion. Weighing about 2 kg as an adult, it is a daytime flier that spends its hours gliding over the grassland. Though still widespread and not extinct, it feeds mainly on the remains of dead animals.
striped_marlin: The striped marlin roams warm seas across the northern and southern Pacific, the Indian Ocean, and tropical waters around Hawaii. It is a meat eater that hunts other fish, and adults can reach about 190 kilograms. Anglers and fishers pursue it, and its flesh is edible, while its long spear-like bill sets it apart from many other swimmers.
regal_angelfish: The regal angelfish cruises over reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It eats a varied mix of foods and grows to about 0.3 kg as an adult. Its bright, colourful body makes it easy to spot as it swims among the coral.
little_owl: The little owl is a small, still-thriving bird that lives across Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran, Anatolia, the China lowlands, and the Sahara. It favors open plains and badlands, and it hunts mainly insects. An adult weighs about 0.18 kilograms, and unlike many owls it is active during the day.
timneh_parrot: The Timneh parrot makes its home along the coast of West Africa, where it moves through jungle and forest. Adults weigh about 0.35 kilograms, and the bird feeds mainly on fruit. Its feathers are a point of note, and it is known for its ability to mimic sounds, and it remains alive in the wild today.
cicada_japanese: Native to Indochina and Sundaland, the giant cicada lives in jungle habitats where it feeds on plants. An adult weighs about 0.01 kilograms, and it is still living today. This insect is known for its flight and for being the loudest of all insects.
tanganyika_cichlid: The Frontosa cichlid makes its home in a lake across the East African savanna, where it feeds on other animals. Adults can reach about 1.5 kg, and the species remains alive and well in the wild. Its bold colouring and steady swimming make it easy to spot, and it carries its young in its mouth as a mouthbrooder.
firefly_european: Across Europe and the British Isles, the glow-worm makes its home in grassland. Its wingless female glows at night to attract mates, while the nocturnal life of the species keeps most of its activity hidden from daylight. Weighing only about 0.00005 kg as an adult, this carnivorous beetle is still very much alive today.
blue_king_crab: The blue king crab is found across the northern Pacific Ocean, with populations in Alaska and the Yukon. It lives in cold ocean waters, feeds on other animals, and can reach an adult mass of about 8 kg. This species is still alive, can be hunted, is prized as food, and is protected by a hard shell.
roman_snail: The Burgundy snail is found across Europe, including the Alps, where it lives in forest settings. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 0.03 kilograms. Its shell is a well-known feature, and the species is also prized as the edible snail used in escargot dishes.
common_cuckoo: The common cuckoo ranges across the Palearctic, much of Africa south of the Sahara, and Indomalaya, moving between forests and open plains. Adults weigh about 0.12 kg and feed mainly on insects. This migratory bird is a brood parasite, leaving its eggs in the nests of other species so that they raise its young instead.
lesser_antillean_macaw: The Guadeloupe macaw once lived in the forests of the island of Guadeloupe, in the Lesser Antilles of the Caribbean. Its diet consisted of fruit, and adults weighed about 0.7 kg. Spending its life in the trees, it was hunted for its feathers, and it was last recorded in 1790 AD.
aplomado_falcon: The aplomado falcon is a small, daytime hunter found across Mexico, the Amazon basin, the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and parts of the southern United States. It favors open plains and savanna, where it chases down its prey on the wing. An adult weighs about 0.3 kilograms, and the species is still thriving today.
money_cowrie: The money cowrie is a small sea snail whose glossy shell has been used as currency across many cultures. Adults weigh only about 0.01 kilograms and graze on plants along reefs in the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. Despite its long history as money, this species is still living and thriving today.
chilean_rose: The Chilean rose tarantula lives in the Andes and across the Southern Cone, where it makes its home in deserts and grasslands. It is a carnivore that hunts small prey, and an adult weighs about 0.06 kg. Although it is venomous, this spider is known for being docile, and it spends much of its time in a burrow.
yellowtail_snapper: The yellowtail snapper lives in the Caribbean Sea, Florida and the Gulf, and across the western Atlantic tropics. It favors reef habitats, where it hunts other creatures. Adults can reach a mass of about 4 kg, and the species is still alive and widespread. People also eat it, since it is edible.
ruffe: The ruffe is a small fish found across Europe and northern Asia, where it lives in lakes and rivers. Adults typically weigh about 0.1 kilograms, making them a modest sized catch for anglers. Its diet consists of insects, and it remains widespread today. Its spiny body and steady swimming help it move through its freshwater home.
ocellated_turkey: Found in southern Mexico and Central America, the ocellated turkey lives in jungle and forest habitats. Adults weigh about 4 kg, and this species eats both plants and animals. It is still alive in the wild and is hunted in places such as the Yucatan, where its colorful feathers are also valued.
hippopus_clam: The bear paw clam is a giant clam that lives in reef habitats across the Coral Triangle and the Great Barrier Reef. Adults can reach a mass of about 7 kilograms. It is still alive in the wild, and it spends its adult life fixed in one spot, filter feeding on tiny particles it draws from the water.
damselfish_blue: The blue green chromis is a small reef fish found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It lives among coral reefs, swimming in schools and feeding on plankton. An adult weighs about 0.01 kg, and the species is still alive in the wild.
bull_trout: Bull trout are native to the Pacific Northwest and northwestern North America, where they live in both rivers and lakes. These carnivores can reach an adult mass of about 5 kilograms. Still living in the wild, they are edible yet protected, and they swim through their cold waters in search of prey.
bobolink: Grassland is home to the bobolink, which breeds across eastern North America and the Great Plains and winters in the pampas and Gran Chaco of South America. Adults weigh about 0.04 kg, and they eat both seeds and insects. Among songbirds, this species is known for one of the longest migrations, a journey that carries it over great distances each year.
immortal_jellyfish: Tiny, with an adult mass of only about 0.0001 kilograms, this jellyfish lives along coasts of the Mediterranean Sea, the Caribbean Sea, and the northern and southern Pacific Ocean. It feeds on other small animals and is still living today. Its most unusual trait is that it can revert from its adult form back into a polyp, a much earlier stage of its life.
white_sucker: The white sucker roams the rivers and lakes of eastern North America, the Canadian Shield, and the Great Plains. It feeds on a mix of plant and animal matter, often grazing along the bottom. Adults commonly reach about 1.2 kilograms, and the fish remains widespread and healthy today. Its flesh is edible, which has long made it a useful catch for people in the region.
humphead_wrasse: The humphead wrasse, also called the Napoleon wrasse, lives on coral reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. Adults can reach about 190 kilograms, and the fish is known for its prominent bump on the forehead. It feeds on carnivorous prey and even eats crown-of-thorns starfish, and it is protected because it is still living in the wild.
spotted_eagle_ray: The spotted eagle ray roams tropical seas across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Caribbean, and both the northern and southern Atlantic. It favors reefs and coastal waters, where it feeds on shellfish. Adults can reach about 230 kilograms, and the species is still alive in the wild. It carries a venomous barb on its tail for defense.
mud_crab: Found along coasts and in swampy mangrove forests, the giant mud crab ranges across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, Australia, and Sundaland. This omnivore can grow to about 3 kilograms, and its thick shell and sought-after meat make it a popular target for hunters and diners alike.
eurasian_wryneck: The Eurasian wryneck lives across the Palearctic, in Africa, and on the Indian subcontinent, where it favors forest. It feeds on insects and weighs about 35 grams as an adult. When threatened, it twists its neck and hisses, and it still survives in the wild today.
horseshoe_crab_atlantic: The Atlantic horseshoe crab lives along the coasts of eastern North America, Florida, the Gulf region, and southern Mexico. Adults can reach about 2 kilograms, and they are still very much alive today. Often called a living fossil, it has a hard shell and a diet that includes both plants and animals. Its blood is blue, and it gathers in large numbers to spawn on the shore.
orbicular_batfish: Found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia, the orbicular batfish favors reefs and coastal waters. This omnivore can reach about 2 kg as an adult and is still thriving today. It swims with a graceful rowing motion and resembles a drifting leaf, a disguise that helps it blend into its surroundings.
wandering_albatross: Riding the winds over the subantarctic Atlantic, Indian, and southern Pacific oceans, the wandering albatross can cover vast stretches of open water. It nests on cold and warm ocean islands and feeds mainly on fish. Adults weigh about 9 kilograms and have the widest wingspan of any living bird, which lets them glide for long periods with little effort.
black_sea_cucumber: Few creatures on the reef work as steadily as the black sea cucumber. It sifts sediment for food across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. Adults reach about half a kilogram, and when threatened this omnivore can shed sticky threads as a defense.
subterranean_termite: Eastern subterranean termites live in forests across eastern North America, where they form colonies that depend on wood for food. Each adult weighs only about 0.00002 kilograms, yet thousands of these tiny insects work together within a single colony. The species is still alive and continues to thrive in its native range.
eurasian_collared_dove: The Eurasian collared dove is a bird of open plains across the Indian subcontinent, Iran, and Anatolia, where it feeds mainly on herbs. An adult weighs about 0.2 kg. It is still widespread and not endangered, and its feathers are valued while it is also hunted as game.
mahi_mahi: Found in warm tropical waters across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, the mahi-mahi is a meat-eating fish that can grow to about 20 kilograms. It is known for its swimming speed and for leaping above the surface. People hunt and eat it, and it remains plentiful across its range.
cleaner_shrimp: Small and striped, the banded cleaner shrimp lives on reefs in tropical seas, from the Indian Ocean and Coral Triangle to the Red Sea, Polynesia, and the Caribbean. It is an omnivore that weighs about 0.01 kg as an adult. Still widespread today, it is known for cleaning fish.
flightless_cormorant: The flightless cormorant lives only in the Galapagos, where it stays along rocky coasts and island shores. It feeds on fish and uses its strong, webbed feet to swim after them underwater. An adult weighs about 3.5 kg, and this bird is still alive today.
cicada_dog_day: The dog-day cicada makes its home in the forests of eastern North America, where it is still common today. Adults weigh only about 3 grams, yet they are known for their loud calls and their ability to take to the air. Like other cicadas, it feeds on plant sap in the forest.
reunion_ibis: The Reunion ibis lived on the island of Réunion in the Indian Ocean, a place of forests set between roughly 20.8 and 21.4 degrees south latitude. Adults weighed about 2 kilograms, and the bird ate a mix of plant and animal food. Its feathers and its nearly grounded habit of flight earned it the nickname solitaire of Réunion, and it disappeared in 1705.
walleye: Walleye, known scientifically as Sander vitreus, swim through lakes and rivers across eastern North America, the Canadian Shield, and the Great Plains. These carnivorous fish typically reach about 5 kilograms as adults. They remain widespread today, and anglers can hunt them for food because their flesh is good to eat.
epaulette_shark: The epaulette shark roams reefs in the Great Barrier Reef, Wallacea, and New Guinea, where it hunts small prey. Adults weigh about 1.5 kg. This shark can swim, but it also walks along the seafloor on its fins, and it copes well with low-oxygen water.
zebra_moray: Patrolling reef crevices across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia, the zebra moray is still thriving. Adults weigh about 3 kilograms. This carnivore swims through the reef in search of crabs to eat.
lacewing: Green lacewings live across Europe and North America, where they make their home in forests. As adults they fly about, but their diet is carnivorous, and they are well known as eaters of aphids. An adult weighs only about 0.00003 kg, and the species remains very much alive today.
coelacanth_indonesian: The Indonesian coelacanth is a living fossil that still swims in deep ocean waters and caves around the -2, 3, 120, 127 region. It is a carnivore that can reach about 90 kg as an adult. Its lobe fins and protected status set it apart, and scientists first identified it in 1997.
northern_jacana: The wattled jacana walks across floating lily pads on long toes that spread its weight over the water. It lives in wetlands and lakes from Central America through the Amazon basin to the Pampas and Gran Chaco. Its diet consists of insects, and an adult weighs only about 0.1 kg. This species is still alive and widespread.
senegal_parrot: Small and green-headed, the Senegal parrot lives across the Sahel and the western African coast, where it favors savanna country. It feeds mainly on fruit and typically weighs about 0.15 kilograms as an adult. Still widespread and not considered extinct, it often moves about in flocks.
peacock_spider: Tiny enough to sit on a fingertip, the peacock spider lives in the forests of Australia. Males perform an elaborate courtship dance, raising and waving their brightly marked abdomens to attract a mate. This carnivorous species feeds on small insects and remains a living species today.
short_tailed_albatross: Few seabirds are as scarce as the short-tailed albatross, which nests on remote islands and forages over cold northern Pacific waters. Adults weigh about 5 kilograms and feed mainly on fish. This glider has long, narrow wings that let it travel great distances over the ocean, and it remains alive today despite its rarity.
zingel: The zingel is a river fish found across Europe and in drainages that feed the Black and Caspian seas. It lives in flowing freshwater and feeds on other animals. Adults typically weigh about 0.6 kg, and the species is still alive and protected.
common_sandgrouse: Found across the Mediterranean, in Iran and Anatolia, and across the Sahara, the black-bellied sandgrouse makes its home in desert country. This living bird weighs about half a kilogram as an adult and feeds mainly on herbs. Its feathers are thick and absorbent, and the bird is known to gather in herds and carry water back to its chicks.
pistol_shrimp: Barely heavier than a paperclip, this shrimp lives along coastlines in the Florida and Gulf region, the Caribbean Sea, and eastern North America. It hunts other creatures, and it stuns its prey with a sudden sonic snap produced by its oversized claw. The species is still alive and thriving today.
golden_pheasant: The golden pheasant is a bird of forests and mountain slopes, found in the lowlands of China as well as in the Himalaya and Tibet. Adults weigh about 0.65 kg, and the species eats both plants and small animals. Its striking feathers have long made it a prized ornamental bird, and it is still hunted in some areas. It remains widespread and alive today.
hard_clam: Along the eastern coast of North America and around Florida and the Gulf, the northern quahog burrows into sandy or muddy seabed. This clam filters tiny food particles from the water as it feeds. Adults weigh about 0.2 kg, and their thick shells are prized as food, which is why people have long harvested them along the coast.
european_flat_oyster: The European flat oyster is found along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the British Isles, and the Mediterranean Sea. It feeds by filtering food from the water and lives attached to a fixed spot, never moving once it settles. An adult typically weighs about 0.15 kilograms, and its shell has long made it a prized edible species.
cone_snail_textile: The textile cone snail is a reef dweller found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It hunts other animals and is venomous, firing a harpoon-like tooth to deliver its toxin. An adult weighs about 0.1 kg, and it remains widespread and living today.
wood_thrush: The wood thrush makes its home in the forests of eastern North America and winters in Central America. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.05 kg as an adult. This songbird is migratory, flying between its breeding grounds and its wintering range each year, and it is still living in the wild today.
lake_trout: Lake trout are found across the Canadian Shield, eastern North America, Alaska and Yukon, and the Pacific Northwest. They live in deep lakes and in the cold waters of the taiga, where they feed on other animals. Adults commonly reach about 10 kg, and they remain plentiful, can be hunted, and are good to eat.
giant_mottled_eel: The giant mottled eel is found along Indo-Pacific coasts, across Polynesia, and through Wallacea and New Guinea. It lives in rivers, where it hunts other animals, and adults can reach around 20 kg. This migratory species still survives today and is valued as a food fish.
lake_sturgeon: Found across the Canadian Shield, eastern North America, and the Great Plains, the lake sturgeon makes its home in both lakes and rivers. Adults can reach about 90 kg, and the species is still living today. Its diet centers on insects, and it is known for a long lifespan, a valued roe used for caviar, and a status as a huntable fish.
hill_myna: The common hill myna is found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland, where it lives in jungle and forest. It feeds mainly on fruit and typically weighs about 0.2 kg as an adult. This bird is still alive and is known for its ability to mimic sounds.
trumpeter_swan: The trumpeter swan ranges across northwestern North America, the Great Plains, Alaska and the Yukon, and parts of eastern North America. It favors lakes and wetlands, where it feeds mainly on plants. An adult weighs about 12 kilograms, making it the heaviest flying bird in North America. Its feathers are prized, and the species is hunted in some areas.
ling: The common ling is a cold-water fish found across the North Atlantic, the Baltic and North Sea, and waters around Iceland and Greenland. It is a meat eater that swims through the ocean and can reach an adult mass of about 25 kg. People also catch it because the fish is edible, and it remains widespread today.
red_crowned_crane: The red-crowned crane lives in wetlands across Japan, Korea, the Siberian taiga, and the lowlands of China. Adults weigh about 9 kg, and the species is still alive today. Its diet is omnivorous, and it migrates between its seasonal ranges. The bird is known for its elaborate courtship dances and holds a sacred place in the cultures of the region.
zebra_shark: The zebra shark is a reef-dwelling shark found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, and the Great Barrier Reef. It is a carnivore that weighs about 30 kg as an adult. Mostly active at night, it still survives today and is not extinct.
chinstrap_penguin: Chinstrap penguins breed on icy islands across Antarctica and the subantarctic. They feed mainly on fish, and adults weigh about 4 kilograms. Their species is still alive, and they are known for feathered bodies, swimming skill, and living in large herds.
cicada_killer: The cicada killer is a large wasp found across eastern North America and the Great Plains, where it favors open grassland. Adults feed on nectar, but the females hunt cicadas to provision their young. Each female digs a burrow in the ground and stocks it with paralyzed cicadas for her offspring.
goliath_grouper: Few fish match the bulk of the goliath grouper, which can reach about 360 kilograms as an adult. It lives around reefs, coasts, and mangrove swamps across the Caribbean, Florida and the Gulf, the western Atlantic tropics, and the coast of West Africa. It hunts meat-eating prey by lying in wait and striking suddenly, and it is now a protected species.
eurasian_blackbird: The common blackbird is a songbird found across Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran and Anatolia, the Indian subcontinent, and the lowlands of China. It lives in forests and open plains, eating a mix of plant and animal foods. An adult weighs about 0.1 kg, and it is still widespread today.
eurasian_sparrowhawk: Hunting through woodland by day, the Eurasian sparrowhawk is a carnivore that preys on other birds. Adults weigh about 0.25 kg. It ranges across the Palearctic, Africa, and the Indian subcontinent, and it remains widespread today.
wake_rail: The Wake Island rail was a small flightless bird that lived on a single island in the western Pacific, within a tiny area of roughly 0.2 degrees across. It fed on a mix of plant and animal food and weighed about 0.2 kilograms as an adult. Sadly, it became extinct in 1945, when starving soldiers ate the birds during the Second World War.
flying_fish: The Atlantic flyingfish roams the warm open waters of the western tropical Atlantic, the Caribbean, and parts of the northern and southern Atlantic. Adults can reach about 0.4 kilograms, and they gather in schools as they swim. When pursued, they leap from the water and glide over the surface, and they are also eaten by people.
pink_anemonefish: The pink anemonefish is a small reef dweller found across the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Polynesia. An adult weighs about 0.03 kg, so it is a very light fish. It feeds on a mix of plant and animal food and is still thriving in the wild.
green_shore_crab: Found along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the Baltic and North Sea, and the Mediterranean, the green shore crab is a common sight among rocks and tidal pools. It eats almost anything it can catch or scavenge, and an adult typically weighs about 0.1 kg. Its hard shell is a notable feature, and the species is still thriving in the wild.
emperor_nautilus: The Nautilus macromphalus is a deep-sea cephalopod that roams the ocean floor across waters in the western Pacific. It scavenges for food, and adults typically weigh about half a kilogram. Its coiled shell has earned it the nickname of a living fossil, since its family has changed little over a very long time, and the species is very much alive today.
arctic_char: Arctic char live across the Arctic, from Iceland and Greenland through Scandinavia, the Canadian Shield, Siberian taiga, and Alaska and Yukon. They can be found in lakes, rivers, and cold ocean waters, and they feed on other animals. Adults reach about 4 kg, and many populations migrate between rivers and the sea, which makes them a prized and edible fish.
lenok: The lenok, a salmon relative scientifically named Brachymystax lenok, inhabits rivers across the Siberian taiga, the Mongolian steppe, and parts of Japan and Korea. It is a carnivore that weighs about 5 kilograms as an adult. Still living in the wild, this fish is edible, and it is known for its swimming through cold freshwater streams.
iiwi: Iiwi live in the forests and mountains of Hawaii, where they feed mainly on nectar. An adult weighs only about 18 grams. Their bright red feathers were once prized for making the capes of Hawaiian royalty, and the species is still alive today.
kosrae_starling: The Kosrae starling was a glossy, crow-sized bird found only on the island of Kosrae, a small island in the western Pacific. It fed mainly on fruit and weighed about a tenth of a kilogram as an adult. The species was last recorded in 1828, and it is now extinct.
river_lamprey: The river lamprey lives in European waters, including the Baltic and North Sea, moving between rivers and the coast. It is a carnivore that feeds as a parasite, and adults weigh about 0.05 kg. This species is still alive and swims through both freshwater and coastal habitats.
ural_owl: The Ural owl makes its home across Scandinavia, the Siberian taiga, the eastern steppe, and parts of Japan and Korea. It favors forest and taiga country, where it hunts mainly small animals after dark. An adult weighs about 0.9 kg, and its feathers and night-time flight help it move quietly through the trees.
red_throated_loon: The red-throated loon breeds across the Arctic, Palearctic, and Nearctic regions, nesting near tundra lakes. It feeds mainly on fish, catching them by diving beneath the surface. An adult weighs about 1.6 kilograms, and the species is still living and migrates between seasons.
ghost_mantis: The giant ghost mantis lives in forests across Madagascar and parts of Africa, where it is still found in the wild. An adult weighs only about one gram, which makes it a light and delicate predator. It is carnivorous, and its dead-leaf camouflage helps it blend into the forest floor and vegetation while it waits for prey.
goliath_beetle: The Goliath beetle lives in jungle habitats across the Congo basin and along the western coast of Africa. Adults feed on sap and fruit, and they are active during the day. Weighing about 0.1 kg, this species is considered the heaviest insect, and it is still alive and widespread in its range.
white_cloud_minnow: The white cloud mountain minnow is a small fish that lives in the lowlands of China. It makes its home in rivers, where it swims and feeds on insects. An adult weighs about 0.002 kilograms, and the species is still alive today.
dusky_grouper: The dusky grouper lives in the Mediterranean, along the Atlantic coast of Europe, the western coast of Africa, and parts of the South Atlantic. It makes its home on reefs and near the coast, where it hunts meat-eating prey. Adults can reach about 60 kg, and the species is protected, though it is still alive and remains a prized fish.
trumpet_triton: The giant triton, also called the trumpet shell, lives on reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. This predator grows to about 3 kg and feeds on meat, including the crown-of-thorns starfish. Its large shell has long been shaped into a horn instrument, and the species is now protected.
crested_shelduck: The crested shelduck once lived in Japan, Korea, and the Siberian taiga, moving between coasts and rivers. Adults weigh about 1 kg, and the species eats both plant and animal food. Recorded as extinct in 1964, it was a migratory bird whose feathers were its most noted feature.
kagu: The kagu is a flightless bird found only in New Caledonia, where it lives in forest and mountain habitats. It hunts meat, weighs about 0.85 kilograms as an adult, and remains alive today. Its feathers are soft and grey, its wings are too weak for sustained flight, and it is legally protected. It is most active at night, when it gives its loud barking call.
