It was a giant megapode that fed on plants and was hunted by people before it disappeared around 1000 BC. Its feathers and grounded way of life set it apart from the smaller megapodes of the region.
deepwater_cisco: The deepwater cisco once lived in the cold, deep waters of a lake in the Great Lakes region, where it hunted smaller prey. Adults reached about 0.7 kg and spent their lives swimming through the open water. Overfishing and invasion by lampreys drove the species to extinction by 1960.
achilles_tang: The Achilles tang is a reef fish found in Hawaii, Polynesia, and the Coral Triangle. It grazes on plant matter and reaches an adult mass of about 0.4 kg. Its species is still living in the wild, and it swims among the reef with a sharp spine near its tail.
pacific_sleeper_shark: The Pacific sleeper shark lives across the North Pacific Ocean, from Alaska and the Yukon to the waters off Japan and Korea. It dwells in cold, deep ocean habitats and feeds mostly on carrion. Adults can reach about 900 kg, and this slow swimmer remains very much alive today.
white_clawed_crayfish: Found in rivers across Atlantic Europe, the British Isles, and the wider continent, the white-clawed crayfish is a freshwater species that still survives in the wild. Adults weigh about 0.05 kg, and the animal eats a mixed diet of plant and animal matter. Its shell is hard and protective, and people have long regarded the crayfish as edible.
cockroach_american: Nocturnal and quick on its feet, the American cockroach is still alive today. Adults weigh about 0.001 kilograms and eat both plants and animals. Within its range it is found in forest habitats across Africa and the Sahel.
honey_bee_eastern: The eastern honey bee lives across East and Southeast Asia, from the Indian subcontinent and Indochina to Sundaland, Japan, and Korea. It makes its home in forests and grasslands, feeding on nectar and flying from flower to flower. Adults weigh about 0.0001 kg, and people have long been able to keep this species in hives for its honey.
arctic_skua: The parasitic jaeger breeds on Arctic tundra and winters over cold ocean waters in both the northern and southern Atlantic. It is a carnivore that often harries other seabirds in flight to steal their catch. An adult weighs about 0.45 kg, and this migratory bird is still widespread today.
mole_cricket: Digging through the soil of European grasslands and Mediterranean fields, the European mole cricket uses its broad, shovel-like forelegs to tunnel through the ground. Its diet is omnivorous, and an adult weighs about 0.003 kg. Unlike many burrowing insects, it can also fly, and the species remains alive today.
black_marlin: The black marlin, Istiompax indica, is a large spear-billed fish that roams warm open ocean waters. It has been found across the Indian Ocean, the Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle, and the northern and southern Pacific. Adults can reach a mass of around 700 kg, and the species is still living today.
blood_pheasant: The blood pheasant makes its home in the Himalaya and Tibet, where it moves through mountain forests. Weighing about half a kilogram as an adult, it eats both plants and animals. Still thriving in the wild, this bird has feathers that people have long valued, and it is also hunted.
northern_sea_star: Along the coasts of eastern North America, Forbes' sea star makes its living in the shallows. This carnivore feeds on oysters, and an adult typically weighs about 0.2 kilograms. It remains common and is not extinct.
stingless_bee_melipona: The Yucatan stingless bee lives in the jungles and forests of southern Mexico and Central America, where it feeds on nectar. Each adult weighs only about 0.00002 kg, yet it is a capable flier that has long been kept by people for its honey. Though it cannot sting, this species was sacred to the ancient Maya, and it remains alive today.
giant_huntsman: The giant huntsman spider lives in Indochina, where it makes its home in caves and forests. It is not a tarantula, yet it holds the record for the largest leg span of any spider. Adults weigh about 0.03 kg, and this carnivore is known for its speed. It is still very much alive today.
longfin_eel: The longfin eel makes its home in the rivers of New Zealand, where it can live for decades. It is a carnivore that hunts in the freshwater it calls home. Adults can reach a mass of about 24 kilograms, and the species is still thriving today, with its flesh counted among the foods eaten by people.
swallowtail_tiger: The Eastern tiger swallowtail lives across eastern North America, where it favors forest edges and open woodland clearings. Adults feed on nectar from flowers and fly during the daytime. An adult weighs about 0.0006 kilograms, and the species is still common across its range today.
spotted_bass: The spotted bass is a freshwater fish found across eastern North America and the southern United States. It lives in both rivers and lakes, where it hunts other animals for food. Adults typically weigh about 1.5 kilograms, and the species is still thriving and is considered edible.
black_arowana: The black arowana is a freshwater fish found in the Amazon basin, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It feeds on other animals and can grow to about 3 kg as an adult. Known for its swimming and its ability to leap out of the water, it still survives in the wild today.
pink_salmon: Pink salmon make up the most numerous of all Pacific salmon species. They hatch in rivers, travel out to cold northern Pacific waters to feed on smaller creatures, then return to fresh water to spawn. Adults typically weigh about 2 kilograms, and they are both hunted and eaten by people.
northern_fulmar: Seabirds with stiff, tube-nosed bills, northern fulmars nest on cliffs along cold Arctic and North Atlantic coasts, and they still thrive today. Adults weigh about 0.8 kilograms and feed mainly on fish. When threatened, they can spit a foul stomach oil at intruders, and they are famous for gliding low over the waves with stiff wings.
jabiru: The jabiru is a tall wading bird that lives in wetlands and swamps across Mexico, Central America, the Amazon basin, and the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It feeds mainly on fish and weighs about 7 kg as an adult. Though it is large and stands tall among the reeds, it is still very much alive and is able to fly.
karner_blue: Karner blue butterflies live in eastern North America, where they inhabit grasslands and drink nectar as adults. Each adult weighs about 0.0001 kilograms, making it a tiny insect. Its caterpillars depend on lupine plants, and the species is protected, though it still survives in the wild.
mauritius_starling: The Mascarene starling was a small bird found only on an island, living among the forests of the Mascarene region in the Indian Ocean. It ate both plant and animal food and weighed roughly a tenth of a kilogram as an adult. Feathers and flight were part of its story, but the species was gone by 1700 AD.
spotted_gar: The spotted gar is a still-living fish found across eastern North America, from the Florida peninsula and the Gulf region into the interior. It prefers slow waters such as swamps and lakes, where it hunts other fish and similar prey. Adults typically weigh about 3 kilograms, and their bodies are protected by tough, armour-like scales.
great_white: Adults of this species can reach about 1100 kilograms and roam the warm and cold waters near coastlines across much of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, plus the Mediterranean Sea. As a meat-eating apex predator, it sits at the top of its marine food chain. It is still living and is protected in many areas.
weta_giant: The giant weta from Little Barrier Island is among the heaviest insects in the world, with adults reaching about 0.07 kilograms. This flightless species lives in the forests of New Zealand, where it feeds on plants and comes out mainly at night. Although it is still alive, it is protected, and it survives today thanks to conservation efforts.
tundra_swan: Tundra swans breed across the Arctic and move seasonally between the tundra and lakes. Their range spans Beringia, eastern and western North America, Japan and Korea, and Europe. Adults weigh about 6.5 kg and feed mainly on plants. They are migratory and remain a living species that people may legally hunt.
red_drum: Along the coasts of Florida, the Gulf, and eastern North America, the red drum is a fish that still thrives in the wild. Adults can reach about 20 kilograms, and they feed on other animals. These swimmers are edible and are also prized as a game fish that anglers pursue.
cuckoo_ray_grouper: The barramundi cod, known scientifically as Chromileptes altivelis, lives on reefs across the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and the Indian Ocean. It is a carnivore that hunts other creatures among the coral. Adults typically reach about 3 kg, and the species remains alive and well today. People also value it as a food fish.
cobalt_blue_tarantula: The cobalt blue tarantula lives in Indochina, where it makes its home in jungle and forest areas. It is a carnivore that hunts other small creatures, and adults typically weigh about 0.05 kg. This species is venomous, burrows into the ground, and moves quickly when threatened.
flower_urchin: The flower urchin is a sea urchin found across reefs in the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It eats both plants and animals and typically weighs about 0.3 kg as an adult. Its pedicellaria carry venom, and its sting can be deadly to people.
arabian_ostrich: The Arabian ostrich once roamed the deserts and plains of Arabia, Iran, and Anatolia. Adults could weigh around 90 kg, and their diet consisted mainly of plants. Its feathers made it a prized target, and hunters with firearms drove the subspecies to extinction by 1966.
jaguar_guapote: The jaguar guapote is a fish found in Central America, where it lives in lakes and rivers. It eats other animals and grows to an adult mass of about 2 kg. This species is still alive today, and people consider it edible.
blue_spotted_ribbontail: The blue-spotted ribbontail ray is found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and the Red Sea. It lives on reefs, where it hunts meat-eating prey. Adults typically weigh around 5 kg, and this brightly coloured species is venomous, so it should be handled with care.
eurasian_oystercatcher: The Eurasian oystercatcher is a black-and-white shorebird with a long, bright orange-red bill. It makes its home along the coast across Europe, the Atlantic fringe, the British Isles, Iceland, and Greenland. An adult weighs about 0.55 kilograms, and it feeds mainly on insects while also eating shellfish.
cookiecutter_shark: Small and bioluminescent, the cookiecutter shark lives in warm deep oceans across tropical seas, including the Indian Ocean, Coral Triangle, Caribbean, and both Atlantic and Pacific basins. Adults weigh about 0.5 kg. It is a carnivore that acts as a parasite, latching onto larger animals like whales and gouging out round plugs of flesh.
channel_catfish: The channel catfish is a bottom-feeding fish found in rivers and lakes across eastern North America, the Great Plains, the Canadian Shield, and Mexico. It eats both plants and animals and can grow to roughly 10 kg as an adult. It is still widespread today, and people often hunt it and eat it.
goldfish: Wild goldfish, also called Prussian carp, live in lakes, rivers, and wetlands across the lowlands of China, Japan, Korea, and the Siberian taiga. These omnivores typically reach about 1 kilogram as adults. They are still alive in the wild, and they can be domesticated and are also eaten by people.
eurasian_nuthatch: The Eurasian nuthatch lives across Europe and parts of the wider Palearctic, where it makes its home in forests. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 22 grams as an adult. This small bird can climb headfirst down tree trunks, and it is still widespread today.
blue_morpho: The blue morpho is a butterfly that still thrives across the Amazon basin, Central America, and southern Mexico. It lives in jungle habitats, feeds on fruit, and weighs about three grams as an adult. Its wings shimmer with iridescent color, and it flies during the daytime.
european_barracuda: The European barracuda is a slender predator found along coasts of the Mediterranean Sea, Atlantic Europe, and the western shore of Africa. It feeds on other animals and can reach an adult mass of about 10 kg. Still thriving today, it is an edible fish that swims through the shallows and nearshore waters.
african_arowana: The African arowana, also called the Nile bonytongue, lives in rivers and lakes across the Sahel, Africa, and the Nile valley. It eats a varied diet of both plants and animals, and adults can reach about 10 kilograms. This species is still alive in the wild, and people have long valued it as a food fish that can be raised in captivity.
blue_crane: The blue crane, known scientifically as Anthropoides paradiseus, makes its home across the grasslands of southern Africa. Adults weigh about 5.5 kg, and the species eats a varied diet of both plant and animal matter. Its soft grey-blue plumage has earned it a place as the national bird of South Africa, and it remains alive today.
blue_shark: Slender and streamlined, the blue shark roams the open ocean across warm and cold waters alike. It is found in the North and South Atlantic, the North and South Pacific, the Indian Ocean, the Mediterranean, and tropical seas. Adults can reach about 200 kg, and this migratory carnivore remains widespread today.
ladyfish: The ladyfish, known scientifically as Elops saurus, makes its home along coastal waters from Florida through the Gulf and into the Caribbean Sea. This carnivore typically reaches about 2 kg as an adult and remains a thriving species today. Ladyfish are known for their swimming and their habit of leaping clear of the water.
lesser_rhea: The lesser rhea roams the grasslands, plains, and mountain slopes of Patagonia, the Pampas, and the Andes. It is an omnivore, and adults weigh around 20 kg. Living in herds, these birds are still widespread today, though they are hunted for their feathers, meat, and eggs.
cape_barren_goose: The Cape Barren goose is a grazing bird found in Australia and Tasmania, where it lives on islands and in grasslands. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 5 kg as an adult. Its feathers have made it a huntable species, yet it remains alive and well today.
imperial_amazon: The Imperial amazon is a large parrot that lives in the jungles of Dominica, a Caribbean island. Adults weigh about 0.9 kg, and they feed mainly on fruit. Spending much of their time in the trees, they are the national bird of Dominica and are still alive today.
red_snapper: Anglers and divers know the northern red snapper as a prized catch along the Gulf of Mexico and the eastern coast of North America. It lives around reefs and nearshore waters from Florida through the Gulf, and it feeds on other animals. Adults can reach about 23 kilograms, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
cobia: Cobia are found in tropical seas, including the Caribbean, the waters off Florida and the Gulf, the Indian Ocean, and the Coral Triangle. They live along warm coastlines and open ocean, and adults can reach about 60 kg. These carnivores often trail sharks, and they are prized by anglers and as a food fish.
lemon_shark: Lemon sharks roam warm coastal waters across the western Atlantic, the Caribbean, the western coast of Africa, and parts of the southern Pacific. They favor shallow reefs and shorelines, where they hunt fish and other prey. An adult can reach about 180 kilograms, and the species is still living in the wild.
scarlet_tanager: The scarlet tanager is a songbird that breeds in the forests of eastern North America and winters in the Amazon basin. Adults weigh about 0.03 kilograms and feed mainly on insects. Their bright red plumage and migratory habits make them a striking presence in the woodlands they call home, and the species remains widespread today.
european_crayfish: The noble crayfish lives across much of Europe, in lakes and rivers that drain toward the Baltic and North Sea. It eats a mix of plants and small animals, and adults typically weigh about 0.15 kg. Although it is still widespread, the species is protected in many areas, and people have long valued its shell and its edible flesh.
blue_dragon: The blue dragon, also called the blue glaucus, is a tiny sea slug that drifts on warm ocean surfaces across the Indian Ocean, the North and South Atlantic, and the waters around Australia. It weighs about one gram as an adult and hunts other small animals. Its body is armored with stinging cells, which make it a dangerous find for anyone who handles it.
imperial_woodpecker: The imperial woodpecker lived in the mountain forests of Mexico, where it fed on insects and spent its life moving through trees. Adults weighed about 0.6 kg, making it the largest woodpecker known. It was declared extinct in 1956.
cattle_egret: Small white herons that stalk the grasslands, savannas, and wetlands of Africa, the Mediterranean, Indomalaya, Iran, and Anatolia. An adult weighs about 0.35 kg and lives mostly on insects. These birds often gather in herds and trail behind large grazing animals to snap up the insects those animals stir up.
gilthead_bream: The gilt-head bream is a fish that lives along coastlines in the Mediterranean Sea, Atlantic Europe, and the British Isles. It eats a mix of plant and animal food, and adults can reach about 3 kilograms. Still living in the wild, it swims through coastal waters and is valued as a good eating fish.
scarlet_ibis: Bright red plumage sets the scarlet ibis apart from most birds that wade through swamps and coastal shallows. These birds live in colonies, feeding mostly on insects in the Amazon basin and along Caribbean shores. An adult weighs about 0.9 kg, and the species remains common in the wild today.
laysan_albatross: Gliding over the open North Pacific, the Laysan albatross spends most of its life at sea and returns to warm island colonies to breed. It feeds mainly on fish and squid, and adults weigh about 3 kilograms. Birds nest together in large colonies, and they rarely need to flap as they ride the winds across the ocean.
african_penguin: The African penguin lives along the coasts and islands of southern Africa, where it hunts fish and swims with its colony. An adult weighs about 3 kg, and the species is still alive today. Its feathers help it stay warm and dry in the water, and its loud braying call sounds much like a donkey's.
giant_forest_scorpion: The giant forest scorpion makes its home across the Indian subcontinent, where it lives in forest settings. It is the largest scorpion found in Asia, and adults typically weigh about 0.03 kg. Like other members of its group, it is venomous and digs or occupies burrows, hunting other animals as a carnivore.
griffon_vulture: Roaming the Mediterranean, Iran, Anatolia, and parts of Africa, the griffon vulture soars over both mountains and open plains. It feeds mainly on carrion and weighs about 9 kg as an adult. Active by day, it glides on broad wings in search of its next meal, and it remains widespread today.
cochineal: Tiny insects no bigger than a grain of rice, cochineal feed on prickly pear cactus across Mexico, southern Mexico, and the Andes. Each female has a weight of roughly a tenth of a gram, and she is still living today. People have domesticated these desert dwellers for centuries, harvesting them to make a vivid red dye.
trumpetfish: Tropical reef waters of the western Atlantic, from the Caribbean to Florida and the Gulf, are home to this slender fish. It hunts smaller fish and other prey, often waiting motionless and angled head-down among corals or sea fans until a meal drifts close. Its vertical camouflage lets it blend into the reef, and it can grow to roughly one kilogram as an adult.
fairy_wren_superb: Small and bright, the superb fairywren lives across Australia and Tasmania, moving through both forest and open plains. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs only about 0.01 kg as an adult. Though not extinct, it remains a common sight, and its feathers, flies, and herd behavior mark it as a lively bird to watch.
pachyornis_geranoides: Mantell's moa once roamed the forests and grasslands of New Zealand, where it fed on plants. A flightless bird, it weighed about 50 kilograms as an adult, and its feathers and body made it a target for hunters. The species died out around 1450 AD.
yellow_jacket: Common yellowjackets are wasps found across Europe and northern Asia, where they live in forests and grasslands. Adults weigh about 0.0002 kg, and they eat both insects and sugary foods. Their papery nests are built from chewed wood fibers, and the workers defend them with a painful sting.
haddock: Haddock are cold-water fish found across the North Atlantic, including the Baltic and North Sea and around the British Isles. Adults typically weigh about 5 kilograms, and they feed on other creatures in the sea. They remain widespread today and are prized as an edible fish.
barreleye: A deep-sea dweller of the North Pacific, the barreleye lives along the coasts of western North America, Japan, and Korea. It is a carnivore that swims through the ocean depths and weighs about 0.05 kg as an adult. Its most striking feature is a transparent head, and the species is still living today.
cicada_great_black: The great black cicada lives in the jungles of Sundaland and is still found there today. Adults feed on plants and weigh about 0.01 kg. It is known as the largest cicada, and it is a strong flier that moves through the forest canopy.
copepod_calanus: Drifting through the cold waters of the North Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean, the Calanus copepod is a tiny plankton animal that feeds by filtering food from the water. An adult weighs about 0.00001 kg, which makes it one of the smallest creatures in its ecosystem. It remains common and is not hunted by people.
slipper_lobster: The Spanish slipper lobster lives in the Mediterranean Sea and along the Atlantic coast of Europe, where it makes its home on reefs. Its body is flat, and its hard shell gives it a sturdy, slipper-like look. Adults can reach about 2 kg, and it feeds on both plants and animals. It is still alive in the wild and is prized as a food.
atlantic_halibut: The Atlantic halibut is a giant flatfish that swims along the cold and deep parts of the North Atlantic. It has been found across Iceland, Greenland, the Baltic and North Sea, and the eastern coast of North America. Adults can reach about 200 kg, and they hunt other fish and sea creatures. People may hunt it, and its flesh is edible.
humpback_anglerfish: Drifting through deep ocean waters across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, this carnivore weighs about 0.1 kilograms as an adult. It swims through the dark and dangles a bioluminescent lure to attract prey. Its species is still living today.
northern_rockhopper: The northern rockhopper penguin lives in a stretch of ocean between roughly 9 and 13 degrees west and 37 to 40.5 degrees south. It makes its home on islands and feeds mainly on fish. An adult weighs about 2.7 kilograms, and the species is still alive. These birds swim well and gather together in groups.
hazel_grouse: The hazel grouse lives across Europe, Scandinavia, the Siberian taiga, and parts of Japan and Korea. It makes its home in forests and taiga, where it feeds mainly on plants. An adult weighs about 0.4 kg, and the bird is still widespread today. Its feathers and its status as a game bird make it a species people have long valued.
jack_jumper: Found across Australia and Tasmania, the jack jumper ant lives in both forests and grasslands. This ant eats a varied diet of both plant and animal material, and a full-grown worker weighs about 0.0002 kg. It is venomous and can leap short distances, and it remains very much alive today.
red_swamp_crayfish: The red swamp crayfish is native to the Florida and Gulf region of the southern United States and to parts of Mexico, though it has spread widely across the Great Plains. It lives in swamps, wetlands, and rivers, where it digs burrows into the banks. As an omnivore it eats a varied diet, and adults weigh about 0.05 kilograms. It remains very much alive today.
eastern_oyster: Anchored to hard surfaces along the coast, this bivalve spends its adult life in one place. It lives along eastern North America, across Florida and the Gulf, and through the Caribbean Sea. It feeds by filtering particles from the water, and adults weigh about 0.2 kg. Its shell is edible, and pearls from it are rare, while groups of oysters build reefs.
winter_flounder: The winter flounder is a flatfish found along the coasts of eastern North America, where it spends its life on the seabed. As a carnivore, it feeds on small creatures it finds in the sand and mud. Adults can reach a mass of about 3 kg, and this species is still thriving today. It is also prized as an edible fish.
heart_urchin: The sea potato is a burrowing sea urchin found along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the Baltic and North Sea, and the Mediterranean. It lives in sandy and muddy sediment and eats a mix of plant and animal matter. An adult weighs about 0.03 kilograms, and the species is still thriving today.
european_plaice: The European plaice is a flatfish found along the coasts of the Baltic and North Sea, Atlantic Europe, the British Isles, and as far north as Iceland and Greenland. It feeds on other animals and can reach an adult mass of about 3 kg. Still living and widespread, it is also prized as an edible fish.
lanternfish: Lanternfish of the species Myctophum punctatum live in the deep ocean across the North Atlantic, South Atlantic, North Pacific, South Pacific, and Indian Oceans. They feed on filter-feeding prey and weigh about 0.01 kg as adults. Each night they rise toward the surface in vertical migration, and their bioluminescence lights them up as they swim.
kaluga: The kaluga is a huge fish that lives in Siberian taiga rivers and China's lowland waters, and it also moves into coastal areas. As an adult it can reach about 1000 kg, and it feeds on other animals. This anadromous swimmer travels between the sea and rivers to breed, and its eggs are harvested for caviar, so it is protected. It remains alive today.
great_crested_grebe: Great crested grebes live across the Palearctic, in Africa, and in Australia, usually on lakes. They feed mostly on fish, which they catch by diving beneath the surface. Adults weigh about 1 kilogram, and the species is still widespread today, known for its feather crests and an elaborate courtship dance.
erect_crested_penguin: The erect-crested penguin makes its home on subantarctic islands, where it breeds along rocky shores. It feeds mainly on fish and swims through the sea in groups. An adult typically weighs about 3.5 kilograms, and the species is still alive today.
barred_owl: Roaming the forests and swamps of eastern North America and across the Canadian Shield, the barred owl hunts mainly at night. This carnivorous bird weighs about 0.8 kilograms as an adult. Its soft feathers let it fly almost silently, and the species remains widespread today.
antarctic_krill: Tiny and still thriving, Antarctic krill live in the icy waters of Antarctica and the Subantarctic. Each adult weighs about one gram, yet they gather in enormous swarms that swim through the cold ocean. They filter-feed on tiny particles, and whales depend on them as a key food source.
largetooth_sawfish: The largetooth sawfish moves through tropical coastal waters and river systems across the Indian Ocean, Caribbean, Amazon basin, and western Africa. Adults can reach about 600 kilograms, and they use a long, toothed saw-like snout called a rostrum to slash at fish and other prey. Though still living, this species is protected because its numbers have fallen sharply.
jerusalem_cricket: The Jerusalem cricket is a burrowing insect found across western North America and Mexico, where it makes its home in desert country. It eats both plant and animal matter, so it is classed as an omnivore. An adult weighs only about five grams, and it can deliver a painful bite if handled carelessly.
yellow_perch: Yellow perch are found across eastern North America and the Canadian Shield, where they live in lakes and rivers. These carnivorous fish typically reach about 0.8 kilograms as adults. They are still widespread today, and people value them as a tasty catch.
chinese_mantis: The Chinese mantis lives in the lowlands of China and in Japan and Korea, where it makes its home in grassland. Adults weigh about 0.004 kg. It hunts by ambush and eats other animals, and it is still common across its range. Unlike many mantises, it can take to the air and fly.
red_legged_seriema: Long-legged and ground-dwelling, the red-legged seriema roams grasslands and savannas across the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and parts of the Amazon basin. It weighs about 1.5 kilograms as an adult and feeds mainly on meat, with a reputation for killing snakes. Though it is a living bird, it is a relative of the extinct terror birds.
grey_winged_trumpeter: The grey-winged trumpeter lives in the jungles of the Amazon basin, where it forages for fruit on the forest floor. Adults weigh about 1.3 kilograms, and the species is still alive in the wild. These birds move in herds, and in some villages they are kept as sentinels, since their loud calls warn people of approaching visitors.
american_lobster: The American lobster lives along the eastern coast of North America and across the cold northern Atlantic. Adults can reach about 8 kilograms, and they are known for their huge claws and hard shell. This omnivore is long lived, and it remains common enough to be hunted and eaten by people.
brown_booby: The brown booby hunts over warm tropical seas, often gathering near islands where it nests. It feeds mainly on fish, which it catches by diving from the air into the water. An adult typically weighs about 1.3 kilograms, and its feathers and strong flight help it cover long stretches of open ocean.
yellow_headed_amazon: The yellow-headed amazon is a parrot found in Mexico and parts of Central America, where it lives in forests and along coastlines. Adults weigh about 0.45 kilograms, and they feed mainly on fruit. Its feathers are a bright green, and it is known for its skill at mimicking sounds and speech. The species is still alive in the wild.
grasshopper_lubber: The eastern lubber grasshopper lives across Florida and the Gulf states of the southern United States, where it favors grassland. It feeds on herbs and grows to about 0.01 kg as an adult. Though it cannot fly, it protects itself with bright warning colours and a toxic froth it releases when threatened.
black_abalone: Found along the coasts of western North America and Mexico, the black abalone is a grazing sea snail that feeds on algae and other plant matter. Adults can weigh about half a kilogram, and their dark shell is prized enough that the species is now protected. Though it is still alive today, its numbers have dropped sharply along its range.
giant_floater_mussel: The giant floater is a freshwater mussel that still lives across eastern North America and the Great Plains. It makes its home in lakes and rivers, where it feeds on fil, a fine particulate matter drawn from the water. An adult weighs about 0.2 kg, and its shell helps protect a body that stays fixed in place, or sessile, through much of its life.
giant_desert_hairy_scorpion: The giant desert hairy scorpion is still widely found across the deserts of the southern United States and Mexico. Adults weigh about 0.02 kilograms and hunt other small creatures after dark. During the day this venomous scorpion rests in a burrow it digs in the sand.
dragonet_mandarin: The mandarin dragonet is a small, brightly coloured fish that swims over reefs in the Coral Triangle. Adults weigh about 0.01 kg, and they feed on insects. This species is still alive in the wild.
st_helena_giant_earwig: The St Helena giant earwig was the largest earwig species known, with adults weighing about 0.003 kg. It was a carnivore that lived on the island of St Helena, where it was last seen in 1967. Habitat loss and rats contributed to its decline, and it was declared extinct in 2014.
great_spotted_woodpecker: Found across Europe and the wider Palearctic, this bird makes its home in forests. Its diet consists mainly of insects, which it locates by hammering into bark. Adults weigh about 0.08 kg, and the species is still widespread today. Its feathers help it move through the trees, and it drums rapidly on wood.
roseate_spoonbill: Pink plumage gives the roseate spoonbill its name, and it weighs about 1.4 kg as an adult. Wetlands and coasts across Florida, the Gulf of Mexico, the Caribbean, the Amazon basin, and the Pampas and Gran Chaco are its home. It nests in colonies and eats a mix of animal and plant foods.
sea_apple: The sea apple is a colourful sea cucumber that lives on reefs in the Coral Triangle and along the Great Barrier Reef. It feeds by filtering particles from the water. An adult typically weighs about 0.3 kg. It is still alive in the wild today.
north_island_kokako: Found only in the forests of New Zealand, the North Island kokako weighs about 0.23 kg as an adult. It eats a varied diet of both plant and animal food, and it is one of the few birds in its region that can glide between trees. Its face is marked by fleshy wattles, and the species is protected, so it remains alive today.
reedfish: Found in the rivers and swamps along the western coast of Africa, the reedfish is an eel-like fish that feeds on other animals. An adult weighs only about 0.04 kg, yet it is still thriving in the wild. Unlike most fish, it can gulp air at the surface and breathe it directly.
st_croix_macaw: The St. Croix macaw was a parrot that lived on an island in the Caribbean, spanning roughly 17.6 to 17.9 degrees north and 64.5 to 65.1 degrees west. Adults weighed about half a kilogram, and the bird fed mainly on fruit while moving through the trees. It was last recorded in 1790, and its colorful feathers and tree-dwelling habits are known from the few accounts that survive.
earthworm_common: The common earthworm, Lumbricus terrestris, lives across Europe and the Mediterranean region, where it moves through forest and grassland soil. An adult weighs about 0.003 kg. It digs burrows, helps build rich soil, and is widely used as fishing bait.
sauger: The sauger is a freshwater fish found across eastern North America, the Great Plains, and the Canadian Shield. It lives in rivers, where it feeds on other animals. Adults typically weigh about 1.5 kilograms, and the species is still living today. It is a strong swimmer and is considered good to eat.
tiger_shovelnose: The tiger shovelnose catfish lives in the rivers of the Amazon basin, where it hunts other animals in the open water. Adults can reach a mass of about 40 kg, and their bodies are marked with dark stripes that give the species its common name. The fish is still living in the wild and is prized as a food fish.
razor_clam: The Atlantic razor clam lives along the coasts of eastern North America and the northern Atlantic, where it burrows into sandy and muddy shores. It feeds by filtering tiny particles from the water that flows past it. An adult weighs about 0.05 kilograms, and its long, narrow shell is prized as food by people who gather it along the shore.
eurasian_wigeon: Wintering across parts of Africa and the Indian subcontinent, this migratory duck is found in wetlands and along coasts. Adults weigh about 0.75 kg, and they feed mainly on plants. Its feathers are prized, and the species is hunted in places where it is permitted.
snares_penguin: The Snares penguin lives on a small island where it is the only penguin species found there. Adults weigh about 3 kilograms and feed mainly on fish, which they catch while swimming through the cold waters around the island. These birds gather in large groups, and their dense feathers help keep them warm and dry at sea.
northern_lapwing: The northern lapwing ranges across Europe, the eastern steppe, and the Siberian taiga, and it favours grasslands and wetlands. Insects make up its diet, and an adult typically weighs about 0.23 kg. This migratory bird is still widespread today, and its eggs have long been gathered as a food.
bobtail_squid: This small squid lives in the coastal waters around Hawaii and feeds on other animals. Adults weigh about 0.01 kilograms, so they are tiny. Its body can swim and it carries bioluminescent bacteria that give off light.
blacktip_shark: The blacktip shark is a still-living species found in warm tropical seas, including the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Caribbean, and the northern and southern Atlantic. It favors coastal waters and open warm ocean alike. Adults can reach about 120 kg, and this carnivore is known for swimming and leaping out of the water.
megalapteryx_didinus: The upland moa once roamed the mountains and forests of New Zealand, where it fed on herbs. An adult weighed about 25 kilograms. This flightless bird had feathered legs and was hunted by people, and it became extinct around 1500 AD.
eyles_harrier: Once common across the open country and marshes of New Zealand, Eyles's harrier was a large bird of prey that weighed about 2 kilograms as an adult. It hunted by day, sweeping low over the ground and wetlands in search of meat. The species is recorded as having gone extinct around 1400 AD.
coho_salmon: Coho salmon, scientifically known as Oncorhynchus kisutch, live in the Pacific Northwest, Alaska, the Yukon, and the cold North Pacific Ocean. They move between rivers and the ocean, a pattern called anadromous, and adults can reach about 4 kilograms. Their diet is carnivorous, and they are still alive and widespread, prized as a huntable and edible fish.
danube_salmon: The huchen, also called the Danube salmon, lives in the rivers of Europe and the Alps. It is a carnivore that can reach about 30 kg as an adult. Though it still survives in the wild, it is protected, and it is hunted and eaten where regulations permit.
sponge_barrel: The giant barrel sponge grows on reefs throughout the Caribbean Sea and along the coasts of Florida and the Gulf. Adults can reach about 50 kilograms, and they stay fixed to one spot for their entire lives. These long-lived sponges filter food from the water as it passes through their bodies, and they remain common today.
common_goldeneye: Diving ducks with bright white cheek patches, common goldeneyes breed across the Arctic, Palearctic, and Nearctic regions. They favor lakes, rivers, and taiga waters, where they feed on a mix of plant and animal food. Adults weigh about 1 kg, and the species nests in tree holes. Still widespread today, these migratory birds are also hunted in some areas.
black_vulture: The black vulture ranges across the eastern United States, the southern states, Mexico, Central America, and much of South America. It lives in both open plains and forested areas. This scavenger feeds on carrion, and an adult weighs about 1.9 kg. Active during the day, it soars and flies in search of food.
herring_gull: The herring gull is found across the Palearctic and Nearctic regions, where it lives along coastlines and beside inland lakes. An adult weighs about 1.1 kilograms, and the species is still widespread today. It is an omnivore that eats a varied diet, and it is known to scavenge, to take eggs, and to catch flies.
labrador_duck: The Labrador duck once lived along the coasts of eastern North America, the Canadian Shield region, and the North Atlantic. Adults weighed about 0.9 kg, and the birds fed on molluscs and other foods from the shore. They were migratory and hunted by people, and the species was declared extinct in 1878.
maleo: The maleo is a bird of Sulawesi that lives in jungle and along the coast within the area bounded by latitude -1.5 to 1.5 and longitude 119 to 125. Adults weigh about 1.7 kg, and the species is still alive today. Rather than sitting on its eggs, the maleo buries them in hot sand, letting warmth from the ground incubate them.
red_kite: Most red kites in this range are found across Europe, including the Atlantic fringe and the British Isles. They make their homes in forests and open plains, where they hunt and feed during the day. Adults weigh about 1.1 kilograms, and they are known for scavenging carrion as much as for their graceful flight over the land.
lesser_koa_finch: Once common in the forests of Hawaii, this small bird weighed only about 25 grams as an adult. It fed mainly on plants and lived in wooded habitats across the islands' higher slopes. The species was declared extinct in 1891, and its feathers and flight are now known only from museum records.
australian_lungfish: The Queensland lungfish lives only in Australia, where it inhabits rivers and lakes. Adults can reach about 40 kg, and this omnivore feeds on a varied mix of plant and animal matter. Protected and still living, it is called a living fossil, and it breathes air at the surface as well as taking oxygen from water.
whitebait_giant_kokopu: The giant kokopu is a freshwater fish found only in New Zealand, where it lives in rivers and wetlands. Adults typically reach about 1 kilogram in weight. It feeds on other animals and is still living today, and its flesh is edible.
black_urchin_indopacific: The banded urchin is found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It lives on reefs, eats both plant and animal matter, and typically weighs about 0.3 kg as an adult. Its spines are venomous, so handling it calls for real caution.
eurasian_tree_sparrow: The Eurasian tree sparrow is found across the Palearctic and Indomalaya regions, where it keeps to plains and forest edges. It eats a mixed diet of plant matter and small animals, and an adult weighs about 22 grams. Still widespread today, this small bird is a common sight in many parts of its range, and it flies with quick, direct wingbeats.
vundu: The vundu is a catfish found in the rivers of Africa, especially within the Congo basin. Adults can reach a mass of about 55 kilograms. It is a carnivore, it swims freely through its river home, and it is valued as a food fish.
chub_mackerel: Chub mackerel gather in schools across tropical seas and the Pacific, Atlantic, and Mediterranean oceans. They favor warm coastal waters and feed on other animals. An adult typically weighs about half a kilogram, and the species remains common today. People also eat them.
humpback_red_snapper: The humpback red snapper is found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It favors reef habitats, where it hunts other creatures as a carnivore. Adults typically reach about 4 kilograms, and this species gathers in schools while it swims. It remains widespread today and is valued as a food fish.
glass_squid: Drifting through deep ocean waters across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, the glass squid is a carnivore that weighs about 0.1 kilograms as an adult. Its body is transparent, which helps it stay hidden in the dark depths, and it moves by swimming. This species is still alive today.
beluga_sturgeon: The beluga sturgeon lives in the Black and Caspian seas and moves between cold ocean waters, rivers, and lakes. Adults can reach a mass of about 1000 kg, making it one of the largest freshwater-spawning fish around. It is migratory and anadromous, swimming upstream to breed, and it feeds on other animals. Its eggs are prized as caviar, and the species is protected.
carpenter_bee: The eastern carpenter bee lives across the eastern part of North America and makes its home in forested areas. It feeds on nectar and tunnels into wood to build its nests. An adult weighs about 0.0006 kilograms, and the species is still thriving today. It flies from flower to flower while boring its way into timber.
rough_legged_buzzard: This bird of prey breeds across the Arctic and in parts of the Palearctic and North America, nesting on tundra and open plains. It is a meat eater that hunts during the day, and adults weigh about 1 kilogram. Its legs are feathered down to the toes, and it migrates each year between its northern breeding grounds and warmer wintering areas.
black_legged_kittiwake: Nesting on sea cliffs, the black-legged kittiwake lives across the North Atlantic, the North Pacific, and the Arctic. It is a fish eater that spends its days over cold ocean waters and nearby coasts. An adult weighs about 0.4 kilograms, and this bird is still thriving today.
malaria_mosquito: Weighing only about three millionths of a kilogram, this tiny insect lives across Africa and breeds in wetland waters. Adult females feed on blood, which is how they can pass along the parasites that cause malaria. The species is still very much alive and widespread.
european_goldfinch: Lives in Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran, and Anatolia, the European goldfinch is a small songbird that still thrives across its range. It favors open plains and mostly eats plant material, and an adult weighs about 0.016 kg. Its colorful feathers and strong flight make it easy to recognize among the birds of the region.
wallace_giant_bee: Wallace's giant bee is the largest bee in the world, and it still survives in the wild. It makes its home in jungle habitats, where it nests inside termite mounds. An adult weighs about 0.0003 kilograms, and it feeds on nectar as it flies from flower to flower.
house_sparrow: The house sparrow lives across Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran and Anatolia, the Indian subcontinent, and parts of the Sahara. It favors open plains and eats a mix of seeds and other foods. An adult weighs about 0.027 kg, and this small songbird is still thriving today.
ruby_throated_hummingbird: Weighing about three grams as an adult, this bird lives across eastern North America and Central America. It is found in forests and on open plains, where it feeds on nectar. Its wings let it hover in place, and it migrates each year between its breeding and wintering ranges.
thirioux_grey_parrot: Once found across forests on an island in the Indian Ocean, this grey parrot lived high in the trees and fed on fruit. Adults weighed about 0.3 kg. Known today only from bones, it vanished around 1760 AD.
hercules_beetle: Among the largest beetles on Earth, this horned insect roams the jungles of the Caribbean, Central America, and the Amazon basin. Adults weigh about 0.035 kg, and the male's long horn helps set it apart from other species. Active at night, it is still thriving today, and it can fly despite its size.
amur_catfish: Found in the lowlands of China, Japan, and Korea as well as the taiga of Siberia, the Amur catfish makes its home in rivers and lakes. This meat-eating species can reach about 5 kilograms as an adult and is still widespread today. It is an active swimmer and is valued as a food fish.
blanket_octopus: Drifting through tropical seas across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans, the blanket octopus is a carnivore that weighs about half a kilogram as an adult. This species is still alive and thrives in warm open waters. It swims freely and is immune to the venom of the Portuguese man-o-war.
great_frigatebird: Great frigatebirds soar over tropical seas and island coasts, including the waters around Hawaii. They feed mainly on fish and often harass other seabirds to steal their catch in mid-air. An adult weighs about 1.5 kilograms, and the species is still widespread today.
malleefowl: The malleefowl is a ground-dwelling bird found across Australia, where it lives in desert and badlands country. It eats both plant and animal food and an adult typically weighs about 2 kilograms. Rather than sitting on its eggs, this bird builds a large mound of soil and leaf litter, using the heat it generates to incubate them.
akoya_pearl_oyster: Found along coasts from Japan and Korea to the China lowlands and across the Indian Ocean, the Akoya pearl oyster lives attached to one spot for its whole adult life. It feeds by filtering particles from the water, and an adult weighs about 0.05 kg. This species is still alive, and it is valued for the pearls it can produce inside its shell.
asian_giant_hornet: The Asian giant hornet is the largest hornet in the world, and it still thrives today. It lives in forests across Japan, Korea, the lowlands of China, Indochina, and parts of East and Southeast Asia. Adults weigh about 2 grams, and they hunt other insects and attack honeybee hives.
marabou_stork: The marabou stork lives across Africa south of the Sahara and in the Sahel, where it frequents savannas and wetlands. It feeds mainly as a scavenger and is the largest of all storks, with adults weighing around 7 kg. Though it is not extinct, its bald head and bare neck give it a distinctive look that sets it apart from other birds.
australian_grayling: The Australian grayling is a freshwater fish found in rivers across mainland Australia and Tasmania. Adults can reach about 0.2 kilograms, and they feed mainly on insects they find in the water. This species still survives in the wild, and it is protected, which helps it persist in the rivers it calls home.
atlantic_silverside: Along the coasts of eastern North America, small schools of Atlantic silversides move through shallow waters, feeding mostly on insects that fall or drift onto the surface. Each adult weighs only about 0.01 kg, so the fish is tiny even among its coastal neighbors. Still thriving today, it swims in tight groups that shift together as one body.
sea_lily: The deep-sea crinoid, also called a sea lily, is a stalked animal that stays fixed in one place on the seafloor. It lives in the deep waters of the northern Pacific Ocean, around Japan and Korea, and feeds by filtering food particles from the water. An adult weighs about 0.1 kilograms. It is still alive today and has not gone extinct.
pacific_cod: The Pacific cod ranges across the cold northern Pacific Ocean, from the waters off Japan and Korea to the coasts of Alaska and the Yukon. It lives in cold ocean habitats and feeds on other animals. Adults can reach about 10 kg, and this species is still thriving today. It is a swimming fish prized as a food source.
firefly_synchronous: Flying through mangrove swamps and coastal stands across Sundaland and Indochina, this firefly lives on nectar as an adult and weighs only about 0.00003 kg. Its bioluminescent light is used in a striking way, since large groups flash together in unison among the mangrove trees. The species remains alive and is not extinct.
desert_locust: The desert locust roams across the Sahara, the Sahel, Arabia, the Nile valley, and the Indian subcontinent, moving through both desert and savanna. Adults weigh about 2 grams and feed on herbs. When conditions allow, they gather into swarms that migrate over long distances and can devastate crops. People in some regions also eat them.
european_hornet: The European hornet is a large wasp found across Europe, northern Asia, and parts of eastern and southern Asia. It lives in forests, where it builds paper nests and hunts other insects for food. Adults weigh about half a gram, and they can fly and sting. The species is still alive and widespread.
greater_pipefish: The greater pipefish is a slender sea fish that still thrives today. It lives along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the Baltic and North Sea, the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas. An adult weighs only about 0.02 kg, and it feeds on other animals while swimming through its coastal waters.
blue_tang: The palette surgeonfish, often called the blue tang, lives on coral reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It grazes on plant material and weighs about a quarter kilogram as an adult. Its bright colours are easy to spot as it swims, and it carries a venomous spine that it can use for defence.
steephead_parrotfish: Found across the Great Barrier Reef, the Coral Triangle, and parts of the Indian Ocean, the steephead parrotfish lives among coral reefs and grazes on plants. Adults can reach about 10 kg. This species is still alive, and it is known as a sand maker because it helps produce the fine sand that gathers on reef floors.
pigeon_guillemot: The pigeon guillemot lives along the northern Pacific Ocean, including the Pacific Northwest and Beringia, and it stays close to the coast. It feeds mainly on fish. Adults weigh about half a kilogram, and this bird swims, dives, and flies with equal ease.
northern_gannet: The northern gannet breeds in colonies on cliffs and islands across the North Atlantic, from the British Isles to Iceland and Greenland. It hunts fish over cold coastal waters, folding its wings and plunging headfirst from the air to catch its prey. An adult weighs about 3 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today.
striped_bass: Striped bass live along the eastern coast of North America, across the North Atlantic, and in Florida and the Gulf. They move between salt water and rivers, and adults can reach about 20 kilograms. Anglers hunt them and prize them as table fish, and they remain widespread today.
atlantic_mackerel: Schools of Atlantic mackerel roam the cold coastal waters of the North Atlantic, the Baltic and North Seas, the Mediterranean, and the eastern coast of North America. Adults typically weigh about a kilogram and feed on other small animals. These oily, edible fish swim together in tight schools, and they remain plentiful today.
helmeted_curassow: The great curassow lives in the jungles of southern Mexico, Central America, and the Amazon basin. This bird weighs about 3.5 kilograms as an adult and feeds mainly on fruit. It spends much of its life in the trees, and people have long hunted it for food, though it remains widespread today.
limpet_common: The common limpet clings to rocks along the coasts of Atlantic Europe and the British Isles, where it grazes on algae and other plant matter. An adult weighs about 0.02 kg, and it remains widespread today. Its conical shell is edible, and the animal is known for returning to the same resting spot on the rock, a behavior called homing.
whitetip_reef_shark: Often seen resting in caves and crevices during the day, the whitetip reef shark hunts over reefs at night. It lives across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, Polynesia, and Hawaii. Adults weigh about 18 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
common_starfish: The common starfish lives along coasts in Atlantic Europe, including the British Isles and the Baltic and North Sea. It is a carnivore that feeds on mussels. A full-grown adult weighs about 0.2 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
little_blue_penguin: The smallest penguin species, the little penguin, lives along the coasts of New Zealand, Australia, and Tasmania. Adults weigh about 1.2 kg, and they feed on fish while swimming through coastal waters. Many return to land only after dark and nest in burrows, and the species is still widespread today.
philippine_eagle: The Philippine eagle, also called the monkey-eating eagle, lives in jungle and mountain forests across islands 5, 19, 119, and 127. Adults weigh about 6 kg, and they hunt during the day, using their wings to fly through the canopy in search of prey. Their diet is carnivorous, and they are still alive today under legal protection.
atlantic_sturgeon: The Atlantic sturgeon lives along the eastern coast of North America, across the northern Atlantic, and as far south as Florida and the Gulf. It moves between the ocean and rivers, spending time in coastal waters and returning inland to spawn. Adults can reach about 180 kg, and the species is protected because its eggs are harvested for caviar.
blue_ringed_octopus: The greater blue-ringed octopus is a small, venomous cephalopod found across the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Wallacea and New Guinea. It lives on reefs and coastal waters, hunts carnivorous prey, and weighs about 0.1 kg as an adult. Its bite delivers tetrodotoxin, and the species is still alive and widespread.
king_bird_of_paradise: The king bird-of-paradise lives in the jungles of Wallacea and New Guinea, where it feeds mainly on fruit. An adult weighs about 0.05 kg, which is very light for a bird with such showy plumes. Its long, flowing feathers are a striking feature, and the species is still alive today.
sheephead_california: Along reefs stretching from the western coast of North America down into Mexico, the California sheephead is a carnivore that hunts among the rocks. Adults can reach about 16 kg, and this species is still thriving in the wild. Its diet includes sea urchins, and individuals are known to change sex during their lives.
firemouth: The firemouth cichlid calls the rivers and lakes of southern Mexico home. It is an omnivore, so it eats both plant matter and animal food. Adults weigh only about 0.03 kilograms, and this small fish is still thriving in the wild, as it swims through its freshwater haunts.
bombardier_beetle: The Bombardier beetle is a small carnivore about the weight of a grain of rice. It lives in grasslands across Europe and the Mediterranean, and it is still widespread today. When threatened, it sprays a hot chemical mixture from its rear end to drive off attackers.
waved_albatross: The waved albatross breeds on the Galapagos Islands and is still living today. It spends its life over warm ocean waters, where it hunts fish and squid. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms and move through the air as a skilled glider.
congo_peafowl: Shy and secretive, the Congo peafowl makes its home in the jungles of the Congo basin. Adults weigh about 1.5 kilograms, and the species has a varied omnivorous diet. Though it is elusive, it is still very much alive today, and its feathers help mark it as a distinct member of the peafowl family.
sablefish: The sablefish, also called black cod, roams the cold deep waters of the North Pacific, from the Pacific Northwest up through Alaska and the Yukon and across to Japan and Korea. Adults can reach about 57 kilograms, and they hunt other animals as carnivores. Their flesh is rich and oily, which makes them prized as an edible fish.
sea_pig: Scotoplanes globosa is a deep-sea creature that walks across the abyssal seafloor on a set of tube-like legs. It lives in the North Atlantic, North Pacific, and South Atlantic oceans and feeds mainly by scavenging. An adult weighs about 0.1 kilograms, and the species is still living.
greater_prairie_chicken: The greater prairie-chicken is a grassland bird of the Great Plains and parts of eastern North America, where it still survives. Adults weigh about 1 kilogram and feed mainly on plants. During spring, males gather at display grounds called leks to perform for females, and the species is also a huntable game bird.
porbeagle: The porbeagle is a cold-water shark that ranges across the North and South Atlantic, the Baltic and North Sea, the Mediterranean, and subantarctic waters. Adults can weigh around 230 kg, and it feeds on other fish and marine animals. Unlike most sharks, it is warm blooded, and its flesh is edible, which has made it a sought-after catch.
bumphead_parrotfish: The green humphead parrotfish grazes on reef algae and other plant matter, and it is one of the largest reef fish alive, with adults reaching around 75 kg. Its strong beak and grinding teeth let it scrape and break coral, which is why it is known as a bio-eroder. It lives across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Polynesia, and it is a protected species.
california_halibut: The California halibut is a flatfish that lives along the coasts of western North America and Mexico. Adults can reach a mass of about 30 kilograms, and this carnivore feeds on other animals in its coastal home. Although it swims freely, it is also valued as a food fish, and it remains widespread today.
african_lungfish: In the rivers and wetlands of West Africa and the Sahel, this carnivorous fish can grow to about 7 kilograms. It breathes air using lungs, which lets it survive in water that runs low or dries up. During dry seasons it buries itself in mud and forms a protective cocoon, entering a resting state until the rains return.
mimic_octopus: The mimic octopus is found across the Coral Triangle and Sundaland, where it lives on coastal reefs. It weighs about 0.5 kg as an adult and feeds on other animals. This species is not extinct, and it is known for swimming and for copying the appearance and movements of other sea creatures.
coconut_octopus: The veined octopus, sometimes called the coconut octopus, lives along coasts in the Coral Triangle, the Indian Ocean, and Sundaland. Adults weigh around 0.4 kg, and they feed on other animals. This species is still alive, and it is known for swimming and for carrying coconut shells that it uses as portable shelter.
franklins_gull: Franklin's gulls breed across the Great Plains and the Canadian Shield, then travel south to spend the winter in the Andes. They favor wetlands and open plains, where they feed mainly on insects. An adult weighs about 0.28 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
common_moorhen: Across much of the world, the common moorhen makes its home in wetlands and along rivers. This omnivore feeds on a mix of plant and animal food, and an adult typically weighs about 0.35 kilograms. Still widespread today, the species is also a huntable bird, and its feathers are noted as a notable feature.
african_fish_eagle: Along the lakes, rivers, and coastlines of sub-Saharan Africa, this bird hunts mostly fish. Adults weigh about 2.8 kilograms and are active during the day, often seen soaring over the water. The species is still widespread and thriving across its range.
trapdoor_spider: Cteniza sauvagesi is a trapdoor spider found across the Mediterranean, where it makes its home in forest ground. It digs a burrow sealed by a hinged lid, waiting behind that door to ambush passing prey. Its diet is made up of other animals, and an adult weighs about 0.01 kg. The species is still living today.
flamboyant_cuttlefish: The flamboyant cuttlefish lives along coasts in the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Sundaland. An adult weighs about 0.2 kg, and it feeds on other animals. Unlike many of its relatives, this species is known to be venomous, and it moves both by swimming and by walking along the seafloor.
pacific_ocean_perch: The vermilion rockfish lives along the western coast of North America and across the northern Pacific Ocean. It favors cold ocean reefs, where it hunts smaller prey as a carnivore. Adults can reach about 7 kilograms, and this species is known for living a long time and for being good to eat.
rainbow_lorikeet: The rainbow lorikeet lives across Australia and Tasmania, where it moves through forests and coastal areas. Its diet is built around nectar, and an adult weighs about 0.1 kg. Its feathers are bright, and it flies in flocks, so it remains widespread and still thrives today.
rudd: The rudd is a freshwater fish found across Europe and the British Isles, where it lives in lakes and wetlands. It eats a mix of plant and animal food, and adults typically reach about 0.8 kg. Rudd remain widespread today and are edible, which makes them a familiar catch for anglers.
sooty_albatross: The sooty albatross breeds on subantarctic islands and ranges across the cold waters of the Indian Ocean. It spends most of its life at sea, where it feeds on fish and glides effortlessly over the waves on long, narrow wings. An adult weighs about 2.8 kilograms, and the species is still alive today.
ballan_wrasse: The ballan wrasse is a coastal fish found along the Atlantic coast of Europe, including the British Isles and the Baltic and North Sea. It is a carnivore that can reach an adult mass of about 4 kg. This species is still thriving, and it is known for swimming close to shore and for picking parasitic lice off salmon, which makes it a helpful partner to fish farms.
purple_sea_urchin: Along the rocky coasts of western North America and the Pacific Northwest, this spiny creature feeds mainly on plants and algae, grazing across the seafloor. An adult typically weighs about 0.2 kilograms. Its body is covered in sharp spines, and its roe is edible, making it a species of interest to people as well as a steady presence in its coastal home.
snail_kite: Snail kites are wetland hunters that feed almost entirely on apple snails, which they pluck from the water with a hooked bill. Adults weigh about 0.4 kg, and they are active during the day as they glide over marshes and swamps. Their range stretches from Florida and the Gulf coast through the Caribbean, the Amazon basin, and the Pampas and Gran Chaco. The species is still alive across this wide area.
common_skate: The common skate, also called the flapper, lives in the cold coastal waters of Atlantic Europe, including the British Isles and the Baltic and North Seas. It is a meat eater, and adults can reach about 100 kg. Although it is still alive and swims these seas today, it is a protected species, and its flesh is edible.
american_flamingo: The American flamingo, Phoenicopterus ruber, is still living today. It can be found across the Caribbean, the Galapagos, Mexico, and Florida and the Gulf coast, where it favors lakes and coastlines. Adults weigh about 3 kg, and these birds gather in large colonial herds that feed by filtering food from the water.
european_turtle_dove: The European turtle dove is a small bird found across Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Sahel. It lives in forests and open plains, feeding mainly on herbs, and an adult weighs about 0.15 kg. This species is still alive, migrates between its breeding and wintering grounds, and is hunted in some areas.
blackfin_tuna: The blackfin tuna is a warm-water fish found across the Caribbean Sea, the tropical western Atlantic, and the waters off Florida and the Gulf. It lives in the open ocean and feeds on other sea creatures. Adults can reach about 20 kilograms, and the species is still plentiful and prized as a food fish.
black_piranha: The black piranha makes its home in rivers of the Amazon basin, where it swims in schools and feeds on other animals. Its mouth holds razor-sharp teeth that let it deliver a powerful bite. Adults can reach a mass of about 3 kilograms, and the species remains common across its range today.
giant_water_bug: Found across eastern North America and the Great Plains, the giant water bug makes its home in lakes and wetlands. Adults weigh about 5 grams and hunt as predators, feeding on frogs and fish. This species still thrives today, and it can fly from one pond to another while it also bites when handled.
blacklip_abalone: The blacklip abalone is a sea snail that grazes on seaweed along rocky coastlines. It is found around Australia and in the waters off Tasmania, where it clings to rocks with a powerful foot. Adults can weigh about 0.8 kg, and its thick shell and tasty flesh have made it a prized catch that remains widespread today.
white_sturgeon: The white sturgeon lives in rivers and along the coast of the Pacific Northwest in western North America. It is carnivorous and anadromous, moving between saltwater and freshwater as it swims. Adults can reach a mass of about 500 kg, and its roe is harvested for caviar.
spotted_saratoga: The spotted saratoga is a freshwater fish found in Australia, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It feeds on other animals, and adults can reach a mass of about 4 kilograms. This species is still alive and is noted for its swimming and for being edible.
madagascan_moon_moth: The comet moth lives in the jungles of Madagascar and is still alive in the wild. As an adult it weighs only about 0.004 kg, and it feeds on nectar. It flies at night and has long tails trailing from its hindwings.
pacific_sardine: Pacific sardines roam the coasts and cold ocean waters of western North America, the northern and southern Pacific, Japan, Korea, Australia, and the Southern Cone. They feed by filtering tiny particles from the water and typically reach about 0.2 kg as adults. Known for their schooling behavior and as an edible fish, they remain widespread and are not extinct.
blue_tit: Small and quick, the Eurasian blue tit lives across Europe and around the Mediterranean, where it favors woodland. Its diet centers on insects, and an adult weighs only about 0.011 kg. This species is still widespread today, and its feathers and ability to fly make it a lively presence in forest canopies.
black_swan: Native to Australia and Tasmania, the black swan makes its home on lakes and wetlands. It feeds mainly on plants, and an adult typically weighs about 6 kg. Though still thriving in the wild, this species has feathers that have been valued, and it can be hunted in some areas.
common_thresher: The common thresher shark ranges across the North and South Atlantic and Pacific, the Mediterranean, the Indian Ocean, the Caribbean, and tropical seas including the Coral Triangle. It lives in both warm and cold ocean waters, feeds on other animals, and can weigh around 350 kg as an adult. Its long tail is used to slap at prey, and the species is still alive and is considered edible.
porcupinefish: Porcupinefish live on reefs across tropical seas, including the Indian Ocean, the northern and southern Pacific, and the Caribbean. These meat eaters grow to about one kilogram as adults. When threatened, they swim away or gulp water to inflate their bodies, raising their sharp spines, and their flesh carries tetrodotoxin, a dangerous poison.
orange_footed_scrubfowl: Orange-footed scrubfowl live across Wallacea, New Guinea, and parts of Australia, where they move between jungle and coastal areas. These birds eat a mix of plant and animal food, and an adult typically weighs about 0.8 kg. Like their relatives, they are known as mound builders, piling up vegetation and soil to create nests.
nurse_shark: Resting under ledges by day, the nurse shark emerges at night to hunt on reefs and along coastlines. This docile fish, which can grow to about 110 kg, lives in the western Atlantic tropics, the Caribbean Sea, and off the coast of West Africa. As a carnivore, it feeds on the creatures it finds on the seafloor.
grunion: The California grunion is a small silvery fish found along the coast of western North America. Adults weigh about 0.03 kilograms and feed on insects. Its most unusual trait is that it swims onto the beach to spawn, laying its eggs in the sand before returning to the sea.
crevalle_jack: The crevalle jack is found across the Caribbean, the western Atlantic tropics, Florida and the Gulf, the coast of West Africa, and parts of the North Atlantic. It favors warm coastal waters and open ocean, and it hunts other fish and marine prey. Adults can reach about 25 kilograms, and anglers and divers both seek this powerful swimmer.
arapaima: The arapaima is a giant freshwater fish of the Amazon basin, where it moves through rivers, lakes, and wetlands. Adults can reach around 200 kilograms, and they feed on other animals. Unlike most fish, it gulps air at the surface to breathe, and it is still very much alive today.
african_grey: Grey parrots make their homes in the jungles of the Congo basin and along the west African coast. They feed mainly on fruit and weigh about 0.45 kilograms as adults. Known for their mimicry and sharp intelligence, these birds live in flocks and spend most of their time in the trees.
american_paddlefish: The American paddlefish is still alive and lives across eastern North America and the Great Plains. It makes its home in rivers and lakes, where it filters tiny food from the water with its gill rakers. Adults can reach about 60 kg, and the long, flat paddle on its snout gives the species its name. Because its eggs are valued as caviar, the paddlefish is protected.
white_stork: Wetlands and open plains from Europe and the Mediterranean through Iran, Anatolia, and the Sahel to sub-Saharan Africa are home to the white stork. Adults weigh around 3.5 kg and feed on meat. This migratory bird is still widespread, and it often builds its large nests on rooftops.
capelin: Capelin are small silvery fish found across the cold waters of the North Atlantic, North Pacific, and Arctic Oceans. They feed on plankton by filtering it from the water, and adults weigh about 0.05 kg. These migratory, schooling fish are edible and still thriving in the wild.
ghost_pipefish: Drifting among coral heads and sea fans, this small reef fish blends into its surroundings by mimicking floating debris and plant matter. It lives across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It feeds on small crustaceans and other tiny prey, and an adult weighs only about three grams.
marble_trout: The marble trout makes its home in rivers across the Alps and the Mediterranean region, where it hunts smaller animals for food. Adults can reach about 6 kg, and this fish is still living in the wild. It is an edible species, yet it is protected, so catching it is restricted in many places.
emperor_scorpion: The emperor scorpion is the largest scorpion in the world, and adults weigh about 0.03 kg. It lives in burrows in jungle and savanna country across the Congo basin and along the west coast of Africa. Active at night, it hunts other animals and glows a bright fluorescent green under ultraviolet light.
white_faced_whistling_duck: The white-faced whistling duck is found across Africa south of the Sahara, in the Amazon basin, and on the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It favors lakes and wetlands, where it feeds on a varied diet of plants and small animals. Adults weigh about 0.7 kg, and the species is still widespread today, though it can be hunted and is active mainly at night.
stickleback_three: Measuring only about a few grams as an adult, the three-spined stickleback lives across Europe, North America, northern Asia, Japan, and Korea. It moves through rivers, coastal waters, and lakes, feeding mainly on insects. Males are known for building nests, a skill that helps them raise their young.
bluefin_trevally: The bluespotted trevally roams reefs and coastal waters across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, Polynesia, Hawaii, and the Red Sea. It hunts other fish and other prey, and adults can reach about 43 kilograms. This species is still abundant, and people catch it for food.
great_tit: The great tit is a small songbird found across Europe and much of Asia, from the Palearctic into the Indomalaya region. It makes its home in forests, where it feeds mainly on insects. An adult weighs about 19 grams, and this species is still widespread today.
sooty_tern: Spending its days over tropical seas, the sooty tern nests on warm islands and feeds mainly on fish. An adult weighs about 0.2 kilograms, and this species is still widespread today. Its feathers help it fly for long stretches, and it can remain at sea for years at a time.
jewel_beetle: The jewel beetle, known as Chrysina resplendens, lives in forests across Central America and southern Mexico. Adults feed on plants and weigh about 3 grams. Its shell gleams with an iridescent sheen, and it is able to fly.
leafcutter_bee: Tiny but tireless, the leafcutter bee lives across Europe and makes its home in grassland. Adults weigh only about 0.00005 kg, and they feed on nectar while flying from flower to flower. As a small pollinator, it helps keep the plants around it reproducing, and it remains very much alive today.
indian_ornamental_regalis: Found in the forests and jungles of the Indian subcontinent, this spider is a carnivore that weighs about 0.04 kilograms as an adult. It lives in trees, moving quickly through the branches, and it is venomous. The species is still alive today.
dragonfly_emperor: Patrolling over ponds and lakes, the emperor dragonfly is a daytime hunter that catches other insects in flight. It lives across Europe, Africa, and the Mediterranean, and it still thrives in the wild. An adult weighs about one gram, roughly the mass of a paper clip.
sheepshead: The sheepshead is a fish found along the eastern coast of North America, particularly in Florida and the Gulf. It lives close to shore and eats a mix of plant and animal foods. Adults can reach about 8 kilograms, and the species is still thriving today. Its teeth look strikingly like human teeth, and it is valued as a good food fish.
silver_carp: The silver carp is a fish native to the lowlands of China and Indochina, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It feeds by filtering tiny particles from the water and can grow to about 20 kg as an adult. Known for leaping out of the water, it is also edible and has been domesticated.
short_eared_owl: Short-eared owls live across the Palearctic, the Nearctic, and South America, where they hunt over plains, tundra, and wetlands. These carnivores weigh about 0.33 kilograms as adults and are active during the day. They are nomadic, moving in search of food, and they fly low over open ground as they hunt. The species is still living and widespread.
tawny_nurse: Dwelling along reefs and coastlines, this shark is found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and the Red Sea. It hunts meat-based prey and is most active at night, when it moves slowly over the seabed. Adults can reach about 90 kg, and the species remains widespread today.
bee_hummingbird: Weighing only about two grams as an adult, this is the smallest bird in the world. It lives in forest habitats and feeds on nectar, hovering and darting among flowers. Still thriving today, it is found in Cuba, where its tiny body and rapid flight make it a striking sight.
blue_footed_booby: The blue-footed booby is a seabird that nests on coastal and island areas, with its range reaching the Galapagos, Mexico, and the Andes. It feeds on fish and weighs about 1.5 kg as an adult. Known for its plunge dives into the water and its elaborate courtship dancing, it is still alive and widespread today.
tiger_pufferfish: The tiger pufferfish, known in Japan as fugu, lives along the coasts of Japan, Korea, and the lowlands of China. Adults can reach about 3 kilograms, and they feed on a mixed diet of plants and animals. This species is still alive and widespread, and it carries tetrodotoxin, a toxin that makes careful preparation essential before anyone eats it.
robber_fly: The giant robber fly lives across eastern North America and makes its home in grasslands. Adults weigh about half a gram, and they hunt other insects. They are still living today, waiting in ambush and catching their prey in midair.
dinornis_novaezealandiae: The North Island giant moa was a flightless bird that lived in New Zealand, roaming both forest and grassland. It fed on plants and could reach an adult mass of about 150 kg. Hunted by people, it died out around 1450 AD.
auckland_merganser: The Auckland merganser once lived in New Zealand and the subantarctic, moving between rivers and coastal waters. It fed on fish and weighed about 0.9 kg as an adult. Its feathers were prized, and it could not fly, which made it easy prey before it was declared extinct in 1902.
