spruce_grouse: Spruce grouse live across the Canadian Shield and into Alaska and the Yukon, where they make their home in the taiga. Adults weigh about half a kilogram and feed mainly on plants. Their feathers are a notable feature, and they are hunted by people, though they can also be quite tame.
stellate_sturgeon: The stellate sturgeon, Acipenser stellatus, lives in the Black and Caspian seas and moves between coastal waters and rivers. Adults reach about 20 kg and eat a mixed diet of both plant and animal matter. Because its eggs are prized for caviar, this species is protected, and it remains alive today.
himalayan_monal: Roaming the mountain slopes of the Himalaya and Tibet, this bird is still alive and well today. Adults weigh about 2 kg, and their feathers shimmer with iridescent colour. Its diet is omnivorous, and it has long been hunted for its striking plumage.
sarus_crane: The sarus crane is found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Australia, where it lives in wetlands and open plains. Standing tall and weighing around 7.5 kilograms as an adult, it is counted among the tallest flying birds. Sarus cranes form bonded pairs that often stay together for life, and they feed on a mix of plant and animal foods.
laughing_owl: The laughing owl was a nocturnal bird of New Zealand, found in both forests and mountain country. It fed on meat and weighed about 0.6 kilograms as an adult. Known for walking on the ground and nesting in burrows, it was last recorded in 1914.
european_edible_crab: The edible crab roams the seabed along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, including the British Isles and the Baltic and North Sea. It is a carnivore, and a full-grown adult can weigh about 3 kg. Its hard shell protects it, and people hunt it for food, so it remains a common and living species.
white_wagtail: The white wagtail is a small songbird found across the Palearctic and in parts of Africa. It favors open plains and river edges, where it hunts insects on the ground and in the air. An adult weighs only about 21 grams, and it is still widespread today.
nelma: The inconnu, also called the sheefish, lives in rivers and lakes across Alaska, the Yukon, Siberian taiga, and the Black and Caspian seas. This carnivorous fish can reach about 14 kilograms as an adult. It is migratory and prized as an edible species, and it remains very much alive today.
spiny_dogfish: Spiny dogfish live in cold coastal waters across the North and South Atlantic, the North Pacific, the Baltic and North Seas, the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian Seas. They are carnivores that gather in schools and grow to about 9 kilograms. Each one carries venomous spines, and its flesh is edible, which is why it appears in fish and chips.
passenger_pigeon: Once numbering in the billions, the passenger pigeon ranged across eastern North America, the Great Plains, the Canadian Shield, and Florida and the Gulf region. It lived in forests, fed on fruit, and weighed about 0.34 kilograms as an adult. Flocks moved in great herds and were hunted heavily until the species became extinct in 1914.
zebrafish: Small and quick, the zebrafish swims through rivers of the Indian subcontinent, where it is still found in the wild. Its diet consists of insects, and an adult weighs only about one gram. Its slender body and constant motion make it easy to spot in its flowing home waters.
old_world_swallowtail: Across Europe, northern and eastern Asia, and parts of North America including Alaska and the Yukon, the Old World swallowtail lives in grasslands and wetlands. Adults feed on nectar and fly during the day. Weighing about half a gram, this butterfly is still thriving across its wide range.
stingless_bee_trigona: The Australian stingless bee lives across Australia, mostly in forest country. It feeds on nectar and weighs only about 0.00001 kg as an adult. Despite its small size, it is still living today, and it is one of the few bee species that people can keep in hives for their honey. Unlike many bees, it has no sting.
monarch_swan_plant_african: The African monarch, Danaus chrysippus, lives across Africa, the Indian subcontinent, and Arabia, where it favors open savanna. Adults feed on nectar and weigh only about 0.0003 kilograms. This species is still alive, and it is known for flying with a steady, drifting motion while being toxic to would-be predators.
okarito_kiwi: The Okarito kiwi lives in the forests of New Zealand, where it forages for insects after dark. Adults weigh about 2.6 kilograms, and like all kiwi they cannot fly. Because it is nocturnal and shelters among the trees by day, it is rarely seen, and it is now a protected species that remains alive today.
banded_demoiselle: Along slow-moving rivers across Europe and northern Asia, the banded demoiselle is a damselfly that hunts insects by day. An adult weighs roughly 0.0003 kilograms, so it is one of the lightest creatures in its watery home. Its population remains healthy, and it continues to flutter over river banks in the sunshine.
firefly_photinus: Glowing through warm summer evenings across eastern North America, the common eastern firefly is a small nocturnal beetle that flashes light from its abdomen. It lives in wetlands and grasslands, where adults and larvae alike hunt other small creatures. An adult weighs only about 0.00005 kilograms, and the species remains common and widespread today.
common_buzzard: The common buzzard is a bird of prey found across Europe, Iran, Anatolia, and much of Africa south of the Sahara. It favors both forest and open plains, and it hunts by day on the wing. Adults weigh about 0.9 kilograms, and the populations breeding in the north travel south when winter comes.
edible_sea_urchin: The European edible urchin is found along the Atlantic coasts of Europe, including the British Isles, and in the Baltic and North Sea. It lives in coastal waters and eats both plant and animal matter. An adult typically weighs around 0.3 kg, and its spines are covered in a protective shell. Its roe is prized as a food, so people have long harvested it from the seabed.
giant_dobsonfly_chinese: Found along rivers in the lowlands of China and Indochina, this insect spends much of its life underwater and feeds on other small creatures. Adults weigh about 0.01 kg, and they are still living today. Once they emerge, they take to the air, and they hold the title of widest-winged aquatic insect.
spiny_lobster_caribbean: The Caribbean spiny lobster roams the Caribbean Sea, the waters of Florida and the Gulf, and the western Atlantic tropics. It lives over reefs and along coastlines, where it feeds on both plants and animals. Adults can reach about 4 kilograms, and it is active at night, when groups travel in long single-file lines across the seabed.
viperfish: Sloane's viperfish lives in the deep ocean across the North Atlantic, South Atlantic, North Pacific, South Pacific, and Indian Oceans. It is a carnivore that swims through the dark water and dangles a glowing lure to draw in prey. Its huge teeth are built for catching meals, and an adult weighs about 0.1 kilograms.
eclectus_parrot: The Eclectus parrot lives across Wallacea, New Guinea, and parts of Australia, where it makes its home in jungle. Adults weigh about 0.45 kg, and it is still widespread today. Males and females look strikingly different from one another, and the species spends its life in the trees, eating fruit.
atlantic_blue_crab: The Atlantic blue crab lives along the eastern coast of North America, around Florida and the Gulf, and in the Caribbean Sea. It is found in coastal waters and swamps, where it eats both plants and animals. Adults can reach about 0.5 kg, and this species is still living. People can hunt and eat it, and it is also known for its strong swimming and hard shell.
long_horned_beetle: The harlequin beetle, Acrocinus longimanus, is still found today across the Amazon basin and Central America. It lives in jungle habitats, where it feeds on plant matter. Adults weigh about 0.01 kilograms, and they are known for their long forelegs and their ability to fly.
thick_billed_murre: Thick-billed murres breed across the Arctic and the cold northern Atlantic and Pacific Oceans, where they gather in dense colonies on rocky coastlines. These birds weigh about 1 kilogram as adults and feed mainly on fish. They are strong swimmers that also fly, and they remain common today.
aepyornis_maximus: The largest bird known to have lived, this flightless giant roamed the forests, grasslands, and swamps of Madagascar. Adults could weigh around 500 kg and fed on plants. Its enormous egg held about 10 litres, and the species is believed to have vanished around the year 1000 AD.
smooth_hammerhead: Found across warm coastal waters and open seas, the smooth hammerhead ranges through the North and South Atlantic, the North and South Pacific, the Mediterranean, the Indian Ocean, the Caribbean, and the Coral Triangle. This carnivore can reach about 200 kilograms as an adult. It is still widespread today and is listed as living, not extinct, and it is known to swim constantly.
wolffish: The Atlantic wolffish lives in the cold waters of the North Atlantic, around Iceland and Greenland and in parts of the Baltic and North Sea. It is a meat eater that swims through the ocean, and adults can reach about 24 kilograms. Its strong teeth help it grip and crush its prey, and people have long valued its flesh as food.
cushion_star: The cushion star is a living reef dweller found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. Its body is pentagonal and plump, and an adult can weigh around 0.8 kg. It eats a mix of plant and animal matter, so it is classed as omnivorous.
gyrfalcon: The gyrfalcon is the largest of all falcons, with adults weighing about 1.4 kilograms. It lives across the Arctic, including Iceland, Greenland, and Scandinavia, and makes its home in tundra and taiga. Hunting by day, it feeds on other animals and is still widespread today. Falconers have long prized it for the sport of falconry.
coconut_crab: The coconut crab roams islands and coastlines across Polynesia, the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and Madagascar. It is the largest land arthropod, weighing around 4 kilograms as an adult, and it climbs trees and cracks open coconuts. Active at night, this omnivore is still alive in the wild and is hunted for its meat.
jumping_spider: Weighing about a tenth of a milligram as an adult, the zebra jumping spider is tiny but still very much alive. It hunts insects in forests and grasslands across Europe and North America. Its excellent eyesight and powerful jumps help it stalk and catch prey.
australian_rock_scorpion: Beneath the sands of Australian deserts, the giant burrowing scorpion digs its home and waits for night. It hunts other small creatures and weighs only about 0.01 kg as an adult. Under ultraviolet light, its body glows with a fluorescent green.
sandbar_shark: Found along coasts in the North and South Atlantic, both sides of the Pacific, the Mediterranean, the Indian Ocean, and tropical seas, the sandbar shark is a living species. Adults reach about 120 kg, and it hunts other animals as a carnivore. Its flesh is edible, which has made it a valued catch for people.
helmet_shell: The emperor helmet is a large sea snail found in the Caribbean Sea and along the coasts of Florida and the Gulf. It lives in shallow coastal waters and feeds on other animals, with a particular taste for sea urchins. Adults can reach about 1 kilogram, and the species is still alive today.
freshwater_jellyfish: Drifting through the still waters of China's lowland lakes, this tiny freshwater jellyfish feeds on other small creatures it catches with its stinging tentacles. An adult weighs only about half a gram, and its sting is mild enough that it poses little trouble to people. Unlike many of its marine relatives, it is still very much alive today.
portuguese_man_o_war: A float of gas rides on the surface of warm tropical seas, carrying a colony of many individual animals that work together as one. Its tentacles can sting, and it feeds on small sea creatures it catches. The Portuguese man o' war lives in the Atlantic, Caribbean, Indian Ocean, and Mediterranean, and it still thrives today.
waitaha_penguin: Once found along New Zealand's coasts, the Waitaha penguin fed on fish and swam through coastal waters. Adults weighed about 6 kg. Early Māori hunted these birds for food, and the species had died out by around 1500 AD.
blue_mussel: Anchored to rocks, pilings, and other hard surfaces along the coast, this bivalve lives in the North Atlantic, the Baltic and North Sea, Atlantic Europe, and eastern North America. It feeds by filtering tiny particles from the water and stays put for most of its life. Adults weigh about 0.05 kg, and its dark blue shell makes it easy to recognize on the shore. People have long harvested it as a food.
king_baboon_tarantula: Native to the savannas of East Africa and the wider region south of the Sahara, this spider is still common in its range. It feeds on other animals and weighs roughly 0.08 kg as an adult. Its venom is part of how it subdues prey, and it spends much of its life in a burrow.
chum_salmon: Chum salmon live across the cold North Pacific, from the Pacific Northwest and Alaska through Yukon, northern Asia, Japan, and Korea. Adults typically weigh about 5 kg. They are anadromous, spending their adult lives at sea and returning to rivers to spawn, and they are hunted and prized as food.
flathead_catfish: Flathead catfish inhabit rivers across eastern North America, the Great Plains, and Mexico. As carnivores, they ambush their prey, and adults can reach about 35 kilograms. Still widespread today, they are hunted by anglers and prized as a food fish.
painted_stork: Wading through shallow lakes and marshes across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, the painted stork feeds mainly on fish. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms. These birds nest in colonies and remain a living species, valued for their colorful plumage.
sea_nettle_pacific: Along the western coast of North America, from the Pacific Northwest southward, this jellyfish drifts through coastal waters. It is a carnivore, and its body can weigh about 1 kilogram as an adult. Still thriving today, it is known for its sting.
earth_worm_giant_gippsland: The Giant Gippsland earthworm lives in a small area of southeastern Australia, where it makes its home in forests and grasslands. Adults can reach about 0.4 kilograms, which makes them some of the largest earthworms anywhere. They dig burrows through the soil and feed on a varied, omnivorous diet, and the species is protected.
sandeel: The lesser sandeel lives in the Baltic and North Sea and along the Atlantic coast of Europe. It feeds on plankton and spends much of its time in schools near the shore. Adults weigh about 0.03 kg, and when the tide is low or night falls, individuals burrow into the sandy seabed to rest.
grey_crowned_crane: Grey crowned cranes roam the savannas of East and Southern Africa, moving between wetlands and open grassland. They eat a mix of plant matter and small animals, and an adult weighs about 3.5 kg. These birds gather in herds and are known for their dancing displays, which involve bowing, leaping, and flapping their wings.
eurasian_teal: The Eurasian teal is a small dabbling duck that weighs about 0.35 kilograms as an adult. It lives across the Palearctic, in Africa, and on the Indian subcontinent, favoring wetlands and lakes. Its diet is omnivorous, and it migrates between seasons. Hunters pursue it as game.
thick_billed_parrot: The thick-billed parrot is found in Mexico, within a range that spans roughly latitudes 31 to 32.5 north and longitudes 110 to 108.5 west. It lives in mountain forests, where it feeds mostly on fruit and pine seeds. An adult weighs about 0.35 kilograms, and the species still survives in the wild.
new_zealand_fantail: The New Zealand fantail lives in the forests of New Zealand, where it hunts for insects. An adult weighs only about 8 grams, and it is still widespread today. Its name comes from the way it spreads its tail feathers into a fan as it flies and darts after prey.
red_king_crab: Adults of this species can reach about 10 kilograms, making them among the heaviest crabs in the world. They live across the cold coastal waters of the North Pacific, from Alaska and the Yukon down to Japan, Korea, and the Pacific Northwest. Their diet is carnivorous, and their hard shells and tasty meat have made them a prized catch for people in the region.
ceylon_junglefowl: The Sri Lanka junglefowl lives in forest across a bounded region of the island of Sri Lanka. It is an omnivore, eating both plant matter and small animals. An adult weighs about 0.9 kg, and it is still living in the wild today. Its feathers are prized, and it is a species that can be hunted.
norfolk_kaka: The Norfolk Island kaka was a parrot that lived on forested land in the small island area near 29 degrees south and 168 degrees east. It ate a mixed diet of plant and animal foods and weighed about half a kilogram as an adult. Its feathers were prized and the bird could be hunted, and it was recorded as extinct by 1851.
common_cockle: The common cockle is a bivalve found along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the British Isles, and the Baltic and North Sea. It lives in sandy or muddy shores and feeds by filtering tiny particles from the water. Adults weigh about 0.02 kg, and the shell is edible, which has made it a long-standing seafood. It burrows into the sediment, where it remains hidden.
mouse_spider: The eastern mouse spider is a venomous spider found across Australia, where it makes its home in both forest and grassland. It digs burrows to shelter in and feeds on other animals. An adult weighs about 0.01 kg, and the species is still alive today.
steppe_eagle: The steppe eagle breeds across the eastern steppe, including the Kazakh and Mongolian steppes, and spends the winter in Africa and the Indian subcontinent. Adults weigh about 3 kg, and they hunt during the day over open plains and grassland. Alongside living prey, they also scavenge, and they are migratory birds that still survive today.
moa_nalo_small: The small-billed moa-nalo, known scientifically as Ptaiochen pau, was a flightless browsing duck that lived in the forests of the Hawaiian Islands, roughly between latitudes 20.5 and 21.3 north and longitudes 157.4 and 156 west. It fed on herbs and weighed about 3 kilograms as an adult. It went extinct around the year 1000 AD.
deathstalker: Found across the Sahara, Arabia, the Nile valley, and southwest Asia, this desert scorpion weighs only about three grams as an adult. It hunts insects and other small prey after dark, and its venom is potent enough to be deadly to people. Under ultraviolet light its body glows a bright green, a trait that helps researchers spot it at night.
lanner_falcon: The lanner falcon ranges across Africa, around the Mediterranean, and into Arabia, where it hunts over plains, savanna, and desert. Adults weigh about 0.7 kilograms and feed on other animals. It is active during the day, and it has long been prized in falconry, a tradition in which people train birds like this one to hunt alongside them.
smallmouth_bass: Found across eastern North America and parts of the Canadian Shield, the smallmouth bass makes its home in both lakes and rivers. As a carnivore, it hunts smaller prey through the water, and adults can reach about 2.5 kg. This species is still thriving, is popular with anglers, and its flesh is good to eat.
hyacinth_macaw: The largest flying parrot in the world, the hyacinth macaw roosts and nests high in trees across the Amazon basin, the Pampas, and the Gran Chaco. It moves through jungle and wetland habitats, feeding mostly on fruit and weighing about 1.4 kilograms as an adult. Its deep blue plumage is well known, and the species is protected, though it remains alive and present in the wild.
ochre_sea_star: The ochre sea star lives along the rocky coasts of western North America, from Alaska and the Yukon down through the Pacific Northwest. It is a carnivore that feeds heavily on mussels, and because it keeps mussel numbers in check, it plays a keystone role in its shoreline community. An adult weighs about 0.8 kg. It remains common and is not extinct.
crane_fly: The European crane fly, known to many as the mosquito hawk, lives across Europe in wetland habitats. Adults feed on nectar and weigh about 0.0002 kg. This species is still alive and well, and it is a familiar sight over wet meadows and marshes.
great_grey_owl: The great grey owl ranges across the Canadian Shield, the Siberian taiga, Scandinavia, and parts of Alaska and the Yukon. It lives in taiga forest and hunts mostly small mammals. Adults weigh about 1.2 kilograms, and this species is the longest owl in the world, though not the heaviest. It is nocturnal and flies silently, and it is still alive and widespread today.
bonefish: Bonefish live on shallow flats along coasts across the Caribbean, Florida and the Gulf, tropical seas, and the Indian Ocean. These carnivores feed on small prey and can reach about 5 kg as adults. Anglers prize them as a game fish, and they remain widespread today.
giant_squid: Drifting through the deep ocean, the giant squid ranges across the North and South Atlantic, the North and South Pacific, the Indian Ocean, and the waters off Japan and Korea. Adults can reach about 275 kilograms, and this carnivore has the largest eyes of any animal. When threatened, it releases ink, and sperm whales are among its known predators.
pinkfoot_goliath: The Pinkfoot goliath spider makes its home in the jungles of the Amazon basin, where it digs and lives in burrows. As a carnivore, it hunts other small creatures, and adults typically weigh about 0.15 kilograms. This species is venomous and remains alive in the wild today.
european_anchovy: The European anchovy lives along the coasts of Atlantic Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Black and Caspian seas. It feeds by filtering tiny particles from the water and typically weighs about 0.03 kg as an adult. Swimming in tight schools, this small fish is edible and remains widespread today.
wolf_spider_common: Found across Europe and northern Asia, this spider makes its home in forests. It feeds on other animals and weighs roughly half a gram as an adult. Females carry their egg sacs with them, and the species is quick on its feet.
stellers_sea_eagle: Steller's sea eagle, a fish-eating bird of prey, lives along coasts and rivers across northern Asia, Japan, and Korea. Adults weigh about 6.7 kg, and the species is still alive today. It is active by day, flies over its range, and some populations migrate.
stag_beetle_european: Adult European stag beetles weigh about 0.006 kg and live across Europe, including Atlantic Europe and the Mediterranean region. They inhabit forests, and their diet is listed as frug. These beetles are still alive today, can fly, and carry antler-like jaws. They are a protected species.
african_darter: The African darter is a waterbird found across Africa south of the Sahara and along the Nile valley. It lives in swamps and rivers, where it hunts fish. Adults weigh about 1.3 kilograms, and the species is still alive today. Its feathers and swimming ability help it move through the water.
night_parrot: Hidden away in the arid deserts of Australia, the night parrot spends its days sheltering on the ground and comes out only after dark. Its diet consists of plant material, and an adult weighs roughly 0.1 kg. Few people have ever seen this elusive bird, but it survives today, which makes it a rare find for anyone exploring the outback.
andean_tinamou: The Andean tinamou is a ground bird that makes its home across the Andes mountains. It keeps to mountain grasslands, where it feeds on both plants and small animals. An adult weighs about 0.4 kg, and the species is still widespread, though it is sometimes hunted.
himalayan_snowcock: Found across the Himalayas and the Tibetan plateau, this bird makes its home in rocky mountain country. It feeds mainly on plants and weighs about 2.4 kilograms as an adult. Although it is still widespread, its dense feathering and its status as a game bird have made it a target for hunters.
golden_king_crab: Found across the North Pacific, from Alaska and the Yukon to Japan and Korea, the golden king crab lives on the deep ocean floor. It feeds on other animals and can reach an adult mass of about 6 kg. Its hard shell and tasty meat make it a valued catch, and it is still thriving today.
coelacanth_west_indian: Caught off South Africa in 1938, this fish was a living fossil long thought extinct for millions of years. It lives in deep ocean waters and caves around Madagascar, where it hunts other fish and squid. Adults can reach about 90 kilograms, and the species is now protected.
somali_ostrich: The Somali ostrich lives across the East African savanna and in Arabia, moving through both desert and open grassland. It feeds mainly on plants and can reach an adult weight of about 105 kilograms. Its feathers and its presence in the Horn of Africa are noted features, and the species remains alive today.
long_tailed_duck: The long-tailed duck breeds across Arctic regions of the Palearctic and Nearctic, nesting in tundra and wintering along coasts. It eats a mix of plant and animal food and weighs about 0.7 kilograms as an adult. Diving deep for its meals, this migratory bird is still widespread and remains a huntable species.
wood_duck: Wood ducks live in eastern North America, the Pacific Northwest, Mexico, and the Caribbean, where they favor swamps, forests, and rivers. They eat a mix of plant and animal foods and weigh about 0.65 kg as adults. Unlike many ducks, they perch in trees and nest in holes, and they remain widespread and alive today.
lord_howe_stick_insect: The tree lobster is a flightless stick insect that once lived on Lord Howe Island, where it was found in forest and fed on plants. Black rats arrived and wiped it out on the main island, and it was declared extinct in 1920. A small surviving colony was later found clinging to Ball's Pyramid, a rocky stack nearby, and this heavy insect can weigh about 25 grams.
glaucous_macaw: The glaucous macaw once lived across the Pampas and Gran Chaco of the Southern Cone, moving between wetland and forest. Adults weighed about 0.9 kg, and the birds spent much of their time in trees. Their diet was made up of fruit. The species is recorded as extinct from 1960 AD, and its feathers and rarity were noted features of its story.
northern_harrier: Flying low over open grassland and marsh, the northern harrier hunts by day, quartering the ground for prey. It lives across the Nearctic and into Mexico, and its diet is made up of meat. An adult weighs about 0.45 kilograms, and the species is still living today.
giant_millipede: Found across the savannas and forests of East Africa and the wider region south of the Sahara, this millipede grows to roughly a tenth of a kilogram as an adult. It feeds mainly on plant material and plays a role as a detritivore, breaking down decaying matter. When threatened, it curls into a tight coil and releases a toxic secretion as a defense.
dumbo_octopus: Found in the deep waters of the North Atlantic, South Atlantic, North Pacific, South Pacific, and Indian Oceans, the dumbo octopus lives far below the surface. It is a meat eater, and adults weigh about 5 kilograms. Its ear fins let it swim, giving it its nickname and a distinctive look among octopuses.
egyptian_goose: The Egyptian goose is a bird of rivers, lakes, and wetlands, found across Africa south of the Sahara and throughout the Nile valley. Adults weigh about 2 kg, and they eat a mixed diet of plants and small animals. Though still common across its range, this species can be aggressive, and it is a huntable bird.
rocky_mountain_locust: The Rocky Mountain locust once lived across the Great Plains, western North America, and the Canadian Shield, where it fed on plants in grasslands and open plains. Adults weighed about two grams, yet they flew in swarms that were the largest insect gatherings ever recorded. The species went extinct in 1902, largely because its breeding grounds were converted to farmland.
rodrigues_rail: The Rodrigues rail was a flightless bird that once lived on the small island of Rodrigues, a volcanic speck in the Indian Ocean. It ate a mix of plant and animal food and weighed about half a kilogram as an adult. The species was lost to extinction in 1761.
bighead_carp: Bighead carp are large filter feeders native to the lowlands of China and Indochina, where they live in rivers and lakes. Adults can reach a mass of about 30 kg, and they use their gill rakers to strain tiny food particles from the water. Their flesh is edible, and the species has long been domesticated for aquaculture.
ide: The ide, also called the orfe, is a fish found across Europe and northern Asia. It lives in both rivers and lakes and eats a varied diet of both plants and animals. Adults can grow to about 3 kilograms, and the species is still living in the wild and is edible.
common_loon: The common loon breeds across the Canadian Shield, Alaska and the Yukon, Iceland, Greenland, and both eastern and western North America. It lives on lakes and along coasts, where it feeds mostly on fish that it catches by diving beneath the surface. Adults weigh about 4 kilograms, and the species is still widespread and migratory, with a haunting call that carries across quiet water.
tarantula_hawk: Found across the southern United States, Mexico, and Central America, this wasp makes its home in deserts and grasslands. Adults feed mainly on nectar, weighing only about 3 grams. Despite its small size, it is known for having the most painful sting of any insect, and it hunts tarantulas to feed its young.
green_abalone: The green ormer is a sea snail with a flattened, ear-shaped shell that clings to rocks along rocky coasts. It grazes on seaweed and other plant matter, and adults typically weigh about 0.2 kg. Found around the Atlantic coast of Europe, the Mediterranean and the British Isles, it remains common today. Its shell and flesh have long been prized as food.
giant_centipede_amazon: Lurking beneath leaf litter across the Amazon basin and parts of the Caribbean, this centipede lives in jungle habitats and hunts at night. It preys on bats and mice, subduing them with a venomous bite. Adults weigh around 0.15 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today.
tiger_cowrie: The tiger cowrie is a sea snail whose glossy shell carries bold dark spots on a warm background. It lives on reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, and Polynesia. It grazes on plant matter, and an adult weighs about 0.15 kg. Its shell was once used as money in parts of the world, and the species remains common today.
tiger_beetle: The green tiger beetle roams the grasslands of Europe and northern Asia, where it hunts other small creatures. An adult weighs only about 0.0003 kg, yet it is still alive and well today. This insect is known as the fastest running insect, and it can also take to the air.
giant_oceanic_manta: Giant oceanic manta rays roam warm tropical seas across the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. As filter feeders, they strain plankton from the water as they swim. Adults can reach a mass of about 1350 kg, and they are known to leap from the water. Protected status helps safeguard this species, which is still living today.
big_bellied_seahorse: The big-bellied seahorse, Hippocampus abdominalis, lives along coastlines in Australia, Tasmania, and New Zealand. It is the largest of all seahorse species and is a carnivore. An adult weighs about 0.05 kg, and this species is still alive today.
fieldfare: The fieldfare is a thrush that breeds across Scandinavia, the Siberian taiga, and much of Europe. It moves through forests and open plains, eating both plants and small animals. Adults weigh about 0.1 kilograms, and the species is still common in the wild. Fieldfares travel in large flocks and migrate between seasons.
crucian_carp: Found across Europe and into Scandinavia, the crucian carp makes its home in lakes and wetlands. It eats both plants and animals, and an adult typically weighs about 1 kilogram. This hardy fish is still thriving today and is considered edible.
ribbon_eel: Glimmering through reef crevices across the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and the Indian Ocean, the ribbon eel is a living, colourful carnivore that weighs about 0.1 kg as an adult. It swims freely among the coral, and over its life it can change sex. Its bright banded body makes it a striking sight for divers who explore these reef waters.
red_tailed_hawk: Still thriving across its range, the red-tailed hawk lives throughout the Nearctic, Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean. It hunts over plains, forests, and deserts, feeding on meat and taking to the air during daylight hours. An adult typically weighs about 1.1 kilograms, and the bird has long been trained for falconry.
laughing_dove: The laughing dove is found across Africa, Arabia, and the Indian subcontinent, where it makes its home on open plains. It feeds mainly on herbs and weighs around 0.1 kg as an adult. Its species is not extinct and remains widespread, and it is known for being a feathered flier.
wood_stork: Wetland dwellers, wood storks wade through swamps and marshes from Florida and the Gulf coast down through Mexico, the Caribbean, and South America. They mostly eat fish, and they hunt by feel, sweeping their partly open bills through the water until they touch prey. Adults weigh about 2.5 kilograms, and the species is still alive and widespread.
stitchbird: The stitchbird, known in Māori as hihi, is a small forest bird found only in New Zealand. It feeds mainly on nectar and weighs about 0.04 kilograms as an adult. Although its numbers have been low, it is still alive today and is a protected species.
burrowing_owl: Burrowing owls live across the Great Plains, western North America, Mexico, the Pampas and Gran Chaco, and in Florida and the Gulf region. They make their homes in plains, grasslands, and deserts, where they hunt insects during the day. An adult weighs about 0.15 kg, and these small owls are often seen walking on the ground rather than flying far.
edible_nest_swiftlet: The edible-nest swiftlet lives in Sundaland and Indochina, nesting in caves and along coastlines. It feeds on insects and weighs about 15 grams as an adult. Known for its ability to echolocate, it navigates dark cave interiors on the wing, and its nests are harvested to make bird's nest soup.
harpy_eagle: The harpy eagle makes its home in the jungles of Central America and the Amazon basin, where it hunts during the daytime and often perches high in the trees. Adults weigh around 7.5 kg, and this bird preys on sloths and monkeys. It is still alive today and is legally protected.
giant_isopod: Deep in the western Atlantic, the giant isopod roams the seafloor around the Caribbean, Florida, and the Gulf. This scavenger feeds on whatever falls from above, and it can go years without eating. An adult may weigh about 1.7 kilograms, and its armored shell protects it in the dark deep sea.
grey_triggerfish: Found across the North and South Atlantic, the Mediterranean, the Caribbean, and tropical western Atlantic waters, this fish favors reefs and coastal zones. It feeds on other animals and can reach about 6 kg as an adult. Its flesh is edible, and it remains widespread today.
red_legged_partridge: The red-legged partridge makes its home across Atlantic Europe and the Mediterranean, where it roams open plains and rugged badlands. It feeds mainly on plants and weighs about half a kilogram as an adult. Its plumage is prized, and the bird is also hunted, though it remains widespread and very much alive today.
atlantic_croaker: The Atlantic croaker is a fish that lives along the coast of eastern North America, from the Gulf of Mexico up to the Atlantic shores. It eats a mix of foods, both plants and animals, and an adult typically weighs about 1 kilogram. Its name comes from the drumming sounds it makes, produced by muscles that vibrate its swim bladder, and it remains common today.
shortbill_spearfish: The shortbill spearfish is found in the Indian Ocean, the northern and southern Pacific, and tropical seas. It lives in warm ocean waters and feeds on other animals. Adults typically weigh around 52 kg, and this species is still alive today. Its long, spear-shaped bill sets it apart as a fast swimmer.
red_vented_bulbul: The red-whiskered bulbul is a small songbird found across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, where it lives in forest settings. It feeds mainly on fruit and weighs about 0.027 kilograms as an adult. Still living and widespread, it is known for its feathers and its flight.
black_headed_gull: Despite the name, the black-headed gull has a chocolate-brown hood during the breeding season rather than a true black one. It ranges across Europe, the Palearctic, Africa, and the Indian subcontinent, favoring wetlands and coastlines. These gulls nest in colonies, and they eat a wide mix of foods while weighing around 0.28 kilograms as adults.
greater_koa_finch: The greater koa finch once lived in the forests of Hawaii, where it fed on plant material. Adults weighed about 0.03 kg. The species was last recorded in 1896 AD, and it is now extinct.
little_spotted_kiwi: Hunting through the forests of New Zealand after dark, the little spotted kiwi relies on its keen sense of smell to find insects in the leaf litter. This flightless bird weighs about 1.2 kilograms as an adult and remains active only at night. Though it is still alive today, it is a protected species.
common_quail: The common quail is a small ground bird weighing about 0.1 kilograms as an adult. It lives in grasslands across Europe, the Mediterranean, Africa, the Indian subcontinent, and the eastern steppe. Its diet is omnivorous, and it is a migratory species that is also hunted by people.
fangtooth: The common fangtooth lives across the North Atlantic, South Atlantic, North Pacific, South Pacific, and Indian Oceans, mostly in the deep sea. It is a carnivore that swims through dark waters, using its huge teeth to catch prey. Adults weigh about 0.1 kg, and the species is still alive today.
blue_and_yellow_macaw: Found across Central America and the Amazon basin, this bird roams jungles and swampy lowlands. It feeds on fruit and weighs about 1.1 kilograms as an adult. Living in flocks and spending much of its time in trees, it is still widely present in the wild and flies with ease between its perches.
brown_trout: The brown trout, known scientifically as Salmo trutta, lives across Europe, the British Isles, Scandinavia, the northern African coast, and southwestern Asia. It inhabits rivers, lakes, and mountain streams, and it is a carnivore. Adults can reach about 4 kg, and the species remains widespread today.
andean_condor: The Andean condor ranges along the Andes and into Patagonia and the Pampas, moving between mountain slopes and coastal areas. It is a scavenger that feeds on carrion, and adults can weigh around 12 kg. Active during the day, this bird soars on its very broad wings and is legally protected, and it remains alive today.
sunbird_malachite: Weighing about 15 grams as an adult, the malachite sunbird lives in southern Africa and the East African savanna. It moves between mountain and savanna habitats and feeds mainly on nectar. Its flight and feathers are among the notable features of this species, which is still living in the wild.
glossy_ibis: The glossy ibis is a wading bird found across much of the world, where it lives in wetlands. It eats a mix of foods and an adult weighs about 0.7 kg. This species is still alive and its feathers are notable, and it is also a migratory bird.
long_eared_owl: The long-eared owl lives across the Palearctic and Nearctic regions, where it hunts in both forests and open plains. It is a carnivore that weighs about 0.28 kg as an adult, and it is active at night. Its feathers and silent, gliding flight help it move unseen through its range.
seychelles_parakeet: The Seychelles parakeet once lived in the forests of the Seychelles islands, a small group of islands in the Indian Ocean. Its diet consisted of fruit, and an adult weighed about 0.15 kg. Coconut farmers regarded it as a pest, and it was last recorded in 1906.
rodrigues_owl: The Rodrigues owl once lived in forests on the island of Rodrigues, a small piece of land in the Indian Ocean. It was a nocturnal bird that hunted meat and weighed about 0.4 kg as an adult. Scientists know it today mainly from its bones, since the species had vanished by around 1700 AD.
armoured_catfish: The sailfin armoured catfish lives in rivers of the Amazon basin, where it grazes mainly on plant matter. Adults typically reach about 1 kg. Its body is covered in bony plates that serve as armour, and it moves steadily through the water. People in some regions eat it, and the species is still alive and widespread.
anhinga: The anhinga is a waterbird that roams the swamps and rivers of eastern North America, Florida and the Gulf coast, the Caribbean, and the Amazon basin. Adults weigh about 1.2 kilograms. It swims low in the water, and it spears fish with its long, sharp bill, feeding mainly on fish.
bonin_thrush: The Bonin thrush lived on a single island, its range recorded across a small area of 26.5 to 27.8 by 142 to 142.5. It fed on insects and weighed about 0.07 kg as an adult. Only four specimens are known, all preserved as feathers, and the species was declared extinct in 1828 AD.
eurasian_hobby: The Eurasian hobby is a small falcon found across the Palearctic and in Africa south of the Sahara. It lives in forests and plains, and it catches insects while flying during the day. Adults weigh about 0.25 kg, and the species migrates between its breeding and wintering grounds.
dobsonfly_eastern: Found along rivers across eastern North America, the eastern dobsonfly is a carnivore that weighs about 5 grams as an adult. Males carry long, oversized jaws that look dangerous but are used mainly in contests and courtship. Its aquatic larva, known as the hellgrammite, lives in the water before it emerges to fly.
tridacna_gigas_sp: The giant clam is a reef dweller found across the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Indian Ocean, and Polynesia. Adults can reach about 200 kilograms, and the heavy shell is shaped to stay put on the reef throughout its life. It feeds through filter feeding and hosts symbiotic algae that live within its tissues. Still living, it is a protected species.
laughing_kookaburra: The laughing kookaburra is a large kingfisher found across Australia, where it lives in forests and open plains. Adults weigh about 0.35 kg, and their diet is carnivorous. Known for its loud laughing call, this bird also hunts flies and even snakes, and it often moves about in small family groups.
garfish: Slender and needle-jawed, this coastal fish ranges from the Atlantic shores of Europe through the Mediterranean, Baltic, and North Seas, and into the Black and Caspian seas. It hunts smaller fish and other prey near the surface, and adults typically weigh about one kilogram. It is still widespread and is good to eat, though its bones have a green tint that surprises many first-time cooks.
goliath_birdeater: The Goliath birdeater is among the heaviest spiders known, with adults reaching about 0.17 kg. It lives in jungle across the Amazon and Orinoco basins, where it spends its days in burrows. This carnivore is venomous and defends itself by flicking urticating hairs from its abdomen.
south_island_kokako: The South Island kokako, known to science as Callaeas cinereus, once lived in the forests of New Zealand. Adults weighed about 0.23 kg and were wattled birds with feathers that let them move through the trees, though they could also fly. Their diet was omnivorous, and the species was declared extinct in 2007 AD.
green_winged_macaw: The green-winged macaw roams the jungles of the Amazon basin, where it moves through the treetops and spends most of its life in the canopy. Adults weigh about 1.2 kilograms. Its diet is made up of fruit, and it gathers in herds and flies between feeding areas. It is still alive in the wild today.
king_vulture: The king vulture lives in the forests and jungles of Mexico, Central America, and the Amazon basin. It is a scavenger that feeds mainly on carrion, and adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms. Active during the day, this bird is still living in the wild today.
australian_trumpet: The Australian trumpet is a large sea snail that lives along coastlines in the Great Barrier Reef, Australia, and the Wallacea and New Guinea region. It is a carnivore, and adults can reach a mass of 18 kg. Its shell is notable because it belongs to the largest living gastropod, and the species remains alive today.
pacu_catfish: The jaú is a large catfish that lives in rivers across the Amazon basin. Adults can reach about 100 kilograms, making them among the heftiest freshwater fish in the region. Hunting for food, they are carnivores, and they swim powerfully through the river waters where they remain widespread today.
unicornfish: The bluespine unicornfish roams reefs across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, Polynesia, and Hawaii. It grazes mainly on plants and grows to about 2 kg as an adult. This species is still thriving in the wild, and people regard its flesh as good to eat.
giant_petaltail: Giant petaltails are dragonflies that live in the Pacific Northwest, where they spend much of their time in wetland habitats. Adults weigh about one gram, and they hunt other insects while on the wing. As a predator, the species still thrives today.
sea_robin: The northern sea robin lives along the coasts of eastern North America, where it remains common and widespread. Weighing about one kilogram as an adult, it is a meat eater that hunts on the seabed. This fish swims through open water but also walks along the ocean floor on specialized fin rays.
kakapo: The kakapo is a flightless, nocturnal parrot that lives in New Zealand's forests and mountains. Adults weigh about 2.5 kg, making it the heaviest parrot in the world. It feeds on plants and gathers at lek sites to display, and it is still alive today under legal protection.
dung_beetle_sacred: Rolling dung balls across sand, the sacred scarab lives in the Nile valley, the Mediterranean region, and the Sahara. It feeds on scavenged material and weighs only about three grams as an adult. Ancient Egyptians revered this beetle, and it is known to navigate by the stars as it travels.
humboldt_penguin: Along the coasts of Chile and Peru, Humboldt penguins nest in burrows dug into guano-rich ground, where the sea birds' droppings have built up over time. These stocky birds weigh about 4.5 kg as adults and feed on fish. Their dense feathers and strong swimming keep them active in the cold Pacific waters.
ancient_murrelet: The ancient murrelet is a small seabird found across the northern Pacific Ocean, breeding along the coasts of Japan, Korea, and the Pacific Northwest. It weighs about 0.2 kg as an adult and feeds on fish. This bird can swim and fly, and it remains alive today.
saker_falcon: The saker falcon hunts across open grasslands and plains, ranging from the eastern steppes of Mongolia and Kazakhstan through Iran, Anatolia, Arabia, and parts of Africa. It is a diurnal bird of prey that feeds on other animals and weighs about 1.1 kilograms as an adult. Many populations migrate with the seasons, and the falcon has long been prized in falconry.
stonefly_giant: Found in rivers across western North America and the Pacific Northwest, the giant stonefly is still widespread today. Adults weigh about two grams and feed on plant material. Anglers often use this insect as bait in fly fishing, and its presence is a sign that the water is clean.
dace: Common dace are small freshwater fish that live in rivers across Europe, the British Isles, and northern Asia. They feed mainly on insects and can grow to about 0.2 kg as adults. Still widespread today, these swimmers move steadily through flowing water.
booted_eagle: The booted eagle is a small, still-living raptor that ranges across the Mediterranean, the eastern steppe, and sub-Saharan Africa. It favors forested country and hunts by day, feeding on other animals. Adults weigh about 0.9 kg, and the species is migratory, flying between its breeding and wintering grounds.
bohemian_waxwing: The Bohemian waxwing is a songbird that ranges across Scandinavia, the Siberian taiga, the Canadian Shield, and Alaska and the Yukon. It favors taiga habitat and lives mostly on fruit. Adults weigh about 0.055 kilograms, and the species is still living and wanders nomadically in search of food.
golden_eagle: Found across the Palearctic, Nearctic, and the Sahara, golden eagles favor mountains, forests, and open plains. These carnivores hunt by day, soaring on broad wings and diving at prey, and northern populations migrate with the seasons. Adults weigh about 4.5 kg, and the species has long been valued in falconry and is still hunted in some regions.
eastern_meadowlark: Found across eastern North America and into Mexico, the eastern meadowlark makes its home in grassland. It eats both plants and animals, and an adult weighs about 0.1 kg. This species is still living, and it is known for its feathers and its flight.
paua: Pāua, also called black foot abalone, is a marine snail found along the coasts of New Zealand. It grazes on seaweed and other plants, and a full-grown adult weighs about 0.8 kilograms. Its shell has an iridescent inner lining, and its flesh is prized as an edible delicacy, yet the species is still thriving today.
great_horned_owl: Found across the Nearctic and Neotropics, the great horned owl makes its home in forests, deserts, and plains alike. This nocturnal hunter feeds on other animals and weighs about 1.4 kg as an adult. Its feathers allow near silent flight, and the species remains widespread today.
common_shrimp: The brown shrimp is found along the Baltic and North Sea, across Atlantic Europe, and in the Mediterranean. It lives on the coast and eats both plants and animals. An adult weighs about 0.01 kg, and it is still widespread today. People eat it, and it has a shell.
haasts_eagle: Once the largest eagle known, this bird ranged across New Zealand through forests, mountains, and grasslands. Adults weighed about 14 kg and spread wings roughly 3 m wide, and they hunted by day. Their prey included the moa, and the species died out around 1400 AD.
pink_headed_duck: A pink head gave this duck its name, and its feathers and rarity marked it out across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina. It lived in swamps and lakes, ate a mix of plant and animal food, and weighed about 0.9 kg as an adult. The species is recorded as extinct from 1949 AD.
major_mitchells_cockatoo: Major Mitchell's cockatoo, known scientifically as Lophocroa leadbeateri, lives across Australia in desert and plain country. Adults weigh about 0.4 kg, and the species is still thriving in the wild. Its diet is omnivorous, and it is often seen moving about in herds across open ground.
bat_ray: The bat ray is a still-living animal found along the western coast of North America and across the northern Pacific Ocean. It swims near the shore, and adults can reach a mass of about 90 kilograms. Its diet is carnivorous, and it carries a mild sting that it uses if threatened.
blue_pike: The blue pike was a freshwater fish that lived in lakes in the 41 to 45 north and 76 to 83 west range, with Lake Erie and Lake Ontario among its known homes. It was a carnivore that swam through open water and grew to about 1.5 kilograms as an adult. People prized it as a good food fish, but overfishing and pollution drove it to extinction, with the last recorded example in 1983.
olomao: The olomao once flitted through forest on Molokai, a Hawaiian island, where it fed mainly on fruit. Adults weighed about 0.05 kilograms, roughly the mass of a small handful of seeds. This songbird was last recorded in 1988, and it is now considered extinct.
bigeye_trevally: The bigeye trevally is a still-thriving fish found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, Polynesia, Hawaii, and the Red Sea. It prefers reefs and coastal waters, where it hunts other creatures as a carnivore. Adults can reach about 18 kg, and they often travel together in schools while swimming through the water.
greater_sage_grouse: Across the sagebrush plains and deserts of western North America and the Great Plains, this bird lives on a diet made mostly of plants. Adults weigh about 2.4 kilograms. Males gather at display grounds called leks, where they puff out their feathers in courtship, and the species is still alive and can be legally hunted.
longtail_tuna: The longtail tuna roams warm coastal waters and open ocean across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, and the Red Sea. It is a meat eater that hunts other fish and squid, and adults can weigh around 35 kg. This species is still thriving in the wild, and people catch it for food.
goliath_birdwing: The Goliath birdwing lives in the jungles of Wallacea and New Guinea, where it feeds on nectar as an adult. A full-grown individual weighs about 0.008 kg, and the species remains common enough to survive in the wild today. Because it is a protected species, collecting it is restricted in the regions where it occurs.
cockroach_madagascar: Found only in the forests of Madagascar, this wingless insect spends its nights foraging across the forest floor. Adults weigh about 0.02 kilograms and eat a varied diet of plant and animal matter. Their name comes from the loud hiss they produce by forcing air through openings in their body.
desert_blonde: Found across the southern United States and Mexico, the desert blonde tarantula makes its home in arid desert country. This carnivore feeds on other small animals and weighs about 0.06 kg as an adult. It is venomous and spends much of its life in a burrow, and it remains a living species today.
swainsons_hawk: The Swainson's hawk is a bird of open country, found across the Great Plains and western North America as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It hunts from the air during the day and feeds on other animals. An adult weighs about 0.9 kilograms. Its long migration between northern breeding grounds and southern wintering areas makes it a species that still thrives today.
lake_titicaca_orestias: The Lake Titicaca orestias, also called the imanto, once swam in the high waters of its namesake lake and nowhere else on Earth. It was a carnivore that reached about 1 kilogram as an adult. The species disappeared around 1950, after trout were introduced to the lake and outcompeted it.
fat_tailed_scorpion: Found across the Sahara, the North African coast, and Arabia, the fat-tailed scorpion makes its home in desert country. It hunts other creatures and weighs only about 0.01 kg as an adult. Its venom is deadly, and it is active at night.
moorish_idol: Found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, the Red Sea, Polynesia, and Hawaii, this reef dweller is easy to spot thanks to its bright coloring and long dorsal fin. It eats a mix of foods and typically weighs around 0.2 kg as an adult. It remains widespread and is not extinct.
snow_crab: Snow crabs inhabit cold waters across the Arctic Ocean, the North Atlantic, and the North Pacific, with populations reaching as far as Alaska and the Yukon. These carnivorous crustaceans can grow to about 2 kilograms, and they are still thriving today. Their hard shells and tasty meat have made them a prized catch.
grey_partridge: The grey partridge is a plump, ground-dwelling bird found across Europe and on the eastern steppe, including the Kazakh steppe. It favors open plains and grassland, where it feeds mainly on plant matter. An adult weighs about 0.4 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today. Its feathers and its status as a game bird have long tied it to people, and it often gathers in coveys.
galapagos_dove: The Galapagos dove lives on the Galapagos Islands, where it moves between island scrub and dry desert country. Its diet is made up of plants, and a full-grown bird weighs about 0.1 kilograms. Its feathers are soft and muted, and it is often tame enough to approach closely, so visitors frequently see it up close.
tigerfish_common: The tigerfish, Hydrocynus vittatus, lives in rivers and lakes across southern Africa and the Sahel. Adults can reach about 10 kg, and they hunt other fish with a set of razor-sharp teeth. Anglers pursue them as a prized catch, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
purple_swamphen: The purple swamphen is a wetland bird found across the Mediterranean, Africa, Indomalaya, Australia, and New Zealand. It eats both plants and animals, and an adult weighs about 0.9 kg. Its feathers are prized, and the species is still hunted in some areas, though it remains alive and widespread.
elf_owl: Hiding in desert saguaro cacti across the southwestern United States and Mexico, this tiny owl hunts insects after dark. At roughly 0.04 kilograms, it is the smallest owl in the world, and it flies quietly through the night in search of its prey. Its species is still thriving today.
bluefin_notothen: Deep in the frigid waters around Antarctica and the subantarctic islands, this fish lives in the cold, dark ocean depths. As a carnivore, it hunts other creatures on the seafloor and in the water column. Adults can reach a mass of about 135 kg, and its blood contains antifreeze that keeps it from freezing. It remains widespread today and is valued as a food fish.
tropical_gar: The tropical gar is a freshwater fish still found today across southern Mexico and parts of Central America. It lives in rivers, lakes, and swamps, where it hunts other animals. Adults can reach about 10 kg, and their body is covered in tough scale armour. People in the region also eat it.
codling_moth: The codling moth is a small pest that lives in Europe and in Iran and Anatolia, where it inhabits forest areas. Adults weigh only about 0.00005 kg and feed on nectar as they fly. It remains widespread today and is known as a pest of apple trees.
rhinoceros_beetle: The European rhinoceros beetle lives across Europe and the Mediterranean, where it makes its home in forests. Its diet is frugivorous, so it feeds on fruit. An adult weighs about 0.008 kg, and it is still widespread today. Its horn and its ability to fly help set it apart from many other beetles.
comb_jelly: Along the coasts of eastern North America, including Florida and the Gulf, the sea walnut drifts through the water as a small carnivore. An adult weighs about 0.05 kilograms, and the animal is still very much alive today. Glowing with bioluminescence, it is not a true jellyfish, despite the way it might look to a casual observer.
walking_stick_northern: Twig-like and nearly motionless, the northern walkingstick blends into the forests of eastern North America. It feeds on plant matter, and an adult weighs about 0.002 kg, roughly the mass of a small paperclip. Its camouflage is its main defense, and the species is still thriving today.
yellow_warbler: The yellow warbler is a small bird that weighs about 0.01 kilograms as an adult. It lives across the Nearctic, Mexico, Central America, and the Amazon basin, and it makes its home in forests. Its diet consists of insects, and it is a migratory species that still thrives today.
lined_seahorse: Along the coasts of eastern North America, the Caribbean, and around Florida and the Gulf, the lined seahorse drifts among shallow seagrass and reef edges. This carnivore weighs only about 0.03 kg as an adult. It swims upright and, remarkably, the male is the one who carries developing young in a pouch.
stellers_eider: Found along Arctic and North Pacific coasts, across Beringia and northern Asia, this diving duck moves between coastal waters and tundra habitats. Adults weigh about 0.8 kilograms, and the species eats a mix of plant and animal food. It is migratory and still thrives in the wild, with no sign of extinction.
shortfin_eel: The shortfin eel makes its home in rivers and lakes across Australia, New Zealand, and Tasmania. It feeds on other animals and can reach an adult mass of about 3 kg. This species is still alive and is valued as an edible fish.
candiru: A small catfish of the Amazon basin, the candiru lives in rivers and is still widespread today. It is no larger than a fingernail clipping at adulthood, weighing roughly 0.01 kg. This fish is a parasite that feeds on blood, and it survives by swimming through the waters of its home rivers in search of a host.
himalayan_griffon: The Himalayan griffon is a large vulture found across the Himalaya and Tibet, where it makes its home in mountain country. It is a scavenger that feeds on carrion and is active during the day, soaring on the air currents above the peaks. Adults weigh around 9 kilograms, and the species remains alive and well today.
bowfin: The bowfin ranges across eastern North America, from the Canadian Shield down through Florida and the Gulf states. It favors swamps, lakes, and other wetlands, where it hunts other fish and prey in ambush. Adults commonly reach about 4 kg, and this survivor is still living today as a classic example of a living fossil, able to gulp air at the surface.
xerces_blue: The Xerces blue was a small butterfly that lived in the San Francisco Bay Area, roughly between latitudes 37.5 and 38 and longitudes -122.6 and -122.3. It fed on nectar, weighed about 0.0001 kg as an adult, and made its home on coastal grassland and sand dunes. Development of the city is what drove it to extinction, and the last recorded individuals were lost by 1943.
common_octopus: The common octopus lives in the Mediterranean, along the Atlantic coast of Europe, in tropical seas, and in the Caribbean, Indian Ocean, Japan and Korea. It favors reefs and coastal waters, where it hunts meat-eating prey. Adults can reach about 10 kilograms, and this species is still thriving in the wild. It can swim, blend into its surroundings, and release clouds of ink to escape danger.
chatham_kaka: The Chatham Island kaka lived in the forests of the Chatham Islands, a remote group east of New Zealand, where it climbed through the trees rather than spending time on the ground. Adults weighed about half a kilogram, and the bird ate a varied diet of both plant and animal foods. This species is recorded as extinct from the year 1600 AD.
orchid_mantis: The orchid mantis lives in the jungles of Sundaland and Indochina, where it hunts insects and other small prey. An adult weighs only about two grams, so it is light enough to drift among flowers without disturbing them. Its body mimics the petals of an orchid, and it is still living in the wild today.
moa_nalo_kauai: The Kauai moa-nalo was a flightless, browsing duck that lived in the forests of Kauai, one of the islands in the Hawaiian chain. Adults weighed about 7 kg, and the bird had a turtle-like jaw suited to cropping plants. It went extinct around 1000 AD, after Polynesians arrived and ate it.
chain_pickerel: The chain pickerel lives across eastern North America and down through Florida and the Gulf region, where it haunts lakes and swamps. It is a meat eater that waits in ambush for its prey. Adults typically reach about 2 kilograms, and the fish is considered edible. It remains widespread and is not extinct.
bean_goose: The taiga bean goose is a plant-eating bird that moves between taiga forests and wetlands. Adults weigh about 3 kg. It lives across Scandinavia, Siberia, Europe, and as far as Japan and Korea. These migratory geese travel in herds and are still common, though hunters pursue them.
giant_trevally: The giant trevally is still widespread, living across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Great Barrier Reef, Polynesia, Hawaii, the Red Sea, and the coasts of Africa south of the Sahara. It favors warm reefs and coastal waters, where it hunts other fish and occasionally seabirds. Adults can reach about 80 kg, and people fish for it as a food source.
helmeted_guineafowl: Native to Africa south of the Sahara and across the Sahel, the helmeted guineafowl roams savanna and grassland in noisy flocks. Adults weigh about 1.4 kg and eat a mix of plant and animal foods. Its speckled feathers have long made it a prized game bird, and it has also been domesticated for its eggs.
apapane: The apapane is a small red honeycreeper that lives only in the forests and mountains of Hawaii. It feeds mainly on nectar and weighs about 14 grams as an adult. Though its feathers are bright, the bird is still alive and flies across the islands in search of flowers.
hammerhead_great: The great hammerhead is a shark of warm tropical seas, found across the Indian Ocean, the Coral Triangle, the Caribbean, and parts of the North and South Atlantic. It moves along reefs and coastlines, where it hunts as an apex predator and feeds heavily on rays. Adults can reach about 450 kilograms, and the species is still living in the wild.
atlantic_cod: The Atlantic cod ranges across the cold northern Atlantic, from the Baltic and North Sea to Iceland, Greenland, and the eastern coast of North America. It lives in cold ocean waters and along coastlines, where it feeds on other animals. Adults can reach about 25 kilograms, and the species is still thriving, though it is hunted and eaten widely, often after being salted.
twig_snake: The twig snake lives in East Africa and southern parts of the continent, moving through both savanna and forest. It is a carnivore, and adults weigh about 0.2 kilograms. Its body is covered in scales, and it spends much of its life in trees, where its coloring blends with the branches. This snake is venomous and remains widespread today.
hutia_cuban: Desmarest's hutia is a rodent found across the Caribbean, where it lives in both forest and wetland settings. An adult typically weighs about 7 kilograms, making it a sizable member of its family. It feeds on plants and is active at night, and it remains alive today, though it is hunted by people.
asteroceras: Asteroceras obtusum is a fossil ammonite that lived roughly 200 to 195 million years ago during the Jurassic period. Its shell fossils are found in limestone of the Blue Lias formation in the British Isles, where collectors know it as the Lyme Regis star ammonite. Adults are thought to have weighed about 0.5 kg, and the animal was a carnivore.
beaver_giant: The giant beaver, Castoroides ohioensis, roamed wetlands, lakes, and rivers across eastern North America, the Great Plains, the Canadian Shield, and Alaska and Yukon. Adults reached about 100 kg, and this semi-aquatic herbivore swam well through the waters it called home. It died out around 8000 BC, one of the many megafauna species lost at the close of the Ice Age.
kimberley_rock_monitor: The black-headed monitor makes its home across Australia, moving through both forest and badlands. Its diet is carnivorous, and an adult typically weighs about 1 kg. Living lizards like this one remain common, and their scaly bodies and tree-climbing habits help them get around the canopy.
placerias: Placerias was a fossil dicynodont that lived during the Triassic, roughly 225 to 215 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Chinle Formation in the southern United States. Adults weighed about 1000 kilograms, and this herbivore looked much like a hippopotamus.
clarks_nutcracker: Clark's nutcracker is a bird of the western and northwestern mountains of North America, where it lives among pine forests. It weighs about 0.12 kilograms as an adult and feeds mainly on plant material, especially pine seeds. Known for its sharp intelligence, this species hoards seeds in caches across the landscape and remembers where many of them are hidden.
chinese_pit_viper: The Chinese moccasin is a venomous pit viper found in the lowlands of China, where it lives in both forest and mountain settings. It is a carnivore, and adults typically weigh around 2 kg. Its body is covered in scales, and it has heat-sensing pit organs along its face along with a distinctive horn-like scale on its nose.
coastal_giant_salamander: Found across the Pacific Northwest, this amphibian lives in forests and along rivers, where it hunts other animals as a carnivore. Active mainly at night, it is a strong swimmer that can move through streams with ease. Adults weigh about 0.15 kilograms, and it holds the title of largest terrestrial salamander. It remains alive and widespread today.
whites_tree_frog: Ranoidea caerulea is an arboreal amphibian found across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea. It lives in forests, savannas, and wetlands, feeding on insects. Adults weigh around 0.1 kg, and the species remains common and alive today.
pancake_tortoise: The Pancake Tortoise is a small reptile of the East African savanna, where it lives in badlands and mountain country. Adults weigh about half a kilogram and feed on herbs. Its most unusual feature is a flexible, flattened shell, which lets it squeeze deep into rock crevices to escape predators.
lace_monitor: The lace monitor is a large lizard found across Australia, where it lives in forests and savannas. It is carnivorous and also scavenges, and adults can weigh around 8 kg. Its scales and a strongly tree-climbing habit make it easy to recognize, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
philippine_crocodile: The Philippine crocodile is a small crocodile that lives in swamps, rivers, lakes, and on islands in the Philippines, where it still survives in the wild. Adults typically weigh about 40 kilograms, and their diet consists of meat from other animals. Because the species is protected, efforts continue to safeguard the wetlands where these reptiles swim and hunt.
desert_tortoise: The Mojave Desert tortoise is a herbivore that roams the deserts and badlands of western North America and northern Mexico. Adults typically weigh about 5 kilograms and carry a domed shell that protects them from predators. They dig burrows to escape the heat and cold, and because their populations are protected by law, they still survive in the wild today.
sidewinder: Sidewinders live in the deserts of western North America and Mexico, where they are still common. Each adult weighs about 0.4 kilograms, and it hunts small animals as a carnivore. This venomous rattlesnake has a pair of horn-like scales above its eyes and moves across loose sand by sidewinding.
brookesia_micra: Few reptiles are as small as the Tiny Leaf Chameleon, which weighs roughly a gram as an adult. This species lives in the forests and island habitats of Madagascar, where it hunts insects and blends into the leaf litter on the forest floor. Its body is no larger than a fingernail scale, and it remains alive today.
dimorphodon: A large-headed flying reptile from the Jurassic, Dimorphodon lived roughly 195 to 190 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Blue Lias formation in the British Isles, with Lyme Regis among the notable sites. Adults weighed about 3 kilograms, and the animal was carnivorous.
neovenator: A large carnivorous theropod that lived roughly 130 to 125 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from the Wessex Formation, a sandstone unit in the British Isles, and it is known from the Isle of Wight. Adults are estimated to have weighed about 1000 kilograms, making it a heavy predator of its time.
harp_seal: Harp seals live in the North Atlantic and the Arctic Ocean, with populations around Iceland and Greenland. They prefer icy, cold waters and travel in herds as they migrate between seasonal areas. Adults can weigh around 135 kg, and their diet consists of meat from other sea creatures. Their newborn pups have distinctive white coats.
new_zealand_sea_lion: The New Zealand sea lion is still alive and lives around New Zealand and the subantarctic islands. It makes its home along coasts and on islands, where it feeds on meat from the sea. Adult males can weigh as much as 320 kilograms, and the animals gather in herds while relying on a thick layer of blubber to stay warm.
japanese_serow: The Japanese serow is a still-living animal that roams forests and mountain slopes in the areas its range covers. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 40 kilograms. Its features include a horn, a thick coat of fur, and a presence on islands.
pangolin_chinese: The Chinese pangolin is a nocturnal mammal found in the lowlands of China, Indochina, and the Himalaya and Tibet. It roams forests and grasslands, feeding on insects, and it digs burrows for shelter. Adults weigh about 5 kg, and when threatened it rolls into a ball, protected by its overlapping scales.
carpet_python: Carpet pythons are found across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea, where they live in forests, savannas, and coastal areas. These carnivorous snakes can reach about 8 kg as adults. They are nocturnal and spend much of their time in trees, and their scaled bodies help them move through that habitat.
marsh_mongoose: Found across Africa south of the Sahara, the marsh mongoose makes its home in wetlands, along rivers, and in swamps. Adults weigh about 3.5 kg, and this carnivore is active at night. Its dense fur helps it move through the water, where it swims with ease while hunting.
aldabra_tortoise: The Aldabra Giant Tortoise roams islands, grasslands, and coastlines across a small region of the western Indian Ocean. Adults can reach about 150 kg, and they feed mainly on plants and grasses. These tortoises are active during the day, can swim when needed, and are known for their very long lifespans.
cape_fox: The Cape fox lives across southern Africa, roaming both desert and grassland landscapes. An omnivore, it eats whatever food it can find, and an adult typically weighs about 3.2 kilograms. Active at night, it rests in burrows and is known for its thick fur.
texas_tortoise: The Texas tortoise is a small herbivore found across the southern United States and northern Mexico. It makes its home in deserts and grasslands, where it feeds on plants and digs burrows for shelter. An adult weighs about 1 kilogram, and this species remains alive and present in the wild today.
gargantuavis: Gargantuavis is known only from fossils, dating to between 70 and 66 million years ago in the Cretaceous period. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Grès à Reptiles formation in Europe. This giant flightless bird weighed about 150 kilograms as an adult and fed on plants.
pneumodesmus: Pneumodesmus newmani was a tiny millipede that lived roughly 428 to 425 million years ago during the Silurian period. Its fossils were preserved in sandstone of the Cowie Formation in the British Isles. Adults weighed only about one gram, and it is the oldest known air-breathing land animal.
dolphin_irrawaddy: Found in rivers, coastal waters, and wetlands across Indochina, Sundaland, and the Indian subcontinent, the Irrawaddy dolphin is a carnivore that often gathers in small pods. Adults can weigh around 130 kilograms. Despite its wide range, this toothed species still survives today, and it is protected in many areas where it lives near estuaries.
gymnure_greater: The moonrat roams the jungles of Sundaland and Indochina, where it hunts insects after dark. An adult weighs about 1 kilogram, making it a sturdy little mammal of the forest floor. Active only at night, it is known for a strong, unpleasant smell, and it remains widespread and alive today.
hedgehog_four_toed: Still widespread today, the four-toed hedgehog roams the Sahel, the East African savanna, and the western African coast. It prefers open grassland and savanna, where it hunts insects after dark. An adult weighs about half a kilogram, and its coat of spines helps protect it from predators. This species can also be kept as a pet.
greater_kudu: The greater kudu is a large antelope found across Southern Africa and the East African savanna. Adults weigh about 220 kilograms and graze mainly on herbs. Males carry long, spiral horns that make them a prized target for hunters, and the species survives today in savanna and badland habitats.
bearded_pig: The bearded pig roams the jungles, forests, and coastal areas of Sundaland, where it lives in herds. Adults can reach about 120 kilograms, and they eat a varied diet of both plants and animals. Males have prominent tusks, and the species still thrives, though it is hunted and some herds travel long distances in search of food.
jambato_toad: The Jambato Toad lived in the Andes, where it made its home in mountain grasslands. It fed on insects and weighed only about five grams as an adult. This amphibian was declared extinct in 1988, likely due to the chytrid fungus, but a small surviving population was rediscovered in 2016.
hutia_giant_puerto_rico: The Puerto Rican giant hutia was a rodent that lived in forests on the island of Puerto Rico, in the Caribbean region between about 17.9 and 18.6 degrees north. Adults weighed roughly 25 kilograms and fed on plants. This large island rodent has been extinct since around 1500 AD.
black_softshell: The black softshell turtle lives in lakes and rivers across the Indian subcontinent, where it eats both plants and animals. Adults can reach about 20 kg, and it is still living in the wild. Its flat, leathery shell helps it glide through the water, and it is found in temple ponds where it is protected.
dolphin_boto: The Amazon river dolphin lives in the Amazon and Orinoco river systems, moving through both open rivers and flooded wetlands. This freshwater toothed whale is a carnivore that can grow to about 150 kg. Its pink coloring and unusually flexible neck let it swim and turn with ease, and it is still living today.
neotropical_otter: The Neotropical Otter is still living and can be found across Mexico and the wider Neotropics. It makes its home along rivers and in wetlands, where it hunts fish. Adults typically weigh around 8 kg, and their dense fur helps them stay warm while they swim.
midwife_toad: The common midwife toad lives across Atlantic Europe and the wider continent, in forests and on mountains. Adults weigh about 0.01 kg and feed on insects. The males are the ones that carry the eggs, wrapped around their legs, and this amphibian is still living in the wild.
snapping_turtle: The common snapping turtle makes its home across eastern North America, from the Canadian Shield down to Florida and the Gulf, and across the Great Plains. It favors rivers, lakes, and swamps, where it eats both plants and animals. Adults can reach about 14 kg, and this species is still widespread today. Its bite is strong, and it spends much of its time in freshwater.
pangolin_white_bellied: Armored in overlapping scales, the white-bellied pangolin makes its home in the jungles of the Congo basin and along the western African coast. Climbing trees after dark, it hunts insects and grows to roughly 2.5 kilograms. Although still alive in the wild, this nocturnal species is protected by law.
