red_footed_tortoise: The red-footed tortoise roams the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It favors both savanna and forest, and it is active during the day. Adults can reach about 8 kg, and they eat a varied diet that includes fallen fruit.
tokay_gecko: The Tokay gecko is a large, nocturnal lizard found across Indochina, Sundaland, and parts of South and Southeast Asia. It lives in jungle and forest, where it hunts insects and other small animals after dark. Adults weigh about 0.3 kg, and its loud, distinctive call gives it a name that echoes through the trees. Its scaly skin is tough, but it can bite hard if handled.
coelophysis: Coelophysis was a slender fossil theropod that lived during the Triassic, roughly 215 to 203 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Chinle Formation at Ghost Ranch in the southern United States. This carnivore weighed about 20 kilograms as an adult, and it is thought to have moved in packs.
arrau_turtle: The Giant South American River Turtle lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, where it moves between rivers and lakes. Adults can reach about 60 kg, and they feed mainly on plants. Their eggs are a favored food for people, and the species is still hunted, which has made it a concern for conservation.
cryptoclidus: Cryptoclidus was a long-necked marine reptile that swam the seas of the Jurassic period, roughly 165 to 160 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the mudstones of the Oxford Clay formation in the British Isles. It fed on fish and weighed around 900 kilograms as an adult, and it is sometimes called the Peterborough plesiosaur.
woma_python: The woma python makes its home across the deserts and grasslands of Australia, where it spends much of its time in burrows. This constrictor hunts other animals and feeds on carnivorous prey, and a full-grown adult typically weighs about 3 kg. Though its scales and secretive habits keep it hidden, the species is still alive and widespread in the wild.
porcupine_indian: Found across the Indian subcontinent, Iran, Anatolia, and Arabia, this porcupine lives in forest, desert, and grassland alike. An adult typically weighs about 13 kg. It feeds on herbs, sleeps in burrows during the day, and goes out at night. Its sharp quills are its main defense.
sloth_ground_mylodon: The Mylodon, known scientifically as Mylodon darwinii, once roamed the grasslands and forests of Patagonia, the Pampas, and the wider Southern Cone. This plant-eating giant weighed around 1000 kg as an adult and carried armoured skin. It disappeared around 8000 years before the present, and remains of its kind have been found in caves.
yellow_backed_duiker: The yellow-backed duiker is a forest antelope found across the Congo basin and along the western African coast. It lives in dense forest and jungle, feeding on herbs, and an adult typically weighs about 60 kg. Both males and females carry small horns, and the species is still alive today, though it is hunted by people.
burmese_python: Found across Indochina, Sundaland, and the lowlands of southern China, this snake makes its home in jungles, swamps, and forests. Adults can reach a mass of about 60 kilograms, and they hunt meat-eating prey by constriction. Their body is covered in scales, and they are strong swimmers that move easily through water.
sloth_antillean_neocnus: Neocnus comes was a small ground sloth that once lived in the forests of the Caribbean island of Hispaniola. It fed on plants and weighed around 10 kilograms as an adult. The species died out around the year 3000 BC, and it belongs to a group of island megafauna that vanished from the region.
common_genet: The common genet is a slender, spotted carnivore about the size of a small cat, weighing roughly 2 kilograms as an adult. It lives across Africa, Atlantic Europe, the Mediterranean, and Arabia, moving through savanna, forest, and badlands. Its dense spotted fur and climbing skill let it spend much of its time in trees, and it hunts mainly at night.
new_zealand_fur_seal: Gathering in dense herds along rocky shores, these seals live across New Zealand, Australia, and the subantarctic islands. Their thick fur keeps them warm in cold ocean waters, where they hunt fish and other prey. Adults can reach about 100 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
bat_long_nosed_lesser: Flying through desert nights, this migratory bat roosts in caves across Mexico, the southern United States, and Central America. It feeds on nectar and pollinates plants as it moves, making it an important nocturnal helper in its ecosystems. An adult weighs only about 25 grams, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
el_hierro_giant_lizard: The El Hierro giant lizard lives on a single Canary Island, El Hierro, where it moves through rocky badlands and other island habitats. It eats a mix of plant and animal food and grows to an adult mass of about 0.3 kg. Active during the day and covered in scales, this species is still alive today and receives legal protection.
gaboon_viper: The Gaboon viper ranges across the Congo basin, the West African coast, and the East African savanna, living in jungle and forest. This heavy-bodied snake relies on leaf-like camouflage to ambush prey, and it carries the longest fangs of any venomous snake. Adults can reach about 8 kg, and the species remains widespread today.
spotted_hyena: Spotted hyenas roam the savannas, grasslands, and deserts of Africa south of the Sahara and across the Sahel. Adults weigh about 60 kg, and they live in packs led by females, with dominance passed down through the matriline. These nocturnal carnivores hunt and scavenge at night, and they can crack bones with their powerful jaws.
nose_horned_viper: The nose-horned viper is a venomous snake found across the Mediterranean, Iran, Anatolia, and parts of Europe. It lives in mountains, badlands, and forests, and it hunts small prey. Adults typically weigh about half a kilogram, and the species remains widespread today, marked by the scaly horn on its snout.
bat_little_brown: The little brown bat is a small nocturnal flyer found across North America. It roosts in forests, caves, and wetlands, and it feeds on insects it catches in flight. Adults weigh only about 8 grams, and they gather in colonies and hibernate through the winter.
elasmosaurus: Elasmosaurus platyurus lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 80 to 74 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the chalk of the Sharon Springs (Pierre) formation on the Great Plains. This fossil taxon fed on fish and weighed about 2000 kg as an adult, and it carried a long neck built from 72 vertebrae.
south_american_sea_lion: Adult males of this species can reach about 300 kilograms and grow a thick mane around the neck and shoulders. Herds gather along cold coastal waters and rocky shores, where the animals rely on a layer of blubber to stay warm. They feed on fish, squid, and other marine prey, and they are still widely found today.
common_basilisk: The Common Basilisk lives in forests, jungles, and along rivers from southern Mexico through Central America to the Amazon basin. Adults weigh about 0.2 kilograms, and they eat both plants and animals. This lizard is active during the day, and it can run across the surface of water and swim when it needs to escape.
capybara_giant_neochoerus: Pinckney's capybara was a giant rodent that once roamed the wetlands and rivers of Florida and the Gulf coast of the southern United States. Adults reached about 100 kilograms, and they spent much of their time in the water while grazing on herbs. This semi-aquatic megafauna vanished around 9000 BC, leaving only fossil remains behind.
wallaby_red_necked: The red-necked wallaby is a hopping marsupial still found in the wild, living across Tasmania and parts of mainland Australia. It makes its home in forest and grassland, where it feeds on herbs. Adults weigh around 16 kg, and it is known to be a huntable species.
round_island_burrowing_boa: The Round Island Burrowing Boa lived in the Mascarene islands and used forest, caves, and island habitats alike. It was a carnivore that ate skinks and burrowed through the ground, and adults weighed about 0.5 kg. Introduced goats and rabbits damaged the vegetation it depended on, and the species was recorded as extinct in 1975.
nile_monitor: The Nile Monitor ranges across Africa south of the Sahara, along the Nile valley, and through the Sahel. It favors rivers, swamps, lakes, and savanna, and it is a strong swimmer that hunts meat and raids eggs. Adults can reach about 8 kg, and the species remains common in the wild.
javan_rhino: The Javan rhinoceros is a herbivore that browses on plants in jungle and forest country across Indochina, Sundaland, and the Indian subcontinent. A full-grown adult can weigh around 1500 kilograms. This species survives today and is protected, and its horn is a feature that has long made it a target for poachers.
marginated_tortoise: The marginated tortoise makes its home in the Mediterranean, moving between mountain slopes, grasslands, and forest. It feeds on herbs and is active during the day. Adults typically weigh around 5 kilograms, and their most recognizable feature is a flared rear shell. This species is still alive in the wild.
rusty_spotted_cat: The rusty-spotted cat lives across the Indian subcontinent, where it moves through both forest and grassland. Weighing around 1.4 kilograms as an adult, it is the smallest wild cat in the world. Its coat carries rusty spots, and it hunts mainly at night while feeding on other animals.
mountain_nyala: The mountain nyala roams the highlands of Ethiopia, moving between mountain slopes and forest edges. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 200 kilograms as an adult. Males carry horns and are sometimes hunted, but the species survives in the wild today.
jaguar: The jaguar, Panthera onca, ranges from the Amazon and Orinoco basins through Central America and Mexico to the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and the southern United States. It lives in jungle, swamp, forest, and river habitats, and it hunts meat in these places. Adults can reach about 90 kilograms, and this species is still alive and protected, with a powerful bite and a willingness to swim.
sand_gazelle: The sand gazelle, known scientifically as Gazella marica, makes its home across the deserts of Arabia. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 28 kg as an adult. Living in herds and carrying horns, this species is still alive today and is huntable.
cape_cobra: The Cape cobra lives across southern Africa, where it moves through deserts, savanna, and open grassland. Adults weigh about 1.2 kilograms, and the species remains common across its range. Its venom is potent, and when threatened it spreads a broad hood as a warning.
amur_tiger: The largest tiger subspecies roams the taiga, forests, and mountains of the Russian Far East, with a range that once reached as far as Japan and Korea. Adults can weigh around 230 kg, and they hunt meat exclusively. A thick winter coat helps them endure the cold, and they are strong swimmers. This living animal is protected.
galapagos_tortoise_floreana: Once found across the highlands and dry lowlands of Floreana in the Galapagos, this giant tortoise fed only on plants and could reach an adult weight of about 250 kilograms. Its domed shell and saddleback profile were distinctive features of the species. Whalers and pirates who visited the island took many of these tortoises, and the population was gone by 1850.
bat_free_tailed_mexican: The Brazilian free-tailed bat roams Mexico, the southern United States, Central America, and the wider Neotropics, roosting in caves and desert shelters. Weighing about 12 grams, it forms large colonies, migrates between seasons, and flies only at night to hunt insects. Its accumulated droppings, called guano, build up beneath these roosts over time.
glyptodont_holmesina: Holmesina was a armored pampathere that once roamed the southern United States, including Florida and the Gulf region. It lived in grasslands and forests, grazing on plants, and an adult could weigh about 200 kilograms. The species vanished around 9000 BC, and it belongs to the group of extinct megafauna that carried a shell.
broad_snouted_caiman: The broad-snouted caiman still lives across the Southern Cone, from the Pampas to the Gran Chaco. It makes its home in wetlands, rivers, and swamps, where it swims and hunts meat. Adults can reach about 60 kg, and the species remains common in the wild.
seychelles_giant_tortoise_arnoldi: Still living today, this giant tortoise roams islands and forests where it feeds on plants. Adults can reach about 120 kg. Its population was badly reduced in the 1800s when sailors harvested it for meat, a pressure that the species has survived despite its heavy shell.
whale_narwhal: Narwhals are toothed whales that live in cold Arctic waters, including the seas around Iceland, Greenland, and the wider Arctic. They eat other animals, and adults can reach about 1500 kg. Males are known for a long spiral tusk, and the animals travel together in groups called pods, which are still hunted by people.
jamaican_boa: The Jamaican boa is a still-living snake found only on the island of Jamaica, where it roams forests and caves. It is nocturnal and hunts other animals as its meat-based diet. A full-grown adult weighs about 3 kilograms, and its scales help it move through its island home. The species is legally protected.
barasingha: Known as the swamp deer, the barasingha roams the Indian subcontinent, moving between wetlands and grasslands. Herds graze on herbs and grow to about 180 kilograms as adults. Its branching antlers are a striking feature, and though it is still alive today, it is hunted in some areas.
onager: The Persian onager is a wild equid that still roams the deserts and plains of its range, where it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh about 250 kilograms, and the animals move together in herds. Hunting has been permitted for this species in some places, so it appears in the library as a huntable animal that remains alive today.
pika_american: Small and rounded, the American pika makes its home among the rocky slopes of western North American mountains. It feeds on plants and gathers grasses and herbs into haypiles to dry in the sun for later. Active during the daytime, this little animal weighs only about 0.15 kg as an adult, and it is still common today.
kawekaweau: Once found across the forests of New Zealand, this nocturnal gecko was the largest gecko ever known, with adults weighing about 0.2 kg. It ate other animals and lived in island woodlands, where it was revered by the Maori people. The species died out around 1870.
serval: The serval roams Africa south of the Sahara and across the Sahel, favoring savanna, wetlands, and grassland. This slender cat weighs about 13 kilograms as an adult and hunts mainly small prey. Its long legs and spotted coat help it stalk through tall grass, and it often leaps high into the air to pounce on birds and rodents.
black_headed_python: The black-headed python lives across Australia, where it moves through savanna and badlands. It is a nocturnal snake that hunts other snakes, and its diet is mainly carnivorous. Adults typically weigh around 4 kg, and the species remains alive and widespread in the wild today.
keel_billed_toucan: Found in the jungles of southern Mexico and Central America, this arboreal bird spends most of its time in the trees. Its diet is mainly fruit, and an adult weighs about 0.4 kg. Though it is a strong flier, it prefers moving through the forest canopy, and it remains widespread today.
boa_madagascar_tree: The Madagascar tree boa is a slim, arboreal snake found only on Madagascar, where it lives in forest and jungle canopy. It is a constrictor that hunts prey such as small mammals and birds, and an adult typically weighs around 2 kilograms. Its scales and coiled body help it grip branches as it moves through the trees. The species is still living in the wild today.
stegosaurus: Stegosaurus stenops lived during the Jurassic, roughly 155 to 150 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Morrison Formation in western North America. This plant-eating dinosaur weighed about 5000 kg as an adult. Its back bore a row of bony plates, and its tail ended in spiked projections known as the thagomizer.
hedgehog_west_european: Active only after dark, the West European hedgehog forages through forests and grasslands across Europe, the British Isles, and Scandinavia. Its diet consists of insects, and an adult typically weighs about 1 kilogram. Covered in protective spines, it curls into a ball when threatened and spends the cold months hibernating.
centrosaurus: Centrosaurus lived in what is now northwestern North America between 77 and 75 million years ago, during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation. Adults weighed around 2500 kilograms, and the plant-eater is known from bonebeds that suggest it moved in herds.
alpine_chough: High in mountain country, the alpine chough lives across the Alps, the Himalaya and Tibet, and parts of the Mediterranean. This omnivore weighs about a quarter kilogram as an adult, and it is still widespread today. It flies at high altitudes, and it is known for being clever.
small_asian_mongoose: The small Asian mongoose lives across Indochina, Sundaland, and the Himalaya and Tibet regions. It makes its home in grasslands and forests, where it hunts mainly during the day. An adult weighs about 0.7 kilograms, and this species is still widespread today.
sea_mink: The sea mink was a large relative of the modern mink that lived along coasts and islands in its range. It fed mainly on fish and was a capable swimmer, with a thick fur that made it a target. Adults weighed about 2.5 kg before the species was hunted out by the fur trade in 1894.
common_krait: The Common Krait is a venomous snake found across the Indian subcontinent, where it moves through wetlands, forests, and grasslands. It is mainly active at night and feeds on other carnivorous prey. An adult typically weighs about 0.5 kg, and it remains widespread in the wild today.
giant_rice_rat_megalomys_martinique: The Martinique giant rice rat once lived in the forests of Martinique, a small island in the Caribbean. It fed on plants and grew to about one kilogram as an adult, making it a large rodent for its region. This animal is now extinct, and its disappearance was recorded in 1902.
protosuchus: Known only from fossils, this early terrestrial crocodyliform lived during the Jurassic, roughly 200 to 190 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Moenave Formation in the southwestern United States. Adults weighed about 10 kilograms, and the animal was a carnivore.
weddell_seal: Weddell seals make their home along the icy coasts of Antarctica, where they spend much of their lives in cold ocean waters. These carnivores are deep divers, and adults can reach a mass of about 450 kg. Thick layers of blubber help them stay warm in the frigid sea. Weddell seals are still alive and thriving today.
gibbon_lar: The lar gibbon, known scientifically as Hylobates lar, is still alive and makes its home in the jungles of Indochina and Sundaland. Adults weigh about 5.5 kg, and they feed mainly on fruit. They spend their days in the trees, moving by brachiation, swinging arm over arm from branch to branch, and they are active during daylight hours.
redlichia: Redlichia takooensis lived in the seas of the Cambrian period, roughly 512 to 510 million years ago, and its fossils have been preserved in shale of the Emu Bay Shale formation in Australia. This early trilobite was a scavenger that grew to about 0.2 kilograms as an adult. Its armored shell was large for an early trilobite and bore spines along its edges.
american_bullfrog: The American bullfrog is a large amphibian found across eastern North America, the Great Plains, and the southern United States. It lives in wetlands, lakes, rivers, and swamps, where it hunts other animals and can swim with ease. Adults typically weigh about half a kilogram, and their loud call carries far across the water. People have long hunted them, and their legs are eaten as food.
mexican_wolf: Roaming the mountains, forests, and grasslands of Mexico and the southwestern United States, this carnivore lives in packs and weighs about 30 kilograms as an adult. Its thick fur helps it endure the region's varied climates. Once pushed to the brink, the Mexican wolf is still with us today and is legally protected.
quokka: The quokka is a small marsupial that still survives in the wild, living across parts of southwestern Australia in wetland areas and on offshore islands. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms and feed on plants. They move by hopping and tend to gather in groups, and the species is protected.
shrew_etruscan: The Etruscan shrew lives along the Mediterranean coast, across northern Africa, and throughout the Indian subcontinent. It makes its home in grassland and forest, feeding mostly on insects. An adult weighs only about 2 grams, which makes it the smallest mammal by mass.
raccoon_dog: Raccoon dogs roam the lowlands of Japan, Korea, and China, moving through forests and wetlands alike. Adults typically weigh about 6 kilograms, and they eat a varied diet of both plant and animal food. Active at night, these omnivores hibernate during cold months, and their fur makes them a huntable species that remains widespread today.
holdridge_toad: The Holdridge's Toad was a small amphibian that lived in the forests and mountains of a narrow band of Costa Rica, where it fed on insects. Adults weighed about 10 grams. It was declared extinct in 1986, and a chytrid fungus is noted among the causes linked to its disappearance.
giant_long_horned_buffalo: The giant long-horned buffalo once roamed savannas and grasslands across the Nile valley, the Sahara, and the lands south of it. Adults reached about 1200 kilograms and carried enormous horns, and they lived in herds that grazed on plants. Hunting pressure is recorded among the reasons this animal disappeared around 10000 years ago.
confuciusornis: Known only from fossils, Confuciusornis lived in the Cretaceous period roughly 125 to 120 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from shale in the Yixian Formation of the China lowlands. This bird weighed about 0.5 kilograms as an adult, had a toothless beak, and was omnivorous, and it also carried long tail streamers.
camelops: The Western camel once roamed the plains and deserts of western North America, from the Great Plains and the southern United States down into Mexico. It grazed on herbs and grew to a mass of about 1000 kilograms as an adult. Hunters could take it, and the species died out around 9500 BC.
viviparous_lizard: Across Europe, the British Isles, Scandinavia, and the Siberian taiga, this small lizard makes its home in forests, tundra, and boggy northern country. It is diurnal, hunting insects during daylight hours, and it weighs only about 0.01 kg as an adult. Unlike many reptiles, it gives birth to live young rather than laying eggs, and it tolerates cold well, which helps it survive in the far north.
walrus: Walruses roam the Arctic Ocean and the cold waters of the northern Atlantic and Pacific, where they rest on icy shores and drift across the sea. An adult can weigh about 1200 kilograms, and a thick layer of blubber keeps it warm. Herds gather together, and the long tusks of these animals were once hunted for ivory, so they are now protected.
yacare_caiman: The yacare caiman lives in the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and the Amazon basin, where it haunts wetlands, rivers, and swamps. It is a carnivore that can reach about 50 kg as an adult, and its body is covered in armored scales. Strong swimmer that it is, this species still lives on today, though people have hunted it.
palaeontina_burmite: Preserved in Burmese amber from the Hukawng deposits of Indochina, this extinct insect lived roughly 99 to 98 million years ago during the Cretaceous. It is the first known mosquito from that period, found sealed in Kachin amber. Adults weighed about 0.00001 kilograms, and they fed on other insects.
chinese_softshell: The Chinese softshell turtle makes its home across the lowlands of China, Japan, Korea, and Indochina. It lives in rivers, lakes, and wetlands, where it swims well and feeds on both plants and animals. Adults typically reach about 3 kg. Its flat, leathery shell is prized as food, and the species is widely farmed for that purpose.
wallaroo_common: The common wallaroo, also called the euro, lives across Australia in both mountain and desert country. It feeds on plants and typically weighs about 36 kilograms as an adult. Known as a rock-dweller, this hopping marsupial is still thriving in the wild.
ceratites: Ceratites nodosus lived in the seas of the Triassic period, roughly 245 to 240 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Muschelkalk formation in Europe. Adults weighed about 0.3 kg, and the animal is thought to have been a carnivore.
nilgiri_tahr: The Nilgiri tahr is a wild goat that lives in mountains and grasslands, where it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh about 80 kg, and the species still survives in the wild. These animals gather in herds and carry horns, and they are protected by law.
bubal_hartebeest: The bubal hartebeest once roamed the coastal lands of North Africa and the edges of the Sahara, moving across both open plains and arid desert country. Grazing on herbs, adults could reach about 180 kilograms, and they lived in herds that were hunted for sport. The last of the subspecies died in 1923.
eoraptor: Eoraptor lunensis was a small early dinosaur that lived during the Triassic, roughly 231 to 228 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Ischigualasto Formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This omnivore grew to an adult mass of about 10 kilograms.
rainbow_boa: Its scales shimmer with iridescence that shifts as light hits them, a feature that gives the snake its common name. This carnivore lives across the Amazon and Orinoco basins in the Neotropics, where it moves through jungle and forest. Active mainly at night, it hunts prey and reaches an adult mass of about 2 kg.
bat_greater_short_tailed_nz: The greater short-tailed bat once lived in the forests of New Zealand, where it foraged on the ground and in the trees by night. Its diet was omnivorous, and an adult weighed about 35 grams. Records place the species' extinction in 1967 AD.
pangolin_indian: The Indian pangolin roams the Indian subcontinent, where it moves through forests and grasslands in search of its main food, insects. Adults weigh about 13 kg, and their bodies are covered in overlapping keratin scales. Active only at night, it shelters in burrows and is legally protected, though it remains alive in the wild.
african_wildcat: The African wildcat ranges across Africa, Arabia, Iran, Anatolia, the Indian subcontinent, and the Mediterranean. It lives in savannas, deserts, grasslands, and forests, hunts mostly at night, and weighs about 4.5 kg as an adult. Its ancestors were domesticated in the Near East around 7500 BC, making it the ancestor of the house cat.
australian_magpie: The Australian magpie is a black and white bird that lives across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea. It makes its home on open plains and in forests, and it eats a varied diet that includes both plant and animal food. An adult weighs about 0.3 kg, and the species is still widespread today. It is known for being clever and for swooping at people who come too near its nest.
european_bee_eater: The European bee-eater lives across the Mediterranean, Europe, Africa south of the Sahara, Iran, and Anatolia. It favors open plains and feeds on insects, which it catches while flying. Adults weigh about 0.055 kg, and this species is still alive and widespread. It is migratory and often gathers in a flock.
golden_mantella: Native to Madagascar, the golden mantella is a small amphibian that lives in forests and wetlands. Active during the day, it feeds on insects and weighs only about 2 grams as an adult. Its skin is toxic, and it remains alive in the wild today.
silvery_cheeked_hornbill: The silvery-cheeked hornbill lives in East Africa and Southern Africa, where it makes its home in forest habitat. Adults weigh about 1.2 kilograms, and the species is still alive today. It feeds on fruit, and it spends much of its life in trees, flying between branches.
nilgai: Found across the Indian subcontinent, the nilgai makes its home in both grasslands and forests. This herbivore weighs about 200 kilograms as an adult and lives in herds. Males carry short horns, and the species is still widely found today, though it can be hunted.
green_mamba: The Eastern Green Mamba is a slender, venomous snake that still thrives today. It lives in East African savanna and Southern Africa, moving through forest, jungle, and coastal areas. Active during the day and at home in trees, it hunts carnivorous prey and typically weighs about 1.5 kg as an adult.
smilodon_fatalis: The Fatal Sabertooth roamed North America south of 42 degrees north, along with the Andes and the Amazon and Orinoco basins. It favored plains, forests, grasslands, and badlands, and it hunted meat. Adults weighed around 230 kilograms, and it became extinct in the year 8500 BC. Its long saber teeth and thick fur marked it as an ambush predator, and fossils from La Brea give scientists much of what they know about it.
roan_antelope: The roan antelope roams the savannas of Africa south of the Sahara and across the Sahel. A large, horned grazer, an adult can weigh around 270 kg. Herds of these herbivores remain widespread today, and they are also hunted by people.
children_python: A small python from Australia, the Children's Python weighs about 0.6 kg as an adult. It lives in savanna and badlands and feeds on other animals. Its scales and compact size set it apart from larger pythons, and it remains alive and widespread in the wild.
armadillo_nine_banded: Armored and mostly nocturnal, the nine-banded armadillo lives across the Neotropics, Central America, southern Mexico, and Florida and the Gulf region. It favors forest, grassland, and jungle, where it feeds mainly on insects and digs burrows for shelter. Adults weigh about 5 kg, and the species is still widespread today. Litters of identical quadruplets are a distinctive feature of its breeding.
proterosuchus: Living roughly 252 to 248 million years ago, this early archosauriform roamed the Triassic landscapes that are now preserved as Southern Africa's Katberg formation. Its fossils turn up in mudstone, and the animal is thought to have been a carnivore weighing about 100 kilograms as an adult. It moved with a sprawling gait, its legs spread out to the sides of the body.
dacentrurus: Dacentrurus armatus was a plant-eating stegosaur that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 155 to 145 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone within the Kimmeridge Clay formation in the British Isles. Adults weighed about 3000 kilograms, and it is known as a spiked European stegosaur.
madagascan_spider_tortoise: The spider tortoise is a small reptile found only on Madagascar, where it lives in dry desert scrub and coastal areas. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 0.4 kilograms. Its domed shell is small, and the species is still alive today.
mamushi: Found across Japan and Korea, this viper moves through forests, mountain slopes, and wetlands alike. It hunts small animals and typically weighs around 0.2 kg as an adult. Heat-sensing pit organs on its face help it locate warm-blooded prey, and its venom is used to subdue what it catches.
common_eland: The common eland is a large antelope found across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It grazes on herbs in open grassland and savanna, and adults can weigh around 600 kg. Living in herds, it is still widespread today, and it can be hunted or domesticated.
japanese_otter: The Japanese otter once lived along rivers and coastlines in Japan and Korea, where it hunted fish. Adults weighed about 8 kilograms, and the species was known for its thick fur and strong swimming. It was declared extinct in 2012, leaving its former range without a species that had shared those waters for generations.
dolphin_baiji: The baiji was a toothed freshwater dolphin found only in the lowlands of China, where it lived in rivers and lakes. Its diet was carnivorous, and an adult could reach about 135 kilograms. Scientists declared it functionally extinct in 2006, after decades of decline in the Yangtze River system.
alpaca: Alpacas are herbivores that graze on grasses and other plants across the grasslands and high mountain slopes of the Andes. An adult typically weighs about 65 kilograms. They live in herds and have been domesticated since around 5000 BC, valued for their soft, warm fleece.
sand_lizard: The sand lizard lives across Europe, reaching the British Isles and the eastern steppe. It favors grassland and forest edges, and it hunts insects during the day. An adult weighs about 0.02 kilograms, so it is a small reptile that remains widespread today.
wallace_flying_frog: Gliding through the forest canopy of Sundaland, this amphibian spends its life in the trees rather than on the ground. Adults weigh about 0.02 kilograms and feed on insects. Still living in the wild, it stretches its webbed limbs to glide between branches.
lemming_collared: Found across the Arctic, in Iceland and Greenland, and on the Canadian Shield, the collared lemming makes its home on open tundra. It feeds on plants and weighs only about 0.06 kg as an adult. In winter it grows a white coat that helps it blend into snow, and it digs burrows for shelter.
white_necked_raven: The white-necked raven is a large, glossy black bird that still thrives across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It makes its home in both mountain and open savanna country, and it eats a wide mix of foods. An adult weighs about 0.9 kg, and it is known for its feathers and its flying.
bat_eared_fox: Its oversized ears help it locate insects, and it is especially fond of termites. Found across East and Southern Africa, this species roams savanna and grassland, where it is active at night and rests in burrows during the day. An adult typically weighs about 4 kilograms, and it remains widespread today.
amargasaurus: Amargasaurus cazaui lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 129 to 122 million years ago. Its fossils were recovered from sandstone of the La Amarga formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This plant-eating dinosaur weighed about 2600 kilograms as an adult and carried a pair of tall spines along its neck.
manatee_west_indian: Grazing on sea grasses and freshwater plants, this slow-moving herbivore lives along coasts, rivers, and wetlands from the western Atlantic tropics through the Caribbean to Florida and the Gulf. An adult can weigh around 500 kg. Though it is still alive and legally protected, the animal remains vulnerable to hunting in some areas.
amur_leopard: The Amur leopard is a big cat that survives in forests, mountains, and taiga across a region stretching from Japan to Korea. Adults weigh about 45 kg, and their thick fur helps them endure cold winters. They hunt mainly at night and prey on other animals. Protected under law, this species is still alive in the wild.
honey_badger: The honey badger roams a wide sweep of territory, from Africa through Arabia and the Indian subcontinent to Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home in savanna, desert, forest, and grassland, digging burrows for shelter. Weighing about 10 kg as an adult, this omnivore is still widespread today, known for its fearless temperament and thick skin.
galapagos_tortoise_pinzon: Pinzon giant tortoises live on the Galapagos, where they roam both island and badlands terrain. These herbivores can reach about 100 kilograms as adults and still survive today. Their domed, saddleback shells set them apart from many relatives. Until the 1970s, introduced rats preyed heavily on the hatchlings.
marbled_cat: Still living in the wild, the Marbled Cat roams jungles and forests across Indochina, Sundaland, and parts of the Himalaya and Tibet. This carnivore weighs about 4 kg as an adult. It is arboreal and nocturnal, spending its nights hunting high in the trees, and its marbled fur helps it blend into the branches.
loggerhead_turtle: The loggerhead sea turtle roams tropical seas, the Mediterranean, and parts of the North Atlantic, North Pacific, and Indian Oceans. Adults can reach about 135 kg, and they have large heads that help them crush the crabs they eat. Still living in the wild, this species travels long migrations and receives legal protection.
spiny_tailed_lizard: The Egyptian mastigure is a herbivorous lizard that roams desert country across the Sahara, Arabia, and the Nile valley. Adults reach about 1.5 kg, and they are active during the day. They shelter in burrows and defend themselves with a spiked tail. This species is still alive and widespread.
palestine_viper: The Palestine viper, known scientifically as Daboia palaestinae, still survives in the wild across Arabia, Iran, and Anatolia. It makes its home in badlands and grasslands, where it hunts small prey as a carnivore. Adults typically weigh about 1 kilogram, and the snake is venomous, relying on its scaled body and venom to defend itself and subdue meals.
bandicoot_southern_brown: Still found across southern Australia and Tasmania, this small marsupial makes its home in forests and grasslands. Adults weigh about 1 kg, and the species eats a mix of plant and animal foods. It is nocturnal and shelters in burrows during the day.
tibetan_gazelle: Roaming the high plains and mountain slopes of the Himalaya and Tibet, this herbivore lives on a diet of plants and grasses. Adults weigh about 15 kg, and they gather in herds that move across the open country. Though still living in the wild, the Tibetan gazelle can be hunted, and both males and females carry horns.
sloth_ground_shasta: The Shasta ground sloth roamed western North America, from the region south of 42 degrees north into Mexico. It lived across deserts, mountains, and grassland, feeding on herbs. Adults could weigh around 500 kilograms, and it is known from dung deposits and long claws. It went extinct around 9000 BC.
iberian_ibex: The Iberian ibex roams rocky mountains and eroded badlands across the Iberian Peninsula, where it grazes on plants and shrubs. Adults typically weigh about 60 kilograms. These animals live in herds, and their long, curved horns make them recognizable to hunters, who are permitted to pursue them in regulated seasons. The species remains very much alive today.
guanaco: Grazing across Patagonia, the Pampas, the Andes, and the Southern Cone, the guanaco roams plains, mountains, and desert alike. This herbivore weighs about 110 kg as an adult and still thrives in the wild. Guanacos live in herds, and their fur is prized, while their relatives the llama and alpaca descend from domesticated populations.
chinese_cobra: The Chinese Cobra lives in the lowlands of China, where it moves through both forest and grassland. It hunts other animals and feeds on flesh. An adult typically weighs about 2 kilograms. It is venomous and raises a hood when threatened, and it remains alive today.
carrion_crow: The carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a still-living bird found across Europe and the wider Palearctic region. It makes its home on open plains as well as in woodland, and it eats almost anything, scavenging carcasses and hunting small prey. Adults weigh about 0.5 kg, and the species is known for its sharp intelligence and its ability to fly with agility.
euphrates_softshell: The Euphrates softshell turtle makes its home in rivers across Iran and Anatolia, where it hunts and feeds on other animals in the water. Adults can reach about 50 kilograms, and the species still survives in the wild. Its leathery, flattened shell lets it glide smoothly through the current, and it is a protected animal.
sun_bear: The smallest bear species roams jungles and forests across Indochina, Sundaland, and the Indian subcontinent. Adults weigh about 50 kg, and they eat an omnivorous diet. They climb trees with ease, and their species is still alive and protected.
cameroceras: A giant straight-shelled cephalopod, Cameroceras trentonense lived in the seas of the Ordovician period roughly 455 to 450 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Trenton Group in eastern North America. Reaching up to 6 meters in length, this carnivore carried a long, straight shell and is thought to have had tentacles.
cyprus_dwarf_elephant: The Cyprus dwarf elephant, Palaeoloxodon cypriotes, lived on the island of Cyprus, where it roamed the forests and fed on plants. Adults weighed about 200 kilograms, a small size for its kind that developed after its ancestors were isolated on the island. It died out around 9500 BC, and its tusks were among the features that set it apart.
common_toad: The common toad lives across Europe, the British Isles, Scandinavia, and the Siberian taiga. It makes its home in forests, grasslands, and wetlands, and it hunts insects mostly at night. An adult weighs about 0.1 kg, and its skin produces toxins that deter predators.
striped_hyena: The striped hyena roams a broad range that stretches across Africa, Arabia, Iran, Anatolia, the Indian subcontinent, and the Himalaya and Tibet. It lives in savanna, desert, badlands, and grassland, and it is mostly a scavenger. An adult weighs about 40 kilograms. It is nocturnal, has a shaggy coat of fur, and is a protected species that is still alive today.
pine_marten: The pine marten lives across Europe, including the British Isles, Atlantic Europe, and Scandinavia. It makes its home in forests, where it spends much of its time in the trees and comes out mainly at night. Its diet is omnivorous, and an adult weighs about 1.5 kg. This species is still alive and is valued for its thick fur.
exaeretodon: Exaeretodon argentinus lived during the Triassic, roughly 230 to 225 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Ischigualasto Formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This herbivorous cynodont weighed about 30 kilograms as an adult, making it a mid-sized plant eater of its time.
island_fox: The island fox lives only on the Channel Islands off the coast of southern California. It weighs about 2 kilograms as an adult and makes its home in both island and coastal settings. Its diet is omnivorous, and the species is still alive today and is protected.
saiga: The saiga roams the steppes of Kazakhstan, eastern Europe, and Mongolia, moving across plains, grassland, and desert in search of grasses and herbs. Adults weigh about 40 kg, and the animals gather in large herds that travel long distances with the seasons. Both sexes carry a short, translucent horn, and the species is still hunted in some areas.
bighorn_sheep: Bighorn sheep range across western North America, from northwestern Canada down into Mexico. They make their homes in mountains and badlands, grazing on herbs throughout the year. Adult males can weigh around 90 kilograms, and they live in herds, carrying large horns and remaining a huntable species today.
brachylophosaurus: Brachylophosaurus lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 78 to 77 million years ago, and its remains are preserved in sandstone of the Judith River Formation. This plant-eating dinosaur grew to about 3500 kilograms as an adult. Its name is often linked to a flat, paddle-shaped crest on its head, and a remarkably preserved mummified specimen nicknamed Leonardo helped scientists learn much about its skin.
vervet: The vervet monkey is a diurnal primate that moves through groups in East and Southern Africa. It makes its home in savanna and forest, and it eats a varied diet of both plants and animal food. An adult typically weighs about 4.5 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today.
mediterranean_gecko: The Moorish gecko is a small nocturnal lizard that lives along the Mediterranean and the northern coast of Africa. It makes its home in both coastal areas and forests, where it hunts insects after dark. An adult weighs about 0.01 kilograms, and its body is covered in fine scales.
marbled_newt: The marbled newt makes its home across Atlantic Europe, moving between forest and wetland. Adults weigh only about 0.02 kilograms, and they are an amphibian that spends much of its time swimming. Its diet is carnivorous, and the species is still alive today.
cuban_giant_tortoise: The Cuban Giant Tortoise once roamed island forests and grasslands across the Caribbean, grazing on plants and reaching adult masses near 100 kilograms. Its heavy shell was a defining feature of the species. The tortoise disappeared after humans arrived in the region, though the exact date of its extinction, placed around 1000 AD, remains uncertain.
possum_greater_glider: Gliding through the eucalyptus canopy at night, the greater glider is a marsupial of eastern Australia's forests. Adults weigh about 1.1 kilograms, and they feed on plant matter while living high in the trees. Although it is not extinct, its survival depends on keeping these forest habitats intact.
giraffe_masai: The Masai giraffe, known scientifically as Giraffa tippelskirchi, roams the open grasslands of East Africa. Adults can reach a mass of about 1100 kilograms, and they browse on herbs across the savanna in herds. Their great height lets them spot predators from far away, and they remain a living species that can be hunted.
st_paul_mammoth: The St Paul Island mammoth was a dwarfed population of woolly mammoths that lived on a small island in the Bering Sea. Cut off from the mainland as sea levels rose, these animals grazed on tundra plants and grew to an adult mass of about 3000 kg. Their shaggy fur and tusks were shared with their relatives, but their smaller island size set them apart. The population disappeared around 3750 BC.
eastern_newt: Eastern newts live across eastern North America and the Canadian Shield, moving between wetlands, lakes, and forest. As adults they weigh about 0.01 kg and feed on small prey. Their skin carries toxins, and their young pass through a terrestrial eft stage before returning to the water.
pteranodon: Toothless and crested, this pterosaur spread a wingspan of roughly 6 to 7 meters. Fossils of Pteranodon longiceps come from the chalk of the Niobrara Formation on the Great Plains, dating to between 87 and 80 million years ago. Adults weighed around 30 kilograms, and the animal likely fed on fish.
lystrosaurus: A stocky herbivore of the early Triassic, this fossil taxon lived roughly 252 to 248 million years ago and weighed about 90 kilograms as an adult. Its remains turn up in mudstone of the Katberg formation in Southern Africa. It was one of the few animals to survive the great extinction that ended the Permian, and it grazed on plants with a pair of tusks.
lord_howe_gecko: The Lord Howe Island Gecko lives on Lord Howe Island, a small island with a limited range that spans roughly 31.4 to 31.7 degrees south and 159 to 159.2 degrees east. This small, scaly lizard is nocturnal and feeds on insects. An adult weighs only about 5 grams, and the species is still alive today.
galapagos_tortoise_wolf: The Volcan Wolf giant tortoise lives on the Galapagos Islands, where it roams both island highlands and rugged badlands. It feeds on plants and grasses, and an adult can weigh around 250 kilograms. Its domed shell is a defining feature, and the species survives today.
royal_python_green_tree: Found in the jungles of Wallacea, New Guinea, and parts of Australia, this nocturnal snake spends its life in the trees. Adults typically weigh about 1.5 kilograms and feed on meat. Its scales and tree-dwelling habits help it stay hidden among the branches, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
urial: The urial is a wild sheep that roams the mountains and badlands across its range, feeding on grasses and other plants. Adults weigh around 60 kilograms, and the animals gather in herds that move together through rugged country. Males carry impressive curled horns, and the species remains alive today and can be hunted in some areas.
yangtze_giant_softshell: The largest freshwater turtle in the world, the Yangtze Giant Softshell Turtle can reach an adult mass of about 100 kilograms. It lives in the lowlands of China and Indochina, where it swims through rivers and lakes and feeds on other animals. Although it is still alive, this species is critically endangered.
steller_sea_cow: Steller's sea cow was a plant-eating sirenian of cold coastal waters, where it grazed on kelp. Adults reached about 8000 kilograms, and their thick, bark-like skin protected them. Because they could not dive, they stayed in shallow coastal zones that made them easy to hunt, and the species was driven to extinction by 1768.
flying_lemur_sunda: Found across Sundaland and Indochina, this nocturnal treetop dweller lives in jungle canopy and feeds on herbs. An adult weighs about 1.2 kg. It glides from tree to tree using a broad membrane stretched between its limbs, and it remains widespread today.
cynognathus: A large, big-headed cynodont that lived in Southern Africa during the Triassic, roughly 247 to 242 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Burgersdorp formation. This carnivore grew to an adult mass of about 70 kilograms.
vicuna: The vicuña roams the high Andes, grazing on grasses and herbs across mountain grasslands. An adult typically weighs about 45 kilograms, and it lives in herds. Its fine fur is prized as the finest wool in the world, and the species is protected, so it remains alive today.
american_toad: Found across eastern North America and the Canadian Shield, this amphibian turns up in forests, grasslands, and wetlands alike. It is nocturnal, emerging after dark to hunt insects, and it weighs only about 0.05 kg as an adult. Its skin secretes toxins, which help protect it from predators.
hutia_giant_anguilla: The Anguilla bank giant hutia was a herbivorous rodent that lived on an island in the Caribbean area near 17.5 degrees north and 64 degrees west. Adults could reach about 100 kilograms, making it one of the largest rodents of its kind. It has been extinct since roughly 3000 BC.
egyptian_tortoise: The Egyptian tortoise is the smallest tortoise found across the Palearctic region, with adults weighing only about 0.2 kg. It makes its home in deserts, ranging across the Sahara, the Nile valley, and Arabia. Feeding mainly on plants, it is still living today and is protected, with its compact shell a key identifying feature.
bush_dog: The bush dog roams the Amazon and Orinoco basins, the Pampas and Gran Chaco, and parts of Central America. It lives in jungle, forest, and wetland, where it hunts in packs and eats mostly meat. Adults weigh about 6 kg, and their short legs and thick fur help them move through damp ground and water, since they are strong swimmers.
veiled_chameleon: The Veiled Chameleon is found in Arabia, where it lives across mountain, desert, and forest settings. It spends most of its time in trees and feeds mainly on insects. Adults typically weigh about 0.15 kg, and its scaly skin can shift colour as its mood and surroundings change.
hare_arctic: The Arctic hare lives across the Arctic, the Canadian Shield, and parts of Iceland and Greenland, where it makes its home on the tundra. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 4.5 kilograms. Many individuals gather in herds, and in winter their coats turn white to blend into the snow. This species is still thriving and is one that people are permitted to hunt.
rook: The rook is a colonial bird found across Europe, the eastern steppe, the China lowlands, and parts of Japan and Korea. It favors open plains and grassland, where it feeds on almost anything it can find. Adults weigh about 0.45 kg, and rooks often gather in large flocks that move together across the land.
megaladapis_edwardsi: Megaladapis edwardsi was a giant lemur that once lived in forest and desert settings in the region spanning roughly -26 to -20 degrees latitude and 43 to 46 degrees longitude. An adult weighed about 85 kg, and it fed on herbs. This arboreal climber vanished around 1500 AD.
shrew_elephant_giant_forest: Despite its name, the giant sengi is a small, long-snouted creature weighing only about half a kilogram as an adult. It lives in forest and jungle habitats across the Congo basin and the East African savanna, and it feeds mainly on insects. Active during the day, it remains a living species.
african_bullfrog: The African bullfrog is a large amphibian that lives across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It inhabits both open grassland and wetland areas, and it is a carnivore. Adults can reach about 1.4 kilograms, and this species is still widespread. It burrows and aestivates through dry periods, and it can be quite aggressive when disturbed.
jungle_cat: The jungle cat roams a wide arc stretching from the Indian subcontinent and Indochina through Iran, Anatolia, and the Nile valley, reaching up into the Himalaya and Tibet. It favors wetlands, swamps, grasslands, and forests, and it hunts mainly small animals. Adults weigh about 8 kg, and this species is active during the day and is known to swim.
northern_fur_seal: Found across the North Pacific, the northern fur seal lives in cold ocean waters and along coastlines. Adults can weigh around 120 kg, and they rely on a thick layer of blubber and dense fur to stay warm. These carnivores gather in herds and travel long distances across the seas as they migrate.
edmontonia: Roughly 76 to 68 million years ago, a heavily armored herbivore moved through what is now northwestern North America. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation. Adults weighed about 3500 kilograms, and long spikes projected from their shoulders.
bolson_tortoise: The largest tortoise native to North America, the Bolson tortoise lives in the deserts and grasslands of Mexico. Adults can weigh about 14 kilograms, and they feed mainly on herbs. These animals dig burrows for shelter, and because their numbers have declined, they are now a protected species that still survives in the wild.
blue_poison_dart_frog: Barely heavier than a paperclip, this small amphibian lives in the jungles of the Amazon and Orinoco river basins. It feeds on insects and carries toxins in its skin that deter predators. Though it is still widespread across its range, its bright coloring signals the danger it carries.
chinkara: The chinkara, also called the Indian gazelle, lives across the Indian subcontinent as well as in Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home in deserts and grasslands, where it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh about 23 kilograms, and they often move together in herds. Though still living in the wild, this gazelle is hunted in some areas.
little_crow: The Torresian crow, known scientifically as Corvus orru, lives across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea. It favors open plains and savanna, eats a wide range of foods, and weighs about half a kilogram as an adult. This clever bird is still common across its range.
sable: The sable is a small, tree-climbing member of the marten family that roams the taiga forests of Siberia and northern Asia, reaching as far as the eastern steppe. It eats both plant and animal foods and weighs roughly 1.2 kilograms as an adult. Its dense, glossy fur has long been prized, and the species remains widespread today.
western_toad: The Western Toad lives across northwestern and western North America, including the Pacific Northwest. It turns up in forests, mountain areas, and wetlands, and it feeds mainly on insects. An adult weighs about 0.06 kilograms, and its skin produces toxins that discourage predators.
green_anole: Small and tree-dwelling, the green anole is found in Florida and the Gulf states of the southern United States. It lives in forests and swamps, where it hunts insects. An adult weighs only about 6 grams, and its skin can shift between green and brown to match its surroundings.
eurasian_lynx: The Eurasian lynx roams a wide arc of territory, from European forests and Scandinavian woodlands across the Siberian taiga to the Himalaya, Tibet, the Mongolian steppe, and the mountains of Iran and Anatolia. It favors taiga, forest, and mountain country, and it hunts mostly at night. Adults weigh around 22 kilograms, and their thick fur has made them a prized target for hunters.
megistaspis: Megistaspis hammondi lived during the Ordovician, roughly 480 to 470 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in the Fezouata Shale of North Africa's coast, where the fine mud captured details of its shell. It is thought to have been a scavenger and weighed about 0.1 kg as an adult.
chimpanzee: Common chimpanzees live across the Congo basin, along the West African coast, and in East African savanna country. They move through jungle, forest, and open grassland, and they eat both plants and animals. Adults weigh about 45 kg, and they are active during the day, climbing through trees and using tools to get food.
bat_greater_bulldog: Active after dark, the greater bulldog bat skims over rivers, coastlines, and wetlands across the Neotropics, Central America, and the Caribbean. It hunts fish, and adults weigh only about 0.06 kg. This species is still alive and widespread.
kinkajou: The kinkajou, known as the honey bear, moves through the forests of Mexico, Central America, and the Amazon and Orinoco basins. Living in jungle and forest canopy, it spends its nights high in the trees, gripping branches with its prehensile tail. Adults weigh about 3 kg, and they feed mainly on fruit.
chiru: Roaming the high plains of the Himalaya and Tibet, this herbivorous antelope weighs about 35 kilograms as an adult. Herds travel long migration routes across icy mountain terrain, and males carry slender horns. Its fine wool, known as shahtoosh, has long drawn hunters, though the species itself survives today.
egyptian_mongoose: The Egyptian Mongoose is a slender predator found along the Nile valley, the North African coast, and across much of Africa. It lives in wetlands, savannas, and forests, and it hunts by day. Adults weigh about 3 kilograms, and this carnivore is known for killing snakes.
persian_fallow: The Persian fallow deer is a herbivore that lives in forest and wetland areas and still survives in the wild. Adults reach about 90 kg, and the males grow broad antlers that they use during the season when herds gather. Because this deer can be hunted, its numbers are watched closely by those who manage its habitat.
spectacled_bear: The spectacled bear roams the Andes of South America, moving through both cloud forest and high mountain terrain. Adults can weigh around 100 kg, and the species feeds largely on plants. Its fur is thick, and it climbs trees with ease, often sleeping or feeding high in the branches. Still living in the wild, it is a protected animal.
saurornitholestes: A small meat-eating dinosaur from the Cretaceous, living roughly 77 to 75 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation in northwestern North America. Adults weighed about 12 kilograms, and this dromaeosaur is known from Alberta.
alpine_newt: The Alpine Newt is a small amphibian found across Europe and the Alps, where it lives in both wetlands and mountain habitats. Adults weigh about 0.01 kg, and they feed on other small animals. This species is still alive and spends much of its time in the water, where it swims with ease.
sloth_ground_lestodon: Lestodon armatus was a giant ground sloth that roamed the grasslands of the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and Patagonia. Adults reached about 3500 kilograms, and they fed on herbs across open country. This megafauna is now extinct, and its remains are often grouped with other tusked creatures of the ancient Americas.
machimosaurus: Machimosaurus hugii was a marine crocodylomorph of the Late Jurassic, living roughly 155 to 145 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Kimmeridge (Solothurn) formation in Europe. Reaching about 9 meters long and weighing around 1000 kilograms, it was a carnivore with powerful jaws suited to crushing shelled prey.
ocelot: The ocelot, Leopardus pardalis, roams from the Neotropics through Mexico into the southern United States. It makes its home in jungle, forest, swamp, and grassland alike. Active mainly at night, this carnivore weighs about 12 kg as an adult and is known to swim well. It remains alive and widespread today.
southern_ground_hornbill: The largest hornbill in the world, this bird walks across the grasslands and open savanna of southern and East Africa in small family groups. Adults weigh around 4.5 kg, and they feed mainly on meat, hunting insects, reptiles, and small animals on foot. Many communities regard the bird as an omen of rain, and it remains widespread and still common in the wild.
crab_eating_raccoon: The crab-eating raccoon lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, across Central America, and in the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It favors wetlands, rivers, and jungle, and it eats both plants and animals. Adults weigh about 7 kg, and this species is still alive, active at night, with a thick coat and a strong ability to swim.
long_tailed_weasel: Found across North America south of 42 degrees north, along with Central America and Mexico, the long-tailed weasel (Neogale frenata) lives in both grasslands and forests. This carnivore weighs about 0.3 kilograms as an adult and is still living today. Its fur is a notable feature of the species.
crested_newt: Found across Europe, the British Isles, and Scandinavia, the great crested newt lives in wetlands, lakes, and forests. This carnivorous amphibian weighs about 0.02 kg as an adult and is still thriving today. Its skin is toxic, and it is a protected species that spends time swimming in water.
anzu: A feathered, bird-like dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous, Anzu wyliei lived roughly 67 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have turned up in mudstone of the Hell Creek formation on the Great Plains. Adults weighed about 250 kilograms, and the animal is thought to have been omnivorous, earning it the nickname "chicken from hell."
desman_russian: The Russian desman is a semi-aquatic animal that lives along rivers and wetlands in the eastern steppe and the Kazakh steppe. It feeds mainly on insects and swims with ease through the water. An adult weighs about 0.45 kg, and its dense fur keeps it warm. The species is still alive and is legally protected.
mouse_house: The house mouse, known scientifically as Mus musculus, is still widespread today. It lives across the Indian subcontinent and southwestern Asia, where it makes its home in grassland and desert. An adult weighs about 0.02 kg, and it eats a mixed diet of plants and animal matter while digging burrows and staying active mostly at night.
wild_boar: Wild boar roam a huge range, from Europe and North Africa through the Indian subcontinent, China, Japan, and Korea. They live in forests, grasslands, and wetlands, eating whatever their omnivorous diet offers. Adults often reach about 100 kilograms, and they gather in herds, carrying tusks that serve them well in the wild. Their meat is pork, and people have hunted them for generations and even domesticated them.
edmontosaurus: Edmontosaurus annectens was a plant-eating dinosaur that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Adults could reach about 4000 kilograms, and its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Hell Creek formation on the Great Plains. Some specimens are known as mummies, preserved with skin impressions that reveal much about its body.
thalassodromeus: Thalassodromeus sethi was a pterosaur, a flying reptile rather than a true bird or mammal, that lived roughly 113 to 108 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from the Romualdo Member of the Santana Formation in South America, preserved within limestone. This fish-eating animal weighed about 30 kilograms as an adult, and it was notable for its giant crest.
dingo: Dingoes live across Australia and roam deserts, grasslands, forests, and badlands alike. Adults weigh about 17 kg, and they hunt in packs while hunting mostly meat. Their ancestors arrived with humans around 3500 BC, and the species has never been found on the island of Tasmania.
galapagos_tortoise_santa_cruz: The Santa Cruz Giant Tortoise makes its home on the Galapagos Islands, moving between forest and grassland habitats. Plants form its entire diet, and a mature adult can weigh around 300 kilograms. Its domed shell and long lifespan help it endure across generations, and this species survives today.
american_crow: Crows of this species range across North America and into Mexico, moving easily between open plains and wooded country. They eat nearly anything, from insects and seeds to carrion and scraps left by people. An adult weighs about 0.45 kg, and while they are still common and thriving, they are known for their sharp intelligence and their habit of gathering in flocks.
european_roller: The European roller is a still-living bird found across Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran and Anatolia, and sub-Saharan Africa. It favors open plains, where it hunts insects. An adult weighs about 0.14 kg. This migratory species flies long distances between its breeding and wintering grounds.
platypterygius: Platypterygius australis was an ichthyosaur, a marine reptile that swam in ancient seas and lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 120 to 95 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Toolebuc Formation in Australia. Adults could reach about 1500 kilograms, and it was a carnivore. It belonged to one of the last groups of ichthyosaurs before the lineage disappeared.
portuguese_ibex: The Portuguese ibex once roamed the mountainous terrain of northern Portugal and nearby Spain, where it grazed on herbs and moved through the rocky slopes in herds. An adult could weigh around 60 kilograms, and males were recognized by their large, curving horns. Hunting was a popular pursuit for these animals, and the subspecies was declared extinct in 1892.
gray_fox: The gray fox ranges across eastern North America, the southern United States, Mexico, and parts of Central America. It lives in forests and badlands, and its diet is omnivorous. Adults typically weigh about 4 kg, and this nocturnal animal is known for climbing trees.
kihansi_spray_toad: The Kihansi Spray Toad is a tiny amphibian that lives in jungle and river habitats in the Kihansi area, where its range spans roughly -8.6 to -8.4 degrees latitude and 35.8 to 36.0 degrees longitude. An adult weighs only about 2 grams, and it feeds on insects. Unusually for a toad, it gives birth to live young. This species is still alive but has disappeared from the wild.
tiktaalik: Tiktaalik roseae lived during the Devonian, a fossil taxon recovered from sandstone of the Fram Formation in the Arctic. This carnivore is noted as a fishapod, measuring about 2.7 metres long and weighing roughly 15 kilograms as an adult. It had a wrist fin and was a shallow water ambusher that swam among the waters it hunted.
lowland_anoa: The lowland anoa is a small wild buffalo that lives in forests and jungle on the island of Sulawesi. It grazes on herbs and adults weigh about 230 kg. Its short, straight horns and compact size earn it the nickname dwarf buffalo, and it remains alive in the wild today.
baryonyx: Baryonyx walkeri lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 130 to 125 million years ago. Its fossils were found in the mudstones of the Wealden, or Weald Clay, formation in the British Isles. Adults weighed about 1700 kilograms, and this dinosaur was a fish eater with a giant thumb claw.
rosy_boa: The rosy boa, known scientifically as Lichanura trivirgata, makes its home across western North America and into Mexico. It favors desert and badlands terrain, where it hunts small prey. Adults typically weigh about half a kilogram, and this constrictor is still widespread today.
coypu: The coypu is a semi-aquatic rodent that lives in the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, Patagonia, and the Andes. It favors wetlands and rivers, where it feeds on plants. Adults weigh about 7 kg, and the animal's dense fur and hunted status make it a notable part of the region's wildlife.
heterodontosaurus: Heterodontosaurus tucki is known only from fossils, which date to the Jurassic period, roughly 200 to 190 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Elliot Formation in Southern Africa. This small animal weighed about 2 kg as an adult and is thought to have eaten both plants and other food. Its canine-like tusks set it apart from many of its relatives.
hutia_hispaniolan: The Hispaniolan hutia is a plant-eating rodent that lives in the forests of the Caribbean, where it feeds on herbs and other vegetation. An adult typically weighs about 1.3 kilograms. This species is still alive today and is found on the island of Hispaniola, where it is a protected animal.
europasaurus: Europasaurus lived during the Jurassic period, roughly 154 to 151 million years ago, and its fossils were found in limestone of the Süntel formation in Europe. This herbivore is known as an island dwarf brachiosaurid, and adults reached about 800 kilograms. Its remains show it was a much smaller relative of the giant sauropods that roamed other regions at the time.
wombat_southern_hairy: Active mostly at night, the southern hairy-nosed wombat digs burrows that shelter it from the heat of its home. It lives across southern Australia, in deserts and grasslands, where it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh about 26 kg, and the species is still alive today.
bullsnake: Found across the Great Plains, western North America, and parts of Mexico, the bullsnake makes its home in grasslands and deserts. This carnivorous snake typically weighs about 1.5 kg as an adult. It is a constrictor that wraps its prey, and when threatened it hisses in a way that mimics a rattlesnake.
mediterranean_monk_seal: The Mediterranean monk seal lives in the Mediterranean Sea and along its coasts, often resting in sea caves. Adults can weigh about 300 kg, and their diet consists of meat from the sea. Thick blubber keeps them insulated, and the species is protected, though it has not gone extinct.
massasauga: The Eastern Massasauga is a small, venomous rattlesnake that still survives today. It makes its home across the Great Plains, eastern North America, and the Canadian Shield, where it favors wetlands and grasslands. Adults weigh about 0.3 kilograms, and they carry a small rattle at the tail tip.
balearic_dormouse: The Balearic giant dormouse lived on islands and in caves, eating a mixed diet of plants and other food. An adult weighed about 0.25 kg. This giant rodent is now extinct, with its disappearance dated to around 1000 BC.
sloth_three_toed_brown: The brown-throated sloth makes its home in the jungles of Central America and across the Amazon and Orinoco basins. It spends nearly its whole life in the trees, moving slowly from branch to branch while feeding on leaves and other plant matter. An adult weighs about 4.5 kilograms. This species is still thriving in the wild.
azure_winged_magpie: The azure-winged magpie is a bird of forests found across Japan, Korea, the China lowlands, and the Mongolian steppe. It eats a varied, omnivorous diet and weighs about 0.07 kg as an adult. Feathers, flies, and herd are its notable traits, and the species remains alive today.
blanfords_fox: Blanford's Fox is a small, pale fox found across Iran, Anatolia, Arabia, and the Himalaya and Tibet. It makes its home in mountains, deserts, and badlands, where it hunts mainly insects after dark. Adults weigh about 1.1 kg, and this species is still alive, climbing cliffs with its thick fur helping it cope with the cold.
potoroo_broad_faced: The broad-faced potoroo was a small nocturnal marsupial that lived in forest habitat in a region of southwestern Australia. It weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult and ate a mix of plant and animal foods. The species was declared extinct in 1875.
beisa_oryx: Beisa oryx roam the grasslands of East Africa, and they can also be found in drier desert margins. Adults weigh around 180 kilograms and feed entirely on herbs. Living in herds, they carry long, straight horns and are still widespread today, though they are hunted in some areas.
numbat: The numbat is a small marsupial found in the southwest of Western Australia, where it lives in forest habitat. An adult weighs about 0.55 kg, and it feeds almost entirely on insects, especially termites. Unlike many marsupials, it is active during the day, and it remains a protected species that is still alive today.
ceratosaurus: Ceratosaurus is a fossil predator that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 153 to 148 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone layers of the Morrison Formation in western North America. Adults weighed around 650 kilograms, and the animal carried a distinctive nasal horn along with blade-like teeth suited to meat eating.
scipionyx: Scipionyx samniticus lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 113 to 110 million years ago. Its fossil was pressed into limestone of the Pietraroja Plattenkalk formation in the Mediterranean region. The juvenile weighed about 0.2 kilograms as an adult, and its preserved gut shows it was a carnivore.
desmatosuchus: Desmatosuchus spurensis lived during the Triassic, roughly 225 to 215 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Dockum, also called Chinle, formation in the southern United States. This armored aetosaur was a plant eater that could reach about 500 kilograms as an adult. Its shoulder spikes set it apart from its relatives.
giant_day_gecko: The Madagascar Giant Day Gecko is a diurnal, arboreal lizard that lives in the jungles and forests of Madagascar. Despite its name, it is a small species, with adults weighing only about 0.05 kg. It is an omnivore, and it remains widespread in the wild today.
squirrel_grey_eastern: The eastern grey squirrel makes its home across the forests of eastern North America, where it spends most of its life in the trees. Adults weigh about 0.55 kilograms, and they are active during the day. Their diet is mainly fruit, and the species remains widespread today. It is also a huntable animal.
california_newt: Found along western North America, the California newt makes its home in forests, rivers, and coastal areas. This amphibian eats meat and weighs only about 0.02 kilograms as an adult. Its skin is toxic, which helps protect it from predators, and the species is still alive today.
eastern_spotted_skunk: The Eastern Spotted Skunk ranges across eastern North America, Mexico, and the southern United States, living in both forests and grasslands. An adult weighs about 0.7 kilograms, and it forages mostly at night on a varied diet of plant matter and animal prey. Before spraying, it may perform a handstand, a warning that is easy to miss in the dark.
tulerpeton: Tulerpeton is a fossil species from the Devonian period, living roughly 367 to 364 million years ago. Its remains were found in sandstone of the Ketleri Formation in Europe. It was a carnivore that weighed about 10 kg as an adult, and it swam while showing six digits on each limb.
black_caiman: The black caiman is a crocodilian that still lives across the Amazon and Orinoco basins. It makes its home in rivers, lakes, swamps, and jungle waters, where it hunts mostly at night. Adults can reach about 300 kilograms, and as an apex predator it feeds on other animals while moving easily through the water.
bobcat: The bobcat ranges across much of North America, from the southern parts of Canada down through Mexico. It makes its home in forests, badlands, swamps, and grasslands, and it is an active hunter that moves mostly at night. An adult weighs about 9 kilograms, and its fur and status as a huntable species are both noted in the record.
black_necked_spitting_cobra: Found across much of Africa south of the Sahara and throughout the Sahel, this snake makes its home in savanna and grassland. Adults typically weigh around 2 kg, and their diet is carnivorous. Its venom is potent, and it can spit that venom at a threat, which makes it a species to respect.
cave_racer: Found across the lowlands of China, Indochina, Japan, and Korea, this snake makes its home in caves, forests, and mountain country. It hunts after dark and eats other animals, and an adult typically weighs about 2 kilograms. Still living in the wild today, it is a nocturnal dweller of caves whose body is covered in scales.
pterodactylus: Known only from fossils, this short-tailed pterosaur lived during the Jurassic period, roughly 150 to 148 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in the limestone of the Solnhofen formation in Europe. Adults weighed about 1 kg, and the animal fed on insects.
queen_of_sheba_gazelle: The Queen of Sheba's gazelle was a small herbivore that weighed about 15 kg as an adult. It lived in mountain country and fed on herbs, and its horns were a distinctive feature. The last known sighting of this species was in 1951, and it has been classed as extinct since then.
polar_bear: Polar bears roam the Arctic, living across Iceland, Greenland, and the Arctic Ocean. They make their homes on ice, tundra, and coastlines, and they are carnivores that hunt. Adults can reach about 450 kilograms, and their thick fur and blubber help them endure the cold. They swim well and are a protected species that still survives today.
archelon: Archelon ischyros was an enormous sea turtle that swam through Cretaceous waters roughly 75 to 70 million years ago. Adults reached about 2200 kilograms, making it the largest sea turtle known. Instead of a hard bony shell, it had a leathery covering, and its fossils have been recovered from chalk within the Pierre Shale formation of the Great Plains.
ocellated_lizard: The ocellated lizard is a large lizard found across Atlantic Europe and the Mediterranean. It lives in forests and grasslands, eats both plants and animals, and typically weighs about half a kilogram as an adult. Active during the day, it can bite hard when handled, and it remains widespread today.
orthoceras: Orthoceras regulare was a straight-shelled nautiloid that lived in the seas of the Ordovician, roughly 470 to 465 million years ago. Its fossils turn up in the limestone of the Volkhov Formation, better known as Orthoceratite Limestone, across Europe. This carnivore grew to about 1 kilogram, and its long, straight shell is what sets it apart from its coiled relatives.
eomaia: Eomaia scansoria lived roughly 125 to 122 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils were preserved in shale of the Yixian Formation in the lowlands of China. This small creature weighed about 0.02 kilograms and ate insects, and it is considered an early relative of placental mammals.
toolache_wallaby: The Toolache wallaby once lived across a stretch of southeastern Australia roughly between latitudes 36 and 39 degrees south.
