It made its home in grasslands, where it fed on herbs and moved in herds while hopping across open ground. Adults weighed about 15 kilograms, and the species was declared extinct in 1943.
nubian_ibex: The Nubian ibex roams rugged terrain across the Sahara, the Nile valley, and Arabia, favoring mountains, deserts, and badlands. Adults weigh about 50 kg and feed on plants. Living in herds, these animals are still alive today, and they are known for their horns and for being hunted.
japanese_fire_belly_newt: Native to Japan and Korea, this amphibian makes its home in wetlands and rivers. It feeds on other small animals and weighs roughly 0.01 kg as an adult. Its skin is toxic, and its bright orange belly serves as a warning to predators that it is best left alone.
opossum_water: The water opossum, also called the yapok, lives in rivers and wetlands from Central America through the Amazon and Orinoco basins in the Neotropics. This marsupial hunts fish and other aquatic prey, and it swims with ease. Active at night, it weighs about 0.7 kilograms as an adult and remains common across its range.
anaconda: The green anaconda lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins of the Neotropics, where it spends its time in swamps, rivers, and wetlands. It is a carnivore, and it hunts by ambush, waiting in the water and then seizing prey with a powerful constriction. Adults can reach a mass of about 100 kilograms, and the species is still alive and widespread.
ozark_hellbender: The Ozark Hellbender is an aquatic amphibian that lives in rivers within a region spanning roughly 36 to 38 degrees north and 90 to 93 degrees west. It is a carnivore that swims through its river home and can reach an adult mass of about 1.2 kilograms. This species is still alive today and is protected.
hog_badger: The hog badger, Arctonyx collaris, is still found across Indochina, Sundaland, the Himalaya and Tibet, and the lowlands of China. It lives in forest and jungle, eats both plants and animals, and typically weighs about 12 kg as an adult. Active at night, it digs burrows and is recognized by its thick fur.
pachyrhinosaurus: Pachyrhinosaurus lakustai lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 73 to 72 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Wapiti Formation. This plant-eater grew to about 4000 kilograms and carried a bony boss on its nose, and evidence points to herds living at high polar latitudes.
red_billed_chough: Found across Europe, the Himalaya and Tibet, the Mediterranean, and Iran and Anatolia, this glossy black bird favors both rugged coastlines and high mountains. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.3 kg as an adult. Its feathers and flight skills, along with its reputation for intelligence, make it a striking resident of these wild places, and it remains widespread today.
cheetah: The cheetah ranges across Africa, from the Sahara and the Sahel to the savannas of the east and south. It favors open savanna, grassland, and plains, and it hunts during the day. Adults weigh about 50 kilograms, and the species is the fastest land animal. Cheetahs are still living today, and they are a protected species.
golden_mole_cape: Burrowing through sand in southern Africa, this small creature lives in both desert and coastal zones. It has no visible eyes and feeds on insects it finds underground. An adult weighs about 0.04 kg, and the species is still living today.
stenopterygius: Stenopterygius was a fish-shaped marine reptile that swam the seas of Europe during the Jurassic, roughly 183 to 175 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in the Posidonia Shale, where adults reached about 160 kilograms. Remarkably, some specimens from Holzmaden preserve embryos, offering a rare glimpse of its early development.
kirks_dikdik: Kirk's dik-dik is a tiny antelope weighing about 5 kg as an adult, roughly the size of a small house cat. It roams the savannas of East Africa and Southern Africa, and it also turns up in desert country. Its diet is made up of herbs, and only the males grow horns. Though still alive, the species is hunted in some areas.
gelada: The gelada is a grass-eating primate that lives in grassland and mountain country. Adults weigh about 18 kilograms, and they spend their days in large herds that sleep on cliffs at night. This species is still alive in the wild.
rock_hyrax: Rock hyraxes live in herds and shelter in burrows among rocky outcrops and broken badlands. They range across sub-Saharan Africa, the Nile valley, the Sahara, and Arabia. These herbivores weigh about 4 kg as adults and are still widespread today.
dolphin_indus: The Indus river dolphin, known scientifically as Platanista minor, lives in river waters and feeds on other animals. Adults weigh about 85 kg, and the species is still alive today. It is a toothed, freshwater dolphin that is nearly blind, and it is a protected animal.
bushbuck: The bushbuck roams across Africa south of the Sahara and into the Sahel, moving through both forest and savanna. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 45 kg as an adult. Still widespread today, this antelope carries horns and is sometimes hunted.
panderichthys: Panderichthys lived in the Devonian seas and rivers roughly 380 to 375 million years ago, and its fossils have been pulled from sandstone of the Gauja Formation in Europe. This carnivore weighed about 20 kg as an adult. It swam like a fish, yet its body shows features resembling those of early tetrapods.
red_river_hog: The red river hog, Potamochoerus porcus, roams the forests and jungles of the Congo Basin and the West African coast. This omnivore can weigh around 90 kilograms as an adult. Living in herds, it remains widespread today, and it is hunted by people in parts of its range.
cuvier_dwarf_caiman: Cuvier's Dwarf Caiman is a small crocodilian still found today in the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It lives in rivers, jungle waterways, and swamps, where it hunts meat-eating prey. Adults reach about 20 kg, and its armored scales and strong swimming ability help it move through its watery home.
prairie_dog_black_tailed: Grassland dwellers of the Great Plains, black-tailed prairie dogs feed mainly on herbs and live in colonies called towns. Each adult weighs about 1 kilogram, and the animals are active during the day, moving among their burrows as they forage. Though still widespread and not extinct, they are hunted in some areas, and their herds remain a familiar sight across open prairie.
tawny_frogmouth: The tawny frogmouth is a nocturnal bird found across Australia and Tasmania, where it lives in forests. It hunts a carnivorous diet and weighs about 0.4 kg as an adult. Its feathers provide camouflage, and it is still alive and widespread today.
eurypterus: A sea scorpion from the Silurian, Eurypterus remipes lived roughly 425 to 420 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in limestone of the Bertie Group's Fiddlers Green Formation in eastern North America. This carnivore swam through ancient waters, and it has been named the state fossil of New York.
indian_roofed_turtle: The Indian Roofed Turtle makes its home across the Indian subcontinent, where it lives in rivers and lakes. Adults weigh about 1 kilogram, and they are still widespread today. This turtle feeds mainly on plants, swims with ease through the water, and often climbs onto logs or rocks to bask in the sun beneath its domed shell.
toxodon: The Toxodon was a large, herbivorous native ungulate that roamed the plains and wetlands of South America. Adults could weigh around 1100 kilograms, and their hippo-like build suited a life spent grazing near water. Its range covered the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, Patagonia, and the Amazon basin, and it became extinct around 9500 years ago.
water_chevrotain: Found along rivers and in forests of the Congo basin and the West African coast, the African water chevrotain is a small plant-eater weighing about 12 kg as an adult. It is not a true deer, though it shares some features with deer, and it is known for swimming well. Males grow tusk-like canine teeth, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
prairie_rattlesnake: The prairie rattlesnake lives across the Great Plains and western North America, where it hunts in grasslands and open plains. Adults typically weigh about 1 kilogram, and the species remains common in the wild. Its diet consists of other animals, and it is venomous. Heat-sensing pit organs help it locate prey, while the rattle at the tail warns nearby creatures to keep their distance.
red_eared_slider: Native to the southern United States, Florida, and parts of Mexico, the red-eared slider makes its home in rivers, lakes, and wetlands. It eats both plants and animals, and adults typically weigh around 1.5 kg. Often seen basking on logs and rocks in the sun, this turtle is a strong swimmer that remains common in the wild today.
rough_skinned_newt: The rough-skinned newt lives across the Pacific Northwest, where it moves between forests, lakes, and rivers. Adults weigh only about 0.02 kilograms and feed on other small creatures. This amphibian carries tetrodotoxin in its skin, a poison strong enough to be deadly to many predators.
tullimonstrum: The Tully monster lived in the Carboniferous period, roughly 307 to 306 million years ago, and its remains are preserved in the shale of the Francis Creek formation in eastern North America. It was a carnivore that weighed about 0.2 kilograms as an adult and appears to have swum through its waters. Its eyes sat at the ends of a long stalk, and its unusual body plan has left scientists uncertain about where it belongs on the tree of life.
california_sea_lion: Found along the Pacific coast of North America, from roughly 22 to 50 degrees north, the California sea lion lives in cold coastal waters. Its diet is carnivorous, and adults can reach about 150 kg. These animals gather in herds, rely on a thick layer of blubber to stay warm, and swim with great agility. The species is still thriving today.
moschops_triassic_replaced: Ischigualastia lived during the Triassic, roughly 230 to 225 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Ischigualasto Formation. This plant eater reached an adult mass of about 1200 kilograms, making it the largest dicynodont known from the Triassic. Its remains tell of a heavy, herbivorous creature that once roamed the ancient landscapes now preserved in Patagonia and the Pampas.
fennec_fox: Active mostly after dark, the fennec fox spends its days in burrows dug into desert sand. Its oversized ears help release body heat and pick up the sounds of prey moving underground. Weighing only about 1.5 kilograms as an adult, it roams the Sahara, the Sahel, and the Nile valley, eating both plants and small animals.
bandicoot_pig_footed: Once common across the grasslands and deserts of Australia, this small nocturnal animal weighed about 0.2 kilograms as an adult. It ran swiftly and fed on herbs, moving on hooved feet that gave it its unusual name. The species was declared extinct in 1957.
tarsier_philippine: The Philippine tarsier is a tiny nocturnal primate that hunts insects through the jungles of the Philippines. An adult weighs about 0.14 kilograms, making it one of the smallest primates alive. Although the species is still living, it is protected, and it is carnivorous, feeding mainly on insects in the dense forest.
przewalski_horse: Przewalski's horse, known scientifically as Equus ferus przewalskii, roams the steppe and desert plains of Mongolia and Kazakhstan. It grazes on herbs and grows to about 300 kilograms as an adult. Living in herds, this horse was once extinct in the wild until 1969, when populations were reintroduced to the land.
egyptian_cobra: The Egyptian cobra ranges across the Nile valley, the Sahel, the northern African coast, and much of Africa south of the Sahara. It favors deserts, savannas, and grasslands, where it hunts small animals. An adult typically weighs around 3 kg, and its spreading hood and venom have made it a symbol of royalty in ancient Egypt.
piapiac: The piapiac is a slender, long-tailed bird of the Sahel that makes its home across the savanna. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs only about 0.08 kg as an adult. Often seen flying alongside grazing animals, it rides on their backs to catch the flies and other insects they stir up.
speke_hingeback: Speke's Hinge-back Tortoise is still living across the savannas of East Africa and Southern Africa, and it also turns up in forest country. Adults usually weigh about 2 kg. Its diet is omnivorous, and its shell has a hinge at the back that lets the rear portion close around the body for protection.
manatee_west_african: The West African manatee lives along the coast and in the rivers of western Africa, reaching into parts of the Sahel. Adults can weigh about 400 kg, and this plant-eating sirenian feeds on vegetation in its watery home. Though it is still alive today, it is hunted in some areas and is legally protected.
mole_rat_naked: Found in the dry grasslands of East Africa, this small rodent spends nearly its whole life in underground tunnels. Colonies are eusocial, with a single breeding queen and a few breeding males while the rest of the group works the burrows and forages for plant roots and tubers. Adults weigh only about 35 grams, and unlike most mammals, they are cold-blooded, so their body temperature shifts with the air around them.
gallotia_goliath: The Tenerife Giant Lizard was a large lacertid that lived on the island of Tenerife, moving through forests and badlands and eating both plants and animals. Adults reached about 2 kilograms, making it a giant among its relatives. It is recorded as extinct from around 500 AD, a decline that followed the arrival of humans on the island.
golden_toad: The orange males of this small amphibian once lived in a cloud forest in the mountains of a tiny corner of Costa Rica, where they fed on insects. Adults weighed about 0.01 kg. The species was declared extinct in 1989 after a chytrid fungus and shifts in climate are thought to have caused its decline.
tyrannosaurus_rex: Tyrannosaurus rex lived during the late Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago, and it is known from fossils. Its remains have been recovered from the Hell Creek formation of the Great Plains, where they are preserved in sandstone. As an apex tyrannosaur with a bone-crushing bite and a carnivorous diet, it could weigh around 8000 kilograms as an adult.
paca_lowland: The lowland paca is a nocturnal rodent that lives in jungle and forest across the Amazon and Orinoco basins, Central America, and southern Mexico. Adults weigh about 9 kg, and they feed mainly on fruit. They shelter in burrows and are still widespread today, though people hunt them for food.
crocodile_newt: The Crocodile Newt is an amphibian found in the lowlands of Indochina and China, where it lives in both forest and mountain settings. It is a carnivore, and adults weigh only about 0.03 kg. Its skin is toxic, and it is active at night. This species is still alive today.
keel_scaled_boa: The Round Island Keel-scaled Boa lives in the Mascarene islands, where it occupies both island forest and open island habitat. It is a carnivore, and adults typically reach about 0.4 kilograms. Its keeled scales and flexible jaw hinge help it handle prey, and the species remains alive today and is protected.
mapusaurus: Known only from fossils, the Mapusaurus roseae lived during the Cretaceous, between 96 and 93 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Huincul Formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. Adults are estimated to have weighed about 5000 kilograms, and it was a carnivore. A bonebed where many of these animals were preserved together hints that they may have hunted or traveled in packs.
solomon_skink: The largest skink in the world, this arboreal lizard lives in jungles on islands scattered across the western Pacific, roughly between 5 and 10 degrees south of the equator and 155 to 162 degrees east. Adults can reach about 0.9 kilograms and feed on plants. Its prehensile tail helps it grip branches as it moves through the canopy, and it remains a living species.
giant_monkey_frog: The Giant Waxy Monkey Frog is an arboreal amphibian that lives in the jungles of the Amazon and Orinoco regions. It feeds on insects and typically weighs about 0.1 kg as an adult. Its skin secretes a substance used in the traditional ritual known as kambo, and the species remains alive today.
gaur: The gaur, a wild cattle species, roams forests, jungles, and grasslands across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina. Adults can weigh around 900 kilograms, and they live in herds. Their massive horns and their status as a huntable animal are notable features in the library's records, and the species remains alive today.
galapagos_tortoise_pinta: The Pinta Island tortoise lived in the Galapagos, where it roamed the dry badlands of its island home and fed on plants. Adults could reach about 200 kg, and they carried a saddleback shell shaped to lift the neck for reaching vegetation. The species was declared extinct in 2012, after the death of Lonesome George, the last known individual.
slender_mongoose: The slender mongoose roams the lands of Africa south of the Sahara, moving through both savanna and forest. Weighing about 0.6 kilograms as an adult, it hunts meat as its main food and is active during the daytime. Its fur is a notable feature, and the species is still alive today.
squirrel_red_eurasian: The Eurasian red squirrel lives across Europe, the Siberian taiga, Scandinavia, and the British Isles. It spends its days in forests and taiga, moving through the trees and feeding during daylight hours. An adult weighs about 0.3 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
smooth_newt: The smooth newt is a small amphibian that spends much of its time in the water, where it swims with ease. It is found across Europe, the British Isles, Scandinavia, and the Siberian taiga. Adults live in wetlands and forests and feed on insects, and they weigh only about 5 grams.
merriams_elk: Merriam's elk, a subspecies of the Cervus canadensis group, once lived in forests and mountain country across a broad area of the American Southwest. Adults reached about 300 kilograms and fed on herbs, traveling in herds and bearing large antlers that made them prized as game. The subspecies was recorded as extinct in 1906.
spiny_tailed_iguana: The Black Spiny-tailed Iguana is a still-living reptile found across Mexico and Central America. It makes its home in forests, savannas, and coastal areas, and it is active during the day. Adults can reach about 1.5 kg, and they eat both plants and animals.
helmeted_hornbill: Still living, the helmeted hornbill makes its home in the jungles of Sundaland and Indochina. Adults weigh about 3 kg and feed mainly on fruit. Its solid casque, the bony crest on its head, has been carved as hornbill ivory, and the bird is known to fly through the forest canopy.
andean_cat: The Andean mountain cat roams the high ranges of the Andes, moving across rocky slopes and badlands where few other predators can survive. It is a meat eater, and an adult typically weighs about 4.5 kilograms. Its thick fur helps it endure the cold at high altitude, and the species is protected, though it remains alive and in the wild.
philippine_cobra: The Philippine cobra roams forests and grasslands across its range in the Philippines, where it lives in areas 5, 19, 117, and 127. It feeds on other animals and typically reaches about 2 kilograms as an adult. Covered in smooth scales, this venomous snake can spit venom at a threat, and the species remains alive and well today.
nyala: The nyala is a medium-sized antelope found across a broad band of southern Africa, stretching roughly from the Limpopo region down toward the eastern coast. It moves between forest edges and open savanna, grazing on herbs and feeding on the tender plants within its range. Adult males weigh about 90 kilograms and carry spiralled horns, and the species remains widespread and alive today, making it a prized target for hunters.
southern_pudu: The southern pudu is one of the smallest deer in the world, with adults weighing about 11 kilograms. It lives in forests across a band of southern South America, roughly between latitudes 35 and 47 degrees south. It feeds on herbs, and the males grow small, sharp antlers. The species is still alive today.
bonobo: Bonobos, known scientifically as Pan paniscus, live in jungle habitats within the area bounded by coordinates -5, 3, 18, and 26. They are omnivores that eat a mixed diet, and adults weigh around 40 kg. These animals live in herds, are active during the day, and are protected, and they are still alive today.
mole_snake: The mole snake of southern Africa makes its home in grassland and savanna, where it often shelters in burrows. It is a carnivore, and adults typically weigh around 1.5 kilograms. Its body is covered in scales, and it hunts by constriction. This species is still widespread and not extinct.
african_buffalo: African buffalo roam the savannas, grasslands, and wetlands of Africa south of the Sahara and across the Sahel. These grazers feed on grasses and other herbs, and adults can weigh around 700 kg. Living in herds, they carry horns and are known as both a hunted game animal and a dangerous one.
ringed_seal: The ringed seal makes its home across the Arctic Ocean and in the Baltic and North Sea, favoring icy waters where it can find cold, open habitat. Adults typically weigh around 70 kg and feed on meat-based prey. Thick blubber keeps it warm, and it keeps breathing holes open in the ice, which is why it is still hunted in some areas.
hydruntine: The European wild ass once roamed the plains of Europe, Iran and Anatolia, and parts of the Mediterranean. It grazed on herbs and grew to an adult mass of about 200 kg. These animals lived in herds and were hunted by people, and the species had died out by around 2000 BC.
eld_deer: Eld's deer lives across Indochina and the Indian subcontinent, moving through grasslands and wetlands where it feeds on herbs. An adult typically weighs about 100 kg. These animals gather in herds, and their antlers make them a recognizable sight, while they remain a huntable species that still survives in the wild.
gorgosaurus: Gorgosaurus libratus lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 77 to 75 million years ago, during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation. Weighing about 2400 kilograms as an adult, this carnivore stood at the top of the food chain in its Judith River age ecosystem.
african_bush_elephant: Roaming the savannas and forests south of the Sahara and across the Sahel, the African bush elephant is a plant eater that can weigh as much as 5500 kilograms. Herds move together under the guidance of experienced females, and the species is still very much alive today. Its long tusks have long been prized for their ivory, and in some places the animal is still hunted.
asiatic_black_bear: The Asiatic black bear roams forests and mountains across the Himalaya, Tibet, Indochina, the Chinese lowlands, Japan, Korea, Iran, and Anatolia. Adults can weigh around 110 kilograms, and they eat a mixed diet of plants and animals. A pale crescent-shaped mark on the chest sets this bear apart, and its thick fur is prized by hunters. Many populations hibernate through the cold months.
rodrigues_day_gecko: The Rodrigues Day Gecko once lived on the island of Rodrigues in the Mascarene archipelago, where it made its home in forest habitats. Active during the daylight hours, this small lizard weighed only about 0.02 kg as an adult and fed on a mixed diet of both plants and animals. It was last recorded in 1917 AD, and its disappearance marks a loss from the island's native wildlife.
travancore_tortoise: The Travancore tortoise, known scientifically as Indotestudo travancorica, lives in forests and jungle across its range, which the records place in areas 8, 13, 74 and 78. It eats both plants and animals, and a full-grown adult weighs about 3 kilograms. Its domed shell is its most notable feature, and the species remains alive today.
tayra: The tayra (Eira barbara) roams the Neotropics, from Mexico through Central America. It lives in jungle and forest, where it moves through the trees during the day. Adults weigh about 5 kg, and this omnivore eats a varied diet while its dense fur keeps it warm.
albertosaurus: Living roughly 71 to 69 million years ago during the Cretaceous, this predator is known only from fossils. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation in northwestern North America. Adults weighed about 2000 kilograms, and it was a carnivore that may have hunted in packs.
eastern_indigo_snake: The Eastern Indigo Snake is the largest native snake in the Americas, and it still lives across Florida and the Gulf Coast states of the southern United States. It moves through forests, grasslands, and swamps, where it hunts other snakes and shares burrows with gopher tortoises. An adult typically weighs about 3.5 kg. It is protected by law.
lemur_ruffed_blackwhite: The black-and-white ruffed lemur is a still-living primate that moves through the jungle canopy. It is active during the daytime and mainly eats fruit. Adults weigh about 3.5 kg, and the species is under legal protection.
phytosaurus: Rutiodon carolinensis was a fossil reptile from the Triassic, living roughly 228 to 210 million years ago. Its remains come from mudstone of the Pekin Formation in the Chatham Group of eastern North America. It looked much like a crocodile, but its nostrils sat far back near the eyes, and adults weighed about 300 kilograms. It ate fish.
european_pond_turtle: The European pond turtle is found across Europe, around the Mediterranean, and into Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home in lakes, wetlands, and rivers, eating a mix of plant and animal food. Adults weigh about 1 kg, and this species, still widespread today, swims well and spends the cold months hibernating.
boa_madagascar_ground: The Madagascar ground boa lives on the island of Madagascar, where it moves through both forest and savanna. It is a constrictor that hunts meat and wraps its prey before swallowing it whole. Adults reach about 10 kilograms, and this species is nocturnal, so it is most active after dark.
anteater_silky: Up in the jungle canopy, the silky anteater spends its nights hunting insects while it hangs from branches. It weighs only about a quarter of a kilogram as an adult and lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as parts of Central America. This species is still alive and widespread, and it is active only after dark.
pterygotus: Pterygotus anglicus was a fossil sea scorpion that lived during the Devonian period, roughly 410 to 400 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Arbuthnott-Garvock Group, part of the Old Red Sandstone in the British Isles. This carnivore is thought to have weighed about 30 kilograms as an adult, and it moved through the water with a swimming motion, using large claws to seize its prey.
kaprosuchus: A fossil crocodyliform from the Cretaceous, living roughly 100 to 95 million years ago, its remains were found in sandstone of the Echkar Formation in the Sahara. This carnivore weighed about 200 kilograms as an adult. Its nickname, BoarCroc, refers to the tusks that marked its skull.
vegas_valley_leopard_frog: The Las Vegas Leopard Frog was an amphibian that lived across the desert wetlands and rivers of the region between roughly 36 and 36.4 degrees north. Adults weighed about 0.1 kilograms and fed on other animals. It was declared extinct in 1950, largely because habitat loss destroyed the spring-fed wetlands it depended on.
northern_leopard_frog: Wetlands and grasslands across much of North America are home to this amphibian, which ranges from the Canadian Shield and Great Plains to the eastern and western parts of the continent. Adults weigh about 0.1 kg and feed mainly on insects. This species is still alive, and it is a strong swimmer that spends time in the water.
thorny_devil: The Thorny Devil is a small lizard of Australia's deserts that lives on a diet of insects, mostly ants. An adult weighs only about 0.05 kg, and its body is covered in spiky scales. It is active during the day, and its skin has grooves that draw water from the ground and channel it toward its mouth.
lowland_tapir: Weighing up to 220 kilograms, this herbivore roams the jungles, forests, and river banks of the Amazon, the Orinoco, the Pampas, and the Gran Chaco. It feeds on plants and is a strong swimmer that often escapes danger by slipping into the water. Though still alive in the wild, it is a hunted animal, which makes its survival a matter of ongoing concern.
sloth_ground_harlan: Harlan's ground sloth roamed grasslands and forests across North America south of 42 degrees north, from the southern United States through the Great Plains into Mexico. This herbivore weighed about 1500 kilograms as an adult and fed on plants. Its armoured skin marked it as one of the great megafauna that later vanished, dying out around 9000 BC.
european_green_toad: The European green toad is a small amphibian found across Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran, Anatolia, and the eastern steppe. It lives in grassland and desert country, where it feeds on insects. An adult weighs about 0.04 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
wapiti: Wapiti, also called elk in North America, roam forests, plains, and mountains across a wide range that stretches from western and northwestern North America to the Great Plains. Their range also reaches northern Asia, including the Mongolian steppe, the Siberian taiga, and parts of Japan and Korea. Adults can weigh around 320 kilograms, and they feed entirely on plants while living in herds.
common_hippo: Common hippos live in rivers, lakes, and wetlands across Africa south of the Sahara, in the Sahel, and along the Nile valley. They are herbivores that graze mostly on plants and move through water with ease. Adults can weigh about 1500 kg, and they gather in herds, though they can be dangerous to people who come too close. The species is still alive and widespread.
leopard_gecko: Found across the Indian subcontinent, Iran, and Anatolia, this living lizard makes its home in deserts and badlands. It is active at night, retreats to burrows during the day, and feeds on insects. An adult weighs only about 0.06 kg, and its body is covered in small scales.
huemul: The huemul is a deer that makes its home in the forests and mountains of the southern Andes, ranging across an area between roughly 35 and 52 degrees south latitude. Adults typically weigh around 90 kilograms and feed on herbs. Males grow antlers, and the species is still living today and is protected by law.
spotted_necked_otter: Found across Africa south of the Sahara, the spotted-necked otter lives in lakes and rivers. It weighs about 5 kg as an adult and feeds mainly on fish. Its dense fur helps it while it swims, and the species is still alive today.
kouprey: The kouprey is a wild ox that roams the forests and grasslands of Indochina, grazing on herbs. Adults can weigh around 750 kilograms, and they usually move through the landscape in herds. Although it is still alive, the species is protected and its numbers are so uncertain that it is considered possibly extinct.
dromedary: Dromedaries are herbivores that live in desert country across Arabia, the Sahara, Iran, and Anatolia. An adult can weigh around 500 kg, and these animals travel in herds. They have been domesticated for a long time and are valued for their milk. Wild populations disappeared around 2000 BC, though the species itself survives.
yellow_footed_tortoise: The yellow-footed tortoise roams the Amazon and Orinoco regions, moving through jungle and forest. Adults can reach about 20 kilograms, and this species is still alive in the wild. It eats a varied, omnivorous diet, is active during the day, and is hunted by people.
mosasaurus: Mosasaurus hoffmannii was a marine reptile that swam the seas of the Cretaceous period, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from chalk deposits of the Maastricht Chalk formation in Europe. Measuring about 12 metres long and weighing around 5000 kilograms as an adult, it hunted meat and stands as a baseline example of the mosasaurs.
capybara: The capybara is the largest living rodent, and adults reach about 50 kilograms. It lives in wetlands, rivers, and grasslands across the Amazon, Orinoco, Pampas, Gran Chaco, and Central America. Grazing on herbs, it moves through herds and spends much of its time in and near the water, where it swims well. Although still widespread, it is hunted in some areas.
himalayan_tahr: The Himalayan tahr roams the Himalaya and Tibet, moving between steep mountain slopes and forested areas. It grazes on plants and gathers in herds, with males and females both carrying curved horns. An adult typically weighs about 65 kg, and the species is still widespread and remains a huntable animal.
wisent: The European bison roams forests and plains across Europe, as well as in Iran and Anatolia. It grazes on herbs and can weigh as much as 600 kilograms as an adult. Once declared extinct in the wild in 1927, it was later reintroduced, and today it lives in herds and remains a huntable animal.
ploughshare_tortoise: The Ploughshare Tortoise makes its home on Madagascar, where it roams both forest and grassland. It feeds on herbs and grows to roughly 10 kg as an adult. A flat, protruding shell and a small horn-like projection under the chin set it apart, and because it is still alive but threatened, it is strictly protected.
pampas_deer: The pampas deer lives across the Pampas and Gran Chaco, as well as in Patagonia, where it roams open grassland and plains. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 35 kilograms as an adult. Males grow antlers, and the species is still alive today, though it is hunted in some areas.
trachyteuthis: Trachyteuthis is a fossil vampyropod, a group of cephalopods related to modern vampire squids and octopuses. It lived during the Jurassic, roughly 152 to 148 million years ago, and its remains have been pressed into the fine limestone of the Solnhofen formation in Europe. Preserved ink sacs in some specimens show that this carnivore weighed about half a kilogram as an adult.
juan_fernandez_fur_seal: The Juan Fernandez fur seal lives around islands and rocky coasts in a band of ocean roughly between 25 and 35 degrees south and 76 and 82 degrees west. Adults can weigh about 100 kilograms, and they feed on fish and other meat from the sea. They gather in herds on land and are protected by a thick, dense coat of fur.
alpine_ibex: Roaming the high Alps, the Alpine ibex makes its home among mountain slopes and icy ground. This herbivore feeds on plants and grows to an adult mass of about 80 kilograms. Living in herds, these animals are known for their long horns, and they remain alive today and can be hunted.
giant_otter: Giant otters hunt in family packs along rivers, swamps, and wetlands of the Amazon, Orinoco, Pampas, and Gran Chaco. Adults can reach about 30 kilograms, and their dense fur helps them stay warm while they swim. They feed mainly on fish and are active during the day. Their species is still alive but is legally protected.
ornitholestes: Ornitholestes was a small carnivorous dinosaur that lived in western North America during the Late Jurassic, roughly 152 to 148 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Morrison Formation. Adults weighed around 20 kilograms, and the animal is often described as a bird-catcher.
bezoar_ibex: Wild goats roam the mountains and badlands of Iran and Anatolia, where they graze on plants and can weigh around 60 kg as adults. They live in herds and carry horns that make them a prized target for hunters. This species is not extinct, and it is the ancestor of the domestic goat.
anhanguera: Known only from fossils, Anhanguera lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 113 to 110 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in limestone of the Romualdo (Santana) formation in South America. This fish catcher ate fish and weighed about 15 kg as an adult.
shuvuuia: Shuvuuia deserti is a feathered fossil known from the Djadochta formation of the Mongolian steppe, where it was preserved in sandstone. It lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago. Weighing about 1 kilogram as an adult, it likely hunted insects such as termites under the cover of night.
star_tortoise: The Indian Star Tortoise roams the Indian subcontinent, moving through savanna, forest, and grassland. Active during the day, it grazes on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 3 kg. Its domed shell bears a striking star-shaped pattern, and the species is still alive in the wild.
ornithocheirus: A crested, toothed pterosaur, Ornithocheirus simus lived during the Cretaceous period between roughly 112 and 105 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Cambridge Greensand formation in Europe, where they were preserved in marine sediment. This flying reptile fed on fish and weighed about 40 kg as an adult.
archaeothyris: Archaeothyris florensis lived during the Carboniferous period roughly 306 to 305 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Joggins Formation in eastern North America. This carnivore weighed about 5 kilograms as an adult and is recognized as the earliest known synapsid, a burrowing animal.
sinornithosaurus: Sinornithosaurus millenii lived in what is now China roughly 125 to 122 million years ago, during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils come from shale deposits of the Yixian Formation in the lowlands. This carnivore was feathered and weighed about 3 kilograms as an adult, and some researchers suspect it had venom.
repenomamus_robustus: Repenomamus robustus lived in the lowlands of what is now China during the Cretaceous, roughly 125 to 122 million years ago. Its fossils come from shale of the Yixian Formation, and adults weighed about 6 kilograms. This carnivore was a fossil mammal that preyed on young Psittacosaurus, a small dinosaur.
aegirocassis: Aegirocassis benmoulai was a giant radiodont that lived during the Ordovician, roughly 480 to 470 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in the shale of the Fezouata Formation on the northern African coast. Reaching about 2 meters long and an estimated 40 kilograms as an adult, it swam through ancient seas and fed by filtering food from the water.
oncilla: The oncilla is a small wild cat found in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, across Central America, and along the Andes. It lives in jungle, forest, and mountain country, where it hunts meat at night. Adults weigh about 2.2 kg, and its coat is patterned, which has earned it the nickname tiger cat. It is still alive in the wild.
cretan_wild_goat: The kri-kri lives only on the island of Crete and its nearby islets, where it climbs rocky mountain slopes. Adults weigh about 55 kilograms, and they graze on herbs while moving through the herd. Both sexes carry horns, and the animal is still alive today, though it may be hunted in some seasons.
indian_bullfrog: Found across the Indian subcontinent, the Indian Bullfrog makes its home in wetlands and rivers. This carnivorous amphibian is a capable swimmer, and adults can reach about 0.4 kg. It remains widespread today, and people in the region have long valued it as a food source.
schomburgks_deer: The Schomburgk's deer once roamed wetlands and grasslands, feeding on herbs and living in herds. Adults weighed around 110 kg, and males carried impressive antlers that made them a prized target for hunters. The last wild individual was shot in 1932, and the species has been extinct since that year.
reticulated_python: The reticulated python ranges across Indochina, Sundaland, Wallacea, New Guinea, and the Indian subcontinent, living in jungles, forests, and along rivers. It is a carnivore that kills its prey by constriction, and it is a strong swimmer. Adults can reach about 75 kg, and it is widely regarded as the longest snake in the world.
macaque_rhesus: The rhesus macaque is a still-thriving primate found across South and Southeast Asia, from the Himalaya and Tibet down through the China lowlands and Indochina. It makes its home in forests, jungles, and grasslands, and it eats a wide range of foods. Adults weigh about 8 kg, and these animals live in herds and are active during the day.
black_backed_jackal: The black-backed jackal roams the savannas and grasslands of East and Southern Africa, and it can also be found in desert country. An adult typically weighs around 9 kilograms. It is an omnivore that scavenges as often as it hunts, and it is most active at night. These jackals often live in pairs or small family packs, and their dark saddle of fur gives the species its name.
orinoco_crocodile: The Orinoco crocodile lives in the Amazon and Orinoco river systems of the Neotropics. It favors rivers, swamps, and wetlands, and it hunts meat as its diet. Adults can reach about 380 kg, and this species still survives in the wild today, where it is protected.
eustreptospondylus: Eustreptospondylus lived during the Jurassic, roughly 166 to 164 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from the Oxford Clay formation in the British Isles. This carnivorous dinosaur is thought to have weighed about 500 kg as an adult. It was a coastal megalosaurid, and its remains were found within limestone.
iguanodon: Iguanodon bernissartensis was a plant-eating fossil dinosaur that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 126 to 122 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in mudstone of the Sainte-Barbe formation near Bernissart in Europe. Adults could weigh around 3500 kg, and each thumb bore a distinctive spike.
persian_leopard: The Persian leopard lives in the mountains, forests, and badlands of Iran and Anatolia. Adults weigh around 65 kilograms, and they hunt meat as their main diet. They are active mostly at night and have thick fur, and the species is still alive today under legal protection.
eastern_racer: The North American Racer roams eastern North America, the southern United States, and the Great Plains, moving through both grassland and forest. This carnivorous snake typically weighs about half a kilogram as an adult. It is a fast, active hunter that is out and about during the day.
stellers_jay: Steller's jays are crested birds with deep blue bodies and dark heads, found across the Pacific Northwest, western North America, and into Mexico and Central America. They favor forests and mountain slopes, and they eat a varied diet of seeds, insects, and other small food. Weighing about 0.1 kg as adults, these clever birds are still common today.
giraffe_northern: Standing among the acacias of the savanna, the northern giraffe ranges across the Sahel, the Nile valley, East African grasslands, and parts of the Sahara. Adults can reach a mass of about 1200 kg, and they browse on herbs while moving through their herds. Though still alive in the wild, this tall species is hunted in some areas.
common_chameleon: The Common Chameleon lives along the Mediterranean coast, across northern Africa, and in parts of Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home in forests, coastal scrub, and savanna, climbing through the branches of trees. Insects make up its diet, and an adult typically weighs about 0.15 kilograms. This species is still alive and can change its colour.
nesophontes_cuban: The Cuban nesophontes was a tiny insect-eating mammal that lived in the forests of the Caribbean. An adult weighed only about 0.04 kilograms, making it a small creature even among shrews and similar animals. It lived on an island, and it disappeared around the year 1500 AD.
beaver_eurasian: The Eurasian beaver ranges across Europe, Scandinavia, and the Siberian taiga, where it makes its home along rivers, lakes, and forested waterways. Adults typically weigh about 20 kg. This semi-aquatic herbivore builds dams, feeds on plants, and has a thick fur coat. It is a huntable species that remains alive and well today.
toco_toucan: The toco toucan roams the Amazon basin as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco, moving between forest and open savanna. Its enormous bill is a striking feature, and it spends much of its time in the trees, though it can fly between branches. Adults weigh about 0.65 kilograms, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
mountain_zebra: The mountain zebra (Equus zebra) is a still-living species found across a region spanning roughly 35 degrees south to 14 degrees north and 15 to 28 degrees east in the south of Africa. It favors rugged mountains and badlands, and it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh around 260 kg, and they live in herds marked by their distinctive stripes, and they can be hunted.
hynerpeton: Hynerpeton bassetti was an early tetrapod that lived during the Devonian, roughly 365 to 362 million years ago. Its fossils come from sandstone of the Duncannon Member of the Catskill Formation in eastern North America. This carnivore reached about 15 kilograms and could both walk and swim, with a strong shoulder that hints at its ability to move on land.
asiatic_cheetah: The Asiatic cheetah ranges across Iran and Anatolia, Arabia, the Indian subcontinent, and the Kazakh steppe. It hunts meat in deserts, plains, and grasslands, and adults weigh about 42 kg. Active during the day and legally protected, it survives today, though the cheetah population in India disappeared during the 1950s.
hyneria: A massive lobe-finned predator, Hyneria lindae swam through Devonian waters roughly 365 to 362 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Catskill Formation, Duncannon Member, in eastern North America. Reaching about 3.5 meters long and weighing around 500 kilograms, it was a carnivore that hunted as it swam.
protoceratops: The Protoceratops lived across what is now the Mongolian steppe roughly 75 to 71 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils are preserved in sandstone of the Djadochta Formation, where it grazed on plants. A sheep-sized herbivore, it weighed about 180 kilograms as an adult and lacked the horns of its later relatives. One specimen is famously preserved locked in combat with a Velociraptor.
platypus: The platypus lives in eastern Australia and in Tasmania, where it makes its home in rivers and lakes. It hunts fish and other aquatic prey while swimming, and an adult weighs about 1.4 kilograms. This semi-aquatic mammal has a thick coat of fur and is an egg-laying species that also carries venom. It is still alive today and is protected.
pied_crow: Pied crows are found across Africa south of the Sahara, where they make their homes on open plains and along the coast. They eat almost anything, scavenging for food and catching insects in flight. An adult weighs about 0.55 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
acutiramus: Acutiramus macrophthalmus lived during the Silurian, roughly 425 to 420 million years ago, and its remains have been recovered from limestone of the Bertie Group's Fiddlers Green Formation in eastern North America. This carnivore was a swimmer that grew to about 2 meters long and weighed around 40 kilograms as an adult. It is known as a sea scorpion, and its club-shaped claws set it apart in the fossil record.
scelidosaurus: Scelidosaurus was an early armored dinosaur that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 196 to 190 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Charmouth Mudstone of the British Isles. This plant-eating animal weighed about 270 kilograms as an adult.
archaeoindris: Archaeoindris was a giant lemur that once lived in the forests of Madagascar, in the area between roughly 18 and 21 degrees south latitude and 45 and 48 degrees east longitude. This ground-dwelling herbivore weighed around 200 kilograms as an adult and moved slowly through its woodland home. It is thought to have died out around 500 AD.
stork_billed_kingfisher: Found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland, this kingfisher haunts rivers and coastlines alike. It feeds mainly on fish and weighs about 0.2 kg as an adult. Its feathers and flight are its notable traits, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
lemming_brown: The brown lemming makes its home across the Arctic, ranging through Alaska, the Yukon, and the Beringia region. It favors open tundra, where it feeds on plants and digs burrows for shelter. Adults weigh only about 0.08 kg, and their populations rise and fall in cyclic booms.
tarbosaurus: Tarbosaurus bataar was a large carnivore that lived between 70 and 66 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone deposits of the Nemegt Formation on the Mongolian steppe. Adults weighed about 4500 kilograms, and as an Asian tyrannosaur it was a close relative of Tyrannosaurus rex.
pere_davids_deer: Once common across the lowland wetlands of China, this deer grazes on herbs and aquatic plants while living in herds. Adults weigh about 200 kg, and males carry large antlers that made them prized as game. The species vanished from the wild around 1900, but a captive population descended from animals kept in European and Chinese collections has since survived.
sitatunga: The sitatunga is a still-living antelope found across the Congo basin, East African savanna, and southern Africa. It makes its home in swamps and wetlands, where it feeds on herbs. Adults weigh about 90 kg, and it is known for its ability to swim and for the horns it carries. It is also a huntable species.
sechuran_fox: Found in a band of coastal and lowland territory stretching roughly between 3 and 7 degrees south of the equator, the Sechuran fox makes its home in desert country. This nocturnal canine weighs about 3.5 kilograms as an adult and eats a mixed diet of both plant and animal food. Its thick fur helps it get through the region's conditions, and the species remains alive today.
european_whip_snake: The Western Whip Snake is found across Atlantic Europe, the Mediterranean, and into the Alps. It favors forests and grasslands, and it hunts other animals as a carnivore. Adults weigh about 0.6 kg, and this species is still alive and widespread. It is a fast, diurnal snake, so it is most active during the day.
new_guinea_crocodile: The New Guinea Crocodile is found across Wallacea and New Guinea, where it lives in rivers, swamps, and lakes. Adults typically weigh around 80 kilograms. Its diet is carnivorous, and it remains a living species. Its body is covered in scales, and it swims well through its watery home.
pliosaurus: Pliosaurus funkei was a marine reptile that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 152 to 145 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Agardhfjellet (Slottsmøya) formation in Scandinavia. It was a carnivore that reached about 10 metric tons in adult mass and stretched around 10 meters long.
brown_hyena: The brown hyena, known to the Khoekhoe as the strandwolf, roams the deserts, savannas, and coasts of southern Africa. It weighs about 42 kilograms as an adult and feeds mainly on carrion. Active at night, it keeps its shaggy brown fur through the dark hours and is still alive across its range today.
plains_zebra: Plains zebras roam the savannas and open plains of East and Southern Africa, grazing on grasses and other herbs. An adult typically weighs about 300 kg. Their herds are known for migrating over long distances in search of fresh pasture, and each animal's bold black and white stripes are unique to it.
eurhinosaurus: Known only from fossils, this marine reptile lived during the Jurassic, roughly 183 to 175 million years ago. Its remains come from the Posidonia Shale formation in Europe, where they were preserved in shale. It was carnivorous and grew to an adult mass of about 400 kg, and it is recognized by its sword-shaped snout.
porpoise_finless_narrow_ridged: The Indo-Pacific finless porpoise lives along coastlines from the Indo-Pacific region across the Indian subcontinent and into Sundaland. Adults weigh about 35 kilograms, and they hunt fish and other prey in coastal waters. Despite the name, this toothed whale is still living today, and it is recognized by the absence of a dorsal fin.
caecilian_seychelles: Burrowing through the soil of the Seychelles, this legless amphibian is a caecilian that lives on islands in forests and caves. It feeds on insects and weighs about 0.05 kg as an adult. Though it is an amphibian, its body is adapted for life underground, and it is still alive today.
tree_kangaroo_goodfellow: Goodfellow's tree-kangaroo makes its home in the jungles and mountain forests of New Guinea and parts of Wallacea. This herbivore feeds on plants and spends its days climbing through the trees, where it is active during daylight hours. Adults weigh about 8.5 kilograms, and the species is protected and still thriving in the wild.
vampyronassa: A small fossil cephalopod from the Jurassic, living roughly 165 to 160 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in limestone at the La Voulte-sur-Rhône site in Europe. Adults reached about 0.3 kg, and the animal was a carnivore. It belonged to a lineage related to the modern vampire squid.
acanthostega: Acanthostega lived during the Devonian, roughly 365 to 362 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Britta Dal Formation in Iceland and Greenland. This early tetrapod was a carnivore that reached an adult mass of about 8 kg. It swam through its watery home and is known for having eight fingers on its limbs.
addax: The addax is a pale antelope that roams the Sahara and the Sahel, where it lives in open desert country. It feeds almost entirely on plants and typically weighs about 100 kilograms as an adult. Addax move in herds and carry long, spiral horns, and they are still alive today, though they are hunted in some areas.
flying_fox_indian: The Indian flying fox roams the forests of the Indian subcontinent, where it feeds mainly on fruit. An adult weighs about 0.9 kilogram, making it one of the larger bats in its range. These nocturnal animals gather in large colonies, flying out after dark, and they are known to act as carriers of disease.
mountain_tapir: The mountain tapir roams the Andean highlands of northwestern South America, roughly between 5 degrees north and 10 degrees south latitude and 72 to 80 degrees west longitude. It favors mountain forests, where it grazes on herbs, and an adult typically weighs around 200 kilograms. Its thick, shaggy fur helps it endure cold, wet conditions, and it is a capable swimmer.
edible_frog: The edible frog lives across Europe and is found in wetlands and lakes. It is an amphibian that swims well and eats other small animals. Adults typically weigh about 0.1 kg, and the species is still alive today.
maiasaura: Maiasaura lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 77 to 76 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Two Medicine Formation. This herbivore grew to about 3000 kilograms, and its name means "good mother lizard," reflecting evidence that parents tended their young in colonial nesting grounds.
african_wild_ass: The African wild ass roams desert country, and the fact sheet places it in the Sahara in areas 8, 18, 34, and 45. It grazes on herbs and grows to about 250 kg as an adult. Living in herds, it is still alive today, and it is the ancestor of the domestic donkey.
cylindraspis_indica: The Reunion Giant Tortoise, known scientifically as Cylindraspis indica, once roamed the Mascarene Islands. It lived in island forests and grasslands, grazing on plants and reaching adult weights of about 150 kg. Sailors took many of these animals as provisions, and the species had died out by 1840 AD.
austroraptor: Austroraptor cabazai lived during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 68 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Allen Formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This dinosaur had a long snout, tiny arms, and an adult mass of about 300 kilograms, and it fed mainly on fish.
florida_scrub_jay: The Florida scrub jay lives in the state of Florida, roughly between 26.5 and 30.5 degrees north and 80 to 82.5 degrees west. It makes its home in open plains and forest, and it eats a mix of plant and animal food. Adults weigh about 80 grams, and this species is still alive today. Groups often breed together, with helpers assisting in raising the young.
olive_python: The olive python roams across northern Australia, moving through savanna, rugged badlands, and the banks of rivers. It is a carnivore that hunts mostly at night, and adults can reach about 20 kg. Like other constrictors, it wraps its body around prey to subdue it, and its smooth scales give it an olive sheen. It remains widespread and is still alive in the wild.
chinchilla_long_tailed: The long-tailed chinchilla lives in the Andes of South America, spanning roughly from central Chile through to northwestern Argentina. It makes its home in both mountain and desert terrain, where it feeds on plants and grasses. Adults weigh about 0.55 kg, and the species remains alive in the wild. Its dense fur, burrowing habits, and nocturnal, herd-dwelling lifestyle help it survive in harsh high country.
european_polecat: The European polecat roams Europe, including the Atlantic fringe and the British Isles, where it moves through forest, grassland, and wetland. It is a carnivore that weighs about 1.2 kilograms as an adult and hunts mainly at night. Its dense fur is prized, and it is the ancestor of the domestic ferret, which can be tamed.
kiang: The kiang is a wild ass that roams the high plains, icy slopes, and mountains of the Himalaya and Tibet. Adults weigh around 350 kilograms, and they graze on grasses and other herbs. They live in herds and are still thriving today, though they can be hunted in some areas.
titicaca_water_frog: The Titicaca water frog lives in the high lakes and mountain waters of the Andes, within a region spanning roughly 15 to 17 degrees south and 68.5 to 70 degrees west. This fully aquatic amphibian never leaves the water, and it has loose skin folds that help it take in oxygen at high altitude. It eats other animals and can reach an adult mass of about 0.5 kilograms. It is still living today.
cape_lion: The Cape lion once roamed the savanna and grassland of southern Africa, within a range stretching from about 35 to 28 degrees south and 17 to 30 degrees east. It was a meat eater, and adult males could reach around 200 kilograms. Its fur was distinguished by a mane with black-tipped hairs. The last known individual was killed in 1865.
miragaia: Miragaia longicollum lived during the Jurassic, roughly 152 to 150 million years ago, and its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Lourinhã Formation in Atlantic Europe. This plant-eating animal grew to an adult mass of about 1500 kilograms. Despite its name, which points to a long neck, it is a stegosaur, a group better known for plates and spikes.
kodkod: The kodkod is the smallest wild cat of the Americas, weighing about 2.2 kilograms as an adult. It makes its home in forests and mountain country within a range spanning parts of southern Chile and Argentina. Its thick fur and tree-climbing habits help it hunt small prey, and it is still alive in the wild today.
olenellus: Olenellus gilberti was a trilobite that lived during the Cambrian period, roughly 510 to 507 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in shale of the Pioche Shale formation in western North America. Adults weighed about 0.08 kilograms, and this spined, shelled creature is a classic example of an Early Cambrian trilobite. It fed by scavenging.
mandrill: Mandrills (Mandrillus sphinx) live in the forests and jungles of the Congo basin and along the western coast of Africa. These omnivores typically weigh about 25 kg as adults, and they are diurnal, moving through the day in herds. Their thick fur helps them get through their forest home, and the species is still alive today.
kentrosaurus: Kentrosaurus aethiopicus was a herbivorous fossil taxon that lived roughly 152 to 150 million years ago during the Jurassic period. Its remains come from the Tendaguru formation, where they were preserved in sandstone beneath what is now East African savanna. Adults weighed about 1500 kilograms, and the animal carried spikes on its shoulders and spines along its hips.
panamanian_golden_frog: Small and bright yellow, the Panamanian Golden Frog lives along jungle streams and rivers in a narrow stretch of western Panama. It feeds on insects and weighs only about five grams as an adult. Its skin carries toxins, and it is known for waving its hands. Although it is still alive, it has disappeared from the wild.
blue_duiker: The blue duiker is a tiny antelope that lives in forests and jungle across the Congo basin, along the West African coast, on the East African savanna, and in parts of southern Africa. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 5 kilograms as an adult. Although it still survives across this wide range, it is a small animal that hunters pursue, and it carries a short horn.
strawberry_poison_frog: Small as a fingernail and bright red, the Strawberry Poison-dart Frog lives in the jungles of Central America. It feeds on insects and weighs only about one gram as an adult. Its skin is toxic, a warning to predators, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
new_caledonian_crow: Found only on the island of New Caledonia and nearby islands, this crow lives in forest and eats a mix of plant and animal food. Adults weigh about 0.3 kg. It is well known for making and using tools from feathers and other materials, and it is considered a clever bird that is still alive today.
american_alligator: Still alive and widespread, the American alligator makes its home in the swamps, rivers, lakes, and wetlands of the southeastern United States, from Florida along the Gulf coast and into the eastern part of the country. Adults can reach about 230 kilograms, and they hunt other animals. Their armored scales protect them as they swim, and their hides and tail meat are valued, which is why alligators are managed as a huntable species.
mexican_grizzly: The Mexican grizzly once roamed the mountains and forests of Mexico, where it fed on a mix of plants and animals. Adults could weigh around 230 kilograms. Its fur was prized, and the last confirmed wild records of the subspecies date to 1964, when it was declared extinct.
sand_boa: The javelin sand boa is a small, still-living snake that spends much of its time underground. It ranges across the Mediterranean region, Iran, Anatolia, and the Sahara, where it favors deserts and badlands. Adults weigh about 0.3 kg, and the animal feeds on other creatures it catches.
barbary_sheep: Ammotragus lervia roams the Sahara and the North African coast, moving through deserts, mountains, and badlands. Adults weigh about 100 kg and feed on herbs. Living in herds, these animals remain widespread today and are often hunted for sport.
parsons_chameleon: Parson's Chameleon is still alive and makes its home in the jungles and forests of Madagascar. As the largest chameleon found on the island, it spends its time in the trees and feeds mainly on insects. An adult can reach about 0.7 kg, and its body is covered in scales.
arctic_wolf: The Arctic wolf, a subspecies of the gray wolf, roams the frozen tundra of the high Arctic, with populations found across Iceland, Greenland, Alaska, and the Yukon. Adults typically weigh about 45 kilograms and live in packs. Their thick white coat and small ears help them withstand icy conditions, and they hunt meat as their main food.
bushpig: Bushpigs roam across southern Africa, the East African savanna, and Madagascar, moving between forest and open savanna. These omnivores weigh around 80 kilograms as adults and eat a varied diet. They live in herds and are still widespread today, and people are permitted to hunt them.
eurasian_magpie: The Eurasian magpie roams the Palearctic across open plains and woodland edges, and it is still widespread today. An adult weighs about 0.22 kg, and it eats nearly anything it can find. Its black-and-white plumage is easy to spot, and it is known for its intelligence, passing the mirror self-recognition test and sometimes carrying off shiny objects.
bat_hammer_headed: The hammer-headed bat roams the jungles and wetlands of the Congo basin and the western African coast. It is a fruit eater that weighs about 0.4 kilograms as an adult, and it is loud and active only at night. Though not extinct, it remains a living bat that flies through its forest home after dark.
irritator: Irritator challengeri is known only from fossils, dating to between 113 and 110 million years ago in the Cretaceous period. Its remains were preserved in limestone of the Romualdo, or Santana, formation in South America, where it lived as a Brazilian spinosaurid. This fish-eating dinosaur is estimated to have weighed around 1000 kg as an adult.
gryposaurus: Gryposaurus notabilis was a plant-eating dinosaur that lived roughly 77 to 75 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation in northwestern North America. Adults reached about 2500 kilograms, and the animal was known for the hooked shape of its nose.
opossum_virginia: The Virginia opossum roams across eastern North America, Florida, the Gulf region, southern United States, and Mexico. It makes its home in forests, wetlands, and grasslands, and it eats almost anything it can find. Active only at night, this marsupial can reach about 3.5 kilograms as an adult, and when threatened it may feign death.
bettong_rufous: The rufous bettong is a small hopping marsupial that is still living today. Its adult mass is about 3 kg, and it spends its time in forest habitat across a range of latitude and longitude that covers parts of the Australian landscape. Active at night, it feeds on herbs and moves by hopping.
kit_fox: The kit fox makes its home in desert country across a broad stretch of western North America. It weighs about 2.2 kilograms as an adult and eats a varied diet of both plants and animals. Its pale fur helps it blend into the sand, and it spends the daylight hours resting in a burrow, emerging to hunt after dark.
african_golden_cat: The African golden cat roams the forests of the Congo basin, where it hunts small mammals and birds. An adult weighs about 11 kilograms. Active mostly at night, this cat is protected across much of its range, and it still survives in the wild today.
styxosaurus: Styxosaurus snowii lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 85 to 80 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the chalk of the Niobrara Chalk formation on the Great Plains. Adults reached about 1500 kilograms and fed on fish, and gastroliths preserved between its ribs hint at how it processed its food.
golden_jackal: Found across Europe, Southwest Asia, Arabia, the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and the Mediterranean, this canid roams grassland, desert, forest, and wetland alike. It eats a mixed diet and typically weighs about 10 kg as an adult. Active mostly at night, it is still widespread today, though its thick fur has made it a target for hunters.
meerkat: Meerkats live in southern Africa, where they make their home in deserts and grasslands. Adults weigh about 0.75 kg, and they feed mainly on insects. These social animals live in groups, stay active during the day, and shelter in burrows, with some members standing watch as sentinels.
knight_anole: The Knight Anole climbs the trees of Caribbean forests and jungles, where it spends most of its life high in the canopy. It is one of the largest anoles, with an adult weight of about 0.15 kilograms, and it feeds on both plants and small animals. Covered in scales and still thriving in the wild, this lizard is a common sight for anyone who looks upward in its home islands.
common_palm_civet: The Asian Palm Civet ranges across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Sundaland, and other parts of the Indomalayan region. It lives in forest and jungle, moving through the trees by night. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms, and their fur helps them stay hidden among the branches. Its diet is mainly fruit, and it is well known for eating coffee cherries.
malayan_krait: The Malayan Krait is a venomous snake found across Indochina and Sundaland, where it lives in forests and wetlands. It is nocturnal and feeds on other animals, and an adult typically weighs about 1 kilogram. Its body is covered in scales, and the species remains alive and widespread in the wild.
tapejara: Tapejara was a pterosaur that lived in what is now South America roughly 113 to 110 million years ago. Its fossils come from the Romualdo member of the Santana Formation, where they were preserved in limestone. Adults weighed about 5 kilograms, and the animal ate fruit. Its most striking feature was a huge sail-like crest on its skull.
indian_python: The Indian rock python roams the Indian subcontinent and reaches into the Himalaya and Tibet, moving through forests, savannas, and wetlands. Adults can weigh around 50 kilograms. As a carnivore, it hunts by constriction, and it is a protected species that still survives in the wild today.
cape_rain_frog: The Cape Rain Frog is a small, round amphibian that still survives in the wild. It lives in the badlands and coastal areas within a narrow band of southwestern Africa, where it feeds on insects. An adult weighs about 0.03 kilograms, and it spends much of its life in burrows.
south_american_coati: The South American coati roams across the Amazon and Orinoco basins, the Pampas and Gran Chaco, and the Andes. It lives in forest and jungle, where it forages by day in troops and climbs trees with ease. Its diet is omnivorous, and an adult typically weighs about 5 kg.
blue_tongued_skink: The Eastern Blue-tongued Skink calls Australia home, ranging across savanna, forest, and grassland. Adults typically weigh around 0.6 kg, and this lizard is active during the day. When threatened, it flashes its bright blue tongue as a warning display, and its diet is omnivorous.
archaeopteryx: A feathered fossil from the Jurassic, living roughly 150 to 148 million years ago, Archaeopteryx is known from specimens preserved in the fine limestone of the Solnhofen formation in Europe. It was a carnivore that weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult. Its feathers and bird-like traits make it one of the earliest known birds, showing how flight-related features first appeared.
mainland_serow: The mainland serow is a stocky goat-antelope that still roams wild across much of Asia. It makes its home in forests and mountain slopes, from Indochina and Sundaland through the Himalaya, Tibet, and the lowlands of China. Adults weigh around 120 kg and graze on herbs. Its horns and its value to hunters have made it a species to watch closely.
white_tailed_mongoose: The white-tailed mongoose roams the savannas of Africa south of the Sahara and across Arabia. It is a carnivore that weighs about 4 kilograms as an adult. Active at night, it has a coat of fur and remains widespread today.
muskox: Shaggy and heavy-set, the muskox roams the icy tundra of the far north, from Alaska and Yukon across Greenland and Iceland. Adults can weigh around 300 kilograms, and they graze on herbs while moving together in herds. Their long fur and the soft underwool called qiviut help them endure the cold, and their curved horns mark them as a traditional game animal.
paradoxides_davidis: Known only from fossils, this trilobite lived during the Cambrian, roughly 505 to 500 million years ago. Its remains turn up in shale of the Menevian Group in the British Isles. It likely fed as a scavenger, and it stood out among the trilobites of Avalonia, where some individuals reached about 40 centimeters with a shell of considerable size.
woolly_mammoth: The woolly mammoth roamed across northern Asia, Siberia, Europe, Beringia, Alaska, the Yukon, and the Great Plains, favoring tundra, taiga, and icy landscapes. Adults could weigh about 5500 kilograms, and they moved in herds while feeding on plants. Their long tusks and thick fur helped them survive the cold, and mainland populations lasted until about 8000 BC.
moose: Across much of the northern world, from Scandinavia and Siberia to the Canadian Shield and eastern North America, the moose roams taiga, forest, and wetland. It is a plant eater that can reach about 450 kg, and it grows large antlers and swims with ease. Hunting is permitted, and the species remains widespread today.
yellow_anaconda: The Yellow Anaconda is a large constrictor found across the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and the Amazon basin. It spends much of its life in wetlands, swamps, and rivers, where it swims well and hunts meat-eating prey. Adults can weigh around 25 kg, and the species remains living today.
wild_yak: Wild yaks roam the high plateaus and icy mountains of the Himalaya and Tibet, where they graze on grasses and other herbs across the tundra. A full-grown adult can weigh around 800 kilograms, and these animals move together in herds, relying on their dense fur and curved horns to endure the cold. Though still living in the wild, they have been hunted in the past and their cousins were tamed long ago.
bat_horseshoe_greater: Across Europe, parts of North Africa, Iran, Anatolia, the Himalaya, Tibet, Japan, and Korea, the greater horseshoe bat roosts in caves and moves through forests after dark. This nocturnal flier feeds entirely on insects and hibernates through the cold months. An adult weighs about 22 grams, and the species remains widespread today.
st_croix_racer: The St Croix Racer was a slender snake that lived on forested islands in the Caribbean, specifically in the area between roughly 17.6 and 17.9 degrees north and 64.5 and 65 degrees west. It fed on other animals and weighed about 0.2 kilograms as an adult. Introduced mongooses are noted among the factors linked to its disappearance, and the species was declared extinct in 1900 AD.
macaque_longtailed: Found across Indochina, Sundaland, Wallacea, and New Guinea, the long-tailed macaque lives in jungle, coastal, and forest habitats. It is an omnivore that weighs about 5 kg as an adult, and it is active during the day. Living in herds, these monkeys are also known to swim, and the species remains widespread today.
aristonectes: The fossil taxon Aristonectes parvidens lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 72 to 66 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from mudstone of the Snow Hill Island formation in Antarctica. Adults reached about 2500 kg, and it is known as a filter feeder.
fiji_banded_iguana: The Fiji Banded Iguana lives in forests on islands within the Fiji archipelago, spanning roughly 16 to 19 degrees south and 177 to 180 degrees east. It feeds on plants and weighs about 0.3 kilograms as an adult. Its body is covered in scales, and it spends much of its life in the trees, where it still survives today.
russells_viper: Russell's Viper is still living across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, where it moves through grassland, savanna, and forest. This carnivore typically weighs around 1.5 kilograms as an adult. Its body is covered in scales, it is venomous, and it defends itself with a loud hiss, making it a deadly snake to be avoided.
ornithomimus: Lived in what is now northwestern North America during the Cretaceous, roughly 71 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Horseshoe Canyon Formation. This feathered ornithomimid is thought to have been omnivorous and weighed about 170 kilograms as an adult.
thomsons_gazelle: Roaming the open grasslands of East Africa, this gazelle lives in herds and often moves across the plains in migrations. Adults weigh about 22 kilograms, and both sexes carry slender horns. It feeds on herbs and is still widespread today, though it remains a animal hunters may pursue.
monocled_cobra: The monocled cobra makes its home across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, moving through wetlands and forests alike. Adults typically weigh about 2 kg, and they hunt other animals for food. Covered in scales and armed with venom, this snake spreads its hood when threatened and is a capable swimmer.
coral_snake: The Eastern Coral Snake makes its home in Florida, the Gulf states, and across the eastern United States, where it moves through forests and swampy ground. It spends much of its time burrowing and feeds on other snakes. Adults weigh about 0.1 kg, and its bright banded scales warn of a venom that is potent enough to be dangerous to people.
atlas_bear: The Atlas bear was a subspecies of brown bear found in the mountains and forests of northwest Africa, in the region spanning roughly 30 to 37 degrees north and 10 degrees west to 12 degrees east. Adults could reach about 250 kilograms, and the animal ate a mixed diet of plants and other food. It was the only bear native to Africa, and its thick fur set it apart from other populations. The last known individual was killed around 1870.
siberian_salamander: The Siberian Salamander makes its home across the taiga, tundra, and wetlands of Siberia, northern Asia, Japan, and Korea. It feeds on insects and weighs about 0.03 kilograms as an adult. This amphibian can freeze solid and still survive, showing an unusual tolerance for extreme cold.
possum_sugar_glider: At night, the sugar glider glides between trees in the forests of Wallacea and New Guinea, using a membrane stretched along its body to cover long distances. It lives high in the canopy, eats a mix of plant and animal foods, and weighs only about 0.13 kilograms as an adult. This small marsupial is still thriving in the wild.
plateosaurus: Known only from fossils, Plateosaurus lived during the Triassic, roughly 214 to 204 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Trossingen Formation in Europe. This herbivore grew to about 600 kilograms as an adult, and researchers link it to herds of prosauropods that roamed the Triassic landscape.
pterosaur_lacewing_kalligrammatid: Known only from fossils pressed into limestone in the Solnhofen formation of Europe, this butterfly-like lacewing lived during the Jurassic, roughly 152 to 148 million years ago. Adults weighed about half a gram and fed on nectar. Its larger relatives are known from the Yixian formation.
jamaican_giant_galliwasp: The Jamaican Giant Galliwasp was a lizard found only on the island of Jamaica, where it lived in forests. It was a carnivore that weighed around 1 kilogram as an adult and was active at night. Introduced mongooses are thought to have contributed to its disappearance, and it was last recorded in 1840 AD.
kangaroo_eastern_grey: Eastern grey kangaroos roam across eastern Australia and Tasmania, moving between forest edges and open grassland. These herbivores feed on plants and gather in groups called herds. An adult typically weighs around 45 kg, and the species remains widespread today.
cape_fur_seal: The Cape fur seal lives along the southern coasts of Africa and in parts of southern Australia, where it favours cold ocean waters near the shore.
