It is a carnivore that hunts in the sea, and adults can reach about 200 kg. Individuals gather in herds, and a thick layer of blubber helps them stay warm. The species is still alive and widespread.
barbary_lion: The Barbary Lion once roamed the mountains, forests, and grasslands of North Africa, where it hunted as a carnivore. Adults could reach about 220 kg, and they were known for their heavy fur and thick manes. Hunting took a severe toll, and the last wild individual was shot in the Atlas Mountains in 1942.
sable_antelope: Sable antelopes graze and browse across the savannas of southern Africa and the East African plains, and they also move through open woodland. Adults weigh about 230 kg and feed on herbs. They live in herds, carry long curved horns, and are hunted as game, though bulls can be aggressive when threatened.
myotragus: Once roaming the mountains of the Balearic Islands, this small herbivore weighed about 50 kilograms as an adult and fed entirely on plants. Its legs were short, and it carried horns, traits suited to life on an isolated island. Settlers hunted it out, and it disappeared around 2500 BC.
amplectobelua: Amplectobelua was a radiodont, a group of early marine predators that swam through Cambrian seas. It lived roughly 518 to 514 million years ago, and its fossils are preserved in the shale of the Maotianshan formation within the Chengjiang Biota in China's lowlands. This carnivore grew to about 0.3 kilograms and used its raptorial appendages to seize prey as it swam.
american_badger: The American badger roams the Great Plains, western North America, and parts of Mexico, where it favors grasslands, prairies, and desert country. An adult typically weighs about 8 kilograms. This nocturnal carnivore is a powerful digger with a thick coat, and it uses its strong claws to excavate burrows in pursuit of prey.
habu: Found on the islands of Japan and Korea, the Okinawa habu makes its home in forests and across island landscapes. This venomous snake feeds on other animals and, as an adult, typically weighs about 2 kg. Active mostly at night, it uses pit organs to sense the warmth of its prey.
archaeolemur: The monkey lemur was a large, baboon-like primate that once lived on Madagascar. It moved mostly on the ground and ate a mixed diet of plant and animal foods. Adults weighed about 22 kg, and the species disappeared around 1500 AD. It was a giant lemur that roamed forests, deserts, and grasslands across the island.
couchs_spadefoot: Spending most of its life underground, this desert amphibian digs burrows across the southern United States and Mexico. It aestivates through long dry spells, staying dormant until rain arrives. Its diet consists of insects, and an adult weighs about 0.04 kilograms.
angulate_tortoise: The Angulate Tortoise lives in southern Africa, where it makes its home in coastal areas and badlands. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 1.5 kilograms. Its shell is a defining feature, and the species remains alive today.
chinese_fire_belly_newt: This small amphibian makes its home in the lowlands of China, where it lives in wetlands and rivers. Adults weigh only about 0.01 kg, and they feed on other small animals. Its skin is toxic, a defense that helps it avoid predators, and the species remains alive today.
sail_fin_monitor_gould: Gould's Monitor is a lizard found across Australia, where it lives in savanna, desert, and grassland. It is a carnivore, and adults typically weigh about 3 kg. This diurnal species is still alive today and often shelters in burrows, where it retreats from the heat and rests.
singing_dog: The New Guinea Singing Dog lives in Wallacea and New Guinea, where it roams mountain, forest, and jungle country. It is a carnivore that typically weighs around 12 kg as an adult. This dog is still alive today, and its thick fur and howling calls set it apart. Its presence on the island dates to after roughly 4000 BC, when humans are thought to have brought it there.
black_footed_ferret: Hunting mostly at night across the Great Plains, the black-footed ferret depends on prairie dog colonies for both food and shelter. Adults weigh about 1 kilogram and spend much of their lives underground in the burrows they share with their prey. Though the species is still alive, it is protected because its numbers have long been very low.
deinosuchus: Deinosuchus was a giant alligatoroid that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 82 to 73 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Aguja Formation in the southern United States. This carnivore could reach an adult mass of about 5000 kilograms, and it preyed on dinosaurs.
large_spotted_genet: The large-spotted genet is a slender, spotted carnivore found across southern Africa, the East African savanna, and the Congo basin. It lives in both forest and savanna, and it hunts mainly at night. Adults weigh about 2.5 kilograms, and it spends much of its time in trees.
brothers_tuatara: Found only on a small island off the coast of New Zealand, the Brothers Island tuatara is still alive today. Adults can reach about half a kilogram and feed mainly on insects. These nocturnal reptiles are covered in scales, rest in burrows, and are protected by law.
common_wall_lizard: The Common Wall Lizard is a small, daytime-active reptile found across Europe and the Mediterranean. It lives in mountain and forest settings, where it hunts insects. An adult weighs roughly 0.01 kg, and the species is still alive and widespread.
crocodile_monitor: Also called the Papuan crocodile monitor, this lizard calls the forests of Wallacea and New Guinea home. It climbs through jungle and woodland canopy and hunts meat-based prey. Adults often weigh around 20 kilograms, and it holds the title of the longest lizard in the world.
western_jackdaw: Found across Europe, the Mediterranean, Iran, and Anatolia, the western jackdaw is a still-thriving bird of plains and coastlines. It eats almost anything it can find, and an adult weighs about 0.24 kg. Known for its intelligence, this smart and social species often gathers in flocks and is a skilled flier.
forest_buffalo: The forest buffalo lives in the Congo basin and along the West African coast, moving through forest and jungle. It feeds on plants and grasses, and a full-grown adult can weigh around 270 kilograms. These animals live in herds and carry horns, and they remain alive today even though people hunt them.
indian_rhino: The Indian rhinoceros, known scientifically as Rhinoceros unicornis, makes its home across the Indian subcontinent. It moves through grassland and wetland areas, grazing on herbs, and an adult can weigh about 2000 kg. Its single horn and its ability to swim are among its most notable traits, and the species is still alive today.
sunda_clouded_leopard: Found on the islands of Borneo and Sumatra, this cat spends much of its life in jungle and forest canopy. It hunts by night and climbs with ease, using its long tail for balance. Adults weigh about 13 kg, and the species is legally protected.
nigersaurus: Nigersaurus lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 115 to 105 million years ago. Its fossils come from sandstone of the Elrhaz Formation in the Sahel region. This herbivore reached an adult mass of about 4000 kilograms and had a broad, wide muzzle packed with hundreds of teeth.
asiatic_lion: Once spread across Iran, Anatolia, Arabia, and the Indian subcontinent, this carnivore now survives only in the Gir forest region. Adults may weigh around 160 kg, and they hunt in grassland, savanna, and forest. Their fur and a distinctive belly fold set them apart, and they live in prides protected by law.
possum_common_ringtail: Dwelling in forests across Tasmania, this nocturnal possum spends its days among the trees and moves through the canopy with ease. Its prehensile tail helps it grip branches as it feeds on plants. An adult typically weighs about 0.9 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today.
fiji_crested_iguana: The Fiji Crested Iguana is a tree-dwelling lizard that still survives today. It lives in the forests of islands within the Fiji region, where it feeds mainly on plants. Adults typically weigh around 0.3 kg, and the species is legally protected.
martinique_giant_ameiva: The Martinique Giant Ameiva once lived across forested areas of the island of Martinique, roughly between 14.3 and 14.9 degrees north latitude. It was an omnivore, eating a mix of plants and small animals, and was active during the day. Adults weighed about 0.2 kg before the species was lost in 1900 AD.
fire_salamander: The fire salamander is an amphibian found across Europe, including the Alps, Atlantic Europe, and the Mediterranean region. It lives in forests and mountain areas, where it hunts small prey and is active mainly at night. Its bright yellow and black markings serve as a warning colour, and its skin is toxic to predators.
mali_uromastyx: The Mali uromastyx is a herbivorous lizard found across the Sahel and Sahara, where it lives in desert and savanna country. Adults typically weigh about half a kilogram. Active by day, it shelters in burrows and is known for its scaly, armored body, and it remains widespread in the wild today.
rattlesnake: The Eastern Diamondback Rattlesnake lives across Florida and the Gulf coast of the southern United States. It moves through forests, grasslands, and coastal areas, hunting other animals for food. Adults can reach a mass of about 4 kilograms. This venomous snake uses heat-sensing pit organs to find prey and shakes its rattle as a warning.
central_bearded_dragon: Native to Australia, the Central Bearded Dragon makes its home in deserts, savannas, and badlands. It is active during the day and eats both plants and insects, so its diet is omnivorous. Adults typically reach about 0.4 kg, and the species is still thriving in the wild. When threatened or courting, it puffs out the spiky, dark skin under its throat to display its beard.
cretaceous_amber_flea: Known only from fossils, this giant flea lived during the Jurassic, roughly 165 to 160 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in mudstone of the Daohugou formation in the lowlands of China. Adults weighed about a tenth of a gram, and the animal fed on insects while it likely lived on pterosaurs and feathered dinosaurs.
armadillo_pink_fairy: The pink fairy armadillo is a tiny, still-living species found across a desert region of South America. Weighing roughly 0.1 kilograms as an adult, it spends its nights foraging for insects and retreats into burrows during the day. Its nocturnal habits and small size make it one of the more elusive armadillos of its region.
asian_golden_cat: The Asian golden cat roams across Indochina, Sundaland, the Himalaya and Tibet, and the lowlands of China. It lives in jungle, forest, and mountain country, and it hunts other animals for its meat. An adult typically weighs about 13 kilograms. Its coat is prized in the fur trade, so the species is legally protected, and it still survives in the wild.
yellow_billed_magpie: The yellow-billed magpie is found only in California, where it lives across open plains and forested areas. It eats a wide mix of foods and weighs about 0.17 kg as an adult. Known for its intelligence and its strong, flapping flight, this bird is still thriving and has not gone extinct.
lord_howe_skink: The Lord Howe Island skink lives on and around the coast of Lord Howe Island, a small island in the Tasman Sea between 31.4 and 31.7 degrees south. It is a small, diurnal lizard that hunts insects and weighs only about five grams as an adult. It remains alive today.
snub_nosed_golden: Golden snub-nosed monkeys live in forests and on mountains, from the lowlands of China to the Himalaya and Tibet. These diurnal primates form herds and feed mainly on plants. Adults weigh about 15 kg, and their thick golden fur helps them handle the cold of high elevations.
capuchin_tufted: Tufted capuchins roam the forests of the Amazon and Orinoco basins in South America. These omnivores eat a mix of fruits, insects, and other foods, and adults typically weigh about 3.5 kilograms. Active during the day, they travel together in troops and are known to use tools.
syrian_wild_ass: The Syrian wild ass once roamed desert lands in the region marked by the coordinates 28, 38, 35, 48. It grazed on herbs and grew to an adult mass of about 200 kg, living in herds that made it a target for hunters. The last known individual died in 1927 AD, and the subspecies is now extinct.
batagur: The Southern River Terrapin is a turtle found in Sundaland and Indochina, living in rivers and along coasts. Adults can reach about 20 kg, and they feed mainly on plants. This species still survives in the wild, and it swims through both freshwater and brackish water.
mountain_gazelle: Roaming the rocky slopes and grassy uplands of the Arabian Peninsula and nearby highlands, the mountain gazelle grazes on herbs and grasses. Adults weigh about 22 kilograms, and they travel together in herds where both males and females carry slender horns. Although the species is still alive, it can be hunted in some places, which makes its wellbeing worth watching.
red_bellied_black_snake: Found across Australia, this venomous snake makes its home in wetlands, forests, and along rivers. It hunts prey such as frogs and other small animals, and adults typically weigh about 1.2 kg. Its strong swimming ability helps it move through the waterways it favors, and it remains widespread today.
nautilus_cenoceras: Cenoceras is an extinct nautiloid that lived during the Jurassic period, roughly 182 to 175 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Lias formation in the British Isles. Adults are thought to have weighed about 0.3 kilograms, and the animal fed on other creatures.
collared_peccary: Collared peccaries roam a huge range that stretches from the southern United States through Mexico and Central America, and on into the Amazon, the Orinoco, the Pampas, and the Gran Chaco. They live in forests, deserts, and jungles, and they travel in herds. An adult typically weighs about 25 kg, and these animals eat both plants and meat. Hunters pursue them, and their strong musky scent is one of their most noticeable traits.
mugger_crocodile: The mugger crocodile makes its home across the Indian subcontinent, where it lives in rivers, lakes, swamps, and other wetlands. It is a meat eater that can grow to about 200 kilograms as an adult. Its body is covered in scales, it swims well, and it digs burrows to shelter in. This species is still alive today.
amethystine_python: Found across Wallacea, New Guinea, and northern Australia, this python makes its home in jungle and forest. Its scales have an iridescent sheen, and like other constrictors it kills prey by coiling tightly around it. Adults can reach about 40 kilograms, and the species is still living in the wild.
ancient_bison: Ancient bison roamed the grasslands and plains of the Great Plains, western and eastern North America, and Mexico. These herbivores grazed on plant matter and could reach an adult mass of about 1000 kg. They lived in herds, and they were hunted for their horns and thick fur before disappearing around 8000 years ago.
gorilla_mountain: Mountain gorillas live in the highlands along the borders of Rwanda, Uganda, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. They roam through forest and mountain habitats, feeding mainly on plants and staying active during the day. Living in herds, adult males can weigh about 160 kilograms, and their thick fur helps them endure cool mountain air. Although still alive, they are a protected species.
big_headed_turtle: The big-headed turtle is found in the lowlands of Indochina and China, where it lives along rivers and in mountain streams. It feeds mainly on meat and typically weighs about half a kilogram as an adult. This species can climb and swim with ease, and its long, hinged shell is one of its most distinctive features.
macaque_japanese: Japanese macaques live in troops in the forests and mountains of Japan and Korea. Active during the day, they eat a varied diet of plants and animal foods. Adults typically weigh about 11 kilograms, and their thick fur helps them endure cold mountain winters.
banteng: The banteng is a wild cattle species found across Indochina and Sundaland, ranging through forest, jungle, and grassland. It feeds entirely on herbs and grazes in herds. Adults can weigh around 650 kg, and both sexes carry horns. Although it is still alive in the wild, it can be hunted, and it has also been domesticated.
fence_lizard: The Eastern Fence Lizard makes its home across eastern North America and the southern United States. It turns up in both forests and grasslands, where it hunts insects. An adult weighs about 0.01 kg, and this small reptile is still thriving in the wild today.
least_weasel: The smallest carnivore in the world, the least weasel weighs only about 0.1 kilograms as an adult. It lives across the Nearctic, Palearctic, and Europe, hunting in grassland, forest, and tundra. Its diet is carnivorous, and it makes its home in burrows, with a fur coat that helps it stay active in cold places.
goliath_frog: The largest frog in the world, the Goliath Frog reaches adult weights of about 3 kg. It lives in rivers and jungle streams along the West African coast and across the Congo basin, where it hunts other animals. Strong swimmer that it is, this amphibian is still alive today, though it is hunted for food and is legally protected.
great_hornbill: Found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland, the great hornbill makes its home in jungle. Adults weigh about 3 kg, and the species is still alive in the wild. Its diet is mostly fruit, and it spends much of its time in the trees, where it sometimes seals its nest with mud and feces. Its distinctive casque sits on top of the bill.
babirusa: Found only on the Indonesian island of Sulawesi, this wild pig lives in forests and wetlands and eats a mix of plant and animal foods. Adults typically weigh about 90 kg. Its most striking feature is a pair of curved tusks, and the species is still alive today.
side_striped_jackal: Roaming across the sub-Saharan savanna, forest edges, and wetlands, the side-striped jackal eats a mix of plant and animal food. An adult weighs about 10 kilograms. Its coat is thick, and it is active mostly at night. This species is still alive and widespread.
echidna_long_beaked_western: The western long-beaked echidna is an egg-laying mammal that roams the jungles and mountains of Wallacea and New Guinea. Its long snout and sharp spines protect it as it searches for insects, and it is mostly active at night. Adults can weigh around 10 kilograms, and the species is still alive and legally protected.
wild_bactrian_camel: The wild Bactrian camel roams the deserts and badlands of Mongolia and its surrounding range, where it grazes on herbs. Adults can weigh around 600 kilograms. Living in herds, these animals are protected, and they still survive in the wild today.
eastern_elk: The eastern elk once roamed the forests and plains of eastern North America, grazing on herbs in herds. Adults could weigh around 350 kg, and males carried large antlers that made them prized by hunters. The last known eastern elk was shot in 1877, and the subspecies was declared extinct that year.
western_black_rhino: The Western black rhinoceros once roamed the savanna of its range, feeding on herbs and weighing about 1000 kg as an adult. Its horn made it a target for poaching, and the subspecies was declared extinct in 2011. Its story remains a sober reminder of how human demand for horn can wipe out a population.
bat_straw_coloured: The straw-coloured fruit bat roams across Africa south of the Sahara and into the Sahel, moving between forest and savanna. Adults weigh about 0.26 kg, and they feed on fruit at night. These bats travel in large colonies and migrate with the seasons, and they remain widespread today.
otter_shrew_giant: Found along rivers in the Congo basin and on parts of the West African coast, this semi-aquatic creature hunts fish beneath the surface. It is nocturnal, so most of its activity happens after dark. An adult typically weighs about 0.4 kg, and the species remains alive and well today.
red_brocket: The red brocket, Mazama americana, roams forests and jungles across the Amazon and Orinoco basins, Central America, and the Southern Cone. This plant-eating deer typically weighs around 30 kilograms as an adult and remains widespread today. Males grow antlers, and the species is hunted in parts of its range.
caspian_seal: The Caspian seal lives in the Caspian and Black seas, where it hunts fish along both lake and coastal waters. An adult typically weighs around 55 kilograms, and a thick layer of blubber keeps it warm in the cold seas it calls home. Living in herds, these seals are still with us today and are protected by law.
orangutan_bornean: The Bornean orangutan is a solitary, tree-dwelling primate found in the jungles of the island of Borneo. It is active during the day and feeds mainly on fruit. Adults weigh around 60 kg, and the species is still living and is protected.
lechwe: Herds of southern lechwe graze the seasonally flooded wetlands and swamps of the southern part of the continent, living across the region spanning roughly latitude -18 to -12 and longitude 22 to 30. These herbivores typically weigh about 100 kg as adults and carry horns of their own. They are strong swimmers, and the species is still alive and can be hunted.
grevys_zebra: Grevy's zebra, known scientifically as Equus grevyi, is the largest of all zebra species, with adults weighing around 400 kg. It lives in deserts and savannas across a region spanning parts of northern Kenya and Ethiopia, where it grazes on grasses and other plants. These animals form herds, and their narrow, closely packed stripes set them apart from other zebras. The species is still alive today, though it is hunted in some areas.
minmi: Minmi was a small armored dinosaur that lived in what is now Queensland, Australia, roughly 119 to 113 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its fossils were preserved in mudstone of the Bungil Formation. This plant eater weighed about 100 kilograms as an adult, making it one of the lighter members of its ankylosaur group.
velociraptor: Known only from fossils, this small predator lived in what is now Mongolia between 75 and 71 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Djadochta formation on the Mongolian steppe. Adults weighed about 15 kilograms, roughly the size of a turkey, and evidence points to feathering across its body.
ribbed_newt: The Iberian ribbed newt makes its home in lakes and wetlands along the Atlantic coast of Europe and the northern coast of Africa. This amphibian spends much of its time swimming and feeds on other small animals. Adults weigh about 0.06 kg, and it still thrives in the wild. When threatened, it can push its sharp rib tips through its skin as a defense, and it is also known for its ability to regenerate lost body parts.
gorilla_western_lowland: Western lowland gorillas live in the forests of the Congo Basin and along the west African coast. These herbivores move on their knuckles and feed on plants throughout the day. A full-grown adult can weigh about 140 kilograms, and the species, though still living, is protected because its numbers are under pressure.
langur_hanuman: Hanuman langurs are found across the Indian subcontinent, where they make their homes in both forests and savannas. These herbivores weigh about 15 kilograms as adults and feed mainly on plants. They live in herds, are active during the day, and are regarded as sacred in many communities.
andean_cock_of_the_rock: The Andean cock-of-the-rock lives in the Andes, where it inhabits both forest and mountain terrain. Adult males weigh about 0.25 kg and feed mainly on fruit. Males gather at communal display sites called leks, where they show off their bright feathers and flutter in courtship displays.
european_adder: The Common European Adder ranges across Europe, the British Isles, Scandinavia, the Siberian taiga, and Atlantic Europe. It lives in forests, grasslands, mountains, and tundra, and it hunts during the day. Adults weigh about 0.2 kg, and this venomous, scaled carnivore tolerates cold well.
hawksbill_turtle: Hawksbill sea turtles glide through warm tropical waters, moving between coral reefs, open ocean, and coastal areas. They live in places such as the Coral Triangle, the Caribbean Sea, and the Indian Ocean, and adults can reach about 60 kilograms. Their diet is varied, though they are known for feeding on sponges, and their shells were once prized as tortoiseshell. Today the species is still alive but is legally protected.
cottontail_eastern: The eastern cottontail is a small rabbit found across eastern North America, reaching south into Mexico and Central America. It lives in forests and grasslands, where it feeds on herbs. Adults weigh about 1.2 kg, and the species remains widespread today, though it is hunted and often shelters in burrows.
greater_grison: The greater grison is still alive and is found in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, across Central America, and in southern Mexico. It moves through jungle, forest, and grassland, and it hunts other animals for food. An adult typically weighs about 2.5 kilograms, and its dense fur is one of its notable features.
sloth_acratocnus: The Puerto Rican ground sloth lived in the forests of Puerto Rico, a region of the Caribbean that sits between 17.9 and 18.6 degrees north. Adults weighed about 25 kilograms, and they fed on plants and climbed trees as they moved through the island's woodland. This island megafauna disappeared around 2500 BC.
steppe_bison: The steppe bison once ranged across northern Asia, from the Siberian taiga and Mongolian steppe to Beringia, Alaska, and the Yukon. It grazed on tundra, plains, and taiga, feeding on herbs, and adults could weigh around 850 kg. Small Beringian groups survived until about 5500 BC.
phacops: Phacops rana lived during the Devonian, roughly 390 to 385 million years ago, and its fossils turn up in shale of the Hamilton Group in eastern North America. This trilobite is thought to have scavenged for food, and adults weighed about 0.05 kilograms. Its hard shell and schizochroal eyes are well preserved in the rock, and it could roll itself into a tight ball for protection.
mortoniceras: A keeled ammonite, Mortoniceras inflatum lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 105 to 100 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Gault Clay formation in the British Isles, where they were preserved in marine sediment. This carnivorous creature reached an adult mass of about 0.5 kg.
common_garter_snake: Common garter snakes live across much of North America, from the southern edges of Canada down past the 42nd parallel, including the Canadian Shield and the Pacific Northwest. They are found in wetlands, forests, and grasslands, and they feed on other animals. Adults weigh about 0.15 kilograms, and the species is harmless to people. Many individuals gather together in dens, where they spend the cold months.
ganges_softshell: The Ganges softshell turtle makes its home in the rivers of the Indian subcontinent, where it spends most of its life in the water. It can grow to an adult mass of about 30 kilograms, and its flat, leathery shell lets it glide smoothly through the current. Feeding on both plants and animals, it also scavenges the remains of other creatures along the riverbed.
troodon: Troodon formosus lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 77 to 74 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Judith River Formation. Adults weighed about 50 kilograms, and the animal was omnivorous, with large eyes and a sickle-shaped claw that suggest it may have hunted in the dark.
red_deer: Red deer roam across Europe, the British Isles, Iran, and Anatolia, moving through both forest and open plains. These herbivores feed on plants and grasses, and adults can weigh around 200 kg. They gather in herds and are hunted in many areas, with males growing large antlers each year.
vero_tapir: The Vero tapir was a large herbivore that lived in Florida, the Gulf region, and the southern and eastern parts of North America. It made its home in forests and wetlands, feeding on plants. Adults weighed about 300 kg, and these animals were known to swim and could be hunted. The species went extinct around 9500 BC.
topi: Found across the East African savanna, the Sahel, and parts of Southern Africa, the topi lives on open plains and grassy savanna. It is a grazer that feeds on herbs and weighs around 130 kg as an adult. Topi gather in herds, and both males and females carry horns. The species is still alive and is hunted in some areas.
palaeoisopus: Palaeoisopus problematicus is a fossil species from the Devonian period, roughly 400 to 395 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in shale of the Hunsrück Slate formation in Europe. It was a carnivore, and adults weighed about 1 kg. Some individuals reached as much as 40 cm across, making it a giant sea spider.
przewalski_gazelle: Przewalski's gazelle is a herbivore that grazes on plant matter across plains and the shores of lakes. Adults weigh about 25 kilograms, and the species still survives in the wild. It moves in herds and carries horns, and it is a protected animal.
pampas_fox: The Pampas Fox, known scientifically as Lycalopex gymnocercus, lives across the Pampas and Gran Chaco as well as in Patagonia. It favors open grassland and is active at night. This omnivore weighs about 5 kg as an adult and its dense fur helps it through the region's varied conditions. It is still widespread today.
savannah_monitor: The Savannah Monitor is a large lizard found across the Sahel, along the west African coast, and through much of Africa south of the Sahara. It favors open savanna and grassland, where it hunts meat-based prey during the day. Adults can reach about 5 kg, and the species is still widespread, with its body covered in scales and a habit of retreating into burrows.
cladoselache: Cladoselache, an early shark, lived during the Devonian period roughly 360 to 358 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Cleveland Shale formation in eastern North America, where they are preserved in shale. This carnivore grew to about 2 meters long, weighed around 50 kilograms as an adult, and swam through ancient seas with a body that lacked scales.
mussaurus: Mussaurus, whose name means "mouse lizard," is a fossil taxon from the Triassic, roughly 215 to 205 million years ago. Its remains come from sandstone of the Laguna Colorada formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. Adults are estimated to have weighed about 1500 kg, and it was a plant eater, yet some of the best-known specimens are its tiny hatchlings.
puma: The puma, also called the cougar, roams from southern Canada through North, Central, and South America, making it the most widespread wild cat of the New World. It lives in mountains, forests, plains, and deserts, and it hunts mainly at night. Adult males weigh around 60 kilograms, and its tawny fur helps it stay hidden in varied terrain. Pumas remain common across their range and are still hunted in some areas.
tiger_salamander: The tiger salamander is an amphibian that lives across the Great Plains, eastern North America, western North America, and the Canadian Shield. It can be found in forests, grasslands, and wetlands, and it spends much of its time in burrows. Active at night, this carnivore grows to an adult mass of about 0.1 kilograms, and it is still thriving today.
inland_taipan: Found only in the arid interior of Australia, this snake lives in deserts and badlands where it hunts small mammals. Adults typically weigh about half a kilogram. Though it carries the most toxic venom of any land snake, it is generally shy and tends to avoid people.
spectacled_caiman: Still thriving, the spectacled caiman ranges from the Amazon and Orinoco basins through Central America and into Mexico. It makes its home in rivers, swamps, wetlands, and lakes, where it hunts other animals. An adult weighs about 40 kg, and its armored scales and swimming ability make it a formidable presence in these waters.
indri: The indri is a leaf-eating lemur that lives in the jungles of Madagascar, in a range spanning roughly 19.5 degrees south and 14.5 to 50 degrees east. Adults weigh about 7 kilograms, and they spend their days high in the trees. Known for its loud calls, this species is protected and still survives in the wild.
rapetosaurus: Rapetosaurus was a plant-eating sauropod that lived in Madagascar during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Maevarano Formation, and adults could reach about 8000 kilograms. Researchers also know a complete skull from a juvenile, which offers a rare look at how the animal developed.
indian_wolf: The Indian wolf, a subspecies known as Canis lupus pallipes, roams the Indian subcontinent as well as Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home across plains, grasslands, and deserts, and it hunts in packs. Adults weigh around 27 kg, and the animal is still very much alive today.
mekosuchus_kalpokasi: Once living on the forests of Vanuatu's islands, this land crocodile was a meat eater that weighed about 35 kilograms as an adult. Its scaly body and terrestrial lifestyle set it apart from its water-dwelling relatives. The species vanished around 1000 BC, soon after humans known as the Lapita arrived in the region.
lesser_kudu: The lesser kudu roams the savannas of East Africa, where it browses on herbs across the landscape. Adults weigh about 90 kilograms, and the species also turns up in desert edges. Still living in the wild, it is a huntable animal prized for its horns.
flying_fox_mascarene_lesser: The Lesser Mascarene flying fox was a bat that lived on the Mascarene islands and roamed their forests. It fed mainly on fruit and weighed about 0.4 kg as an adult. Active only at night, it flew across the islands until it disappeared entirely in 1864.
grass_snake: The grass snake is found across Europe, from the British Isles and Atlantic coasts to the Mediterranean, and extends into Iran and Anatolia. It favors wetlands, rivers, lakes, and forest edges, where it moves easily through the water. Adults weigh around 0.4 kg, and this harmless species feeds mainly on amphibians.
lesothosaurus: Known only from fossils, this small plant-eater lived in what is now Southern Africa roughly 200 to 190 million years ago during the Jurassic. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Elliot Formation. Adults weighed about 3 kilograms, and paleontologists count it among the early ornithischian dinosaurs.
sand_cat: The sand cat is a small wild cat found across the Sahara, Arabia, Iran, and Anatolia. It lives in desert country and hunts meat as its diet. An adult weighs about 3 kilograms, and it remains a living species. Its thick fur, furred paws, nocturnal habits, and burrows help it survive the harsh desert environment.
javan_tiger: The Javan tiger once roamed the jungles, forests, and mountains of Java, a small island in Indonesia. It was a carnivore, and adult males could weigh around 130 kg. Its short, dense fur was well suited to the island's climate, and it was known to swim. The last confirmed evidence of the species dates to 1976, and it is now extinct.
barbary_stag: The Barbary stag roams the forests and mountains of its range, living in herds and grazing on herbs. Adults weigh about 180 kilograms, and the males carry impressive antlers that make them a prized quarry for hunters. Although it is hunted in parts of its range, the subspecies remains alive today.
loris_slow_greater: In the jungles of Sundaland, the Sunda slow loris moves through the trees only after dark. An adult weighs about 0.65 kilograms, and it eats a mix of plant and animal foods. This species is one of the few primates known to be venomous, and it is still living in the wild today under legal protection.
saola: The saola, scientifically known as Pseudoryx nghetinhensis, lives in forest and jungle habitats within the areas coded 15, 22, 103, and 108. It is a herbivore, grazing on plants, and an adult weighs about 90 kilograms. Both males and females carry a pair of straight horns, and the species is protected because it is rare, though it survives in the wild.
madagascar_giant_tortoise_abrupta: The Abrupt Giant Tortoise once roamed Madagascar, moving across both open savanna and forest. It grazed on herbs and could reach an adult mass of about 150 kilograms, carried on a heavy shell. This species disappeared around 1300 AD, a loss linked to the arrival of humans on the island.
flat_tailed_tortoise: The Flat-tailed Tortoise makes its home in the forests of Madagascar, where it feeds mostly on herbs. A fully grown adult weighs about half a kilogram, making it a small reptile with a compact shell. Though it remains alive in the wild, its tidy size and forest life set it apart among the island's tortoises.
pacific_tree_frog: The Pacific Tree Frog ranges across the Pacific Northwest and western North America, living in forests and wetlands. It is a small amphibian, weighing only about five grams as an adult, and it feeds on insects. Males gather in loud choruses during the breeding season, filling the air with their calls.
common_house_gecko: Weighing about five grams as an adult, the Common House Gecko is a small reptile that still thrives across Indochina, Sundaland, and the Indian subcontinent. It lives in forest and jungle settings, where it hunts insects after dark. Its scaled body lets it climb walls with ease.
gray_kingsnake: The gray kingsnake lives across the southern United States and into Mexico, where it moves through deserts, badlands, and mountain country. It is a carnivore that hunts other snakes and hunts them by constriction. An adult typically weighs about half a kilogram. This species is still alive and is not considered extinct.
american_mink: The American mink is a semi-aquatic carnivore found across North America, from the eastern parts of the continent through the Canadian Shield to the Pacific Northwest. It lives along wetlands, rivers, and lakes, and it is a strong swimmer that hunts in and around water. Adults weigh about 1.1 kilograms, and the species has long been valued in the fur trade for its dense pelt.
south_china_tiger: The South China tiger, known scientifically as Panthera tigris amoyensis, once roamed the lowlands of China. It lives in forest and mountain country and hunts other animals for its meat-based diet. Adults can weigh around 150 kg, and although the species is still alive, it is considered functionally extinct in the wild, so its survival now depends on protection and captive breeding.
desert_monitor: The desert monitor roams a huge range, from the Sahara and Arabia across Iran, Anatolia, and the Kazakh steppe to the Indian subcontinent. It lives in deserts, badlands, and grasslands, and it hunts meat while active during the day. Adults reach about 3 kg, and they shelter in burrows and are covered in scales.
blue_wildebeest: The blue wildebeest roams the savannas and plains of East and Southern Africa, grazing on grasses and herbs. Adults can weigh around 220 kilograms, and they gather in herds that travel long distances in search of fresh pasture. Both males and females carry horns, and the species remains widespread today and is also hunted as game.
cape_verde_giant_skink: The Cape Verde giant skink once lived across the arid islands and coastal deserts of Cape Verde, a range spanning roughly 14.8 to 17.2 degrees north. This endemic reptile was active during daylight and ate a mix of plant and animal food. Adults could reach about half a kilogram, but drought and hunting pushed it toward extinction, and the last known individuals disappeared around 1940.
grey_seal: The grey seal ranges across the North Atlantic, the Baltic and North Seas, the British Isles, and the waters around Iceland and Greenland. It favors cold coastal waters and rocky islands, where it hunts fish and other meat. Adults can weigh around 250 kg, and they gather in herds that are still thriving today.
suchomimus: Suchomimus lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 125 to 112 million years ago. Its fossils were recovered from sandstone of the Elrhaz Formation in the Sahara. This fish-eating dinosaur had a long, crocodile-like snout, a low sail along its back, and an adult mass of about 3800 kilograms.
sloth_ground_giant: Standing up on its hind legs, this giant ground sloth could reach tall branches and grasses with ease. Adults weighed about 3500 kilograms, and its long claws helped it pull vegetation within reach. It lived across the Pampas and Gran Chaco, Patagonia, and the Andes, moving through both grassland and forest before going extinct around 8000 years ago.
mole_star_nosed: The star-nosed mole makes its home in wet ground across eastern North America and the Canadian Shield. It tunnels through marshy soil and swims with ease, hunting insects in the water and the mud. An adult weighs about 55 grams, and its dense fur keeps it warm while it works through damp burrows.
pachylemur: The giant ruffed lemur once lived in the forests of Madagascar, where it spent its life moving through the trees. Adults weighed around 11 kilograms, and its diet was made up of fruit. This giant lemur, a member of the giant-lemur group, went extinct around 1300 AD.
caecilian_thompson: Thompson's Caecilian is a legless amphibian that lives across the Andes and the Amazon basin. It moves through jungle, caves, and river habitats, and it burrows as it hunts prey. Adults weigh around 0.6 kg, and this species is the largest of all caecilians.
temnodontosaurus: A fossil marine reptile from the Jurassic, living roughly 200 to 190 million years ago, Temnodontosaurus was a carnivore that could reach about 4500 kilograms. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Blue Lias formation in the British Isles. Its large eyes and length of roughly 9 meters made it a formidable hunter of its time.
iberian_lynx: The Iberian lynx roams a corner of southwestern Europe, mainly in Spain and Portugal, where it moves through forest, grassland, and rugged badlands. It is a meat eater that depends heavily on rabbits, and adults typically weigh about 13 kilograms. Though it is still alive, its population has been protected by law because it came close to vanishing entirely.
flying_dragon: The Common Flying Dragon is a small lizard that lives in the jungles of Sundaland and Indochina. It spends its life in the trees, where it hunts insects and glides from branch to branch. An adult weighs only about 0.02 kg, and this species is still alive and common across its range.
caucasian_wisent: The last Caucasian wisent was shot in 1927, and the subspecies has been extinct since then. It lived in the forests and mountains of the Caucasus, where it fed on herbs and grew to an adult mass of about 550 kg. Herds roamed the region, and the animal was hunted for its horns and fur.
dormouse_hazel: Weighing about 25 grams as adults, the hazel dormouse is a small creature that spends much of its life in the trees. It lives across Europe and the British Isles, where it favors woodland habitats. Its diet includes both plant and animal foods, and it sleeps through the cold months in a long hibernation.
araripesuchus: Araripesuchus gomesii lived between 113 and 110 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils come from limestone of the Crato Formation in South America. This omnivore weighed about 10 kg as an adult, and its dog-like face earned it the nickname of a small dog-faced crocodyliform.
western_rattlesnake: Found across the southern United States, Mexico, and parts of western North America, this venomous snake makes its home in deserts, badlands, and grasslands. It hunts small animals and can grow to about 3 kilograms. Pit organs help it sense warm prey, while the rattle at its tail warns nearby creatures to keep their distance.
oilbird: The oilbird roosts in caves across the Andes, the Amazon basin, and parts of the Caribbean, leaving them only at night to feed on fruit. Adults weigh about 0.4 kilograms, and they find their way through dark passages by echolocation, a rare ability among birds. Local people once rendered the fat of nestlings for oil, which is how the bird earned its common name.
spinosaurus: Spinosaurus lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 99 to 93 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from sandstone deposits of the Kem Kem formation in Africa. This large fossil taxon weighed about 7400 kilograms as an adult, with a tall sail along its back and a paddle-like tail suited to life in the water. Its diet was piscivorous, meaning it fed mainly on fish.
black_mamba: The black mamba roams the savannas, forests, and badlands of Africa south of the Sahara, including the East African savanna and southern parts of the continent. This diurnal, venomous snake is known for its speed and its smooth scales. Adults weigh around 1.6 kg, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
pika_sardinian: The Sardinian pika was a small herbivore that lived on the island of Sardinia, where it shared the landscape with few other mammals of its kind. Adults weighed about 0.4 kilograms, and the animal dug burrows for shelter. It fed on herbs before disappearing from the island in 1774 AD.
chinese_giant_salamander: Rivers, caves, and mountain streams across China host this amphibian, which can reach about 25 kilograms. It is the largest amphibian alive, and it spends most of its time swimming and hunting other animals. Sadly, it is critically endangered, partly because people have long prized it as a delicacy.
bongo: The bongo is a large forest antelope found in the Congo Basin and along the western African coast. It lives in forest and jungle habitats and feeds on plants. Adults can weigh around 250 kg, and the species is still alive today. Its horns make it a prized target for hunters.
rabbit_european: The European rabbit has a native range along the coasts of southwestern Europe and North Africa, with the area spanning roughly 35.5 to 43.5 degrees north and 9.5 degrees west to 3.5 degrees east. It lives in grassland and forest, feeding on herbs, and an adult typically weighs about 1.8 kg. These animals dig burrows and live in groups, and they can be hunted or domesticated.
leopard_tortoise: The leopard tortoise roams the grasslands and savannas of East and Southern Africa, south of the Sahara. It grazes on herbs and is active during the day. Adults can weigh around 20 kg, and their domed shell is marked with patterns that give the species its name. It is still living in the wild, though it can be hunted.
olm: The olm is a blind, cave-dwelling amphibian that spends its whole life in water. It lives only in caves within the area bounded by roughly 43 to 46.5 degrees north and 13 to 20 degrees east, where it hunts small prey. An adult weighs about 20 grams, and individuals can reach an age of around 100 years. The species is protected and still survives in the wild.
colobus_black_white: The guereza colobus is a leaf-eating monkey that spends its days moving through forest canopy. It lives across East Africa's savanna margins and the Congo basin, and it is still widespread rather than endangered into extinction. Adults weigh around 9 kilograms, and their long, shaggy fur is a striking feature of the species.
pangolin_ground_temminck: Temminck's ground pangolin is still alive and lives across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It roams grassland and savanna habitats, where it hunts insects at night and digs burrows for shelter. An adult weighs about 10 kg, and its body is covered in protective scales. The species is legally protected.
materpiscis: Materpiscis attenboroughi is a fossil placoderm that lived during the Devonian, roughly 380 to 375 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in limestone of the Gogo Formation in Australia. This carnivore weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult and was a swimmer that gave birth to live young.
porpoise_harbour: Shy and small, the harbour porpoise roams cold coastal and open waters across the North Atlantic, the North Pacific, the Baltic and North Seas, and even the Black and Caspian seas. Adults weigh about 60 kilograms, and like all toothed whales they hunt fish and other prey. It remains widespread today and is not extinct.
japanese_giant_salamander: Found only in the rivers and mountain streams of Japan and Korea, this amphibian is among the largest salamanders alive, with adults reaching about 25 kilograms. It hunts after dark, gliding through the water on its own and feeding on other animals. Because of its size and rarity, it is protected as a national monument, and it still survives in the wild today.
baboon_chacma: Roaming across southern Africa, the chacma baboon makes its home in savanna, grassland, and mountain country. These omnivores eat a varied diet and typically weigh around 30 kg as adults. Living in herds and active during the day, they remain widespread and are not extinct.
aye_aye: The aye-aye is a nocturnal, tree-dwelling primate found only on Madagascar, where it lives in jungle and forest habitats. It weighs about 2.6 kilograms as an adult and feeds mainly on insects it locates by tapping on wood. Still living today, it is a protected animal, and in parts of the island it is regarded as taboo.
palaeolama: The stout-legged llama (Palaeolama mirifica) once ranged across the southern United States, Mexico, Central America, the Andes, and the Amazon basin. It lived in both forest and mountain country and fed on herbs. Adults reached about 300 kg, and people hunted it. It became extinct around 10000 BC.
agile_frog: The Agile Frog makes its home in the woodlands of Europe and the Mediterranean region, where it hunts insects among the trees and undergrowth. An adult weighs only about 0.02 kg, yet it is known as a powerful long jumper for its size. Though amphibious like its relatives, this species remains widespread and is still very much alive today.
springhare: Springhares live across southern Africa and the East African savanna, where they make their home in both deserts and open grassland. Weighing about 3 kg as adults, they are herbivores that feed on plants. Active at night, they move by hopping and retreat into burrows during the day.
sciurumimus: Known only from fossils, Sciurumimus lived during the Jurassic period roughly 152 to 150 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in limestone of the Painten (Solnhofen) formation in Europe. This meat-eating dinosaur is thought to have weighed about 0.7 kilograms as an adult, and its specimen is a juvenile megalosaurid that still bore filament-like structures on its body.
marine_otter: The marine otter lives along the coasts of southern Chile and Peru, between roughly 55 and 65 degrees west and 5 to 82 degrees south in the region covered here. It feeds mainly on fish and grows to an adult mass of about 4 kg. Its dense fur keeps it warm as it swims through cold coastal waters, and it is still alive today and protected.
fer_de_lance: Found from Mexico through Central America and into the Amazon basin, the fer-de-lance lives in jungle and forest. It is still common across its range. Adults weigh about 3 kilograms, and the snake has heat-sensing pit organs that help it hunt meat-eating prey. Its scales are keeled, and its venom is strong, so it is known to strike aggressively when disturbed.
box_turtle_ornate: Built to close up tight, the Ornate Box Turtle carries a hinged shell that lets it seal itself inside when danger comes near. It makes its home across the Great Plains, where it moves through open grassland and flatlands. This omnivore eats a varied diet of plants and animals, and adults typically weigh about 0.4 kg. It is still living today and often shelters in a burrow dug into the soil.
galapagos_tortoise_santa_fe: Known only from bones, the Santa Fe giant tortoise once lived on the island of Santa Fe in the Galapagos. It grazed on plants across the island's badlands and reached adult masses near 100 kg. The species is believed to have died out around 1850 AD, and its shell remains are the main evidence of its existence.
glyptodont_doedicurus: Doedicurus was a heavily armored, turtle-like mammal that roamed the grasslands of the Pampas, Gran Chaco, and Patagonia. Adults weighed around 1400 kg, and they fed on herbs across open country. Its tail ended in a club-like structure, and it disappeared around 8000 years ago as one of the extinct megafauna.
emerald_tree_boa: The emerald tree boa spends its life in the canopy of jungles and forests across the Amazon and Orinoco basins. It hunts at night and is built for climbing, with a prehensile tail that grips branches. Adults typically weigh about 1.2 kilograms, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
patagonian_weasel: The Patagonian weasel is a small carnivore found across Patagonia and the Pampas of South America. It makes its home in grasslands and deserts, where it lives in burrows. An adult weighs about 0.3 kilograms, and its dense fur helps it cope with the region's conditions. It is still alive and not extinct.
rock_wallaby_yellow_footed: Still living today, the yellow-footed rock-wallaby makes its home in the mountains and deserts of South Australia and nearby areas. Adults weigh about 8 kg, and they feed mainly on herbs. This rock-dweller gets around by hopping over rough, rocky ground.
hare_wallaby_spectacled: Active only after dark, the spectacled hare-wallaby moves across savanna country in northern Australia, where it feeds on herbs. An adult typically weighs about 3.5 kilograms. Unlike many species of its kind, it is still living in the wild, and it covers ground by hopping.
bat_egyptian_fruit: Roaming the Nile valley, sub-Saharan Africa, Arabia, Iran, and Anatolia, this bat roosts in caves and forests. It is a fruit eater that weighs about 0.14 kg as an adult. Active only at night, it flies in colonies and finds its way by making tongue clicks to echolocate.
chihuahuan_raven: The Chihuahuan raven is found across the southern United States, Mexico, and the Great Plains, where it lives in deserts and open plains. It is an omnivore that eats whatever food it can find, and adults weigh about 0.65 kilograms. Known for its intelligence and its skill in flight, this species is still thriving today.
chaco_tortoise: The Chaco tortoise lives across the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and parts of the Southern Cone, where it moves through desert and grassland. It feeds on herbs and grows to about 4 kilograms as an adult. Its domed shell and burrows help it survive the region's dry and open terrain.
black_rat_snake: Found across eastern North America, the Eastern Rat Snake moves easily through both forest and grassland. This carnivore reaches an adult mass of about 1.5 kg. Its body is covered in scales, it hunts by constriction, and it climbs trees with skill.
resplendent_quetzal: Found from southern Mexico through Central America, this bird lives in mountain and cloud forests. Its diet consists mainly of fruit, and adults weigh about 0.2 kg. Long, flowing tail plumes trail behind it in flight, and the Maya and Aztec peoples held the bird sacred.
chital: The chital, also called the spotted deer, lives across the Indian subcontinent in both forest and grassland. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult weight of about 60 kg. Herds gather in open areas, and the males carry antlers that they use in contests. This species is still widespread and is hunted by large predators.
forest_cobra: The forest cobra roams the western coast of Africa and the Congo basin, where it hunts through jungle, forest, and river country. Adults typically weigh about 5 kg, and the species is still alive and widespread. It is venomous, it is a capable swimmer, and it feeds on other animals.
chinese_elephant: The Northern Chinese elephant once roamed the lowlands of China, moving through forest and wetland habitats where it fed on herbs. Adults weighed around 4000 kg and lived in herds, and their tusks were prized for ivory. By about 500 BC these elephants had been pushed south of the Yangtze, and the population later died out.
japanese_badger: The Japanese badger, known to science as Meles anakuma, makes its home in forest country across the areas listed in our records. Adults weigh about 8 kg, and they eat a mixed diet of both plant and animal foods. They are nocturnal, digging burrows where they rest, and their coarse fur helps them live through the seasons. The species is still living in the wild today.
hare_wallaby_eastern: The Eastern hare-wallaby once lived across grasslands in southeastern Australia, roughly between 37 and 27 degrees south latitude and 141 and 150 degrees east longitude. It fed on herbs and weighed about 2.8 kilograms as an adult. Its hopping movement carried it over open ground, and the species was declared extinct in 1890.
globidens: Globidens alabamaensis was a marine reptile that lived in the seas of the Cretaceous period, roughly 84 to 80 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Mooreville Chalk formation in the southern United States, preserved in marine sediment. This carnivore grew to about 500 kilograms, and its round, shell-crushing teeth suggest it fed on hard-bodied prey.
eastern_hog_nosed_skunk: Active mostly at night, the American hog-nosed skunk roams the badlands and grasslands of Mexico, the southern United States, and Central America. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 3 kg as an adult. Like its relatives, it defends itself with a strong-smelling spray, and it remains widespread today.
milk_snake: Found across eastern North America, the Eastern Milksnake makes its home in both forests and grasslands. This carnivorous constrictor weighs about 0.4 kilograms as an adult, and it is still thriving in the wild. Its scale patterns allow it to mimic the appearance of venomous snakes, which helps deter predators.
leptoceratops: Known only from fossils, Leptoceratops gracilis lived during the late Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Scollard Formation in northwestern North America. It was a plant eater that weighed about 200 kilograms as an adult, and it was a hornless late survivor among its relatives.
raso_giant_gecko: The Cape Verde Giant Gecko lives on islands and in desert land within a range stretching from about 14.8 to 17.2 degrees north and from 22.6 to 25.4 degrees west. It feeds on insects and weighs roughly 0.05 kilograms as an adult. Active at night, this species is still living and is protected.
jacksons_chameleon: Jackson's Chameleon is a slow-moving lizard found across the savanna of East Africa, where it climbs through forest and mountain country. Males carry three horn-like projections on their heads, and the species spends nearly all its life in trees. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.1 kg as an adult, and it remains widespread in the wild today.
southern_elephant_seal: The Southern Elephant Seal is the largest seal in the world, with adults reaching about 3000 kg. It lives in the subantarctic and Antarctic waters within roughly 55 to 40 degrees south and 70 to 55 degrees west, moving between coastal areas and the deep ocean. These seals feed on meat, live in herds, rely on a thick layer of blubber, and are migratory.
jaguarundi: The jaguarundi roams the Neotropics, reaching Mexico and the southern United States. It is found in jungle, forest, swamp, and grassland alike. Weighing about 6 kg as an adult, this carnivore is active during the day, swims well, and has a slender, otter-like build.
steller_sea_lion: The largest eared seal, the Steller sea lion roams the cold coastal waters of the North Pacific Ocean, from Japan and Korea across to the shores of the wider region. Adults can weigh as much as 600 kilograms, and they are carnivores that hunt in the ocean. Thick blubber keeps them warm, and they gather together in herds along the coast.
sloth_two_toed_hoffmann: Hoffmann's two-toed sloth spends nearly its whole life in the trees of jungles and forests across Central America, the Andes, and the wider Neotropics. It feeds on leaves and other plant matter, and an adult weighs about 6 kilograms. Moving slowly through the canopy, this species is still thriving today.
spotted_seal: The spotted seal makes its home across the cold North Pacific, from the waters of Japan and Korea up to the Beringia region. It favors icy coasts and chilly ocean habitats, where it hunts for fish and other prey. Adults can weigh around 100 kg, and the species often gathers in herds while relying on a thick layer of blubber to stay warm. It remains alive today.
crabeater_seal: The crabeater seal lives in the icy waters around Antarctica and the nearby subantarctic region, where it is still common. An adult weighs about 220 kg. Despite its name, it feeds mainly on krill, and it gathers in herds while it hunts and rests on the ice, insulated by a thick layer of blubber.
baboon_olive: Olive baboons roam across the Sahel, the East African savanna, and the Congo basin. They move through savanna, grassland, and forest, and they eat both plants and animals. An adult typically weighs around 24 kg. These active daytime animals live in herds, and the species is still widespread today.
asian_small_clawed_otter: Weighing about 4 kilograms as an adult, this is the smallest of all otter species. It lives across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Sundaland, and the lowlands of China, where it frequents rivers, wetlands, and coasts. Living in close family groups, it hunts fish and swims with a dense coat that keeps it warm in the water.
hooded_seal: The hooded seal makes its home in the North Atlantic and Arctic Ocean, with populations near Iceland and Greenland. It lives in icy, cold, and deep waters, and it feeds on other animals. Adults can weigh around 250 kilograms, and thick blubber keeps them warm. Males also carry an inflatable nasal hood that they puff up as a display.
malagasy_hippo_madagascariensis: The Malagasy giant dwarf hippo once lived on Madagascar, moving between wetlands and forest. It fed on plants and grew to an adult mass of about 500 kg. Hunted by people, it went extinct around 1500 AD, though it was a capable swimmer that thrived on this island.
struthiomimus: Struthiomimus altus lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 76 to 74 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation. Adults weighed around 150 kilograms, and the animal was an omnivore. Its ostrich-like build earned it the name "ostrich dinosaur."
rock_monitor: The rock monitor is a large lizard found across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It makes its home in savanna, badlands, and grassland, where it digs burrows and is active during the day. Adults can reach about 7 kilograms, and they feed on other animals.
echidna_short_beaked: The short-beaked echidna roams across Australia, Tasmania, and parts of Wallacea and New Guinea, making its home in forests, deserts, and savannas. It feeds almost entirely on insects, and adults typically weigh around 4 kg. This spiny mammal lays eggs, shelters in burrows, and is still alive and thriving today.
swamp_moccasin: The cottonmouth, also called the water moccasin, lives in the southern United States, especially Florida and along the Gulf coast, with range reaching into eastern North America. It makes its home in swamps, wetlands, and rivers, where it hunts as a carnivore. Adults typically weigh about 1 kilogram, and this venomous snake is still widespread today.
kaisers_spotted_newt: Kaiser's Spotted Newt makes its home in the mountains and rivers of Iran and Anatolia, where it is still found today. As an amphibian, it feeds on other small animals and weighs only about 0.03 kilograms as an adult. This newt is a protected species, so it is safeguarded under the law.
mononykus: Known only from fossils, Mononykus lived during the Cretaceous period, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago. Its remains were pressed into sandstone in the Nemegt formation of the Mongolian steppe. This creature weighed about 5 kilograms as an adult, and it fed on insects, using a single large claw on each forelimb to dig and break open its prey.
protostega: Protostega gigas was a large sea turtle that swam the Cretaceous seas roughly 85 to 80 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Niobrara Chalk of the Great Plains, where they are preserved within the chalk. Adults reached a mass of about 200 kilograms, and it is thought to have eaten both plants and animals.
large_indian_civet: The Large Indian Civet is a still-living animal found across Indochina, the Indian subcontinent, and the lowlands of China. It makes its home in forests and grasslands, eating a mix of plant and animal food. Adults weigh around 8 kg, and this nocturnal creature is known for its coat of fur.
marsh_deer: The marsh deer roams the wetlands of the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and the Amazon basin. Adults weigh about 110 kg and feed on herbs found among the swamp vegetation. Males grow antlers, and the species is an accomplished swimmer that still survives in the wild today, though it can be hunted.
alpine_salamander: High in the Alps, the Alpine Salamander makes its home among mountain slopes, where it hunts insects across the damp terrain. Adults weigh about 0.02 kg, a small body for an amphibian that still thrives in this range. Unlike many of its relatives, it gives birth to live young, and its skin contains toxins that help deter predators.
fisher: Fishers roam the forests of the Canadian Shield, eastern North America, and the northwest of the continent, as well as the Pacific Northwest. They favor taiga and forest country, where they hunt as carnivores and climb easily through the trees. Adults weigh about 4.5 kilograms, and they are known to prey on porcupines.
natterjack_toad: Found along the coasts and grasslands of Atlantic Europe, the British Isles, and wider Europe, the natterjack toad still thrives across its range. An adult weighs about 0.03 kg, and it feeds mainly on insects. Unlike many amphibians, it tends to run rather than hop, and males are known for a loud call.
blue_jay: The blue jay is a bird of eastern North America, the Great Plains, and the Canadian Shield, where it favors forested country. It eats both plants and animals, and it is known for burying acorns and for its clever mimicry of other birds' calls. An adult weighs about 0.09 kilograms, and the species is alive and thriving today.
tropites: Tropites subbullatus was a fossil ammonite that lived during the Triassic period, roughly 235 to 228 million years ago. Its remains are preserved in the limestone of the Hallstatt Limestone formation in the Alps. Adults weighed about 0.3 kilograms, and the animal is classed as a carnivore.
mozambique_spitting_cobra: The Mozambique spitting cobra is a venomous snake found across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It lives in both open savanna and forest, and it feeds on other animals. Adults typically weigh about 1.2 kg. Its scales are a notable feature, and it is known for spitting venom as a defense.
platecarpus: Platecarpus lived during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 86 to 80 million years ago, and its remains have turned up in the chalk of the Niobrara Chalk formation on the Great Plains. This carnivore could reach about 700 kilograms as an adult. Impressions of its skin have been preserved in the rock, giving researchers a rare look at the texture of its body.
syrian_elephant: The Syrian elephant once roamed wetlands and forests across its range, where it fed on herbs. An adult could weigh about 4000 kg, and it lived in herds. Its tusks were prized for ivory and were hunted by Assyrian kings, and the subspecies is recorded as extinct from the year -700 AD.
shou: The shou, a deer of the Himalaya and Tibet, lives among mountain forests and feeds on herbs. Adults weigh around 180 kg, and it moves through its range in herds. Its antlers are prized, and the species is still widely found today.
brown_anole: The Brown Anole is a small lizard that still thrives across the Caribbean. It makes its home in forests and along coastlines, where it hunts insects. An adult weighs only about 4 grams, and its body is covered in small scales.
gopher_tortoise: Gopher tortoises live across Florida and the Gulf Coast states of the southern United States. They roam forests, grasslands, and coastal areas, grazing on plants and weighing about 5 kg as adults. Their burrows provide shelter for many other animals, which is why they are considered keystone species. Although still alive, they are a protected species.
malayan_horned_frog: Among the leaf litter of the jungles of Sundaland, this amphibian is hard to spot. Its body mimics a dead leaf, helping it blend into the forest floor. Adults weigh about 0.1 kg, and the species remains common in the wild and is not extinct.
bothriolepis: Bothriolepis canadensis lived during the Devonian, roughly 378 to 375 million years ago, and its fossils turn up in the sandstone of the Escuminac Formation at Miguasha in eastern North America. This antiarch, a type of armored fish, had jointed arms and swam through its watery home. Adults weighed about 1 kilogram, and it is thought to have eaten plant matter.
smooth_coated_otter: The smooth-coated otter lives across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland. It is found in rivers, coastal areas, and wetlands, where it hunts fish and swims well. Adults weigh about 9 kg, and the species moves in packs.
steppe_polecat: The steppe polecat roams the eastern steppe, from Mongolia and Kazakhstan to the Himalaya and Tibet, across grassland and desert. This carnivore has a slender body and weighs about 1.3 kg as an adult. It is nocturnal, sheltering in burrows during the day, and its thick fur helps it survive harsh conditions.
ophthalmosaurus: Ophthalmosaurus icenicus was a marine reptile that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 165 to 160 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Oxford Clay formation in the British Isles. It was a carnivore with a body mass of about 1000 kg and notably enormous eyes.
glyptodont_panochthus: Panochthus was a plant-eating armored mammal that roamed the grasslands of the Pampas and Gran Chaco, as well as Patagonia. Adults weighed around 1000 kilograms, and they carried a rigid shell along with a spiked tail. This extinct megafauna disappeared around 8000 BC.
clouded_leopard: The clouded leopard roams forests and jungles across Indochina, the Indian subcontinent, the Himalaya, Tibet, and the lowlands of China. Adults weigh about 18 kilograms and hunt meat at night, using their long canine teeth and tree-climbing skill. Their cloud-shaped coat keeps them hidden in the branches, and they remain a protected species.
ankylosaurus: Ankylosaurus was a plant-eater that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone in the Hell Creek formation of the Great Plains. Weighing about 6000 kg as an adult, it was the largest of the ankylosaurs, and it carried a bony club at the end of its tail.
australian_sea_lion: The Australian sea lion lives along the coasts and islands of southern Australia, roughly between latitudes 27 and 36 degrees south and longitudes 112 and 138 degrees east. It is a carnivore that hunts fish, squid, and other marine prey. Adults can weigh around 150 kilograms, and the species still survives today, living in groups and relying on a thick layer of blubber to stay warm in cool waters.
deinocheirus: Known only from fossils, Deinocheirus lived roughly 71 to 69 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Nemegt Formation on the Mongolian steppe. Adults may have weighed about 6400 kilograms, and this large dinosaur carried a hump on its back, possessed enormous arms, and likely ate fish alongside other foods.
galapagos_land_iguana: The Galapagos Land Iguana makes its home across the islands of the Galapagos, where it lives in desert, coastal, and island settings. It is a plant eater that feeds on herbs and cactus, and it is active during the day. Adults can reach about 10 kg, and they dig burrows to rest and shelter in.
chinese_giant_frog: The Spiny Frog, known to science as Quasipaa spinosa, makes its home in the lowlands of China and across Indochina. It favors rivers and forests, and it hunts other small animals as a carnivore. An adult can reach about 0.4 kg, and although it is an amphibian prized as food, it remains widespread in the wild.
tiger_snake: Found across Australia and Tasmania, the tiger snake makes its home in wetlands, coastal areas, and grasslands. It is a carnivore that weighs about 1 kilogram as an adult. This venomous reptile is covered in scales and is a confident swimmer.
ringtail: Nocturnal and omnivorous, the ringtail roams the badlands, deserts, and mountains of Mexico, the southern United States, and western North America. An adult typically weighs about 1 kilogram, and its banded fur helps it blend into rocky terrain. Few animals climb cliffs as skillfully, and this species remains widespread and very much alive today.
hesperornis: Hesperornis regalis was a flightless, toothed bird that lived in the seas of the Cretaceous period, roughly 83 to 78 million years ago. Adults weighed around 15 kilograms, and they fed mainly on fish. Its fossils have been recovered from chalk deposits of the Niobrara Chalk formation on the Great Plains.
pig_nosed_turtle: The pig-nosed turtle makes its home in the rivers and swamps of Wallacea and New Guinea. Adults can weigh about 22 kilograms, and they eat a mix of plant and animal food. Unlike most turtles, this species swims using broad flippers instead of paddle-like legs, and it still survives in the wild today.
arabian_leopard: The Arabian leopard roams the mountains, deserts, and badlands of Arabia, where it hunts meat as its main food. Adults weigh about 30 kilograms, making it the smallest leopard subspecies. It is nocturnal, keeping to the cover of night, and it is protected, though it still survives in the wild today.
kangaroo_red: The red kangaroo, Osphranter rufus, is the largest marsupial alive today and roams the deserts, grasslands, and savannas of Australia. Adults commonly weigh around 50 kilograms. These animals live in herds and feed on herbs, moving across the land by hopping. They are still plentiful in the wild.
klipspringer: The klipspringer makes its home across the rocky mountains and badlands of Africa south of the Sahara. Weighing about 13 kilograms as an adult, this small antelope feeds on herbs and remains widely found today. Hunters are permitted to pursue it, and its horns are a notable feature.
wood_frog: The wood frog lives across the Canadian Shield, eastern North America, Alaska, the Yukon, and Beringia. It inhabits forests, wetlands, taiga, and tundra, and it feeds on insects. Remarkably hardy, it is the northernmost amphibian and survives winter by freezing solid.
tarpan: The tarpan was a wild horse that once roamed Europe, the eastern steppe, the Kazakh steppe, and parts of Iran and Anatolia. It lived on plains, grasslands, and forest edges, grazing on herbs and moving in herds. Adults weighed about 300 kilograms, and the species could be hunted or domesticated. The last known individual died in captivity in 1909.
common_reed_frog: The Painted Reed Frog is a small amphibian, weighing only about three grams as an adult, that still thrives today. It lives in wetlands across southern Africa and parts of the East African savanna. Its colorful markings and insect-based diet help make it a familiar sight among the reeds.
green_basilisk: The Green Basilisk lives in the jungles and along the rivers of Central America. It spends much of its life in trees, and it is one of the few lizards able to run across the surface of water on its hind legs. Adults weigh about 0.2 kg, and their eat both plants and small animals. Its head bears a crest, and its body is covered in scales.
daspletosaurus: Daspletosaurus torosus was a robust tyrannosaur that lived in northwestern North America roughly 77 to 74 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Two Medicine Formation. This carnivore weighed about 3800 kilograms as an adult.
timber_rattlesnake: The timber rattlesnake lives across eastern North America, moving through forests and mountain ranges. It feeds on other animals and typically weighs around 2 kilograms as an adult. This venomous species is still alive today and can be recognized by its heat-sensing pit organs and the rattle at the end of its tail.
bilby_lesser: The lesser bilby was a small desert marsupial that once lived across parts of the Australian interior, roughly between latitudes 22 and 28 degrees south and longitudes 133 and 141 degrees east. It weighed about 0.4 kilograms as an adult, ate both plants and animals, and spent its nights above ground while retreating into burrows during the day. The species was declared extinct in 1931.
argentine_horned_frog: The Argentine Horned Frog lives across the Southern Cone, in the Pampas and the Gran Chaco. It favors grasslands and wetlands, where it waits in ambush for prey. Adults can reach about 0.4 kg, and this carnivorous amphibian spends time in burrows. It is still alive in the wild.
hooded_crow: The hooded crow ranges across Europe, the eastern steppe, the Mediterranean, and Iran and Anatolia, where it favors open plains and rocky coastlines. Adults weigh about half a kilogram, and the bird eats almost anything, scavenging carrion and scraps alongside other food. Known for its intelligence, it is still widespread and not endangered.
spur_thighed_tortoise: The Greek tortoise is found along the northern coast of Africa, across Iran and Anatolia, and around the Mediterranean. It favors badlands and grasslands, where it grazes on herbs. An adult typically weighs about 3 kg, and it is active during the day. The species is still alive today.
hooded_skunk: Active mostly at night, the hooded skunk roams across Mexico, the southern United States, and parts of Central America. It makes its home in badlands and grasslands, eating a mix of plant and animal foods. An adult typically weighs about 1 kilogram, and like its relatives it defends itself by releasing a strong-smelling spray.
bat_spectral: The spectral bat lives in the Neotropics, ranging through Central America and into parts of South America. It makes its home in jungle, where it hunts at night. Adults weigh about 0.17 kg, and the species is still alive today. It is the largest bat in the New World.
mole_european: The European mole lives across Europe, the British Isles, and the Siberian taiga, where it makes its home in forests and grasslands. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.1 kilograms as an adult. Its velvety fur and tunneling burrows help it get around underground, and the species is still living today.
cylindraspis_vosmaeri: The Rodrigues Domed Tortoise once roamed the forests of Rodrigues, an island in the Mascarene group. It grazed on plants and could reach an adult weight of about 100 kilograms.
