Its domed shell made it a valuable source of food for passing sailors, and the species was gone by 1795.
painted_turtle: Painted turtles range across eastern North America, the Canadian Shield, the Great Plains, and the Pacific Northwest. They make their homes in lakes, wetlands, and rivers, eating both plants and animals. Adults weigh about half a kilogram, and they bask in the sun, swim with ease, and hibernate underwater through the winter.
malayan_pit_viper: The Malayan pit viper makes its home across Indochina and Sundaland, moving through both jungle and forest. Adults typically weigh about 0.6 kg, and they feed on other animals. This venomous snake is still widespread today, and it relies on heat-sensing pit organs to locate prey.
sea_otter: Sea otters live in cold coastal waters of the North Pacific, from Beringia down the Pacific Northwest and around to Japan and Korea. Adults weigh about 25 kilograms, and they feed mainly on fish and other marine prey. They have the densest fur of any animal, and they use tools while they float on their backs.
lion: Lions still roam Africa, southwest Asia, and parts of the Indian subcontinent, favoring savanna, grassland, plains, and even desert edges. These carnivores live in prides, hunt during the day, and grow a mane that marks adult males. Adults can weigh around 180 kg. Lions once lived in Greece and the Balkans, but those populations vanished long before 1500 AD, and European lions disappeared around 100 AD.
dolphin_striped: Striped dolphins live in the Mediterranean, tropical seas, and the North Atlantic, moving through both warm surface waters and deep ocean. These toothed carnivores weigh about 150 kg as adults and hunt in groups called pods. They are known for leaping and spinning acrobatics above the waves.
asian_box_turtle: The Asian Box Turtle is found across Indochina, Sundaland, and the Indian subcontinent, where it moves between wetlands, forests, and rivers. Its most distinctive feature is a hinged shell that lets it close its body tightly for protection. Eating both plants and animals, this semiaquatic turtle typically reaches about 1 kilogram as an adult.
solenodon_hispaniolan: Found only on the island of Hispaniola in the Caribbean, this nocturnal mammal roams forests and sheltering caves in search of insects. An adult weighs about 1 kilogram. It is venomous, and it remains alive today under legal protection.
bengal_monitor: The Bengal Monitor is found across the Indian subcontinent and into Indochina, where it moves through forest, savanna, and riverbank country. It is a carnivore that is active during the day and spends time climbing. Adults typically weigh about 7 kg, and the species is still alive today.
eastern_hognose: The Eastern Hognose Snake lives across eastern North America, where it moves through forests and grasslands in search of prey. Adults typically weigh around 0.3 kg. When threatened, it may flip onto its back, open its mouth, and lie motionless as if dead. Its diet is largely made up of toads, which it hunts with particular interest.
yellow_mongoose: The yellow mongoose lives across southern Africa, where it roams both grassland and desert. Its diet consists mainly of insects, and an adult weighs about 0.6 kg. Active during the day, it shelters in burrows and is still widespread today.
galapagos_fur_seal: The Galapagos fur seal lives on the coasts and islands of the Galapagos, where it hunts for fish and other prey in the surrounding waters. Adults weigh about 35 kilograms. It is the smallest of the eared seals, and it gathers in herds along the shore. The species is still alive and thriving across the archipelago.
badlands_bighorn: The Badlands bighorn once roamed the rugged badlands and open plains across a broad stretch of the northern interior. These herbivores grew to an adult mass of about 85 kilograms and lived in herds, with the males carrying large curved horns. The subspecies was hunted until its last known individual died in 1925.
tufted_deer: The tufted deer lives in the lowlands of China and is still widespread today. It makes its home in both forest and mountain terrain, where it feeds on herbs. An adult typically weighs about 20 kg, and males carry small fangs that jut from the upper jaw.
cane_toad: Native to the Amazon basin, Central America, and southern Mexico, the cane toad lives in forests, savannas, and wetlands. This amphibian is nocturnal and omnivorous, and adults can reach about 1 kilogram. Its skin secretes toxins that make it dangerous to animals that try to eat it.
groundhog: The groundhog, also called the woodchuck, roams across eastern North America and the Canadian Shield. It makes its home in forests and grasslands, feeding mainly on herbs. An adult typically weighs about 3.5 kilograms, and the species digs burrows and hibernates through the cold months. It remains widespread today and can be hunted in some areas.
palaeopropithecus_ingens: The giant sloth lemur once lived in the forests of Madagascar, and its habitat notes also list desert areas. It fed on herbs and weighed about 45 kg as an adult. Slow and tree-dwelling, this giant lemur went extinct around 1500 AD.
long_horned_bison: The long-horned bison once roamed the grasslands and plains of North America south of 42 degrees north. These herbivores grazed on grasses and other plants, and a fully grown adult could weigh around 1500 kilograms. They lived in herds, and their long horns and thick fur set them apart. The species is believed to have died out around 12900 BC.
jerboa_greater_egyptian: The Greater Egyptian jerboa is a small desert rodent that lives along the northern coast of Africa and across the Sahara. It is nocturnal, spending the day in burrows and emerging after dark to feed on plants. Adults weigh about 0.14 kg, and the species moves by hopping rather than running. It is still alive and common across its range.
mojave_rattlesnake: The Mojave Rattlesnake makes its home in the deserts of western North America and Mexico, where it hunts small animals for food. Adults typically weigh about 1.5 kilograms. This species is venomous, and its venom is neurotoxic, meaning it acts on the nervous system.
bat_ghost: The ghost bat is a nocturnal, carnivorous bat found across Australia. It roosts in caves and moves through desert and savanna country in search of prey. Weighing only about 0.12 kg as an adult, it is still very much alive today.
common_duiker: The common duiker roams the lands of Africa south of the Sahara, moving easily between open savanna and forest edges. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 18 kilograms as an adult. Both males and females grow short horns, and the species remains widespread and still lives in the wild today, though hunters pursue it.
takin: Takins roam the Himalaya and Tibet, moving between mountain slopes and forested valleys. These herbivores grow to about 300 kilograms as adults and live in herds. Both males and females carry horns, and their thick coat keeps them warm in cold, high country. Takins are still alive today, though they are hunted in some areas.
flat_headed_cat: The flat-headed cat lives in swamps, rivers, and wetlands, where it hunts mostly fish. Adults weigh about 2.5 kg, and their dense fur helps them in damp surroundings. They are nocturnal and known to swim well. This species is still alive and is protected.
herrerasaurus: Herrerasaurus lived during the Triassic, roughly 231 to 228 million years ago, and it is known only from fossils. Its remains come from sandstone of the Ischigualasto Formation in what is now Patagonia and the Pampas. An adult weighed about 200 kilograms, and it ate meat. It is counted among the earliest large dinosaur predators.
tarsier_western: The western tarsier is a small nocturnal primate that lives in the jungles of Sundaland. It feeds mainly on insects, and an adult typically weighs about 0.12 kg. Though it is nocturnal, it remains a living species that continues to inhabit its forest home.
ouranosaurus: Ouranosaurus was a plant-eating dinosaur that lived between 125 and 112 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils were recovered from sandstone of the Elrhaz Formation in what is now the Sahara. An adult could weigh about 4000 kilograms, and it carried a dorsal sail along its back.
dsungaripterus: Known only from fossils, Dsungaripterus weii lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 130 to 120 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from mudstone of the Tugulu Formation in the lowlands of China. Adults weighed around 15 kilograms, and the animal had a bony crest and a diet of crushed shells.
hawaiian_crow: The Hawaiian crow, known locally as the alala, is a forest bird found only on the island of Hawaii. It weighs about 0.45 kg as an adult and eats a varied diet of both plant and animal foods. The species was declared extinct in the wild in 2002, and today it survives only through captive breeding programs.
shingleback: Active by day, the shingleback roams the deserts and savannas of Australia in search of food. This omnivore weighs about 0.6 kg as an adult and remains widespread today. Its thick, scaly body and stubby, stump-like tail set it apart from other lizards in its range.
nile_crocodile: The Nile crocodile ranges across much of Africa south of the Sahara, along the Nile valley, through the Sahel, and onto Madagascar. It favors rivers, lakes, swamps, and wetlands, where it lies in wait as an ambush predator. Adults can reach about 410 kilograms, and females guard their eggs in nests on land.
gerenuk: The gerenuk, a slender antelope of the East African savanna and desert, is still thriving in the wild. Adults weigh around 40 kg and feed on herbs. Its habit of rising onto its hind legs to browse higher foliage sets it apart from many of its relatives.
sauropelta: Sauropelta was a plant-eating ankylosaur that roamed western North America during the Cretaceous, between about 115 and 108 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Cloverly Formation. Adults weighed around 1500 kilograms, and it is thought to have been prey for the predator Deinonychus.
pachycephalosaurus: Known only from fossils, this dinosaur lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone in the Hell Creek Formation of the Great Plains. Adults weighed around 450 kg, and the animal ate plants. Its most striking feature was a thick, domed skull.
plains_bison: Plains bison live in grasslands and open plains across the Great Plains, the Canadian Shield, eastern North America, and western North America. These grazers eat mostly herbs and can reach an adult mass of about 700 kilograms. They move in migratory herds, and their horns and thick fur are distinctive features. Plains bison are still alive today, and they are a huntable species.
tibetan_sand_fox: The Tibetan sand fox makes its home across the Himalaya and the Tibetan plateau, where it roams mountain slopes and open grassland. Weighing about 4.5 kilograms as an adult, it is a meat eater that often hunts pikas. Its thick fur helps it withstand the cold, and it rests and raises young in burrows dug into the ground.
marrella: Marrella splendens is a fossil arthropod from the Cambrian period, dating to roughly 508 to 505 million years ago. Its remains are preserved in shale of the Burgess Shale formation in northwestern North America. Adults weighed about 0.002 kilograms, and they are thought to have filter fed while swimming, protected by a spined shield.
jamaican_racer: The Jamaican Racer was a snake that once lived across forests on the island of Jamaica. It fed on other animals and weighed about 0.3 kilograms as an adult. Introduced mongooses are often blamed for its disappearance, and the species was declared extinct around 1900.
black_footed_cat: Sleek and spotted, this cat prowls the deserts, grasslands, and savannas of southern Africa after dark. It hunts small prey and rests by day in burrows dug by others or found among rocks. Weighing about 2 kilograms as an adult, it is the smallest cat on the African continent, and it remains alive in the wild today.
south_american_rattlesnake: The South American rattlesnake makes its home across the Neotropics and down through the Southern Cone. It favors savanna, grassland, and badlands, where it hunts other animals. An adult typically weighs about 1.5 kg, and its venom and rattle set it apart as a species still thriving today.
dilophosaurus: Dilophosaurus wetherilli is known only from fossils, which date to the Early Jurassic, roughly 193 to 183 million years ago. Its bones were recovered from sandstone of the Kayenta Formation in the southwestern United States. This meat-eater weighed about 400 kilograms as an adult and carried a pair of thin crests running across the top of its skull.
squirrel_monkey: Common squirrel monkeys roam the jungles of the Amazon and Orinoco basins, moving through the canopy in large herds. These small primates weigh about 0.8 kilograms as adults and stay active during the day, spending most of their time in the trees. They eat a varied diet of both plants and animals, and the species remains widespread today.
siberian_ibex: The Siberian ibex, Capra sibirica, roams mountain country across the Mongolian steppe, the Himalaya and Tibet, the Kazakh steppe, and the Siberian taiga. It lives among icy peaks and grazes on herbs, and an adult typically weighs about 90 kg. This species is still alive, moves in herds, carries impressive horns, and is huntable.
radiated_tortoise: The Radiated Tortoise lives in Madagascar, where it moves through both forest and dry badlands. Its domed shell bears a striking star-shaped pattern of yellow lines on dark plates. Adults typically reach about 15 kg, and they feed mainly on plants. Although the species is still alive, it is protected because of threats to its survival.
giant_eland: The giant eland is one of the largest antelopes alive, with adults weighing around 700 kilograms. It roams a wide range that stretches across the Sahel, the West African coast, and the Congo basin, moving between open savanna and forest. Living in herds and feeding on herbs, it still survives in the wild today, and it is a species that hunters are permitted to pursue.
fowlers_toad: Fowler's Toad lives across eastern North America and the southern United States, where it favors coastal areas and wetlands. This amphibian feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.04 kg as an adult. Its skin produces toxins, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
gobi_bear: The Gobi bear roams the Mongolian steppe, moving between desert and badlands in search of food. As an omnivore, it eats a mix of plants and animals, and an adult typically weighs around 100 kg. This subspecies is still alive today and is legally protected, and its thick fur helps it endure the harsh climate.
buitreraptor: Buitreraptor gonzalezorum was a slim unenlagiine known only from fossils. It lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 97 to 93 million years ago, and its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Candeleros Formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This carnivore weighed about 2 kg as an adult.
rabbit_volcano: The volcano rabbit is a small, herbivorous mountain dweller that weighs about 0.5 kilograms as an adult. It lives in a limited area between roughly 19 and 19.5 degrees north and 98.5 and 99.2 degrees west, where it digs burrows for shelter. Though still alive, this species is protected, so it is safeguarded under the law.
triceratops: A plant-eating giant of the Cretaceous, Triceratops lived between 68 and 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been found in sandstone of the Hell Creek formation on the Great Plains. An adult could reach about 6000 kg, and its three horns make it a classic example of the ceratopsian group.
sloth_ground_scelidotherium: Scelidotherium was a ground sloth that roamed the grasslands of the Pampas, Gran Chaco, and Patagonia. Weighing roughly 1000 kilograms as an adult, it fed on herbs and belonged to the group of extinct megafauna. It is thought to have dug burrows, and it disappeared around 8000 BC.
beaked_cuviers: Cuvier's beaked whale is a toothed species found in oceans around the world, and it lives in deep water. It hunts squid far below the surface and is known for being hard to spot, since it rarely comes near the shore or ships. Adults weigh around 2500 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today.
caudipteryx: Caudipteryx lived in what is now China roughly 125 to 122 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its fossils were preserved in shale of the Yixian Formation, and this small, feathered dinosaur weighed about 5 kg as an adult. It had an omnivorous diet, and a fan of feathers at the end of its tail, while gastroliths, or stones swallowed to aid digestion, have been found with specimens.
mara_patagonian: The Patagonian mara roams the grasslands and deserts of Patagonia, the Pampas, and the Gran Chaco. It grazes on herbs and weighs about 9 kg as an adult. These animals are active during the day, gather in herds, and form monogamous pairs. They remain widespread today.
tanystropheus: Tanystropheus is a fossil reptile from the Triassic, living roughly 242 to 240 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in limestone of the Besano Formation in the Alps. Its neck was longer than its body and tail combined, and it is thought to have eaten fish. Adults reached about 130 kg.
musk_turtle: Also called the stinkpot, this small turtle roams the eastern regions of North America. It makes its home in rivers, lakes, and swamps, where it hunts meat-based prey. Adults typically weigh about 0.3 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today. When disturbed, it releases a musky odor from glands near its shell.
kannemeyeria: Kannemeyeria was a large dicynodont that lived during the Triassic, roughly 247 to 242 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Burgersdorp Formation in Southern Africa. Adults may have reached about 500 kilograms, and the animal is thought to have fed on plants.
blue_coral_snake: The blue Malayan coral snake lives across Sundaland and Indochina, moving through jungle and forest. An adult weighs about 0.2 kg, and it hunts other snakes, so its diet is carnivorous. Its smooth scales and venom mark it as a species that is still very much alive today.
green_black_poison_frog: This small amphibian lives in the jungles of Central America and parts of the Amazon basin. Its skin is toxic, a defense that helps keep predators away from its body, which weighs only about two grams as an adult. Insects make up its diet, and the species is still alive and widespread in its native range.
asian_badger: The Asian badger roams across Siberian taiga, Mongolian and Kazakh steppe, and the Himalayas and Tibet, moving through forest, grassland, and mountain country. It eats both plants and animals and weighs about 11 kilograms as an adult. Active at night, it digs burrows and has thick fur. It is still widespread today.
razanandrongobe: Razanandrongobe sakalavae was a giant crocodylomorph that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 168 to 166 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Bathonian Mahajanga Formation in Madagascar. This carnivore is estimated to have weighed about 1000 kilograms as an adult.
indian_spitting_cobra: The Javan spitting cobra is a venomous snake found across Sundaland, where it lives in both forest and grassland. It feeds on other animals and typically weighs around 2 kilograms as an adult. Its scales are a key feature, and it can spit venom as a defense against threats.
perentie: Among the largest lizards on Earth, the perentie roams the deserts and badlands of Australia. It is the biggest lizard native to the continent, and adults can weigh around 15 kilograms. Active during the day, this carnivore hunts across open country and remains very much alive today.
opossum_woolly: Found from southern Mexico through Central America and into the Neotropics, the woolly opossum lives in jungle habitat. This marsupial spends its time in the trees, using a prehensile tail to grip branches as it moves. Adults weigh about 0.35 kg, and the species fruit makes up its diet. It is still alive and not extinct.
australian_raven: The Australian raven is a bird of Australia that lives on open plains and in forests. It eats both plants and animals, and adults weigh about 0.65 kg. This species is still alive and is known for its sleek feathers, its flight, and its intelligence.
glyptodont_glyptodon: The Glyptodon was a heavily built grazer that roamed grasslands across the Pampas and Gran Chaco, with records also placing it in Patagonia and the Amazon and Orinoco regions. An adult could weigh about 1000 kg, and it fed on herbs. Its body was protected by a domed shell of armour, and it died out around 8000 BC.
dunkleosteus_terrelli: Dunkleosteus terrelli was a fossil fish from the Devonian period, living roughly 360 to 358 million years ago. Its remains come from shale of the Cleveland Shale formation in eastern North America. Adults reached about 1000 kg, and this armoured carnivore used bony bite plates to become a top predator in its waters.
steenbok: The steenbok is a small antelope found across southern Africa and the East African savanna. It favors open grassland and savanna, where it feeds on herbs and weighs about 11 kg as an adult. Still living in the wild, this species has horns and is an animal that hunters are permitted to pursue.
plotosaurus: Plotosaurus was a carnivorous marine reptile that lived in the seas of western North America during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Moreno Formation, where they were preserved in marine sediment. An adult could weigh about 1000 kg, and its fish-like tail suggests it was a fast swimmer.
european_green_lizard: The European green lizard lives across Europe and around the Mediterranean, where it moves through forest edges and open grassland. This small, daytime-active reptile weighs about 0.04 kg as an adult and is covered in fine scales. It feeds mainly on insects and remains widespread today.
impressed_tortoise: The Impressed Tortoise makes its home in the forests and mountain slopes of Indochina. It eats both plants and animal matter, so it is classed as omnivorous. A full-grown adult weighs about 4 kilograms, and its shell is its most notable feature. Happily, this species survives in the wild today.
muskrat: Muskrats are semi-aquatic rodents found across North America, where they make their homes in wetlands, rivers, and lakes. Each adult weighs about 1.2 kilograms and feeds mainly on plants. Their dense fur is valued by trappers, and the species remains widespread and thriving today.
parasaurolophus: Known only from fossils, this herbivore lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 77 to 74 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation in northwestern North America. Adults weighed about 2500 kilograms, and a long tubular crest projected from the head.
duvaucel_gecko: Active only after dark, Duvaucel's Gecko lives in New Zealand on islands, along coastlines, and within forests. This species eats a mix of foods and typically weighs about 0.1 kg as an adult. It is the largest gecko still living in New Zealand, and it remains widespread rather than extinct.
bushbaby_senegal: The Senegal bushbaby is a small, still-thriving primate found across the Sahel and the East African savanna. Adults weigh about 0.25 kilograms, and they spend the night foraging through open woodland. Known for their powerful leaps from branch to branch, they eat a mixed diet of insects, fruit, and other small food.
asian_vine_snake: Slim and bright green, this snake glides through the branches of jungles and forests across the Indian subcontinent. It hunts other animals and usually weighs around 0.3 kg as an adult. Its color helps it blend into leafy vines, and while it is only mildly venomous, it remains a species still thriving in the wild.
tilos_dwarf_elephant: Small enough to walk through a doorway, this island-dwelling herbivore once roamed the Tilos area of the Aegean, where it fed on plants. Adults weighed about 300 kg, and its tusks were a notable feature of its build. The species became extinct around 4000 BC.
alligator_snapping_turtle: The alligator snapping turtle is a freshwater reptile found across the southern United States, from Florida and the Gulf coast up into the Great Plains. It lives in rivers, swamps, and lakes, where it hunts mostly by ambush. Adults can reach about 70 kilograms, and it still survives in the wild today.
woolly_monkey: The common woolly monkey lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as the Andes, where it moves through jungle and forest. Its diet is mainly fruit, and an adult typically weighs about 7 kg. Active by day and spending most of its life in the trees, it remains a living species, though it is hunted in parts of its range.
belemnitella: Belemnitella is an extinct cephalopod known only from fossils, and its remains are most often preserved in chalk. Individuals lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 80 to 66 million years ago, and their shells have been recovered from the Maastricht Chalk formation in Europe. Adults are estimated to have weighed about 0.3 kg, and the animal is classed as a carnivore.
cryolophosaurus: A fossil predator from the Jurassic, the Cryolophosaurus lived roughly 190 to 182 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from volcanic ash in the Hanson Formation of Antarctica, a region that was once home to polar forests. Adults weighed about 465 kg, and the distinctive crest on its head earned it the nickname "Elvis" among researchers.
corsac_fox: The corsac fox roams the steppes of Mongolia and Kazakhstan, where it lives across open grassland and desert. Adults weigh about 3 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today. It is a carnivore, and it often shelters in burrows dug into the ground.
grants_gazelle: Grant's gazelle roams the open grasslands of East Africa, where it grazes on herbs across the plains. Adults weigh about 55 kg, and both sexes carry horns. Herds gather on the savanna, and the species remains alive today, though it is huntable in some areas.
bali_tiger: The Bali tiger once roamed the jungles and forests of Bali, a small island in Indonesia, where it hunted meat-eating prey. Adults weighed about 95 kilograms, making it the smallest of the tiger subspecies. It was known for its thick fur and its ability to swim. The last known individual was shot in 1937, and the subspecies is considered extinct.
galapagos_tortoise_fernandina: The Fernandina Giant Tortoise lives in the Galapagos, where it roams island badlands and feeds on plants. Adults can weigh around 120 kg. Once thought to have vanished, this saddleback-shelled species was rediscovered in 2019 and is still alive today.
yellow_throated_marten: The yellow-throated marten roams forests, jungles, and mountains across Indomalaya, the China lowlands, and the Himalaya and Tibet. It eats a mixed diet of both plants and animals, and an adult weighs about 3 kg. Active during the day, it lives in packs and is still widespread today.
south_american_fur_seal: Dense fur keeps this seal warm in cold coastal waters, where it gathers in large herds along the shore. Adults weigh about 100 kilograms, and the species still thrives along the southern coasts of South America. Its diet is carnivorous, and it spends much of its time hunting in the ocean.
bootherium: Harlan's muskox, Bootherium bombifrons, roamed North America south of 42 degrees north as well as Alaska and the Yukon. It grazed on herbs across plains and forest, and adults weighed about 450 kilograms. Herds, horns, and shaggy fur were part of its life before the species vanished around 9500 BC.
porcupine_crested_old_world: The crested porcupine lives along North Africa's coast, across the continent south of the Sahara, and in parts of the Mediterranean. It makes its home in savanna, forest, and desert, and feeds on plants. Adults typically weigh about 17 kg, and the species is still living, active at night from burrows, with quills for defense and a population that people hunt.
opossum_common: Active only at night, this marsupial roams the forests and jungles of Central America, southern Mexico, and the Amazon and Orinoco basins. Adults weigh about 1.3 kg, and they climb trees with ease while eating a mix of plant and animal foods. Their range remains wide, and the species is still thriving across its territory.
macaque_barbary: The Barbary macaque lives along the northern coast of Africa, in a range that stretches roughly from 35 to 37 degrees north and from 6 to 4 degrees west. It makes its home in both forests and mountain country, and it eats a mixed diet of plants and animal food. Adults weigh about 11 kilograms, and the species moves through the day in herds while remaining active only during daylight hours.
african_civet: The African civet roams the land south of the Sahara and across the Sahel, moving through savanna, forest, and wetland alike. This nocturnal omnivore weighs about 12 kg as an adult and is still widespread today. It is known for its coarse fur and for the musk it produces, which has long been valued in perfumery.
jackrabbit_black_tailed: Found across western North America, Mexico, and the Great Plains, the black-tailed jackrabbit makes its home in deserts and grasslands. It feeds on plants and typically weighs about 2.3 kilograms as an adult. Built for speed, this species can outrun many predators, and it remains widespread today and is hunted in parts of its range.
bilby_greater: Shuffling through the deserts and savannas of Australia, the greater bilby is a nocturnal creature that spends its days in deep burrows. Adults weigh about 1.5 kilograms, and they eat a mix of plant and animal foods. Though still living in the wild, this long-eared marsupial is a species worth keeping an eye on.
coyote: Found across western North America, the Great Plains, Mexico, and Central America, the coyote thrives in plains, deserts, forests, grasslands, and mountains. This still-thriving canine is mostly carnivorous and weighs about 15 kg as an adult. It hunts mainly at night and may travel in packs, and its fur is valued by hunters.
northern_elephant_seal: Massive males of this species can weigh around 2000 kg, and their inflatable proboscis gives them a distinctive look. They live along coasts and in deep ocean waters across a broad stretch of the northeastern Pacific, from roughly 22 to 50 degrees north. These carnivores gather in herds, carry thick layers of blubber, and travel long migrations across the sea.
okapi: The okapi, known scientifically as Okapia johnstoni, lives in the forests of the Congo basin. Weighing around 250 kilograms as an adult, it feeds on herbs and is still living in the wild. Its legs carry bold zebra-like stripes, and the species is protected.
postosuchus: Postosuchus kirkpatricki was a fossil taxon that lived during the Triassic, roughly 220 to 210 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Chinle Formation in the southern United States. As a carnivore weighing about 300 kilograms as an adult, it was an apex predator among the rauisuchians of its time.
crab_eating_mongoose: The crab-eating mongoose roams the lowlands of Indochina, Sundaland, the Indian subcontinent, and southern China. It makes its home in wetlands, rivers, and forests, and it is a skilled swimmer that hunts mostly meat. Adults typically weigh around 2 kilograms, and the species is still living in the wild today.
thescelosaurus: A plant-eating ornithopod, Thescelosaurus neglectus lived during the late Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone deposits of the Hell Creek formation on the Great Plains. Adults reached about 300 kilograms, making this late small ornithopod a sturdy herbivore of its time.
prestosuchus: Prestosuchus was a carnivore that lived in what is now southern Brazil during the Triassic, roughly 241 to 235 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Santa Maria Formation in the Southern Cone. An adult weighed about 300 kilograms, and it belonged to the rauisuchian group of archosaurs.
solenodon_cuban: The Cuban solenodon is a shrew-like mammal found only in the Caribbean, where it roams forests and caves. It feeds mainly on insects and hunts through the night. Adults weigh about one kilogram, and this species carries venom in its bite. It remains alive today and is protected by law.
metriorhynchus: Metriorhynchus lived in ancient seas during the Jurassic, roughly 165 to 160 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Oxford Clay formation in the British Isles. This marine crocodylomorph was a meat eater that reached an adult mass of about 150 kilograms, and it swam using a tail fluke.
komodo_dragon: The Komodo dragon is a large monitor lizard found across savanna, forest, coast, and island settings in a region spanning roughly -9 to -8 degrees latitude and 119 to 121 degrees longitude. It is a carnivore that can reach an adult mass of about 70 kg. Covered in scales and armed with a venomous bite, it stands as an apex predator, and it remains alive today under legal protection.
torvosaurus: Torvosaurus tanneri was a large meat-eating megalosaurid that lived in western North America during the Jurassic, roughly 153 to 148 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Morrison Formation. Adults reached a mass of about 4500 kilograms, making it one of the heavier predators of its time.
fossa: The fossa is the largest carnivore found on Madagascar, weighing about 8 kg as an adult. It lives in the island's forests and jungles, where it hunts meat at night and spends much of its time in the trees. Still living in the wild, this cat-like animal has dense fur that helps it move through its arboreal home.
north_american_river_otter: The North American river otter roams across much of the continent, from the eastern half of the United States to the Pacific Northwest. It makes its home along rivers, lakes, wetlands, and coastlines, where it hunts fish. An adult typically weighs about 9 kilograms, and its dense fur and strong swimming skills help it thrive in these waters.
swift_fox: The Swift Fox, known scientifically as Vulpes velox, makes its home across the Great Plains. It favors open plains and grassland, where it hunts mainly meat in the cover of night. An adult weighs about 2.5 kilograms, and the species survives today with a thick coat and a burrow for shelter.
bharal: The bharal, also called the blue sheep, roams the Himalaya and Tibet. It lives among icy mountain slopes and grazes on herbs. Adults typically weigh around 60 kg, and they move in herds across rugged terrain. This species remains widespread today, though it is hunted in some areas.
abelisaurus: Known only from fossils, Abelisaurus comahuensis roamed Patagonia roughly 80 to 79 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its remains were preserved in sandstone of the Anacleto Formation, a rock unit that also reveals the landscapes it once inhabited. This carnivore weighed about 1400 kilograms as an adult and serves as the type species for the abelisaurids, a group of meat-eating dinosaurs.
hoopoe: The Eurasian hoopoe lives across the Palearctic, Africa, and Indomalaya, moving between plains and forest. Its diet consists of insects, and an adult weighs about 0.07 kg. Its fan-shaped crest and the way it flies are its most noticeable features, and the species is still alive.
manatee_amazonian: The Amazonian manatee lives in the Amazon basin, moving through rivers and wetlands where it feeds on aquatic plants. A full-grown adult can weigh about 400 kilograms. This freshwater sirenian is still alive today, although it is hunted in some areas and is legally protected.
madagascar_giant_tortoise: Once roaming the forests, grasslands, and savannas of Madagascar, this herbivore could weigh as much as 200 kilograms as an adult. Its shell was enormous, and it is thought to have died out around 1200 AD, soon after humans arrived on the island.
king_cobra: The king cobra makes its home in jungles and forests across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland. It is a carnivore that feeds mainly on other snakes, and it is venomous. Adults can reach a mass of about 9 kg. Females build nests from leaf litter, and the species spreads a hood when threatened.
staurikosaurus: Staurikosaurus pricei is a fossil species from the Triassic, roughly 233 to 230 million years ago. Its remains come from mudstone in the Santa Maria Formation of the Southern Cone. This early dinosaur was a carnivore that weighed about 30 kg as an adult.
copperhead: The copperhead is a venomous snake found across eastern North America and the southern United States. It makes its home in forests and in badlands, and it hunts meat-eating prey. Adults typically weigh about 0.3 kilograms, and the species remains alive and widespread today.
chinese_alligator: The Chinese alligator lives in the lowlands of China, where it inhabits swamps, rivers, wetlands, and caves. It is carnivorous and typically weighs around 36 kg as an adult. Its body is covered in protective scales, and it digs burrows and hibernates through the cold months. This species is still alive and is legally protected.
leopard_seal: The leopard seal lives in the icy, cold waters of Antarctica and the subantarctic. It is a carnivore that hunts penguins, and an adult can weigh up to 400 kg. Thick blubber keeps it warm in the frigid ocean, and it is still common today.
acrocanthosaurus: Acrocanthosaurus is known only from fossils, and it lived roughly 113 to 110 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Antlers Formation in the southern United States. This carnivore grew to an adult mass of about 5600 kilograms, and its back bore a distinctive ridge formed by tall neural spines.
red_wolf: Once spread across the forests, swamps, and grasslands of eastern North America, the red wolf now survives only in small numbers in parts of Florida, the Gulf coast, and the southern United States. Adults typically weigh about 25 kilograms and live in packs, hunting small prey as carnivores. Though nearly wiped out in the wild, the species remains alive and is legally protected.
scimitar_oryx: The scimitar-horned oryx lives across the Sahara and Sahel, where it roams open desert and feeds on plants. An adult typically weighs about 180 kilograms and moves in herds. Wild populations died out around 2000, but the species survives and has since been reintroduced into parts of its former range.
opabinia: Known only from fossils, Opabinia lived during the Cambrian period, roughly 508 to 505 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in shale of the Burgess Shale formation in northwestern North America. This swimming carnivore weighed about 0.02 kg as an adult and had five eyes plus a grasping proboscis at the front of its head.
nesophontes_puerto_rican: Once living in the forests of Puerto Rico, this tiny shrew-like mammal weighed only about 50 grams as an adult. Its diet consisted of insects, and it shared the island's woodlands with few other mammals. The species went extinct around 1500 AD, leaving behind only fossil remains.
european_wildcat: The European wildcat roams forests, mountains, and grasslands across Europe, Atlantic Europe, Iran, and Anatolia. An adult weighs about 5 kg and feeds on meat. It hunts mostly at night, and its thick fur helps it survive cold woodland. Its lineage is separate from the ancestors of the cats of the Near East.
pachycormus: Pachycormus was a fossil fish that swam the seas of the Jurassic period, roughly 182 to 175 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from the Posidonia Shale formation in Europe, where they are preserved in shale. Adults reached about 60 kg, and the animal was a carnivore, with a body that resembled a swordfish.
asian_elephant: The Asian elephant ranges across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland, moving through forest, jungle, and grassland. These herbivores graze on plants and can reach an adult mass of about 4000 kg. Living in herds, they are a species that has long been domesticated, and only some males grow tusks, which have historically been prized for their ivory.
sulawesi_warty_pig: The Sulawesi warty pig lives on the island of Sulawesi, roaming the forests of the region that spans roughly from -6 to 2 degrees latitude and 118 to 126 degrees longitude. Adults can reach about 60 kilograms, and the species eats both plants and animals. Males carry tusks, and people on the island hunt these pigs, but the species remains alive today.
culpeo: The culpeo is a fox-like canid that roams the Andes, Patagonia, and the Pampas, moving across mountains, grasslands, and deserts alike. Adults weigh about 10 kilograms and are mostly carnivorous in their eating habits. Unlike many foxes, this species is active during the day, and it remains widespread and alive today.
asian_common_toad: The Asian common toad is found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, and Sundaland, where it lives in forests, wetlands, and grasslands. It feeds mainly on insects and typically reaches about 0.1 kg as an adult. Like other amphibians, it has toxic skin, and it remains widespread today.
galapagos_tortoise_san_cristobal: Roaming the Galapagos archipelago, this giant tortoise makes its home on islands and rugged badlands. Adults can reach about 230 kilograms, and their domed shells carry much of that weight. Its diet consists of plants and herbs, and the species survives today.
dwarf_mongoose: The smallest of the mongooses, the dwarf mongoose weighs about 0.3 kilograms as an adult. It lives in groups within the savanna and grasslands of East and Southern Africa, where it is active during the day and shelters in burrows. Insects make up its diet, and it is still widespread today.
cuban_rock_iguana: Found on Caribbean islands, the Cuban rock iguana lives in forests and along coastlines. It feeds mainly on plants, and an adult typically weighs about 6 kilograms. Active during the day, it shelters in burrows and is still alive in the wild today.
concavenator: A fossil theropod from the Cretaceous, living roughly 130 to 125 million years ago. Its remains were found in limestone of the Calizas de la Huérguina formation in Europe. This meat-eater weighed about 400 kilograms as an adult, and it is known for a distinctive hump on its back along with knobs on its arms where quills once attached.
false_gharial: The false gharial lives in the swamps, rivers, and wetlands of Sundaland, where it hunts mostly fish. Its long, slender snout is well suited to snapping up prey in the water. Adults can reach about 200 kg, and the species is still alive today. Its body is covered in scales, and it moves easily through the water as a strong swimmer.
loris_slender_red: The red slender loris lives in the jungles of southern India and Sri Lanka, where it spends its nights moving through the trees. Insects make up its diet, and an adult weighs around 0.15 kg. Because it is nocturnal and arboreal, it rests in the canopy by day and forages in the branches after dark.
quagga: The quagga was a southern African plains animal, a subspecies of zebra whose range spanned roughly the southern tip of the continent between about 34 and 27 degrees south. It grazed on grasses across open grassland and lived in herds, weighing around 270 kilograms as an adult. Hunting pressure drove it to extinction, and the last known individual died in Amsterdam in 1883.
oribi: The oribi is a small antelope found across sub-Saharan Africa and the Sahel, where it lives in grasslands and savanna. It feeds on herbs and typically weighs about 16 kilograms as an adult. Although still living in the wild, the oribi has horns that make it a sought-after target for hunters.
european_mink: The European mink lives across Europe, from the Atlantic coast to the eastern steppe, where it makes its home in wetlands and along rivers. It is a carnivore that weighs about 0.8 kilograms as an adult, and it is a capable swimmer. Still living today, this species is protected because its dense fur has long made it a target.
siamang: In the dense jungles of Sundaland, the siamang moves through the treetops during the day. It feeds mainly on fruit and weighs about 11 kilograms as an adult. Loud calls carry across the forest, and this species is protected and still survives in the wild.
walliserops: A Devonian fossil taxon, Walliserops trifurcatus lived roughly 390 to 385 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from limestone of the Hamar Laghdad Formation along the North African coast. This animal is thought to have scavenged for its food, and adults weighed about 0.05 kilograms. Its shell and three-pronged rostrum are its most notable features.
bushmaster: The bushmaster, Lachesis muta, roams the jungles of the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as parts of Central America. It is the largest viper in the Americas and can weigh up to about 5 kilograms as an adult. This carnivore is venomous and uses pit organs to sense the warm bodies of its prey, and unlike most vipers it lays eggs.
canary_giant_rat_tenerife: The Tenerife giant rat once lived on the island of Tenerife, where it fed on plants. Adults weighed about 1.5 kilograms, making this rodent a true giant among its kind. It went extinct around 1000 AD.
rat_cane_greater: Found across sub-Saharan Africa, the greater cane rat makes its home in wetlands and grasslands. This nocturnal herbivore weighs about 4.5 kg as an adult and is able to swim. It is still widespread, though people hunt it as game.
bluebuck: The bluebuck was a grazing antelope that once roamed the grasslands and savannas of southwestern Africa, in a range stretching from about 35 degrees south to 26 degrees south. Adults weighed around 160 kilograms, and they lived in herds and fed on herbs. Hunters pursued them, and the last one was shot around 1800, the year the species is recorded as extinct.
koala: Koalas (Phascolarctos cinereus) live in forests across eastern and southern Australia, roughly between latitudes -38 and -16 and longitudes 138 and 153. They spend most of their lives in trees, feeding on eucalyptus leaves and resting by night when they are most active. An adult typically weighs about 9 kg, and the species is still alive and protected.
blue_winged_kookaburra: The blue-winged kookaburra is a living bird found across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea. It makes its home in savanna country, where it hunts meat-based prey. An adult weighs about 0.3 kg, and this species is able to fly.
masiakasaurus: Known only from fossils, this predator lived in Madagascar during the Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Maevarano Formation. Adults weighed about 35 kilograms, and the animal ate meat, with forward-pointing teeth suggesting it caught fish.
sifaka_verreaux: Verreaux's sifaka is a lemur found in Madagascar, where it lives in both forest and desert habitats. Adults weigh about 3.5 kg, and the species feeds mainly on herbs. Active during the day, it spends its time in the trees and moves by leaping from trunk to trunk, and it is still alive in the wild today.
giraffe_reticulated: The reticulated giraffe, Giraffa reticulata, roams savanna country in parts of East Africa. Adults can weigh around 1100 kg, and the species is still alive in the wild. These tall grazers feed mainly on plants and tend to move through the landscape in herds.
tropeognathus: Tropeognathus lived in what is now South America between 113 and 110 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Romualdo, or Santana, formation. It was a fish eater with a keeled snout, and adults weighed about 40 kg. Its wingspan reached roughly 8 meters.
flapshell_turtle: Found across the Indian subcontinent, the Indian flapshell turtle makes its home in wetlands and lakes. Its diet is omnivorous, and adults typically weigh about 1 kilogram. This small turtle is a strong swimmer and is known to aestivate, a dormant state it enters during dry periods.
chinchilla_short_tailed: The short-tailed chinchilla lives in the Andes, where it makes its home among mountain rocks and scrub. It feeds only on plants and grows to about 0.6 kilograms as an adult. Living in herds, it is active at night and relies on its dense fur for warmth. Though still alive in the wild, it is a protected species.
achillobator: Achillobator was a large dromaeosaur that roamed what is now the Mongolian steppe during the Cretaceous, roughly 96 to 90 million years ago. Its fossils were recovered from sandstone of the Bayan Shireh formation. It was a carnivore and an adult weighed about 300 kg.
pikaia: Pikaia lived in the seas of the Cambrian period, roughly 508 to 505 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in shale of the Burgess Shale formation in northwestern North America. This small swimmer weighed about 5 grams as an adult and fed on fine particles, and it is considered an early chordate.
sunda_stink_badger: The Sunda stink badger roams jungles, forests, and mountain slopes across the Sunda region, where it lives in the area bounded by roughly -8 to 6 degrees latitude and 100 to 120 degrees longitude. A nocturnal feeder, it mostly eats insects and digs burrows for shelter. Adults weigh about 2.5 kilograms, and when threatened they release a powerful spray scent from glands near the rear.
ribbon_seal: The ribbon seal roams the cold northern Pacific and the Bering Sea, where it spends much of its life on icy ocean waters. Adults weigh about 90 kilograms, and they feed on other sea creatures. A thick layer of blubber keeps them warm, and each one wears a bold, banded coat that gives the species its name.
eudimorphodon: Eudimorphodon ranzii was an early flying reptile from the Triassic, living roughly 210 to 205 million years ago. Its fossils come from limestone of the Calcare di Zorzino formation in the Alps. It is the oldest known pterosaur, and it had multicusp teeth suited to catching fish, weighing about half a kilogram as an adult.
senegal_chameleon: Found along the West African coast, through the Sahel, and into the Congo basin, the Senegal chameleon makes its home in both forest and savanna. It lives mostly in trees and feeds on insects. An adult weighs about 0.1 kg, and its body is covered in fine scales. This species is still alive and widespread across its range.
bontebok: The bontebok is a grazing antelope that lives in grasslands within a small coastal stretch of southwestern South Africa. It feeds mainly on herbs and typically weighs around 65 kilograms as an adult. Living in herds, it carries distinctive horns and remains alive today, though it is also a species that can be hunted.
marmot_bobak: Found across the Kazakh and Eastern steppe, the steppe marmot makes its home in open grassland. It feeds on plants and grasses, and adults weigh around 5.5 kg. Living in burrows, it hibernates through the cold months, and it is still widely found today.
atlas_wild_ass: The Atlas wild ass once roamed the deserts and mountains of northern Africa, living on a diet of plants. Adults weighed about 230 kg. Herds moved across this range, and the animal was hunted by people until it vanished around 400 AD during the Roman era.
hadropithecus: Hadropithecus was a giant lemur that lived on the ground in Madagascar. It fed on herbs and moved through desert and grassland habitats. Adults weighed about 35 kg, and the species died out around the year 1000 AD.
patas_monkey: The patas monkey roams the Sahel and the East African savanna, where it moves through open grassland and scrubby savanna. An adult typically weighs about 9 kilograms. It is an omnivore that is active during the day and lives in herds. This species is still alive and is known for being an exceptionally fast runner.
african_egg_eating_snake: This slender snake lives across Africa south of the Sahara, where it moves through both savanna and forest. Its diet consists entirely of eggs, which it swallows whole, and it is nocturnal and harmless to people. An adult weighs only about 0.1 kg, and the species remains widespread today.
golden_poison_frog: Found only in a small patch of rainforest on Colombia's Pacific coast, this tiny frog weighs about one gram as an adult. Its skin carries toxins strong enough to make it the most poisonous animal known, and Indigenous peoples have long used that poison to tip blowdarts. It feeds on insects and remains alive in the wild today.
stoat: Found across the Nearctic, Palearctic, Europe, and the British Isles, this carnivore lives in forests, grasslands, and tundra. Adults weigh about 0.25 kg. In winter its brown coat turns white, a form known as the ermine, and its fur is hunted for trade.
raccoon: Raccoons roam across much of North America, from the eastern woodlands and Great Plains down through Mexico and Central America, and also along the Pacific Northwest and the southern United States. They make their homes in forests, wetlands, and river banks, eating a mix of plant and animal foods. An adult typically weighs about 7 kilograms, and these nocturnal animals use their sensitive, nimble paws and their strong swimming ability to hunt and forage.
leopard_cat: The leopard cat is a small, spotted wild cat that roams much of Indomalaya, the China lowlands, and parts of Japan and Korea. It lives in forests, jungles, grasslands, and mountains, hunting mostly at night and sometimes taking to the water. An adult weighs about 4 kg, and it is still alive in the wild.
green_frog: Green frogs make their home across eastern North America and parts of the Canadian Shield, where they settle in wetlands, lakes, and rivers. These amphibians are strong swimmers and spend much of their time in the water. As carnivores, they hunt insects and other small prey, and an adult typically weighs about 0.2 kilograms. The species is still thriving today.
cylindraspis_inepta: The Mauritius saddle-backed tortoise once roamed the forests of the Mascarene islands, where it fed on plants and grew to adults weighing around 100 kilograms. Its high, saddle-shaped shell helped it reach up for vegetation. Sailors who landed on these islands took many of these tortoises as food, and the species was gone by 1735.
elephant_trunk_snake: The Elephant Trunk Snake lives in Sundaland and Indochina, where it moves through rivers, swamps, and coastal waters. It is an aquatic, nocturnal swimmer that hunts fish, and adults typically weigh about 2 kg. Its rough, scale-covered skin sets it apart, and it remains widespread in the wild.
common_frog: The common frog ranges across Europe, the British Isles, Scandinavia, and Atlantic Europe. It lives in wetlands, forests, and grasslands, feeding on insects. Adults weigh about 0.03 kilograms, and this amphibian swims well and spends the winter in hibernation.
cylindraspis_triserrata: The Mauritius Domed Tortoise once roamed the forests of its island home in the Mascarene archipelago. Its diet consisted of herbs, and adults could reach a mass of about 100 kg. Sailors took many of these tortoises as provisions, and the species became extinct by 1735 AD.
sloth_cuban_parocnus: Parocnus serus lived in the forests of the Caribbean and fed on plants. An adult weighed about 30 kilograms. This island megafauna disappeared around 2500 BC, leaving the forests of the region without one of their largest herbivores.
european_badger: The European badger is found across Europe, the British Isles, Atlantic Europe, and parts of Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home in forests and grasslands, where it roams at night and eats both plants and animals. Adults typically weigh around 12 kg, and the species remains widespread today, living in burrows and wearing a thick coat that can be hunted.
hamster_european: The European hamster is a grassland dweller found across Europe and on the Kazakh steppe. Adults weigh about 0.4 kilograms, and the animal eats a mix of plant and animal foods. It digs burrows where it lives and hibernates through the cold months, and it remains alive in the wild today.
water_holding_frog: The Water-holding Frog lives across Australia, where it moves between desert and savanna country. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 0.05 kg as an adult. When the dry season arrives, this amphibian burrows underground and wraps itself in a cocoon, then aestivates until rain returns.
tetrameryx: Shuler's pronghorn once roamed the plains and deserts of the southern United States and Mexico. It fed on herbs and grew to an adult mass of about 60 kilograms. Its most striking feature was its set of four horns, a rare trait among hoofed animals. This species has been extinct since around 9500 BC.
flying_fox_grey_headed: The grey-headed flying fox is a nocturnal bat that roams forest habitats across a wide stretch of eastern Australia. It gathers in large colonies, and adults weigh about 0.7 kilograms. Fruit makes up its diet. The species is still alive today.
bairds_tapir: Baird's tapir roams the jungles, forests, and wetlands of Mexico and Central America. It is a herbivore that weighs about 300 kilograms as an adult, and it is still alive today. This animal is a strong swimmer and is hunted in parts of its range.
round_island_day_gecko: The Round Island day gecko is a small, colorful lizard that lives on islands and in forest habitats in the Mascarene region. Adults weigh about 0.05 kilograms, and they are active during the day. Their diet is omnivorous, and they are covered in fine scales. This species is still alive today and is protected.
bat_kitti_hog_nosed: The bumblebee bat roosts in caves and jungle, and it hunts insects through the night. An adult weighs about 0.002 kilograms, and the species ranks as the smallest mammal by length. It is still alive today and receives legal protection.
desert_iguana: The desert iguana is a small lizard, weighing about a tenth of a kilogram as an adult, found across western North America and into Mexico. It lives in deserts and badlands, where it is active during the day and spends nights in burrows. Its diet is made up of plants, and it remains widespread today.
placodus: Placodus gigas lived during the Triassic, roughly 245 to 235 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Muschelkalk formation in Europe. This marine reptile weighed about 90 kilograms as an adult. Its broad, flattened teeth were built for crushing shells, and it fed on hard-shelled prey.
xiphactinus: A bulldog-jawed predator from the Cretaceous, Xiphactinus audax lived roughly 87 to 80 million years ago. Its fossils come from the chalk of the Niobrara Formation across the Great Plains. Adults reached about 400 kilograms, and it ate other fish, as shown by fossils of smaller fish found inside its body.
sloth_bear: Sloth bears roam the Indian subcontinent, moving through forests, grasslands, and badlands alike. Most of their diet is insects, especially termites, which they dig out of mounds and suck up with a gap in their front teeth. Adults weigh around 100 kilograms, and their shaggy fur helps them stay hidden as they forage mostly after dark. Mothers even carry their young on their backs.
bat_fringe_lipped: The fringe-lipped bat roams the jungles of Central America and the wider Neotropics. It is a nocturnal flier that weighs only about 32 grams as an adult. Its diet is carnivorous, and it is known for hunting frogs, which it locates after dark.
banded_sea_krait: The banded sea krait roams warm coastal waters and reefs along the Indo-Pacific coast and through the Coral Triangle. It hunts fish, swims with ease through the ocean, and is venomous, yet it still comes ashore to lay its eggs. Adults typically weigh about 1.5 kilograms.
scaphites: A hook-shaped shell marks this Cretaceous ammonite relative, which lived roughly 85 to 80 million years ago. Its fossils turn up in the chalk of the Niobrara Chalk formation across the Great Plains. The creature was a carnivore and grew to about 0.3 kilograms as an adult.
kangaroo_western_grey: The Western grey kangaroo lives across Australia, moving through both forest and open grassland. Adults weigh around 40 kilograms and feed on herbs. These animals travel in herds and move by hopping, and they remain alive and widespread today, though they can be hunted.
king_brown_snake: The mulga snake roams the deserts and savannas of Australia, where it hunts small prey. Adults typically weigh about 3 kilograms, making them one of the heavier venomous snakes on the continent. Its scales and venom mark it as a dangerous predator, and the species remains widespread and common in the wild today.
wiwaxia: Wiwaxia corrugata lived during the Cambrian, roughly 508 to 505 million years ago, and its fossils come from shale in the Burgess Shale formation of northwestern North America. This small creature weighed about 0.01 kilograms as an adult and is thought to have fed on plants. Its body was covered in armoured scales, and it is often described as an armoured slug.
caiman_lizard: The caiman lizard roams the Amazon and Orinoco river systems, moving through swamps, rivers, and jungle. It weighs about 3 kg as an adult and feeds mainly on meat, with a notable taste for snails that it crushes with powerful jaws. Its armored scales and strong swimming ability help it thrive in its watery home.
diamondback_terrapin: The diamondback terrapin lives along the eastern coast of North America and around Florida and the Gulf. It favors coastal wetlands and brackish water, where it swims and hunts for its meals. Adults typically weigh about half a kilogram, and the patterned shell helps identify this living species.
crab_eating_fox: The crab-eating fox roams the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It moves through forest, savanna, and wetland, and it eats a varied diet of both plants and animals. Adults weigh about 6.5 kg, and this species is still widespread today. It is active at night and has a coat of dense fur.
jamaican_iguana: The Jamaican Iguana is a plant-eating lizard found on the island of Jamaica, where it lives in forested areas. Adults typically weigh around 5 kilograms. This species is active during the daytime and remains alive today, and it is a protected animal.
night_monkey: Active only after dark, the northern night monkey moves through the forest canopy in search of food. It makes its home across the Amazon and Orinoco basins, where dense jungle gives it cover among the trees. Weighing about 0.8 kilograms as an adult, this species is still thriving in the wild. Its diet centers on fruit.
wombat_common: Burrowing through forest and mountain country, the common wombat lives in Tasmania and grazes on plants. An adult typically weighs about 28 kg. Active mostly at night, it shelters in burrows and leaves behind distinctive cube-shaped droppings.
marsh_frog: The marsh frog is an amphibian found across Europe, Iran, Anatolia, the eastern steppe, and the Mediterranean region. It lives in wetlands, lakes, and rivers, where it swims well and feeds on other animals. Adults weigh about 0.2 kg, and the species is still alive and widespread. It is known for its loud calls and for its legs, which people have long eaten.
capromeryx: The diminutive pronghorn, Capromeryx minor, once roamed the plains and deserts of the southern United States and Mexico. It grazed on herbs and weighed about 20 kilograms as an adult. It was hunted for its horns, and it went extinct around 9500 BC.
tylosaurus: A fossil mosasaur from the Cretaceous, living roughly 87 to 80 million years ago. Its remains come from the Niobrara Chalk formation of the Great Plains, where they have been preserved in chalk. This carnivore could reach an adult mass of about 6000 kg, and it was known for its long snout.
gemuendina: Gemuendina stuertzi was a ray-like placoderm that lived during the Devonian period, roughly 400 to 395 million years ago. Its fossils come from shale in the Hunsrück Slate formation of Europe. Adults reached about 3 kilograms, and the animal swam through its waters as a carnivore.
mouflon: Wild sheep of mountain slopes and badlands, the mouflon ranges across Iran and Anatolia. Adults weigh about 45 kg and feed on herbs while moving through herds. Males carry curved horns, and the species is still alive today, hunted in some areas and known as an ancestor of domestic sheep.
gila_monster: Gila monsters are venomous lizards with beaded, black-and-pink skin that roam the deserts and badlands of western North America and Mexico. They spend much of their lives in burrows and feed mainly on eggs and other small animals. An adult typically weighs around 0.7 kilograms, and because the species is protected, collecting one from the wild is restricted.
japanese_tree_frog: Small and climbing, the Japanese Tree Frog lives across Japan, Korea, the lowlands of China, and parts of northern Asia. It moves through forests and wetlands, where it hunts insects and spends much of its life in trees. An adult weighs only about 5 grams, and the species is still widespread today.
royal_antelope: Among the smallest antelopes in the world, this tiny forest dweller weighs only about 3 kilograms as an adult. It lives along the coast of West Africa, where it browses on herbs in dense woodland. Males carry small, slender horns, and the species is still widespread, though it can be hunted.
giant_tree_frog_brazil: Found in the Amazon and Orinoco regions, this amphibian lives along rivers and in the surrounding jungle. It feeds on other animals and weighs about 0.1 kilograms as an adult. Males build mud nests, and the species is still living today.
yukon_horse: The Yukon horse once roamed the tundra and plains of Alaska, the Yukon, and Beringia. It lived in herds and grazed on herbs, with adults reaching about 300 kg. People hunted these animals for food and their thick fur. The species is long gone, having died out around 3700 BC.
hawaiian_monk_seal: The Hawaiian monk seal lives around the islands of Hawaii, where it spends its time along the coast, over reefs, and on the shores of small islands. It eats meat and can grow to an adult mass of about 230 kilograms. Thick layers of blubber keep it warm, and the species is protected, which is why it still survives today.
hokkaido_wolf: The Hokkaido wolf once roamed the forests and taiga of Hokkaido, between roughly 41.5 and 45.5 degrees north and 140 and 146 degrees east. This carnivore lived in packs and grew to an adult mass of about 35 kilograms, with a thick coat suited to the island's cold winters. The last known individual was killed in 1889, and the subspecies is now considered extinct.
pentecopterus: An extinct sea scorpion relative, Pentecopterus was a carnivore that lived during the Ordovician, roughly 467 to 466 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in shale of the Winneshiek Shale formation in the Great Plains. It swam through ancient seas and grew to about 1.7 meters long, weighing around 20 kilograms as an adult, making it the oldest known eurypterid of its size.
agouti_orange_rumped: The orange-rumped agouti roams the jungles and forests of the Amazon and Orinoco basins. Adults weigh about 3.5 kg, and the species remains widespread today. It feeds mainly on fruit, and it is active during the day. Because it buries seeds, it helps plant life spread through the forest.
tiger: The tiger roams the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Sundaland, and the China lowlands, where it lives in jungles, forests, swamps, and grasslands. An adult can weigh as much as 220 kg, and it hunts other animals for meat. It is nocturnal, swims well, and has a striking coat, with the Bengal form being one of its best-known varieties. Still living today, the tiger is a protected species.
bactrian_camel: The Bactrian camel roams the steppes of Mongolia and Kazakhstan, with wild and domestic populations also found in Iran and Anatolia. It makes its home across deserts and open plains, grazing on herbs and living in herds. Adults can weigh around 600 kilograms, and the species has been domesticated for its thick fur and milk.
wolverine: Wolverines roam the Arctic, Scandinavia, the Siberian taiga, Alaska and the Yukon, the Canadian Shield, and northwestern North America. They live in taiga, tundra, and mountain country, and they mostly feed by scavenging carcasses. An adult typically weighs about 15 kg, and its thick fur is prized, though the species is still alive and widespread.
death_adder: The Common Death Adder is a venomous snake found in Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea, where it lives in forests and grasslands. It hunts by ambush, lying still until prey comes near, and feeds on other animals. Adults typically weigh around 0.4 kg, and the species is still alive and widespread.
cymbospondylus: Cymbospondylus petrinus was an eel-like ichthyosaur that swam the seas of the Triassic, roughly 244 to 242 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Favret Formation in western North America. This carnivore could reach an adult mass of about 2000 kilograms.
armadillo_southern_three_banded: Found across the Pampas and Gran Chaco, this small armadillo makes its home in grassland and desert country. It feeds mainly on insects and weighs about 1.2 kg as an adult. Its three bands of armor let it roll into a tight ball when threatened, and it remains widespread today.
pygmy_hippo: Pygmy hippos roam the forests, swamps, and rivers of West Africa, where they graze mainly on plants. An adult typically weighs about 240 kilograms, a fraction of its larger cousin's bulk. Though still living in the wild, this species is protected, and it is known for its strong swimming ability.
odontochelys: Known only from fossils, this half-shelled turtle lived during the Triassic, roughly 220 to 215 million years ago. Its remains were found in limestone of the Wayao formation in the lowlands of China. It was a carnivore with teeth, and adults weighed about 1 kilogram.
madagascar_bullfrog: The Madagascar bullfrog lives on the island of Madagascar, where it makes its home in savanna and wetland areas. It is a carnivore, and adults typically weigh around 0.1 kg. Being an amphibian, it spends time in burrows, and it remains alive today.
african_wild_dog: Across sub-Saharan Africa and the Sahel, this painted hunter roams savanna, grassland, and badlands in packs. Adults weigh about 25 kg, and their mottled coats of black, tan, and white make each animal easy to recognize. Active during the day, they hunt together as a pack, and the species is protected, though it still survives in the wild.
dawson_caribou: Dawson's caribou once roamed the forests of an island off the coast of British Columbia, where it fed on herbs and grazed in herds. Adults weighed around 120 kilograms, and the animals carried antlers that made them a target for hunters. The subspecies was declared extinct in 1935.
hispaniolan_monkey: The Hispaniolan monkey once lived in the forests of Hispaniola, an island in the Caribbean. It ate a mixed diet of both plant and animal foods and weighed about 7 kilograms as an adult. This primate was lost around 1500 AD, and it is one of the extinct monkeys known from the Caribbean islands.
jamaican_monkey: The Jamaican monkey once lived in the forests of Jamaica, a Caribbean island, where it moved through dense jungle canopy. Adults weighed about 3 kilograms, and this omnivore ate a mixed diet. It became extinct around 1500 AD, making it one of the few primates lost from the Caribbean in recorded times.
elongated_tortoise: The Elongated Tortoise is found across Indochina and the Indian subcontinent, where it makes its home in forests and jungles. It is an omnivore, eating a mix of plant and animal foods. An adult typically weighs about 3 kg, and its long, domed shell marks it as a species still thriving in the wild. It is active during the day.
box_turtle_eastern: The eastern box turtle roams across eastern North America, moving through forests and grasslands in search of food. Its diet is omnivorous, and an adult typically weighs about half a kilogram. Its domed shell has a hinge across the lower part, allowing the turtle to close its body inside almost completely. Active during the day, it is known for a long lifespan, and it remains widespread today.
pronghorn: Across the Great Plains, western North America, and parts of Mexico, pronghorn roam open country and desert scrub. These herbivores weigh about 50 kilograms as adults and live in herds. They are the fastest land mammal in the Americas, and they are still hunted in some areas.
checkered_sengi: Active during the day, this small mammal forages for insects in forest habitats across the East African savanna, Southern Africa, and the Congo basin. An adult weighs about 0.5 kilograms. It is not extinct, and it remains widespread across these regions.
black_billed_magpie: The black-billed magpie ranges across western North America, from the Great Plains up through Alaska and the Yukon. It makes its home in both open plains and woodland, and it eats nearly anything, from insects to seeds to carrion. An adult weighs about 0.17 kg, and this bird is still thriving in the wild, known for its long tail feathers, strong flight, and sharp intelligence.
chinese_water_dragon: Found along rivers and through the jungles of Indochina and Sundaland, this lizard spends its days active in the daylight. It climbs trees with ease and drops into the water to swim when danger appears. Adults weigh around 0.6 kilograms, and the species eats both plants and animals.
morelet_crocodile: Found in southern Mexico and parts of Central America, this crocodile makes its home in swamps, rivers, and other wetlands. Adults typically reach about 100 kilograms, and the species remains alive in the wild. It hunts meat as its diet and moves through the water with strong swimming.
mountain_goat: Mountain goats roam the rugged peaks of northwestern North America, from Alaska and the Yukon down through the Pacific Northwest. They make their homes on steep, icy slopes and feed on plants and herbs. Adults can weigh around 90 kg, and they live in herds, with a thick coat of fur and sharp horns that help them hold their ground.
perisphinctes: Perisphinctes was a ribbed ammonite that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 160 to 155 million years ago. Its fossils have been found in limestone of the Solnhofen region in the Franconian Jura of Europe. Adults reached about 0.3 kg, and the animal is classed as a carnivore.
brontoscorpio: Brontoscorpio anglicus was a fossil arthropod of the Silurian period, living roughly 420 to 418 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from shale in the Ludlow Bone Bed formation of the British Isles. It is thought to have been a carnivore, an aquatic giant scorpion weighing about 3 kilograms as an adult, though that size is an estimate.
panther_chameleon: Native to Madagascar, the panther chameleon lives in forests, jungles, and coastal areas. It climbs through the trees and feeds on insects. Adults weigh about 0.15 kilograms, and the species is still found in the wild. Its skin is covered in scales, and it is well known for changing colour.
dolphin_bottlenose: Found across the world's oceans, the common bottlenose dolphin lives in warm waters, cold waters, and coastal zones alike. It is a carnivore, and adults can reach about 250 kg. Toothed and intelligent, it swims in pods, and it remains very much alive today.
parapuzosia: Parapuzosia lived during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 80 to 78 million years ago, and its fossils have been recovered from chalk in the Münsterland Cretaceous Basin near Coesfeld in Europe. This ammonite is thought to have eaten meat and reached an adult mass of about 700 kg. Its shell measured 1.8 m across, making it the largest known ammonite.
sloth_ground_eremotherium: Eremotherium laurillardi was a giant ground sloth that roamed South America, Central America, and the Florida and Gulf regions. It lived in forests and savannas, feeding on plants, and adults could reach about 3000 kilograms. Its long claws set it apart, and it vanished around 9000 BC as one of the extinct megafauna.
aardvark: Aardvarks live across Africa south of the Sahara, where they roam savanna and grassland. Their nighttime diet consists of insects, especially ants, and they dig burrows to rest in during the day. An adult aardvark can weigh around 55 kilograms, and the species is still alive and widespread.
snow_leopard: Adapted to high mountain terrain, the snow leopard lives across the Himalaya, Tibet, and the Mongolian steppe. Adults weigh about 40 kg, and they hunt meat in rocky, icy, and badland country. Their thick fur and long tail help them stay warm in cold conditions, and the species is still alive and protected.
orangutan_sumatran: Sumatran orangutans, known scientifically as Pongo abelii, live in the jungle, where they spend much of their lives in the trees. They are solitary, active during the day, and feed mainly on fruit. An adult typically weighs about 50 kg, and the species is still alive and protected.
striped_skunk: Nocturnal and omnivorous, the striped skunk weighs about 3 kilograms as an adult. It lives across North America south of 42 degrees north, including the Canadian Shield, the Great Plains, and eastern regions, and it is found in both grassland and forest. Its black fur with white stripes warns predators, and when threatened it sprays a strong-smelling scent. It often shelters in burrows.
proganochelys: Known only from fossils, this shelled reptile lived during the Triassic, roughly 215 to 210 million years ago. Its remains come from mudstone of the Trossingen Formation in Europe. Adults reached about 40 kg, and the animal fed on plants, while a club at the end of its tail offered protection.
saurosuchus: Saurosuchus lived during the Triassic, roughly 230 to 225 million years ago, and is known only from fossils. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Ischigualasto formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This rauisuchian was a carnivore that grew to an adult mass of about 300 kg.
sloth_maned: The maned sloth lives in forest habitats within a small coastal region of eastern Brazil, roughly between latitudes 12 and 23 degrees south. Adults weigh about 4.5 kilograms, and they feed only on plants. This slow-moving animal spends nearly its whole life in the trees, and it remains alive today.
rice_paddy_snake: The Rice Paddy Snake is found across the lowlands of Indochina, China, and the Indian subcontinent, where it lives in wetlands and rivers. It is a carnivore that swims well and is harmless to people. An adult weighs about 0.2 kg, and the species is still alive today.
carnotaurus: Carnotaurus sastrei lived during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 72 to 69 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the La Colonia formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. This meat-eater reached an adult mass of about 1500 kilograms and was known for the bony horns above its eyes and its strikingly tiny arms.
spider_monkey_geoffroy: Found across southern Mexico and Central America, this spider monkey moves through jungle canopy with its long, grasping tail acting almost like a fifth limb.
