Adults weigh about 8 kg, and the species is active by day, spending most of its life high in the trees. Its diet is mainly fruit, and it remains a living species today.
liopleurodon: Liopleurodon ferox was a marine reptile that swam the Jurassic seas roughly 165 to 160 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Oxford Clay formation in the British Isles. As an apex pliosaur measuring 6 to 7 metres long and weighing around 2500 kilograms, it was a carnivore at the top of its ocean food chain.
giant_deer: The giant deer roamed Europe, the British Isles, Siberia, the eastern steppe, and parts of Iran and Anatolia. It moved through forests, plains, and tundra, grazing on plants and reaching adult masses near 600 kilograms. Often called the Irish elk, it carried enormous antlers, and its last survivors lingered in the Urals until about 5500 BC.
howler_red: The red howler monkey roams the jungles of the Amazon and Orinoco river basins, where it feeds mainly on plants. Adults weigh about 7 kilograms, and they live in troops that stay active during the day. Their loud calls carry far through the forest, and the species is still thriving in the wild.
voay_robustus: The Malagasy horned crocodile once roamed the swamps, lakes, rivers, and wetlands of Madagascar. Adults could reach about 250 kg, and their heavy bodies were protected by thick scales and a skull crowned with distinctive horns. This massive meat-eater vanished around 500 BC, following the arrival of humans on the island.
asian_giant_softshell: The Asian Giant Softshell Turtle lives across Indochina, the Indian subcontinent, Sundaland, and Wallacea and New Guinea. It favors rivers and coastal waters, where it swims and hides by burying itself in mud. Adults can reach about 100 kg, and this carnivore waits in ambush for prey to pass by.
hellbender_eastern: Hellbenders are large salamanders that live on the rocky bottoms of rivers across eastern North America. They spend their nights hunting prey and rely on their wrinkled skin to take in oxygen straight from the water. An adult can weigh around 1.5 kilograms, and the species is protected because its populations have declined.
smoky_mountain_salamander: This small amphibian has no lungs and breathes entirely through its skin and the lining of its mouth. It lives in forests and on mountain slopes within a range spanning roughly 35 to 36 degrees north and 82.5 to 84 degrees west. Adults weigh only about 5 grams, and they feed on insects. The species is still living today.
puff_adder: Found across Africa south of the Sahara, in Arabia, and along the Sahel, this venomous snake waits in savanna, grassland, and desert for prey to come close. Adults weigh about 3 kg, and they feed on other animals. Its bite is deadly, and it relies on ambush rather than chasing, so it stays hidden until the moment to strike.
frilled_lizard: Spreading a large neck frill and hissing, this lizard startles predators when threatened. It lives in savanna and forest across Australia, Wallacea, and New Guinea, climbs trees, and sometimes sprints on its hind legs. Adults weigh about half a kilogram and feed mainly on insects.
horned_viper: Found across the Sahara, Arabia, and the Nile valley, this venomous desert snake gets its name from the pair of raised scales above its eyes. Adults weigh about 0.3 kg, and the species still thrives in the wild. It moves by sidewinding across loose sand and preys on small animals.
indian_cobra: The Indian Cobra, known scientifically as Naja naja, is still living across the Indian subcontinent. It moves through savanna, forest, and wetland, and it feeds on other animals. Adults reach about 3 kilograms, and the species is covered in smooth scales and carries venom. When threatened, it spreads its hood, and in parts of the region it is regarded as sacred.
hutia_quemisia: Once roaming the forests of the Caribbean, the Quemisia was a giant rodent that fed on plants. Adults weighed about 10 kg, making them a substantial mammal of their island home. The species became extinct around 1500 AD.
african_golden_wolf: The African golden wolf is still living across a wide belt of northern and eastern Africa, from the Sahara and the Sahel to the savannas of the east and the Mediterranean coast in the north. It roams savanna, desert, and grassland, and it eats a mix of plant and animal food. Adults weigh about 12 kilograms, and its golden fur helps it blend into dry, open country where it hunts mainly at night.
red_necked_pond_turtle: The Long-necked Turtle makes its home in Australia, where it lives in lakes, wetlands, and rivers. It is a carnivore that swims well through these waters and grows to an adult mass of about 1 kilogram. Its most striking feature is a snake-like neck that it can thrust out quickly to catch its prey.
malagasy_hippo_lemerlei: The Malagasy dwarf hippo once lived on Madagascar, where it made its home along rivers, lakes, and wetlands. It fed on plants and grew to an adult mass of about 300 kg. Its ability to swim and the isolation of its island home are noted features, and it is believed to have died out around the year 1000 AD, after being hunted by people.
bambiraptor: Bambiraptor feinbergi is a fossil dinosaur from the Cretaceous period, living roughly 75 to 71 million years ago. Its remains were found in sandstone of the Two Medicine Formation in northwestern North America. This small Montana raptor was a carnivore and weighed about 2 kilograms as an adult.
shrew_christmas_island: The Christmas Island shrew once lived in the jungles of a small island in the Indian Ocean, roughly between latitudes 10.4 and 10.6 south and longitudes 105.6 and 105.8 east. This tiny creature weighed about 0.01 kilograms as an adult and fed on insects. It was last recorded as extinct in 1985.
pacman_frog: Found in the Amazon and Orinoco regions, this amphibian lives in the jungle and is still thriving today. Adults weigh about 0.4 kilograms, and they hunt by ambush, waiting for prey to pass close by. Its huge mouth lets it take in a wide range of meat-based food.
saltwater_crocodile: Found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Sundaland, Wallacea, New Guinea, and northern Australia, this crocodile favors coastlines, rivers, swamps, and warm ocean waters. It is the largest living reptile, with adults reaching about 450 kilograms. Its meat-based diet is gathered by lying in wait and striking suddenly, and it is still alive and widespread today.
dhole: The dhole is a wild canine still found across much of Asia, from the Indian subcontinent and Indochina to the Himalaya, Tibet, and the Mongolian steppe. It lives in forest, jungle, and mountain country, where it hunts in packs during the day. An adult typically weighs about 15 kg, and its thick fur helps it cope with cold highland winters. Dholes communicate with whistles, and the species is legally protected.
maned_wolf: The maned wolf roams the pampas and Gran Chaco of South America, moving through grassland, savanna, and wetland. Adults weigh about 23 kg, and they stand on long legs that help them see over tall grass. This nocturnal animal eats a varied, omnivorous diet and is a protected species that is still alive today.
cylindraspis_peltastes: The Rodrigues saddle-backed tortoise once lived in the forests of Rodrigues, a small island in the Mascarene group. It grazed on plants and grew to an adult mass of about 80 kilograms. Its domed shell made it a valued source of food for sailors, and the species was extinct by 1795.
ruppells_fox: Ruppell's Fox lives across the Sahara, Arabia, Iran and Anatolia, and the Sahel. It makes its home in desert country, where it rests in burrows during the day and comes out to hunt at night. Weighing about 2 kg as an adult, it eats both plants and animals, and its thick fur helps it cope with the desert climate. It is still alive and widespread.
dwarf_crocodile: The African dwarf crocodile lives along the west coast of Africa and throughout the Congo basin. It makes its home in swamps, rivers, and jungle waters, where it hunts meat-eating prey after dark. Adults reach about 40 kilograms, and this small, scaly reptile is still widespread today.
borealopelta: Borealopelta markmitchelli is known only from fossils, and it lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 112 to 110 million years ago. Its remains were preserved in shale of the Clearwater, or Wabiskaw, formation in northwestern North America. This plant eater weighed about 1300 kilograms as an adult, and it is notable for being found mummified with its skin preserved, showing countershading.
notiomastodon: A huge herbivore of South America, the notiomastodon roamed forests, plains, and savannas. An adult could weigh around 6000 kilograms, and it lived in herds and grazed on plants. It was a gomphothere with prominent tusks, and it became extinct around 9500 BC.
dakosaurus: Dakosaurus andiniensis was a short-snouted marine crocodile-relative that hunted in the seas of the Jurassic, roughly 150 to 140 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Vaca Muerta formation in Patagonia and the Pampas. Adults reached about 800 kilograms, and it was a carnivore that lived as a powerful predator in its ocean home.
wood_turtle: Found across eastern North America and the Canadian Shield, the wood turtle moves between forest and river habitats. Adults weigh about 1 kilogram, and this omnivore eats a varied diet while it swims in streams. It spends the cold months hibernating, and the species remains alive today.
sacabambaspis: Among the earliest known armored fishes, this jawless creature swam in Ordovician seas roughly 470 to 465 million years ago. Its fossils are preserved in sandstone of the Anzaldo Formation in the Andes. Adults are thought to have weighed about 1 kilogram, and the animal is described as a swimmer with a bony armored body.
banded_krait: The banded krait is found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Sundaland, and the lowlands of China, where it makes its home in wetlands, forests, and jungle. It is a carnivore that hunts mostly at night, and it is venomous. Adults typically reach about 2 kilograms in mass.
ball_python: Found along the western coast of Africa and across the Sahel, the ball python thrives in savanna, forest edges, and grassland. Adults typically reach about 1.8 kilograms, and they hunt small mammals after dark. When threatened, this species tucks its head into a tight coil, which gives it the name a ball python.
viscacha_plains: Plains viscachas roam the grasslands of the Pampas, the Gran Chaco, and Patagonia, where they feed on herbs. A full-grown adult weighs about 5 kg. These social rodents live in herds, dig burrows to shelter in, and stay active mostly at night.
black_rhino: The black rhinoceros (Diceros bicornis) roams the lands of Africa south of the Sahara, moving through savanna and forest country. Adults weigh about 1100 kg, and they feed entirely on herbs. Its horn makes it a target for poachers, and the animal can be dangerous when provoked, though it still survives in the wild today.
paradoxides_gracilis: A large trilobite, Paradoxides gracilis lived during the Cambrian period, roughly 505 to 500 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from shale of the Jince Formation in Europe. It is thought to have fed as a scavenger, and adults reached about 0.4 kilograms.
grey_wolf: Grey wolves roam a wide stretch of the world, from North America through Eurasia to Arabia and Mexico. They make their homes in forests, taiga, tundra, plains, mountains, and grasslands. Living in packs, they hunt mostly at night and are the ancestors of domestic dogs.
ichthyosaurus: Ichthyosaurus communis swam the seas of the Jurassic, roughly 200 to 190 million years ago. Its fossils turn up in the limestone of the Blue Lias formation across the British Isles, with famous finds at Lyme Regis. This carnivore weighed about 90 kg as an adult and had a streamlined, dolphin-like body.
belemnite_acrocoelites: Acrocoelites vulgaris lived during the Jurassic, roughly 182 to 175 million years ago. Its fossils turn up in the shale of the Posidonia Shale formation in Europe, where the ink sac has been preserved. This belemnite was a carnivore and reached an adult mass of about 0.2 kg.
turtle_headed_sea_snake: The turtle-headed sea snake lives in warm reef waters of the Great Barrier Reef and the Coral Triangle. It is venomous and swims through the reef in search of fish eggs, which make up its diet. An adult weighs about 0.2 kg, and the species is still alive today.
giant_panda: The giant panda makes its home in forested mountains and lowland areas of China, where it is a protected species. Adults can weigh around 110 kilograms, and nearly all of their diet is plant matter, especially bamboo. This animal is active during the day and is still alive in the wild today, its thick fur helping it endure the cool mountain climate.
oviraptor: Oviraptor lived in what is now Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Djadochta formation, which preserves the remains of an ancient steppe landscape. Adults weighed about 33 kilograms, and the animal had a crested, toothless beak and was an omnivore. Specimens found on nests suggest it brooded its eggs.
navahoceros: The mountain deer roamed western North America, where it made its home in highland country and fed on herbs. Adults reached a mass of about 120 kilograms, and the males carried antlers. This animal became extinct around 9500 BC.
ichthyornis: Ichthyornis dispar lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 85 to 83 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Niobrara Chalk formation of the Great Plains, where they are preserved within chalk. This toothed, tern-like bird weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult and fed on fish.
yellow_bellied_sea_snake: The Yellow-bellied Sea Snake lives in tropical seas, including parts of the Indian Ocean, where it spends its life in warm open water and near coastlines. It is a venomous swimmer that drifts through the ocean and feeds on fish. An adult typically weighs about 0.2 kg, and the species is still widespread today.
american_marten: The American marten is a small omnivore that lives across the Canadian Shield, Alaska, the Yukon, northwestern North America, and parts of the east. It makes its home in taiga and forest, where its fur and climbing skills help it get by. Adults weigh about 1 kg, and the species is still alive and widespread.
taipan: The coastal taipan lives across northern and eastern Australia, along with Wallacea and New Guinea. It hunts in savanna, forest, and grassland, and it is a diurnal, fast-moving predator that feeds on other animals. Adults typically weigh around 3 kilograms, and the species remains widespread today.
greater_siren: The greater siren is an eel-like amphibian that lives in swamps and wetlands across the southern United States, mainly in Florida and along the Gulf coast. It has no hind legs and spends its life in the water, eating a varied diet of both plants and animals. Adults reach about 1 kilogram, and when ponds dry up, it can aestivate, sheltering through the dry period until conditions improve.
slender_snouted_crocodile: The slender-snouted crocodile lives along the western coast of Africa and throughout the Congo basin. It is found in rivers, swamps, and jungle waterways, where it hunts fish. Adults weigh about 100 kg, and its long, narrow snout and armored scales help it swim with ease.
elrathia: This small trilobite lived during the Cambrian, roughly 507 to 505 million years ago, and it is the most common trilobite found in the United States. Its remains are preserved in shale of the Wheeler Formation in western North America, where enormous fossil beds have been uncovered. Scientists consider it a scavenger, and adults weighed only about 0.03 kilograms.
galapagos_tortoise_espanola: The Espanola giant tortoise, Chelonoidis hoodensis, lives only on Espanola Island in the Galapagos. It roams the island's dry, rocky badlands and feeds on plants. Adults can reach about 80 kg, and their saddleback-shaped shell is a clear sign of this species. Although it is still alive, the tortoise remains a species to watch.
common_warthog: Found across Africa south of the Sahara and into the Sahel, the common warthog makes its home in savanna and grassland. Adults can weigh about 80 kg, and they feed on both plants and animal matter. Their tusks are a distinctive feature, and they often shelter in burrows they dig or take over from other animals.
margay: The margay is a small wild cat that lives across the Neotropics, reaching as far north as Mexico. It makes its home in jungle and forest, where it hunts meat-based prey. Adults typically weigh about 3.5 kg, and this cat is still alive in the wild. Its dense fur, climbing skill, and nighttime activity suit life high in the trees.
pale_fox: The Pale Fox, known to science as Vulpes pallida, makes its home across the Sahel, moving between desert and savanna country. An adult weighs about 3 kg, and its pale fur helps it blend into dry, sandy ground. It is nocturnal, spending the day in a burrow and emerging after dark to hunt and forage. Its diet is omnivorous, and it remains widespread and alive today.
red_fox: The red fox has a range that spans much of the Northern Hemisphere, from North America and Eurasia to the Indian subcontinent, the Sahara, and parts of North Africa and China. It lives in forests, grasslands, mountains, tundra, and deserts, and it eats both plants and animals. An adult typically weighs about 6 kilograms. Active mostly at night, it often rests or raises young in burrows, and its fur has long made it a hunted animal. It was absent from Australia until the 1850s.
desert_crocodile: The West African crocodile lives across the Sahel, the western coast, and parts of the Sahara, where it uses rivers, lakes, wetlands, and even desert oases. It is a carnivore, and adults can reach about 100 kg. These animals swim well and often survive dry spells by aestivating, slowing their bodies to wait out drought until water returns.
euoplocephalus: Roughly 76 to 75 million years ago, this armored herbivore roamed what is now northwestern North America. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation. An adult could weigh around 2000 kilograms, and it was protected by bony eyelid plates and a heavy tail club.
springbok: Springboks roam the deserts and plains of Southern Africa, where they graze on herbs and move in herds in search of good grazing. An adult weighs about 35 kilograms, and both sexes carry horns. When alarmed, these antelope leap high into the air with stiff legs in a display called pronking. They are still widespread today and are also hunted.
caspian_tiger: The Caspian tiger once roamed from Iran and Anatolia to the Kazakh steppe, where it hunted in river forests, swamps, and grasslands. Adults could weigh around 170 kg, and their thick fur kept them warm while they swam through riverine tugai woodland. Hunting and habitat loss drove the subspecies to extinction, and the last confirmed sightings came around 1970.
dolphin_common_short_beaked: Found across the northern Atlantic and Pacific oceans as well as the Mediterranean Sea, this toothed species thrives in both warm and cold waters. Adults weigh about 90 kilograms, and they are fast swimmers that travel together in pods. As carnivores, they hunt in these social groups, and the species remains widespread today.
entelognathus: Entelognathus lived in the seas of the Silurian, roughly 423 to 419 million years ago, and its fossils come from mudstone of the Kuanti Formation in the lowlands of China. This carnivore grew to about 2 kilograms and moved through the water by swimming. It is known as one of the earliest jawed fishes to have a bony skull.
lemur_mouse_grey: The grey mouse lemur is a small primate found only on Madagascar, where it lives in forest and desert settings. Weighing about 0.06 kg as an adult, it is active at night and spends most of its time in the trees. Its diet is omnivorous, and the species is still alive today.
thylacine: The last known thylacine died in captivity in Tasmania in 1936, though the species once roamed mainland Australia before disappearing from there around 1000 BC. This striped marsupial hunted at night across forest, grassland, and island habitats, and an adult weighed about 25 kilograms. Its body plan closely resembled that of a dog, a case of convergent evolution with placental canids.
black_bear: The American black bear roams forests, mountains, and taiga across a wide range that stretches from Alaska and the Yukon down into Mexico and the Pacific Northwest. Adults commonly weigh around 110 kilograms, and this omnivore eats both plants and animals. Known for its dense fur and its skill at climbing trees, it hibernates through the winter and remains a huntable species in many areas.
cretaceous_amber_ant: The Hell Ant lived roughly 99 to 98 million years ago during the Cretaceous period, and it is known only from fossils preserved in Burmese amber from the Hukawng formation in what is now Indochina. Its name is a nod to its scythe-shaped jaws, which set it apart from other ants of its time. Adults weighed about 0.00001 kilograms, and the species fed on insects.
hildoceras: This ammonite is a fossil taxon that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 182 to 175 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from shale of the Whitby Mudstone formation in the British Isles. Adults are thought to have weighed about 0.2 kilograms, and the animal is classed as a carnivore.
nothosaurus: Living roughly 245 to 230 million years ago during the Triassic, this sea creature is known from fossils pressed into limestone of the Muschelkalk formation across Europe. Its diet was fish, and adults are estimated to have reached about 200 kilograms. It belonged to the sauropterygians, a group of marine reptiles that swam the Triassic seas.
utahraptor: Known only from fossils, this predator lived during the Early Cretaceous, roughly 126 to 124 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone layers of the Cedar Mountain Formation in western North America. Adults weighed about 500 kilograms, making it the largest known dromaeosaur, and it carried a large sickle-shaped claw on each foot.
cuban_crocodile: The Cuban Crocodile lives across the Caribbean, mostly in swamps, wetlands, and slow rivers. It hunts other animals and grows to about 80 kilograms as an adult. Though still living, this reptile is known for its armored scales, strong swimming, and surprising bursts of aggression, including leaping out of the water.
caecilian_sao_tome: This small, legless amphibian lives in the forests, caves, and island habitats of São Tomé. It burrows through soil and feeds on insects. Adults weigh about 0.1 kg, and the species is still living today.
montpellier_snake: The Montpellier Snake is found along Mediterranean and Atlantic Europe as well as the North African coast. It favors grassland and badlands, where it hunts for prey. Adults typically weigh about 1 kg, and this species is still living today. It is venomous and rear-fanged, with a scaled body built for its dry, open surroundings.
isotelus_rex: Isotelus rex was a trilobite that lived during the Ordovician, roughly 450 to 445 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from limestone of the Churchill River Group on the Canadian Shield. It is the largest known trilobite, reaching about 70 centimeters long, and it fed as a scavenger with an adult mass of around 4 kilograms.
dolphin_pacific_white_sided: Found in the cold waters of the North Pacific, this toothed dolphin lives in tight social groups called pods. Adults weigh around 150 kilograms, and they feed on fish and other prey. Known for their acrobatic leaps and playful displays, they remain common and are still thriving today.
bog_turtle: The bog turtle is a small, omnivorous reptile found across the eastern parts of North America, where it makes its home in wetlands. An adult weighs only about 0.1 kilograms, and its shell is tiny enough to fit in the palm of a hand. Still living today, this species is protected because its wetland habitat is easily lost.
dolphin_franciscana: The franciscana is a small toothed whale found along the coasts and river mouths of the southwestern Atlantic, ranging between about 18 and 42 degrees south latitude. Adults weigh roughly 40 kilograms, and the animal feeds mainly on fish and other small prey. It favors estuarine waters, and it is still living today.
arthropleura: Roughly 50 kilograms and stretching about 2.5 meters from head to tail, this extinct millipede is among the largest arthropods ever known. Fossils of Arthropleura armata have been pressed into mudstone of the Joggins Formation in eastern North America, dating to the Carboniferous period between 315 and 299 million years ago. Its body was protected by a hard shell, and it walked across the ancient landscape, likely feeding on plant matter.
majungasaurus: Majungasaurus was a meat-eating theropod that lived in Madagascar between 70 and 66 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Maevarano Formation, and adults weighed about 1100 kilograms. Bones bearing signs of cannibalism suggest that members of this species sometimes preyed on their own kind.
falcarius: Falcarius utahensis lived in western North America during the Early Cretaceous, roughly 126 to 124 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Cedar Mountain Formation, and it is known from fossil remains rather than living specimens. Adults weighed around 100 kilograms, and this basal therizinosaur fed on plants.
haikouichthys: Haikouichthys ercaicunensis lived roughly 518 to 514 million years ago, during the Cambrian. Its fossils come from shale of the Chengjiang Biota, the Maotianshan Shale formation in the lowlands of China. This small swimmer weighed about 2 grams as an adult and fed on filter-feeding, and it is regarded as one of the earliest known craniates.
asian_box_tortoise: The Asian forest tortoise makes its home in the forests and jungles of Indochina and Sundaland, where it lives among the leaf litter. It eats both plants and animals, so its diet is omnivorous. A full-grown adult can weigh about 30 kg, and it is active during the day. This species is still alive in the wild.
spotted_salamander: Eastern North America is home to this amphibian, which ranges as far north as the Canadian Shield. It spends time in forests and wetlands, often hiding in burrows, and feeds on insects. An adult weighs about 0.04 kilograms, and its skin produces toxins that discourage predators.
goral: The Himalayan goral is a stocky goat-antelope that still roams the Himalaya, Tibet, and parts of the Indian subcontinent. It favors steep mountain slopes and forested ground, where it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh around 30 kilograms, and both sexes carry short horns. Hunting pressure makes it a species of note, though it has not gone extinct.
bat_christmas_pipistrelle: The Christmas Island pipistrelle once roosted and hunted across the jungle and forest of its small island home in the Indian Ocean. This tiny nocturnal flier weighed only about four grams as an adult and fed on insects caught on the wing. It was declared extinct in 2009, leaving behind only a few historical records of its presence.
red_panda: The red panda, known scientifically as Ailurus fulgens, lives in the Himalayas and Tibet, sharing part of its range with the giant panda. It makes its home in mountain forests, where it spends much of its time in trees. Plant-eating by nature, it feeds mainly on bamboo, and an adult weighs about 5 kg. Its thick fur and protected status help it survive in the wild today.
geoffroys_cat: Geoffroy's Cat is a small wild cat still found across the Pampas, Gran Chaco, Patagonia, and the wider Southern Cone. It roams grassland, forest, and swamp, and hunts mainly meat. An adult weighs about 4 kg, and this animal is active at night and is able to swim.
dorcas_gazelle: The Dorcas gazelle roams the Sahara, the Sahel, the Nile valley, and Arabia, making its home in desert country. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 18 kilograms as an adult. Small herds move across the sands together, and both sexes carry horns. The species is still alive today, though it can be hunted.
quoll_eastern: Dwelling across Tasmania and parts of mainland eastern Australia, this small carnivore roams forests and grasslands after dark. Adults weigh about 1.4 kilograms, and their coats are marked with distinctive spots. Still living in the wild, the eastern quoll hunts through the night and feeds on meat.
four_horned_antelope: The four-horned antelope roams the Indian subcontinent, moving between forest and grassland in search of its meals. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 20 kilograms as an adult. Its name comes from the pair of horns on its head, and that trait makes it a target for hunters.
boomslang: Found across Africa south of the Sahara and in the southern parts of the continent, the boomslang lives in forests and savannas. This venomous, tree-dwelling snake is active during the day and hunts other animals, weighing about half a kilogram as an adult. It remains alive and common in its range today.
rhinoceros_iguana: The rhinoceros iguana is a plant-eating lizard that still survives in the wild, living across forest, desert, and island habitats in the region between latitudes 17.5 and 20 north and longitudes 68 and 75 west. Adults weigh about 9 kg. It is active during the day, digs burrows for shelter, and is protected by law.
galapagos_tortoise_alcedo: The Alcedo giant tortoise, known to science as Chelonoidis vandenburghi, makes its home on the Galapagos Islands. It roams both island terrain and rugged badlands, feeding on plants and grasses. A full-grown adult can weigh around 250 kilograms, and its high, domed shell is a key identifying feature.
rinkhals: The rinkhals is a venomous snake found across southern Africa, where it lives in grasslands and mountain areas. Adults weigh about 1.5 kilograms, and they feed on other animals. When threatened, this species can spit venom at an attacker, and it may also roll over and play dead to avoid danger.
eastern_brown_snake: The Eastern Brown Snake roams the grasslands and savannas of Australia, where it hunts small prey. Adults typically weigh about 1 kilogram. This species is venomous and fast, and its bite is deadly, so it commands respect from anyone who crosses its path. It remains widespread and alive today.
cyprus_dwarf_hippo: The Cyprus dwarf hippo lived on the island of Cyprus, where it roamed coastal areas and fed on plants. Adults weighed about 200 kilograms, making them far smaller than their mainland relatives. Early human settlers hunted them, and the species vanished around 9500 BC.
dryosaurus: Known only from fossils, Dryosaurus altus lived during the Jurassic period, roughly 155 to 148 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Morrison Formation in western North America. This plant-eating dinosaur weighed about 90 kilograms as an adult and is thought to have been a fast runner.
tamandua_southern: The southern tamandua is an insect-eating mammal found across the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It lives in forest and jungle, climbing through trees with the help of a prehensile tail. Adults weigh about 5 kg, and the species is still alive today.
hare_cape: The cape hare roams across Africa and Arabia, making its home in grasslands and deserts. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 2.2 kg as an adult. Known for its speed, this species is still thriving today and is hunted by people in parts of its range.
galapagos_sea_lion: The Galapagos sea lion lives along the rocky coasts and beaches of the Galapagos Islands, where it still thrives. Adults can weigh about 90 kilograms and rely on a meat-based diet to fuel their days at sea. These animals gather in herds on land and carry a thick layer of blubber that keeps them warm in cool ocean waters.
rajasaurus: Rajasaurus narmadensis was a meat-eating dinosaur that lived roughly 70 to 66 million years ago during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Lameta Formation on the Indian subcontinent. An adult could weigh around 3000 kilograms, and it belonged to the abelisaurids, a group known for its crested heads.
argentine_tegu: The Argentine Black and White Tegu is found across the Southern Cone, living in the Pampas and Gran Chaco. It moves through forest, grassland, and savanna, and it eats both plants and animals. Adults reach about 5 kg, and this species remains widespread today. It is active during the day, shelters in burrows, and raids the eggs of other animals.
chacoan_peccary: The Chacoan peccary roams a patch of South American lowlands stretching across parts of Paraguay, Bolivia, and Argentina, where it moves through both badlands and forest. It is an omnivore, eating a mix of plant and animal foods, and an adult typically weighs about 40 kilograms. Living in herds, these animals remain alive today, and they are hunted by people in the region.
cuban_monkey: This extinct primate once roamed the forests of Cuba, where it lived on the ground rather than in the trees. Adults weighed around 10 kilograms, and the species ate a varied diet of both plants and animals. It disappeared around 2000 years ago, leaving behind only fossil evidence of its island life.
cuban_boa: The Cuban boa is a large constrictor found across the Caribbean, where it lives in forests, caves, and on islands. Adults can reach a mass of about 35 kilograms. This nocturnal snake is carnivorous and remains alive today, with a body covered in scales that helps it move through its varied habitats.
pallass_cat: Pallas's Cat roams the steppe and rocky grasslands of Mongolia, the Himalaya, Tibet, Kazakhstan, Iran, and Anatolia. It favors mountain slopes, grassy plains, and badlands, where it hunts small prey by ambush. Adults weigh about 3.5 kg, and their thick coat keeps them warm in harsh conditions. The species is still alive and is legally protected.
gemsbok: The gemsbok roams the deserts and savannas of southern Africa, where it grazes on herbs. An adult typically weighs about 210 kilograms. Herds of these animals are a common sight, and their long, straight horns make them easy to recognize, and they are also hunted in some areas.
potto: The potto is a slow-moving primate that lives in the jungles of the Congo basin and along the western coast of Africa. It is active only at night and spends nearly all of its life in the trees. Adults weigh about 1 kilogram, and the species is still widespread today, eating a mixed diet of both plants and animals.
muttaburrasaurus: A plant-eating dinosaur known only from fossils, Muttaburrasaurus lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 104 to 98 million years ago. Its remains were found in mudstone of the Mackunda Formation in Australia, and adults reached about 2800 kilograms. This iguanodont from Queensland fed on herbs.
african_clawless_otter: The African clawless otter roams the rivers, lakes, and coastlines of sub-Saharan Africa. It feeds mainly on fish and weighs about 20 kg as an adult. This species is still alive and its dense fur helps it stay warm while swimming.
arabian_oryx: The Arabian oryx is a herbivore that lives in the deserts of Arabia and weighs about 70 kg as an adult. It moves in herds and carries long, straight horns. The species became extinct in the wild in 1972, but it was later reintroduced, and it survives today.
baculites: Baculites compressus is a fossil ammonite that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 80 to 66 million years ago. Its straight shell, unlike the coiled shells of most of its relatives, sets it apart in the record. Specimens are found preserved in shale of the Pierre Shale formation across the Great Plains, and it is thought to have been a carnivore weighing about 1 kg as an adult.
bay_cat: The bay cat is a small wild cat found only on the island of Borneo, where it lives in jungle and forest habitats. It hunts meat and is active mainly at night. Adults weigh around 3.5 kilograms, and its reddish fur helps it blend into the forest. Still living in the wild, this species is protected by law.
placenticeras: Placenticeras meeki was a fossil ammonite that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 75 to 72 million years ago. Its remains are found in shale of the Pierre Shale formation across the Great Plains. Adults reached about 3 kilograms, and the shell can show an iridescent sheen, which is why some specimens are known as Bearpaw ammolite.
white_nosed_coati: The White-nosed Coati (Nasua narica) lives in Mexico, Central America, and the southern United States. It makes its home in forests and jungles, where it moves through the trees and forages during the day. Adults weigh about 4.5 kg, and this omnivore travels in herds while remaining a living species today.
anchiornis: Anchiornis huxleyi was a small feathered dinosaur that lived in what is now China roughly 161 to 160 million years ago during the Jurassic period. Its fossils were preserved in shale of the Tiaojishan Formation, in lowland deposits. This carnivore weighed about 0.11 kilograms as an adult, and it is known as a black-and-white feathered troodontid.
whale_pilot_short_finned: Found in tropical seas across warm and deep ocean waters, this toothed whale is still widely living today. Adults can reach about 2500 kg, and they hunt fish and squid as carnivores. They travel in tight social groups called pods, and their cooperative habits make them a target for drive hunts.
hare_snowshoe: The snowshoe hare roams the taiga and forests across the Canadian Shield, Alaska, the Yukon, the Pacific Northwest, and eastern North America. Adults weigh about 1.5 kg and feed on plants. Its coat turns white in winter, and its population rises and falls in regular boom-and-bust cycles.
dolphin_tucuxi: Found only in the rivers of the Amazon basin, the tucuxi is a small toothed dolphin that lives in freshwater rather than the sea. It moves in pods and feeds on meat-based prey, and an adult typically weighs about 45 kg. Though its numbers are not extinct, it remains a living species that depends on these rivers.
gigantoraptor: Gigantoraptor was a giant feathered oviraptorosaur that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 86 to 83 million years ago. Its fossils come from sandstone of the Iren Dabasu formation on the Mongolian steppe. Adults reached about 1400 kilograms, and the animal is thought to have been omnivorous.
uroplatus_leaf_gecko: Found only in the forests of Madagascar, this gecko spends its days pressed flat against tree trunks, where its leafy shape and mottled coloring make it nearly invisible. After dark it comes out to hunt insects among the branches. Weighing about ten grams as an adult, it is still very much alive in the wild today.
pocket_gopher_plains: Dwelling in the grasslands of the Great Plains, this small rodent spends most of its life underground in a network of burrows. It feeds on plant matter and typically weighs about 0.2 kilograms as an adult. Though it remains widespread and is not extinct, its hidden tunnel system is what sets it apart from many of its neighbors.
yellow_pond_turtle: The Yellow Pond Turtle is found across the lowlands of China, in Indochina, and in Japan and Korea. It lives in rivers and wetlands, where it swims with ease and eats a varied diet of both plants and animals. Adults typically reach about 1.5 kilograms, and their smooth shell helps them move through the water.
rhomaleosaurus: Rhomaleosaurus cramptoni was a short-necked pliosaurid, a marine reptile that swam in the seas of the Jurassic period roughly 182 to 178 million years ago. Adults reached about 1000 kilograms, and its diet was carnivorous. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Whitby Mudstone Formation in the British Isles.
carcharodontosaurus: Known only from fossils, this large meat-eater roamed what is now the Sahara between 99 and 94 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Kem Kem formation. An adult may have weighed around 6200 kilograms, and its name, meaning "shark-toothed lizard," refers to its serrated teeth.
thrinaxodon: Thrinaxodon was a small fossil reptile that lived in what is now Southern Africa roughly 252 to 247 million years ago during the Triassic. Its remains have been recovered from mudstone of the Katberg formation. An adult weighed about one kilogram, and it fed on other animals. Evidence suggests it was a burrowing cynodont that may have had early fur.
elpistostege: A fossil from the Devonian period, roughly 378 to 375 million years ago, Elpistostege watsoni was found in sandstone of the Escuminac Formation at Miguasha in eastern North America. This carnivore reached about 1.5 meters in length and weighed around 15 kilograms as an adult. It swam using a fin that bore digits.
jaekelopterus: Jaekelopterus rhenaniae lived during the Devonian period, roughly 400 to 390 million years ago, and its remains have been recovered from sandstone of the Klerf Formation in Europe. It is the largest arthropod known, measuring over 2.3 meters, and it likely swam while hunting prey. Its diet was carnivorous, and its powerful claws would have been used to seize food.
arctic_fox: The arctic fox lives across the Arctic, from Iceland and Greenland through Scandinavia, Alaska, the Yukon, and the Siberian taiga. It makes its home on icy tundra and rocky coasts, where it digs burrows and eats a mix of plants and animals. Adults weigh about 3.5 kg, and in winter a thick white coat helps it blend into the snow.
geometric_tortoise: The geometric tortoise is a small herbivore with a lightly built shell that is about 0.3 kilograms as an adult. It lives in the southwestern corner of Africa, where it moves between badlands and grassland and feeds on plants. Its shell shows a neat pattern of lines, and it survives in the fynbos scrub of the region. The species is still alive today and is legally protected.
uganda_kob: Grazing on grasses and herbs, the Uganda kob roams open savanna and wetland across the Sahel, East Africa, and the West African coast. Adults weigh around 90 kilograms, and the males carry curved horns. These animals gather in herds and remain alive today, though they are a huntable species.
microraptor: Microraptor gui lived in what is now China around 125 to 120 million years ago, during the Cretaceous period. Its fossils come from shale of the Jiufotang Formation in the lowlands. This carnivore weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult and is known as a four-winged glider.
porcupine_prehensile: Spending its days curled up in the forest canopy, this nocturnal creature is at home in the jungle and forest of the Amazon and Orinoco regions. Its prehensile tail grips branches as it climbs, and its body is covered in quills for protection. Adults weigh about 4 kg, and the animal feeds mainly on fruit.
dakotaraptor: Dakotaraptor steini was a large fossil dromaeosaurid that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 67 to 66 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from sandstone in the Hell Creek Formation of the Great Plains. It was a carnivore weighing around 350 kilograms as an adult, and its forearm bones bear quill knobs.
hesperosaurus: Hesperosaurus lived during the Jurassic, roughly 156 to 150 million years ago, and it is known only from fossils. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Morrison Formation in western North America. Adults weighed about 3500 kilograms, and this plant eater came from Wyoming.
yutyrannus: Yutyrannus huali lived in what is now China during the Cretaceous, roughly 125 to 122 million years ago. Its fossils were preserved in shale of the Yixian Formation, and the animal was a carnivore that reached an adult mass of about 1400 kilograms. Feathers covered its body, making it a feathered tyrannosauroid with a fuzzy coat.
blackbuck: The blackbuck is a graceful antelope found across the Indian subcontinent, where it roams open plains and grasslands. Adults weigh about 40 kilograms and feed on herbs. Living in herds and active by day, this species still survives today and is recognized for its spiral horns and its appeal to hunters.
large_billed_crow: Found across eastern and southern Asia, from Japan and Korea into the Indomalaya region, the large-billed crow lives in both forests and open plains. It is an omnivore that scavenges readily, and adults weigh about 0.65 kilograms. This bird is clever, flies well, and remains widespread today.
fishing_cat: The fishing cat lives across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, and it is also found in parts of the islands to the south. It hunts in swamps, rivers, wetlands, and coastal areas, mostly at night. Adults weigh about 11 kilograms, and this species is still alive and legally protected.
white_tailed_deer: The white-tailed deer roams a wide stretch of the Americas, from eastern North America and the Great Plains through Mexico and Central America to the Amazon basin and the Canadian Shield. It favors forests and open plains, feeding on herbs, and an adult typically weighs about 75 kg. Still thriving across this range, it is a game animal, and the males grow antlers each year.
bat_lesser_short_tailed_nz: This nocturnal bat lives in the forests of New Zealand, where it is still alive today. Unlike most bats, it moves about on the ground as well as in the air, foraging across the forest floor. Its varied diet is reflected in its omnivorous habits, and an adult weighs only about 14 grams.
american_crocodile: Still living today, the American crocodile ranges from southern Florida and the Gulf coast through Mexico, Central America, and the Caribbean, reaching even into the Amazon basin. It favors coastal waters, rivers, swamps, and lakes, where it hunts other animals. An adult can weigh around 380 kg. It is a protected species.
golden_rumped_sengi: Foraging through the leaf litter of forest floors, this small creature hunts insects during daylight hours. It weighs about half a kilogram as an adult and makes its home in the forests of the region spanning roughly 39 to 40.5 degrees east and 3 to 4 degrees south. Though it is small and rarely seen, it remains alive today.
fallow_deer: The European fallow deer, Dama dama, still roams wild in forest country, where it grazes on herbs. Adults weigh about 70 kg. Herds are a common sight, and the species is hunted in some areas, with males carrying distinctive antlers.
harbor_seal: Found along coasts in cold northern waters of the Atlantic and Pacific, the harbor seal ranges from the Baltic and North Sea to the Pacific Northwest and eastern North America. Adults can reach about 90 kg, and they feed entirely on meat. Groups of these seals gather in herds, and a thick layer of blubber helps them stay warm.
enantiornis: Known only from fossils, Enantiornis leali lived during the late Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago. Its remains were recovered from sandstone of the Lecho Formation in the Andes. This carnivore weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult, and it belonged to a group of birds that differed from the lineage leading to modern birds.
siamese_crocodile: The Siamese crocodile is a freshwater reptile found across Indochina and Sundaland. It makes its home in rivers, swamps, and other wetlands, where it hunts meat-eating prey. Adults can reach about 100 kg, and the species is still alive today and protected under law.
aesculapian_snake: The Aesculapian Snake ranges across Europe, the Mediterranean, and the Alps, living in both forests and mountain country. This carnivorous species can reach about 1 kilogram as an adult and is still widespread today. It is a constrictor that climbs well through trees, and in ancient times it was regarded as sacred to Asclepius, the Greek god of medicine.
argali: The argali, a wild sheep, roams the Mongolian steppe, the Himalaya and Tibet, and the Kazakh steppe. It moves between mountain slopes and open grassland, grazing on herbs. Adults can weigh around 130 kg, making it the largest wild sheep, and it lives in herds, with its large curled horns a striking feature.
glyptodont_neosclerocalyptus: Neosclerocalyptus paskoensis was a grassland herbivore whose range covered Patagonia, the Pampas, and the Gran Chaco. Adults weighed about 500 kg, and the species is counted among the extinct megafauna. It had a shell and a horned skull, and it disappeared around 8000 BC.
steneosaurus: Steneosaurus bollensis roamed the seas of Europe during the Jurassic, roughly 182 to 175 million years ago. Its slender snout suited a diet of fish, and adults reached about 300 kg. Fossils of this teleosaurid have been recovered from the shale of the Posidonia Shale formation.
zorilla: The zorilla is a small, nocturnal carnivore that roams the savannas, deserts, and grasslands of Africa south of the Sahara and across the Sahel. Adults weigh about 1.1 kilograms, and their striped fur gives them a skunk-like look. When threatened, they release a strong spray scent to drive off attackers. They remain widespread and are not considered extinct.
scrub_python: The scrub python lives in Australia, where it makes its home in jungle and forest country. It is a carnivore, and its adults can reach a mass of about 35 kilograms. This constrictor spends much of its time in trees, and its scales help it grip branches as it moves.
cuvieronius: Cuvier's gomphothere once roamed the Andes, Central America, Mexico, and the southern United States. It lived in mountain and forest country, feeding on herbs and moving through herds. Adults reached about 4500 kilograms, and their twisted tusks set them apart. The species went extinct around 10000 BC, and people are known to have hunted it.
hatzegopteryx: A giant pterosaur that once ruled the skies over Europe, Hatzegopteryx lived during the late Cretaceous, roughly 70 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils were preserved in mudstone of the Sânpetru Formation, and it is known as an island apex predator. Adults weighed around 200 kilograms, making it one of the heaviest flying creatures of its time.
armadillo_giant: The giant armadillo roams the Amazon and Orinoco basins as well as the Pampas and Gran Chaco, moving through jungle, forest, and savanna. An adult typically weighs about 30 kg, and it spends its nights hunting insects, especially termites. Digging burrows and protected by its tough shell, this species is still alive today.
pangolin_giant: Covered in overlapping scales, the giant ground pangolin roams the Congo basin, the West African coast, and the East African savanna. This nocturnal digger feeds on insects and shelters in burrows through both jungle and grassland. Adults can reach about 33 kilograms, and the species is protected and still living today.
anteater_giant: Ranging from Central America through the Amazon and Orinoco basins to the Pampas and Gran Chaco, this insect eater roams savanna, grassland, and jungle. Adults weigh about 33 kilograms, and their long snout and shaggy fur set them apart. Still living in the wild, the giant anteater is a protected species that feeds mainly on termites and ants.
surinam_toad: Flat and fully aquatic, the Surinam toad spends its life in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, moving through rivers and swamps. It hunts other animals and grows to an adult mass of about 0.2 kg. Its young hatch from skin on the mother's back, and the species is still alive today.
spiny_softshell: The Spiny Softshell Turtle roams eastern North America, the Great Plains, and the southern United States, where it lives in rivers and lakes. It is a meat eater that can grow to about 8 kilograms as an adult. Its leathery shell lacks the hard plates of many turtles, and it is known for swimming quickly and burying itself in sand.
stegoceras: Stegoceras validum lived in what is now northwestern North America roughly 76 to 75 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Dinosaur Park Formation. This plant eater weighed about 40 kilograms as an adult and carried a small dome on its skull.
sailfin_lizard: Found across Wallacea and New Guinea, this lizard makes its home along rivers, through jungle, and on the coast. It eats both plants and animals and weighs about 1.2 kilograms as an adult. Active during the day, it swims well and displays a tall crest along its back that gives it its name.
red_eyed_tree_frog: Hidden in the leaves of Central American and southern Mexican jungles, this colorful amphibian spends its life in the trees. It is active at night, when it hunts insects. An adult weighs only about seven grams, and the species is still thriving in the wild.
porpoise_vaquita: The vaquita is a small, shy porpoise found along the coast of the upper Gulf of California, where its range falls between about 30.5 and 32 degrees north. Adults weigh around 45 kilograms, making it the smallest cetacean in the world. It feeds on fish and other small sea creatures, and it remains alive today under strict legal protection.
florida_softshell: The Florida softshell turtle lives in Florida and along the Gulf Coast of the southern United States. It makes its home in rivers, lakes, and swamps, where it hunts other animals. Adults can reach about 20 kilograms, making it the largest softshell turtle found in America. Its flattened, leathery shell helps it glide through the water.
bengal_fox: The Bengal fox roams the Indian subcontinent as well as the Himalaya and Tibet, moving through grasslands, deserts, and badlands. It eats a mixed diet and weighs about 3 kilograms as an adult. This species is still alive, and it relies on its thick fur and its burrows to get through harsh conditions.
atlas_elephant: Once roaming the northern coast of Africa, the Sahara fringe, and the Nile valley, this elephant lived in both forest and savanna. Adults could reach about 3500 kilograms, and they fed on herbs while moving through herds. Their tusks were prized for ivory, and they were used as war elephants by Carthage. The subspecies had disappeared by about 400 AD.
macrauchenia: Macrauchenia patagonica was a litopternid that roamed the plains of the Pampas and Gran Chaco, as well as Patagonia and the Andes. It grazed on herbs and grew to an adult mass of about 1000 kg. It died out around 9500 BC, and its long neck suggests it could stretch to reach vegetation.
rat_black: The black rat, also called the roof rat, lives across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, where it makes its home in forests and jungle. It is nocturnal, digs burrows, and eats a varied diet of both plant and animal food. Adults weigh around 0.2 kilograms, and the species is still widespread today, though it is known as a carrier of diseases that can affect people.
small_indian_civet: The small Indian civet is a slender, nocturnal mammal found across the Indian subcontinent, Indochina, Sundaland, and the lowlands of China. It lives in both forests and grasslands and eats a varied diet of both plants and animals. An adult typically weighs about 3 kg, and its coat is dense and fur-covered.
giant_rice_rat_megalomys_lucia: The St Lucia giant rice rat once lived in the forests of St Lucia, a small island in the Lesser Antilles, between roughly 13.6 and 14.2 degrees north. An adult could weigh about 1 kilogram, making it a giant among rodents. It fed on plant matter. The species was last recorded in 1881.
proboscis_monkey: Found only on the island of Borneo, this monkey is known for its long, drooping nose. Groups move through wetlands, jungle, and coastal mangroves, where they feed on plants and rest by day. Adults weigh about 15 kilograms, and these animals are known to swim well.
whale_beluga: Belugas, known scientifically as Delphinapterus leucas, make their home in the Arctic Ocean and the northern parts of the Pacific and Atlantic. They prefer cold, icy coastal waters and feed on meat such as fish and other marine prey. Adults can reach about 1300 kg, and these toothed whales travel in pods while communicating through a wide range of vocal sounds.
cuscus_common_spotted: The common spotted cuscus lives in the jungles of Wallacea and New Guinea, where it spends its days high in the trees. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms, and this nocturnal marsupial uses its grasping, prehensile tail to hold onto branches as it feeds on plants. It remains widespread and is still alive in the wild.
javan_rusa: The Javan rusa is a large deer that still roams the wild, found across a broad band of land stretching roughly from 105 to 125 degrees east and from about 6 to 10 degrees south. It makes its home in both forest and grassland, grazing on herbs and grasses. Adults can weigh around 100 kilograms, and the males carry impressive antlers. These deer live in herds and are hunted by people.
siberian_roe: Found across Siberian taiga, the Mongolian steppe, Chinese lowlands, and parts of Japan and Korea, this deer lives mainly in forests and taiga. It feeds on herbs and weighs about 45 kg as an adult. Still living in the wild, it is hunted in some areas, and males grow antlers.
lemur_ring_tailed: The ring-tailed lemur, known scientifically as Lemur catta, lives in a range spanning roughly latitude -26 to -21 and longitude 43 to 47. It makes its home in forest, badland, and desert settings, and it feeds on herbs. Adults weigh about 2.2 kg, and these animals live in herds and are active during the day. They are still alive in the wild.
goitered_gazelle: The goitered gazelle roams desert and plain country from Iran and Anatolia across the Kazakh and Mongolian steppes into Arabia. It grazes on herbs and gathers in herds, and adults weigh about 30 kg. Both sexes carry horns, and the species is still alive, though it can be hunted.
brown_bear: Across the Nearctic and Palearctic, plus the Himalaya, Tibet, Iran and Anatolia, brown bears roam forests, taiga, mountains and tundra. These omnivores can reach about 270 kilograms as adults, and they are still widespread today. Thick fur keeps them warm, they swim well, and they spend winter hibernating.
dactylioceras: Dactylioceras commune was an ammonite that lived during the Jurassic, roughly 182 to 175 million years ago. Its shells turn up in the shale of the Whitby Mudstone formation, and they have been found along the Yorkshire coast of the British Isles. The animal is listed as carnivorous and weighed about 0.1 kg as an adult.
giant_forest_hog: The giant forest hog is still alive and roams forests and jungles across the Congo basin, the East African savanna, and the West African coast. Adults can reach about 200 kilograms. These animals live in herds, feed on both plant and animal matter, and grow tusks that are a notable feature of the species. They are huntable in some areas.
darwins_fox: Darwin's fox lives in the forests and island habitats of the Chiloé region, an area running from about 33 to 43 degrees south. Adults weigh around 3 kg, and the animal eats a mixed diet of both plants and animals. Its thick fur is one reason it has been given legal protection, and it survives today.
african_clawed_frog: The African clawed frog makes its home in the lakes and wetlands of southern Africa. Adults reach about 0.2 kilograms and spend nearly all their lives in water, swimming freely rather than hopping across land. Its diet is omnivorous, and the species remains widespread and alive today.
flying_fox_guam: The Guam flying fox once roamed the forests of its island home, moving through the night on wide leather wings. Adults weighed about 0.4 kg, and the species fed mainly on fruit. It was declared extinct in 1967 AD, leaving the island's forests without one of their nocturnal fliers.
hippidion: Hippidion, a extinct South American equine, roamed the plains and mountains of Patagonia, the Pampas, the Andes, and the wider Southern Cone. Adults weighed about 400 kg, and they fed on herbs. These animals lived in herds, were hunted by people, and had distinctive nasal bones. They disappeared around 9500 BC.
western_tree_hyrax: The Western tree hyrax is a small herbivore found in the Congo Basin and along the western African coast. It lives in forest and jungle habitats, where it feeds on plants and grows to an adult weight of about 3 kilograms. Active at night and spending its life in trees, this species is still alive and widespread.
tamandua_northern: Gripping branches with a prehensile tail, this anteater spends much of its life in the trees. It ranges from southern Mexico through Central America and across the Neotropics, favoring forest and jungle. Insects make up its diet, and an adult weighs about 5 kilograms. It is still alive and widespread.
castorocauda: Castorocauda lived in what is now China roughly 165 to 160 million years ago, during the Jurassic. Its fossils were preserved in shale from the Daohugou formation, and it weighed about 0.8 kilograms as an adult. It fed on fish and had a broad, beaver-like tail that helped it swim.
malayan_tapir: Found in the jungles and forests of Sundaland and Indochina, this herbivore feeds on plants and can weigh as much as 350 kilograms as an adult. It is still living in the wild and is known to swim well. Hunting is a threat that the species faces across its range.
hemione: The hemione, also called the Gobi wild ass, roams the steppes of Mongolia and Kazakhstan, where it lives across both desert and plains. Adults weigh around 250 kilograms, and they feed on herbs while moving through the open country in herds. Though it is still alive in the wild, this animal is one that people have traditionally hunted.
lemming_norway: The Norway lemming makes its home across Scandinavia, where it lives in tundra and mountain country. This small rodent weighs about 0.07 kilograms as an adult and feeds on plants. Its population swings in cycles of boom and crash, and some groups move from one area to another as conditions change.
gallimimus: Gallimimus bullatus was a fossil dinosaur that lived between 70 and 66 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Its remains have been found in sandstone of the Nemegt Formation on the Mongolian steppe. Adults reached about 440 kilograms, and the animal was built a lot like a modern ostrich, likely living and moving in herds.
shunosaurus: Shunosaurus lived in China during the Middle Jurassic, roughly 170 to 165 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Xiashaximiao Formation in the lowlands. This plant-eating dinosaur grew to an adult mass of about 4000 kilograms and carried a tail club at its end.
titanichthys: Titanichthys was a placoderm, an armored fish from the Devonian period roughly 360 to 358 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from the Cleveland Shale in eastern North America, where they are preserved in shale. This giant swam and fed by filtering food from the water, and adults reached about 1200 kilograms.
collared_lizard: The Eastern Collared Lizard ranges across the Great Plains, western North America, and Mexico, where it turns up in badlands, deserts, and grasslands. It is a meat eater that hunts during the daytime and can run quickly when threatened. An adult weighs only about 0.04 kilograms, and this species remains common in the wild today.
meiolania_damelipi: The Vanuatu Horned Turtle, which weighed around 100 kg as an adult, lived in the forests of island habitats in the southwest Pacific region. It grazed on plants and was known for its heavy shell, its horned skull, and a spiked tail club. This species went extinct around 1000 BC, a period that followed the arrival of Lapita people to the islands.
aurochs: The aurochs once roamed a vast range, from Europe and Iran through the Indian subcontinent, North African coast, Mongolian steppe, China, Japan, and Korea. It lived in forests, plains, and wetlands, grazing on herbs and moving in herds. Adults could weigh about 900 kilograms, and their horns and size made them prized as game and as a source for domestication. The last known cow died at Jaktorow in 1627.
quoll_spotted_tailed: The spotted-tailed quoll is a carnivorous marsupial that lives in forests, and it is still found today in Tasmania and parts of mainland Australia. Adults weigh about 3.5 kilograms. Active only at night, it is easy to recognize by the bold spots covering its coat and tail, and it is the largest marsupial carnivore on the Australian mainland.
dugong: The dugong grazes on seagrass across shallow coastal waters and reef flats, moving from the Red Sea through the Indian Ocean and Coral Triangle to the Great Barrier Reef. Adults can reach about 300 kilograms. It is a sirenian, and although it is still living and protected, it can be hunted in some places.
hypsilophodon: Hypsilophodon foxii was a small herbivorous dinosaur that lived between 130 and 125 million years ago during the Cretaceous period. Adults weighed about 20 kilograms. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Wessex Formation, part of the Wealden sequence in the British Isles, and specimens have turned up on the Isle of Wight.
sulcata_tortoise: The African spurred tortoise is the third largest tortoise in the world, with adults reaching about 70 kg. It lives across the Sahel and Sahara, moving through desert, savanna, and grassland. Its diet consists of herbs, and it uses burrows as shelter from the heat.
chinese_mountain_cat: The Chinese Mountain Cat roams high country, where it hunts from mountain slopes and open grassland. Adults weigh about 7 kilograms and live entirely on meat. Its thick fur has made it a target for hunters, so the species is now protected, and it still survives in the wild.
white_lipped_peccary: Roaming in large herds through jungle and forest, the white-lipped peccary can be found from Mexico down through Central America, the Amazon and Orinoco basins, and as far south as the Pampas and Gran Chaco. Adults weigh about 30 kilograms, and the species eats both plants and animals. Still thriving across its range, it is a herd animal that hunters pursue.
ethiopian_wolf: The Ethiopian wolf, known scientifically as Canis simensis, roams the grasslands and mountains of the Ethiopian highlands. Adults weigh about 16 kg and live in packs, hunting mostly during the day. Their thick fur and focus on rodents set them apart, and they remain alive today under legal protection.
nile_softshell: The Nile softshell turtle is the largest freshwater turtle found in Africa, and it lives across a broad range that stretches from the Sahara's southern edge to the Nile valley. It can also be found in Iran and Anatolia, where it swims through rivers, lakes, and coastal waters. Adults may reach about 60 kilograms, and it feeds mainly on other animals. Its flat, leathery shell gives it a soft, smooth edge rather than a hard, bony rim.
nyctosaurus: Nyctosaurus gracilis was a fossil pterosaur that lived during the Cretaceous, roughly 86 to 83 million years ago. Its remains have been found in the chalk of the Niobrara Chalk formation on the Great Plains. It ate fish and weighed about 2 kg as an adult. Its most striking feature was an antler-like crest on its head, and unlike many relatives, it had no claws on its hands.
indian_grey_mongoose: Found across the Indian subcontinent and Arabia, the Indian grey mongoose makes its home in grassland, desert, and forest. This daytime hunter weighs about 1.5 kg as an adult and feeds mainly on meat, with a reputation for killing snakes. It remains common and is not extinct.
quetzalcoatlus: Quetzalcoatlus northropi was a pterosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Its fossils have been recovered from mudstone of the Javelina Formation in the southern United States. Adults weighed about 250 kilograms and had wingspans of 10 to 11 meters, making this giant azhdarchid roughly the size of a giraffe.
matamata: The matamata is a freshwater turtle that lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, where it haunts rivers and swamps. Adults can reach about 15 kg, and their broad, flattened shells help them blend into leaf litter and submerged debris. This carnivore waits motionless on the bottom, then opens its mouth to create a sudden suction that pulls in passing fish.
three_toed_amphiuma: The Three-toed Amphiuma is a long, eel-like amphibian that lives in the southern United States, mainly in Florida and along the Gulf coast. It makes its home in swamps, wetlands, and rivers, where it spends its life in the water. Adults can reach about 1 kg, and they hunt other animals, so bites should be treated with caution.
chinese_ferret_badger: Out in the forests of the Chinese lowlands and Indochina, the Chinese ferret-badger roams mostly after dark. It eats a varied, omnivorous diet and weighs around 2 kilograms as an adult. Its thick fur helps it get by in its woodland home, and the species remains alive and well today.
seychelles_giant_tortoise_hololissa: The Seychelles Domed Giant Tortoise lived on islands and in forests, feeding on plants and herbs. Adults could reach about 120 kilograms. Overharvesting by people drove this species to extinction around the year 1900 AD.
allosaurus: Living roughly 155 to 145 million years ago during the Jurassic, this carnivore left its fossils in the sandstone of the Morrison Formation across western North America. An adult weighed about 2000 kg. It serves as a baseline example of the theropod group, the broader family of meat-eating dinosaurs.
baikal_seal: The Baikal seal lives only in Lake Baikal and the surrounding waters, a freshwater lake that stays icy for much of the year. It feeds mainly on fish and grows to an adult mass of about 85 kilograms. Thick blubber and a tendency to gather in herds help this species survive the cold, and it remains alive today.
beaver_american: The American beaver lives across North America in rivers, lakes, wetlands, and forests. It is a semi-aquatic herbivore that can swim well and builds dams. An adult typically weighs about 20 kilograms, and its dense fur has made it a huntable species, though it remains widespread today.
malagasy_ring_tailed_mongoose: The ring-tailed mongoose lives in the forests of Madagascar, where it hunts during the day. It is a meat eater that weighs about 0.8 kilograms as an adult. This animal has thick fur and is known to swim, and it remains alive in the wild today.
deinonychus: A fossil predator from the Cretaceous, living roughly 115 to 108 million years ago, Deinonychus is known from mudstone deposits of the Cloverly Formation in western North America. This carnivore weighed about 73 kg as an adult. It is thought to have hunted in packs and carried a large sickle-shaped claw on each foot.
tenrec_common: The tailless tenrec lives in the forests and jungles of Madagascar, where it eats a mix of plant and animal food. An adult weighs about 1.5 kilograms. It is active at night, hibernates during the colder months, and is covered in spines. This species is still alive and can be hunted.
baboon_hamadryas: The Hamadryas baboon roams the savanna of East Africa and the Arabian Peninsula, moving across desert, badlands, and open grassland. Adults weigh about 18 kg, and this still-thriving species eats both plants and animals. Active during the day, these primates live in herds.
prognathodon: Prognathodon overtoni swam the seas of the late Cretaceous, between 76 and 66 million years ago. Its fossils have turned up in the chalk of the Maastricht Chalk formation in Europe. This carnivore reached an adult mass of about 3000 kilograms, and its massive jaws mark it as a powerful predator.
wild_water_buffalo: Wild water buffalo roam across the Indian subcontinent and Indochina, moving through wetlands, grasslands, and swamps. Adults can weigh as much as 900 kilograms, and they feed on herbs while living in herds. Their large horns and strong swimming ability help them get around their watery homes, and they are still alive today.
white_rhino: The white rhinoceros, known scientifically as Ceratotherium simum, roams the savanna and grasslands of Africa south of the Sahara. It is a grazer that feeds on herbs and can reach an adult mass of about 2300 kg. Though it is still alive, its horn and its habit of living in herds set it apart in the region's grasslands.
reindeer: Reindeer roam the Arctic and subarctic, from the Scandinavian peninsula and Siberian taiga across to Alaska, the Yukon, and the Canadian Shield. They live in tundra, taiga, and icy terrain, feeding entirely on plants. Adults average around 130 kilograms, and they travel together in migratory herds that people have hunted and, in some regions, domesticated.
pampathere_pampatherium: The Southern pampathere was a heavy, armored mammal that roamed the pampas and Gran Chaco, as well as the Amazon and Orinoco regions. It grazed on herbs across open grassland and savanna, and an adult could weigh around 200 kilograms. Its body was protected by a bony shell, and it belonged to the group of large extinct animals known as megafauna. It disappeared roughly 8000 years ago.
lesser_mouse_deer: The lesser mouse-deer weighs about 2 kilograms as an adult and lives in the forests and jungles of Sundaland and Indochina. Despite its name, it is not a true deer, and males carry small tusk-like canines. It feeds on plants and remains widespread today.
torosaurus: Torosaurus latus is a fossil taxon that lived during the Cretaceous period, roughly 68 to 66 million years ago. Its remains have been recovered from sandstone in the Hell Creek formation of the Great Plains. Adults reached about 6500 kilograms, and this herbivore carried a huge frill with holes in it.
hangul: The Hangul is a deer that lives in mountain and forest country across its range. It feeds on herbs and grows to an adult mass of about 180 kg. Living in herds and carrying antlers, it remains alive today and is under legal protection.
schneider_dwarf_caiman: Schneider's Smooth-fronted Caiman lives in the Amazon and Orinoco basins, where it is still found today. It makes its home in rivers, jungle streams, and swamps, and an adult typically weighs about 30 kg. This small, nocturnal caiman is a strong swimmer with armored scales and a carnivorous diet.
jararaca: The jararaca is a venomous pit viper known scientifically as Bothrops jararaca, and it still thrives today. It lives across the Southern Cone and the Amazon basin, moving through forest and jungle habitats. Adults typically reach about 1 kilogram, and the snake hunts meat prey, relying on the heat-sensing pit organs on its face to locate targets.
green_pit_viper: The White-lipped Pit Viper is a venomous snake that still thrives in the lowlands of Indochina, the Indian subcontinent, and China. It lives among trees in forest and jungle, where it hunts other animals and spends much of its time off the ground. Adults weigh about 0.2 kilograms, and heat-sensing pit organs help it locate prey.
rat_brown: Active mostly at night, the brown rat is a burrowing species that still thrives today. It lives across the lowlands of China and the eastern steppe, moving through grassland and wetland alike. Eating a varied, omnivorous diet, an adult typically weighs about 0.3 kilograms, and it is a capable swimmer.
tuatara: The tuatara is a reptile found only in New Zealand, where it lives in forests, along coasts, and on islands. It feeds mainly on insects, and adults weigh about 1 kilogram. Although it looks like a lizard, it belongs to a separate lineage, and it remains alive today under legal protection.
giganotosaurus: Giganotosaurus carolinii lived in what is now Patagonia roughly 99 to 97 million years ago, during the Cretaceous. Its fossils have been recovered from sandstone of the Candeleros Formation. An adult may have weighed about 8000 kilograms, and it is considered the largest meat-eating predator known from South America.
rat_kangaroo_desert: The desert rat-kangaroo once lived across an area of central Australia spanning roughly 26 to 30 degrees south and 136 to 141 degrees east. This nocturnal hopper weighed about 1 kilogram as an adult and fed on plants found in its dry desert home. It was last recorded in 1935, and it is now extinct.
rubber_boa: The Rubber Boa roams the forests and mountains of the Pacific Northwest and western North America. This small snake weighs about 0.1 kilograms as an adult and feeds on other animals. It is a docile constrictor with smooth scales that burrows into the ground, and it remains widespread today.
marine_iguana: The Galapagos marine iguana lives along the rocky coasts of the Galapagos Islands, where warm ocean waters meet the shore. Adults weigh about 4 kg, and they spend their days foraging in the sea. They swim well, grazing on algae, and bask on the rocks afterward to warm their bodies. Large groups often gather together along the shoreline.
pygmy_hog: The pygmy hog is a small wild pig that makes its home in grasslands, where it builds burrows for shelter. It eats both plants and animals and weighs about 9 kg as an adult. Although it still survives in the wild, it is a protected species.
bahamas_giant_tortoise: The Bahamian Giant Tortoise lived across a stretch of islands, coastlines, and forests within the Bahamas, roughly between 21 and 27 degrees north. It fed on plants and grew to an adult mass of about 30 kg, with a domed shell that marked it as a notable island reptile. This species went extinct around 1300 AD, shortly after the Lucayan people arrived in the region.
flying_fox_golden_crowned: The giant golden-crowned flying fox roams jungle habitats across the area coded 5, 19, 119, and 126.5, where it survives in the wild. Adults weigh about 1.2 kg, and the species feeds mainly on fruit. It lives in colonies, flies at night, and is a protected animal.
canada_lynx: The Canada lynx roams the northwestern reaches of North America, from Alaska and the Yukon across the Canadian Shield. It prefers taiga, forest, and tundra, where it hunts mainly. Adults weigh about 10 kilograms, and their dense fur has long made them a sought-after catch for trappers. The species remains widespread and is not extinct.
binturong: The binturong, also called the bearcat, lives in the jungles and forests of Indochina, Sundaland, and the Indian subcontinent. Adults weigh about 14 kg, and their shaggy fur helps them move through the trees, where they spend much of their time. Active at night, this omnivore uses its prehensile tail to grip branches, and it gives off a distinctive popcorn-like scent.
water_deer: Roaming the lowlands of China, Japan, and Korea, this small deer favors wetlands and grassy areas where it grazes on herbs. An adult weighs about 15 kilograms, and it stands out among deer for lacking antlers, since males instead grow prominent tusks. It remains widespread today and can be hunted in some areas.
anomalocaris: Anomalocaris lived during the Cambrian, roughly 508 to 505 million years ago, and its fossils turn up in shale of the Burgess Shale formation in northwestern North America. This swimming predator was a carnivore that reached about 2 kilograms as an adult and ranked among the top hunters of its time. Its body plan stretched out like a swimmer's, marking it as a radiodont, an early relative of the arthropods.
flying_fox_large: The large flying fox is a nocturnal bat found across Sundaland, Indochina, Wallacea and New Guinea. It roosts in colonies and lives in both jungle and coastal areas, where it feeds on fruit. Adults weigh about 1.1 kg, and the species is still alive, though it can be hunted.
